arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُقَدِّمُ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلرَّكَعَاتِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ سِتَّ رَكَعَاتٍ» قُلْتُ فَأَيُّهُمَا أَفْضَلُ أُقَدِّمُ اَلرَّكَعَاتِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ أَمْ أُصَلِّيهَا بَعْدَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ قَالَ« تُصَلِّيهَا بَعْدَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ أَفْضَلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I perform some rak’ahs on the day of Friday beforehand?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, six rak’ahs.” I asked: “Which of the two is better, that I perform the rak’ahs on the day of Friday beforehand, or that I pray them after the obligatory prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Praying them after the obligatory prayer is better.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 16

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, he said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the recitation on the day of Friday if I pray alone four rak’ahs, should I recite aloud? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes,” And Imam (a.s) said: “Recite Surah al-Jumu’ah and al-Munafiqun on the day of Friday.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ فِي يَوْمِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ إِذَا صَلَّيْتُ وَحْدِي أَرْبَعاً أَجْهَرُ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» وَ قَالَ« اِقْرَأْ بِسُورَةِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَ اَلْمُنَافِقِينَ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the recitation on the day of Friday if I pray alone four rak’ahs, should I recite aloud? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes,” And Imam (a.s) said: “Recite Surah al-Jumu’ah and al-Munafiqun on the day of Friday.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 16

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Imran al-Halabi, he said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say and Imam (a.s) was asked about a man who performs the Friday prayer as four rak’ahs, should he recite aloud in it? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and the qunut is in the second rak’ah.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْخَطَّابِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: وَ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي اَلْجُمُعَةَ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ أَ يَجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ وَ اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad ibn Uthman from Imran al-Halabi, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say and Imam (a.s) was asked about a man who performs the Friday prayer as four rak’ahs, should he recite aloud in it? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and the qunut is in the second rak’ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 16

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ali ibn al-Numan from Abdillah ibn Muskan from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said to us: “Perform the Friday prayer (Salat Al Jumu'ah) in congregation while traveling, without a sermon, and recite aloud.” So I asked: “It is objected against us to recite aloud during travel.” Imam (a.s) said: “Recite aloud.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ لَنَا« صَلُّوا فِي اَلسَّفَرِ صَلاَةَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ جَمَاعَةً بِغَيْرِ خُطْبَةٍ وَ اِجْهَرُوا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ» فَقُلْتُ إِنَّهُ يُنْكَرُ عَلَيْنَا اَلْجَهْرُ بِهَا فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَقَالَ« اِجْهَرُوا بِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ali ibn al-Numan from Abdillah ibn Muskan from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said to us: “Perform the Friday prayer (Salat Al Jumu'ah) in congregation while traveling, without a sermon, and recite aloud.” So I asked: “It is objected against us to recite aloud during travel.” Imam (a.s) said: “Recite aloud.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 16

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn Abdillah al-Arrajani, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, he said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the Dhuhr prayer on the day of Friday, how should we perform it while traveling? Imam (a.s) said: “You perform it while traveling as two rak’ahs, and the recitation in it is aloud.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْأَرَّجَانِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ كَيْفَ نُصَلِّيهَا فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَقَالَ« تُصَلِّيهَا فِي اَلسَّفَرِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ اَلْقِرَاءَةُ فِيهَا جَهْراً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from al-Husayn ibn Abdillah al-Arrajani, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the Dhuhr prayer on the day of Friday, how should we perform it while traveling? Imam (a.s) said: “You perform it while traveling as two rak’ahs, and the recitation in it is aloud.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 17

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil, he said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about congregational prayer on the day of Friday while traveling. Imam (a.s) said: “You do as you would do on other than Friday for the Dhuhr prayer, and the imam (of prayer) does not recite aloud, he only recites aloud if there is a sermon.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْجَمَاعَةِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ فَقَالَ« تَصْنَعُونَ كَمَا تَصْنَعُونَ فِي غَيْرِ يَوْمِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فِي اَلظُّهْرِ وَ لاَ يَجْهَرُ اَلْإِمَامُ إِنَّمَا يَجْهَرُ إِذَا كَانَتْ خُطْبَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about congregational prayer on the day of Friday while traveling. Imam (a.s) said: “You do as you would do on other than Friday for the Dhuhr prayer, and the imam (of prayer) does not recite aloud, he only recites aloud if there is a sermon.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 17

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, he said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the Friday prayer (Salat Al Jumu'ah) while traveling. Imam (a.s) said: “You do as you do for Dhuhr, and the imam (of prayer) does not recite aloud in it. He only recites aloud if there is a sermon.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ قَالَ« تَصْنَعُونَ كَمَا تَصْنَعُونَ فِي اَلظُّهْرِ وَ لاَ يَجْهَرُ اَلْإِمَامُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ وَ إِنَّمَا يَجْهَرُ إِذَا كَانَتْ خُطْبَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about the Friday prayer (Salat Al Jumu'ah) while traveling. Imam (a.s) said: “You do as you do for Dhuhr, and the imam (of prayer) does not recite aloud in it. He only recites aloud if there is a sermon.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 17

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, he said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a group of people in a village who do not have anyone to lead the Friday prayer for them, should they perform the Dhuhr prayer in congregation on the day of Friday? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, if they are not in fear.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ فِي قَرْيَةٍ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ مَنْ يُجَمِّعُ بِهِمْ أَ يُصَلُّونَ اَلظُّهْرَ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ قَالَ« نَعَمْ إِذَا لَمْ يَخَافُوا» فصرح ع
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a group of people in a village who do not have anyone to lead the Friday prayer for them, should they perform the Dhuhr prayer in congregation on the day of Friday? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, if they are not in fear.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 17

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Husayn from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn Isa from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and Safwan from Abu Ayyub, he said: Sulayman ibn Khalid narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Qunut on the day of Friday is in the first rak’ah.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Husayn from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn Isa from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and Safwan from Abu Ayyub, he said: Sulayman ibn Khalid narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Qunut on the day of Friday is in the first rak’ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 18

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Ismail al-Jufi, from Umar ibn Hanzalah, he said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “(What about) the qunut on the day of Friday?” Imam (a.s) said: “You are my messenger to them in this matter, if you pray in congregation, then it is in the first rak’ah; and if you pray individually, then it is in the second rak’ah.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلْجُعْفِيِّ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِاَ للَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلْقُنُوتُ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ« أَنْتَ رَسُولِي إِلَيْهِمْ فِي هَذَا إِذَا صَلَّيْتُمْ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَفِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى وَ إِذَا صَلَّيْتُمْ وُحْدَاناً فَفِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Ismail al-Jufi, from Umar ibn Hanzalah, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “(What about) the qunut on the day of Friday?” Imam (a.s) said: “You are my messenger to them in this matter, if you pray in congregation, then it is in the first rak’ah; and if you pray individually, then it is in the second rak’ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 18

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zurah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Basir, he said:
He said: “Qunut is in the first rak’ah before ruku.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zurah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Basir, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: He said: “Qunut is in the first rak’ah before ruku.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 18

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, he said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “In the qunut of Friday, if he is the imam, he performs qunut in the first rak’ah. But if he is praying four rak’ahs, then in the second rak’ah, before ruku.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« فِي قُنُوتِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ إِذَا كَانَ إِمَاماً قَنَتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى وَ إِنْ كَانَ يُصَلِّي أَرْبَعاً فَفِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “In the qunut of Friday, if he is the imam, he performs qunut in the first rak’ah. But if he is praying four rak’ahs, then in the second rak’ah, before ruku.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 18

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Salih from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, he said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The qunut of Jumu‘ah, should it be in the first rak‘ah before the bowing (ruku), and in the second after it?” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Neither before nor after.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ بْنِ عَمْرٍو قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قُنُوتُ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ بَعْدَهُ فَقَالَ لِي« لاَ قَبْلُ وَ لاَ بَعْدُ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Salih from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The qunut of Jumu‘ah, should it be in the first rak‘ah before the bowing (ruku), and in the second after it?” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Neither before nor after.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 19

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Sa’ad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, he said:
I heard Muammar ibn Abi Riab ask Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and I was present about the qunut in the Friday prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no qunut in it.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ اَلْحُصَيْنِ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ مُعَمَّرَ بْنَ أَبِي رِئَابٍ يَسْأَلُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَنَا حَاضِرٌ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ فِيهَا قُنُوتٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And Sa’ad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Muammar ibn Abi Riab ask Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and I was present about the qunut in the Friday prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no qunut in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 19

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir, he said:
Abd al-Hamid asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, while I was with him about the qunut on the day of Friday. Imam (a.s) said: “In the second rak’ah.” So he (Abd al-Hamid) asked Imam (a.s): “Some of our companions have narrated to us that you said it is in the first rak’ah.” Imam (a.s) replied: “In the last one.” And there were many people present with Imam (a.s). But when Imam (a.s) saw that they were inattentive, Imam (a.s) said: “O Aba Muhammad, it is in the first and the last.” I asked: “May I be your ransom, before rukuh or after it?” Imam (a.s) said: “All qunut is before rukuh, except on Friday for in the first rak’ah the qunut is before rukuh, and in the last one, after ruku.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ عَبْدُ اَلْحَمِيدِ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَنَا عِنْدَهُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي يَوْمِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ قَالَ« فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ» فَقَالَ لَهُ قَدْ حَدَّثَنَا بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا أَنَّكَ قُلْتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى فَقَالَ« فِي اَلْأَخِيرَةِ» وَ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ نَاسٌ كَثِيرٌ فَلَمَّا رَأَى غَفْلَةً مِنْهُمْ قَالَ« يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ هُوَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى وَ اَلْأَخِيرَةِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُ قَالَ« كُلُّ اَلْقُنُوتِ قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ إِلاَّ اَلْجُمُعَةَ فَإِنَّ اَلرَّكْعَةَ اَلْأُولَى اَلْقُنُوتُ فِيهَا قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلْأَخِيرَةَ بَعْدَ اَلرُّكُوعِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abd al-Hamid asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, while I was with him about the qunut on the day of Friday. Imam (a.s) said: “In the second rak’ah.” So he (Abd al-Hamid) asked Imam (a.s): “Some of our companions have narrated to us that you said it is in the first rak’ah.” Imam (a.s) replied: “In the last one.” And there were many people present with Imam (a.s). But when Imam (a.s) saw that they were inattentive, Imam (a.s) said: “O Aba Muhammad, it is in the first and the last.” I asked: “May I be your ransom, before rukuh or after it?” Imam (a.s) said: “All qunut is before rukuh, except on Friday for in the first rak’ah the qunut is before rukuh, and in the last one, after ruku.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 19

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, he said:
He said regarding the qunut of Friday: “O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and upon the leaders of the Muslims. O’ Allah (swt), make me among those whom You (azj) created for Your religion, and among those whom You (azj) created for Your Paradise.” I asked: “Should I name the Imams (a.s) one by one?” Imam (a.s) said: “Name them collectively.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: فِي قُنُوتِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ« اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ عَلَى أَئِمَّةِ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ اَللَّهُمَّ اِجْعَلْنِي مِمَّنْ خَلَقْتَهُ لِدِينِكَ وَ مِمَّنْ خَلَقْتَهُ لِجَنَّتِكَ» قُلْتُ أُسَمِّي اَلْأَئِمَّةَ قَالَ «سَمِّهِمْ جُمْلَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Aban from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: He said regarding the qunut of Friday: “O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and upon the leaders of the Muslims. O’ Allah (swt), make me among those whom You (azj) created for Your religion, and among those whom You (azj) created for Your Paradise.” I asked: “Should I name the Imams (a.s) one by one?” Imam (a.s) said: “Name them collectively.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 20

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from some of our companions, from Sama’ah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The qunut on the day of Jumu‘ah is in the first rak‘ah after the recitation. In the qunut you say: ‘There is no God but Allah (swt), the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no God but Allah (swt), the Most High, the Most Great. There is no God but Allah (swt), Lord (azj) of the seven heavens and the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them, Lord (azj) of the Mighty Throne, and all praise is due to Allah (swt), Lord (azj) of the worlds. O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), just as You (azj) guided us through him. O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), just as You (azj) honored us through him. O’ Allah (swt), make us among those whom You (azj) have chosen for Your religion and created for Your Paradise. O’ Allah (swt), do not let our hearts deviate after You (azj) have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself (azj), indeed, You (azj) are the Bestower.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْقُنُوتُ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى بَعْدَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ تَقُولُ فِي اَلْقُنُوتِ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ اَلْحَلِيمُ اَلْكَرِيمُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ اَلْعَلِيُّ اَلْعَظِيمُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ رَبُّ اَلسَّمَاوَاتِ اَلسَّبْعِ وَ رَبُّ اَلْأَرَضِينَ اَلسَّبْعِ وَ مَا فِيهِنَّ وَ مَا بَيْنَهُنَّ وَ« رَبُّ اَلْعَرْشِ اَلْعَظِيمِ»« وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ رَبِّ اَلْعٰالَمِينَ» اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا هَدَيْتَنَا بِهِ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَمَا أَكْرَمْتَنَا بِهِ اَللَّهُمَّ اِجْعَلْنَا مِمَّنِ اِخْتَرْتَهُ لِدِينِكَ وَ خَلَقْتَهُ لِجَنَّتِكَ اَللَّهُمَّ« لاٰ تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنٰا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنٰا وَ هَبْ لَنٰا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَلْوَهّٰابُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from some of our companions, from Sama’ah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The qunut on the day of Jumu‘ah is in the first rak‘ah after the recitation. In the qunut you say: ‘There is no God but Allah (swt), the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no God but Allah (swt), the Most High, the Most Great. There is no God but Allah (swt), Lord (azj) of the seven heavens and the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them, Lord (azj) of the Mighty Throne, and all praise is due to Allah (swt), Lord (azj) of the worlds. O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), just as You (azj) guided us through him. O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), just as You (azj) honored us through him. O’ Allah (swt), make us among those whom You (azj) have chosen for Your religion and created for Your Paradise. O’ Allah (swt), do not let our hearts deviate after You (azj) have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself (azj), indeed, You (azj) are the Bestower.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 20

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughirah from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever says, after the Friday prayer when he finishes and is seated before performing any rak’ah; Surah al-Hamd once, and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) seven times, and ‘Qul Audhu bi-Rabbi al-Falaq’ (Surah al-Falaq) seven times, and ‘Qul Audhu bi-Rabbi al-Nas’ (Surah An-Nas) seven times, and Ayat al-Kursi, and Ayat al-Sukhrah, and the ending part of His (swt) saying: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves…” (Surah At Tawbah 9:128) to the end of the verse, This will be an expiation (of sins) for what is between that Friday and the next.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ قَالَ بَعْدَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ حِينَ يَنْصَرِفُ جَالِساً مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ اَلْحَمْدَ مَرَّةً وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» سَبْعاً وَ« قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ اَلْفَلَقِ» سَبْعاً وَ« قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ اَلنّٰاسِ» سَبْعاً وَ آيَةَ اَلْكُرْسِيِّ وَ آيَةَ اَلسُّخْرَةِ وَ آخِرَ قَوْلِهِ« لَقَدْ جٰاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ» إِلَى آخِرِهَا كَانَتْ كَفَّارَةً مَا بَيْنَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ إِلَى اَلْجُمُعَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughirah from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever says, after the Friday prayer when he finishes and is seated before performing any rak’ah; Surah al-Hamd once, and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) seven times, and ‘Qul Audhu bi-Rabbi al-Falaq’ (Surah al-Falaq) seven times, and ‘Qul Audhu bi-Rabbi al-Nas’ (Surah An-Nas) seven times, and Ayat al-Kursi, and Ayat al-Sukhrah, and the ending part of His (swt) saying: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves…” (Surah At Tawbah 9:128) to the end of the verse, This will be an expiation (of sins) for what is between that Friday and the next.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 20

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from a group, among them al-Fudayl and Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, combined between Dhuhr and Asr with one adhan and two iqamahs, and He (saws) combined between Maghrib and Isha with one adhan and two iqamahs.”
arabicText: رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ رَهْطٍ مِنْهُمُ اَلْفُضَيْلُ وَ زُرَارَةُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ جَمَعَ بَيْنَ اَلظُّهْرِ وَ اَلْعَصْرِ بِأَذَانٍ وَ إِقَامَتَيْنِ وَ جَمَعَ بَيْنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءِ بِأَذَانٍ وَاحِدٍ وَ إِقَامَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from a group, among them al-Fudayl and Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, combined between Dhuhr and Asr with one adhan and two iqamahs, and He (saws) combined between Maghrib and Isha with one adhan and two iqamahs.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 21

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abu Ja’far from his father from Hafs ibn Ghiyath from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, he said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The third adhan on the day of Friday is an innovation (bidah).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ غِيَاثٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «اَلْأَذَانُ اَلثَّالِثُ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ بِدْعَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abu Ja’far from his father from Hafs ibn Ghiyath from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The third adhan on the day of Friday is an innovation (bidah).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 21

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini, from Zakariya al-Mumin, from Ibn Najah, from Dawud ibn al-Numan, from Abdillah ibn Sayabah, from Najah, he said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you perform the Asr prayer on the day of Friday, then say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), the appointed successors who are pleasing to You (azj), with the best of Your blessings; and bless them with the best of Your blessings; and peace be upon them, and upon their souls and their bodies; and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His (azj) blessings.” Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever says this after the Asr prayer, Allah (swt) will write for him one hundred thousand good deeds, and erase from him one hundred thousand evil deeds, and fulfill for him one hundred thousand needs, and raise him by it one hundred thousand degrees.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى اَلْيَقْطِينِيِّ عَنْ زَكَرِيَّا اَلْمُؤْمِنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ نَاجِيَةَ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سَيَابَةَ عَنْ نَاجِيَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ اَلْعَصْرَ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَقُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْأَوْصِيَاءِ اَلْمَرْضِيِّينَ بِأَفْضَلِ صَلَوَاتِكَ وَ بَارِكْ عَلَيْهِمْ بِأَفْضَلِ بَرَكَاتِكَ وَ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ عَلَى أَرْوَاحِهِمْ وَ أَجْسَادِهِمْ وَ رَحْمَةُ اَللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ» قَالَ« مَنْ قَالَهَا فِي دُبُرِ اَلْعَصْرِ كَتَبَ اَللَّهُ لَهُ مِائَةَ أَلْفِ حَسَنَةٍ وَ مَحَا عَنْهُ مِائَةَ أَلْفِ سَيِّئَةٍ وَ قَضَى لَهُ مِائَةَ أَلْفِ حَاجَةٍ وَ رَفَعَ لَهُ بِهَا مِائَةَ أَلْفِ دَرَجَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Yaqtini, from Zakariya al-Mumin, from Ibn Najah, from Dawud ibn al-Numan, from Abdillah ibn Sayabah, from Najah, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you perform the Asr prayer on the day of Friday, then say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), the appointed successors who are pleasing to You (azj), with the best of Your blessings; and bless them with the best of Your blessings; and peace be upon them, and upon their souls and their bodies; and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His (azj) blessings.” Imam (a.s) said: “Whoever says this after the Asr prayer, Allah (swt) will write for him one hundred thousand good deeds, and erase from him one hundred thousand evil deeds, and fulfill for him one hundred thousand needs, and raise him by it one hundred thousand degrees.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 21

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Asim ibn Humayd from Abu Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory in every seven days; thirty-five prayers, among them is a prayer that is obligatory upon every Muslim to attend, except for five; the sick person, the slave, the traveller, the woman, and the child.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَاصِمِ بْنِ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَرَضَ فِي كُلِّ سَبْعَةِ أَيَّامٍ خَمْساً وَ ثَلاَثِينَ صَلاَةً مِنْهَا صَلاَةٌ وَاجِبٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ أَنْ يَشْهَدَهَا إِلاَّ خَمْسَةً اَلْمَرِيضَ وَ اَلْمَمْلُوكَ وَ اَلْمُسَافِرَ وَ اَلْمَرْأَةَ وَ اَلصَّبِيَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Asim ibn Humayd from Abu Basir and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory in every seven days; thirty-five prayers, among them is a prayer that is obligatory upon every Muslim to attend, except for five; the sick person, the slave, the traveller, the woman, and the child.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 21

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama’ah, he said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the prayer on the day of Friday. Imam (a.s) said: “As for with the (just) imam, then it is two rak’ahs. And as for one who prays alone, then it is four rak’ahs, like the Dhuhr prayer meaning, when there is an (just) imam delivering the sermon. But if there is no (just) imam delivering the sermon, then it is four rak’ahs, even if they pray in congregation.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَرَكْعَتَانِ وَ أَمَّا مَنْ صَلَّى وَحْدَهُ فَهِيَ أَرْبَعُ رَكَعَاتٍ بِمَنْزِلَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ يَعْنِي إِذَا كَانَ إِمَامٌ يَخْطُبُ فَإِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ إِمَامٌ يَخْطُبُ فَهِيَ أَرْبَعُ رَكَعَاتٍ وَ إِنْ صَلَّوْا جَمَاعَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama’ah, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the prayer on the day of Friday. Imam (a.s) said: “As for with the (just) imam, then it is two rak’ahs. And as for one who prays alone, then it is four rak’ahs, like the Dhuhr prayer meaning, when there is an (just) imam delivering the sermon. But if there is no (just) imam delivering the sermon, then it is four rak’ahs, even if they pray in congregation.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 21

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When the (just) imam delivers the sermon on the day of Friday, it is not appropriate for anyone to speak until the (just) imam finishes his sermon. Then, once the (just) imam has finished his sermon, he may speak between that and the time the prayer is established. And whether he hears the recitation or does not hear it, it suffices him.”

thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-Ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When the (just) imam delivers the sermon on the day of Friday, it is not appropriate for anyone to speak until the (just) imam finishes his sermon. Then, once the (just) imam has finished his sermon, he may speak between that and the time the prayer is established. And whether he hears the recitation or does not hear it, it suffices him.”

Ali ibn Mahziyar from Uthman ibn Isa from Abu Maryam from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the sermon of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was it before the prayer or after it? Imam (a.s) said: “Before the prayer, then He (saws) would pray.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī

From him, from Fadalah, from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb, he said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The first one who delivered a sermon while sitting was Mu‘awiyah, and he sought the people’s permission for that due to a pain that was in his knees. So he would deliver one sermon while sitting and one sermon while standing, then he would sit between the two.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “The sermon while standing consists of two sermons between which he sits for a sitting during which he does not speak, (lasting) the amount of time that separates the two sermons.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِنَّ أَوَّلَ مَنْ خَطَبَ وَهُوَ جَالِسٌ مُعَاوِيَةُ وَ اِسْتَأْذَنَ اَلنَّاسَ فِي ذَلِكَ مِنْ وَجَعٍ كَانَ فِي رُكْبَتَيْهِ وَ كَانَ يَخْطُبُ خُطْبَةً وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ وَ خُطْبَةً وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ بَيْنَهُمَا» ثُمَّ قَالَ« اَلْخُطْبَةُ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ خُطْبَتَانِ يَجْلِسُ بَيْنَهُمَا جَلْسَةً لاَ يَتَكَلَّمُ فِيهَا قَدْرَ مَا يَكُونُ فَصْلٌ مَا بَيْنَ اَلْخُطْبَتَيْنِ»

thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The first one who delivered a sermon while sitting was Mu‘awiyah, and he sought the people’s permission for that due to a pain that was in his knees. So he would deliver one sermon while sitting and one sermon while standing, then he would sit between the two.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “The sermon while standing consists of two sermons between which he sits for a sitting during which he does not speak, (lasting) the amount of time that separates the two sermons.”

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Friday prayer is obligatory upon seven individuals from among the Muslims, and it is not obligatory upon fewer than them; the (just) imam, his judge, the one claiming a right, the one against whom the claim is made, the two witnesses, and the one who carries out the punishments before the (just) imam.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَكَمِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« تَجِبُ اَلْجُمُعَةُ عَلَى سَبْعَةِ نَفَرٍ مِنَ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ لاَ تَجِبُ عَلَى أَقَلَّ مِنْهُمْ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ قَاضِيهِ وَ اَلْمُدَّعِي حَقّاً وَ اَلْمُدَّعَى عَلَيْهِ وَ اَلشَّاهِدَانِ وَ اَلَّذِي يَضْرِبُ اَلْحُدُودَ بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اَلْإِمَامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Friday prayer is obligatory upon seven individuals from among the Muslims, and it is not obligatory upon fewer than them; the (just) imam, his judge, the one claiming a right, the one against whom the claim is made, the two witnesses, and the one who carries out the punishments before the (just) imam.”

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The minimum (number of individuals) that suffices for Friday prayer is seven, or five the minimum.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَدْنَى مَا يُجْزِي فِي اَلْجُمُعَةِ سَبْعَةٌ أَوْ خَمْسَةٌ أَدْنَاهُ» وليس بين هذين الخبرين تناقض لان الخبر الاول الذي تضمن اعتبار سبعة انفس فهو على طريق الفرض والوجوب والخبر الاخير على طريق الندب والاستحباب وعلى جهة الاولى والافضل
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadalah from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The minimum (number of individuals) that suffices for Friday prayer is seven, or five the minimum.”

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Allah (swt) has made obligatory upon the people from one Friday to the next thirty-five prayers, among them is one prayer which Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory in congregation, and that is the Friday prayer. And He (azj) has exempted it from nine (categories of people); the child, the elderly, the insane, the traveller, the slave, the woman, the sick person, the blind person, and the one who is at a distance of two farsakhs.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« فَرَضَ اَللَّهُ عَلَى اَلنَّاسِ مِنَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ إِلَى اَلْجُمُعَةِ خَمْساً وَ ثَلاَثِينَ صَلاَةً مِنْهَا صَلاَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَرَضَهَا اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ وَ هِيَ اَلْجُمُعَةُ وَ وَضَعَهَا عَنْ تِسْعَةٍ عَنِ اَلصَّغِيرِ وَ اَلْكَبِيرِ وَ اَلْمَجْنُونِ وَ اَلْمُسَافِرِ وَ اَلْعَبْدِ وَ اَلْمَرْأَةِ وَ اَلْمَرِيضِ وَ اَلْأَعْمَى وَ مَنْ كَانَ عَلَى رَأْسِ فَرْسَخَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Allah (swt) has made obligatory upon the people from one Friday to the next thirty-five prayers, among them is one prayer which Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has made obligatory in congregation, and that is the Friday prayer. And He (azj) has exempted it from nine (categories of people); the child, the elderly, the insane, the traveller, the slave, the woman, the sick person, the blind person, and the one who is at a distance of two farsakhs.”

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Abbad ibn Sulayman from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, he said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say regarding a man who caught the Friday prayer and the people were crowded, and he said the takbir along with the (just) imam and bowed (in ruku‘), but was not able to prostrate due to the crowding. Then the imam (of prayer) and the people stood up for the second rak‘ah, and he stood with them. The imam (of prayer) bowed, but he was not able to bow in the second rak‘ah because of the crowding, yet he was able to prostrate what should he do? Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “As for the first rak‘ah, it is complete up to the point of bowing (ruku‘), but since he did not prostrate for it until he had entered into the second rak‘ah, that (first rak‘ah) was not valid for him. Then, when he prostrated in the second rak‘ah if he intended that this prostration was for the first rak‘ah, then the first rak‘ah is complete for him. So when the imam (of prayer) finishes with the salam, he stands and prays one rak‘ah, in which he prostrates, then performs the tashahhud and the salam. But if he did not intend that the prostration was for the first rak‘ah, then neither the first nor the second rak‘ah is valid for him. In that case, he must perform two prostrations and intend them for the first rak‘ah, and after that he must perform a complete second rak‘ah in which he prostrates.” Hafs said: “So I asked Ibn Abi Layla about it, but he did not criticize it nor come close (to answering it). And I heard one of their followers asking Ibn Abi Layla about the Friday prayer, whether it is obligatory upon a woman, a slave, and a traveller. So Ibn Abi Layla said: “The Friday prayer is not obligatory upon any of them, nor upon the one who is afraid.” The man then said to him (Ibn Abi Layla): “What do you say if one of them attends the Friday prayer with the imam (of prayer) and prays it with him; does that prayer suffice for the Dhuhr of that day?” He replied: “Yes.” So the man said to him: “And how can something which Allah (swt) has not made obligatory upon him, suffice for that which Allah (swt) has made obligatory upon him? You have said that the Friday prayer is not obligatory upon him, and whoever it is not obligatory upon, the obligation upon him is to pray four units. It follows, then, from your view, that Allah (swt) has made four obligatory upon him, so how can two rak‘ahs suffice for him? And from this it also follows that whoever enters into that which Allah (swt) has not obligated upon him, it does not suffice him for what Allah (swt) has obligated upon him.” So Ibn Abi Layla had no answer for it, and the man requested him to explain it, but he refused. Then I asked him about it, and he explained it to me. He said: “The answer to that is that Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has made it obligatory upon all believing men and women, and granted a concession to the woman, the traveller, and the slave not to attend it. But when they are present at it, the concession falls away, and the original obligation becomes incumbent upon them. For that reason, it suffices them.” So I asked: “From whom is this (explanation)?” He said: “From our master Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَبَّادِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ غِيَاثٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: فِي رَجُلٍ أَدْرَكَ اَلْجُمُعَةَ وَقَدِ اِزْدَحَمَ اَلنَّاسُ وَ كَبَّرَ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ رَكَعَ وَ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى اَلسُّجُودِ وَ قَامَ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ اَلنَّاسُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ وَ قَامَ هَذَا مَعَهُمْ فَرَكَعَ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ هُوَ عَلَى اَلرُّكُوعِ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ مِنَ اَلزِّحَامِ وَ قَدَرَ عَلَى اَلسُّجُودِ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« أَمَّا اَلرَّكْعَةُ اَلْأُولَى فَهِيَ إِلَى عِنْدِ اَلرُّكُوعِ تَامَّةٌ فَلَمَّا لَمْ يَسْجُدْ لَهَا حَتَّى دَخَلَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ ذَلِكَ فَلَمَّا سَجَدَ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ فَإِنْ كَانَ نَوَى أَنَّ هَذِهِ اَلسَّجْدَةَ هِيَ لِلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى فَقَدْ تَمَّتْ لَهُ اَلرَّكْعَةُ اَلْأُولَى فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ اَلْإِمَامُ قَامَ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَةً يَسْجُدُ فِيهَا ثُمَّ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يُسَلِّمُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ لَمْ يَنْوِ أَنْ تَكُونَ تِلْكَ اَلسَّجْدَةُ لِلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى لَمْ تُجْزِ عَنْهُ اَلْأُولَى وَ لاَ اَلثَّانِيَةُ وَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ سَجْدَتَيْنِ وَ يَنْوِيَ أَنَّهُمَا لِلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى وَ عَلَيْهِ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ رَكْعَةٌ تَامَّةٌ ثَانِيَةٌ يَسْجُدُ فِيهَا» قَالَ حَفْصٌ فَسَأَلْتُ عَنْهَا اِبْنَ أَبِي لَيْلَى فَمَا طَعَنَ فِيهَا وَ لاَ قَارَبَ قَالَ وَ سَمِعْتُ بَعْضَ مَوَالِيهِمْ يَسْأَلُ اِبْنَ أَبِي لَيْلَى عَنِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ هَلْ تَجِبُ عَلَى اَلْمَرْأَةِ وَ اَلْعَبْدِ وَ اَلْمُسَافِرِ فَقَالَ اِبْنُ أَبِي لَيْلَى لاَ تَجِبُ اَلْجُمُعَةُ عَلَى وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ وَ لاَ اَلْخَائِفِ فَقَالَ اَلرَّجُلُ فَمَا تَقُولُ إِنْ حَضَرَ وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمُ اَلْجُمُعَةَ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَصَلاَّهَا مَعَهُ فَهَلْ تُجْزِيهِ تِلْكَ اَلصَّلاَةُ عَنْ ظُهْرِ يَوْمِهِ فَقَالَ نَعَمْ فَقَالَ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ وَ كَيْفَ يُجْزِي مَا لَمْ يَفْرِضْهُ اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَمَّا فَرَضَهُ اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ قَدْ قُلْتَ إِنَّ اَلْجُمُعَةَ لاَ تَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ وَ مَنْ لَمْ تَجِبْ عَلَيْهِ اَلْجُمُعَةُ فَالْفَرْضُ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ أَرْبَعاً وَ يَلْزَمُكَ فِيهِ مَعْنَى أَنَّ اَللَّهَ فَرَضَ عَلَيْهِ أَرْبَعاً فَكَيْفَ أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُ رَكْعَتَانِ مَعَ مَا يَلْزَمُكَ أَنَّ مَنْ دَخَلَ فِيمَا لَمْ يَفْرِضْهُ اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ لَمْ يُجْزِ عَنْهُ مِمَّا فَرَضَ اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فَمَا كَانَ عِنْدَ اِبْنِ أَبِي لَيْلَى فِيهَا جَوَابٌ وَطَلَبَ إِلَيْهِ أَنْ يُفَسِّرَهَا لَهُ فَأَبَى ثُمَّ سَأَلْتُهُ أَنَا عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَفَسَّرَهَا لِي فَقَالَ اَلْجَوَابُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ« أَنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَرَضَ عَلَى جَمِيعِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ اَلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَ رَخَّصَ لِلْمَرْأَةِ وَ اَلْمُسَافِرِ وَ اَلْعَبْدِ أَنْ لاَ يَأْتُوهَا فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهَا سَقَطَتِ اَلرُّخْصَةُ وَ لَزِمَهُمُ اَلْفَرْضُ اَلْأَوَّلُ فَمِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُمْ» فَقُلْتُ عَمَّنْ هَذَا فَقَالَ عَنْ مَوْلاَنَا أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from ‘Abbad ibn Sulayman from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say regarding a man who caught the Friday prayer and the people were crowded, and he said the takbir along with the (just) imam and bowed (in ruku‘), but was not able to prostrate due to the crowding. Then the imam (of prayer) and the people stood up for the second rak‘ah, and he stood with them. The imam (of prayer) bowed, but he was not able to bow in the second rak‘ah because of the crowding, yet he was able to prostrate what should he do? Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “As for the first rak‘ah, it is complete up to the point of bowing (ruku‘), but since he did not prostrate for it until he had entered into the second rak‘ah, that (first rak‘ah) was not valid for him. Then, when he prostrated in the second rak‘ah if he intended that this prostration was for the first rak‘ah, then the first rak‘ah is complete for him. So when the imam (of prayer) finishes with the salam, he stands and prays one rak‘ah, in which he prostrates, then performs the tashahhud and the salam. But if he did not intend that the prostration was for the first rak‘ah, then neither the first nor the second rak‘ah is valid for him. In that case, he must perform two prostrations and intend them for the first rak‘ah, and after that he must perform a complete second rak‘ah in which he prostrates.” Hafs said: “So I asked Ibn Abi Layla about it, but he did not criticize it nor come close (to answering it). And I heard one of their followers asking Ibn Abi Layla about the Friday prayer, whether it is obligatory upon a woman, a slave, and a traveller. So Ibn Abi Layla said: “The Friday prayer is not obligatory upon any of them, nor upon the one who is afraid.” The man then said to him (Ibn Abi Layla): “What do you say if one of them attends the Friday prayer with the imam (of prayer) and prays it with him; does that prayer suffice for the Dhuhr of that day?” He replied: “Yes.” So the man said to him: “And how can something which Allah (swt) has not made obligatory upon him, suffice for that which Allah (swt) has made obligatory upon him? You have said that the Friday prayer is not obligatory upon him, and whoever it is not obligatory upon, the obligation upon him is to pray four units. It follows, then, from your view, that Allah (swt) has made four obligatory upon him, so how can two rak‘ahs suffice for him? And from this it also follows that whoever enters into that which Allah (swt) has not obligated upon him, it does not suffice him for what Allah (swt) has obligated upon him.” So Ibn Abi Layla had no answer for it, and the man requested him to explain it, but he refused. Then I asked him about it, and he explained it to me. He said: “The answer to that is that Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, has made it obligatory upon all believing men and women, and granted a concession to the woman, the traveller, and the slave not to attend it. But when they are present at it, the concession falls away, and the original obligation becomes incumbent upon them. For that reason, it suffices them.” So I asked: “From whom is this (explanation)?” He said: “From our master Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 24

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “There must be three miles between the two congregational prayers meaning that there should not be a Friday prayer unless there is a distance of three miles between it and another. And there is no Friday prayer except with a sermon. And if there is a distance of three miles between the two congregational prayers on Friday, then there is no harm in these ones holding the congregational prayer and those ones also holding the congregational prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَكُونُ بَيْنَ اَلْجَمَاعَتَيْنِ ثَلاَثَةُ أَمْيَالٍ يَعْنِي لاَ تَكُونُ جُمُعَةٌ إِلاَّ فِيمَا بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ ثَلاَثَةِ أَمْيَالٍ وَلَيْسَ تَكُونُ جُمُعَةٌ إِلاَّ بِخُطْبَةٍ وَ إِذَا كَانَ بَيْنَ اَلْجَمَاعَتَيْنِ فِي اَلْجُمُعَةِ ثَلاَثَةُ أَمْيَالٍ فَلاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يُجَمِّعَ هَؤُلاَءِ وَ يُجَمِّعَ هَؤُلاَءِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “There must be three miles between the two congregational prayers meaning that there should not be a Friday prayer unless there is a distance of three miles between it and another. And there is no Friday prayer except with a sermon. And if there is a distance of three miles between the two congregational prayers on Friday, then there is no harm in these ones holding the congregational prayer and those ones also holding the congregational prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The Friday prayer is obligatory upon whoever is within two farsakhs of it. And the meaning of that is when there is a just Imam.” And Imam (a.s) said: “If there is a distance of three miles between the two congregational prayers, then there is no harm in these ones holding the congregational prayer and those ones holding it as well. And there should not be less than three miles between the two congregational prayers.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« تَجِبُ اَلْجُمُعَةُ عَلَى مَنْ كَانَ مِنْهَا عَلَى فَرْسَخَيْنِ وَ مَعْنَى ذَلِكَ إِذَا كَانَ إِمَامٌ عَادِلٌ» وَ قَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ بَيْنَ اَلْجَمَاعَتَيْنِ ثَلاَثَةُ أَمْيَالٍ فَلاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ يُجَمِّعَ هَؤُلاَءِ وَيُجَمِّعَ هَؤُلاَءِ وَ لاَ يَكُونُ بَيْنَ اَلْجَمَاعَتَيْنِ أَقَلُّ مِنْ ثَلاَثَةِ أَمْيَالٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Jamil from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The Friday prayer is obligatory upon whoever is within two farsakhs of it. And the meaning of that is when there is a just Imam.” And Imam (a.s) said: “If there is a distance of three miles between the two congregational prayers, then there is no harm in these ones holding the congregational prayer and those ones holding it as well. And there should not be less than three miles between the two congregational prayers.”

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from a man from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Darir from Hammad ibn Isa from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam Ali (a.s) said: “When the caliph enters a city from among the cities, he leads the Friday prayer with the people, that is not for anyone other than him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ اَلضَّرِيرِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا قَدِمَ اَلْخَلِيفَةُ مِصْراً مِنَ اَلْأَمْصَارِ جَمَّعَ بِالنَّاسِ لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ لِأَحَدٍ غَيْرِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from a man from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Darir from Hammad ibn Isa from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) said: “When the caliph enters a city from among the cities, he leads the Friday prayer with the people, that is not for anyone other than him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 26

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Congregational Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, he said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “What do the people narrate, that prayer in congregation is better than a man’s individual prayer by twenty-five prayers?” Imam (a.s) said: “They have spoken the truth.” I asked: “Two men, are they considered a congregation?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and the man stands to the right of the Imam.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا يَرْوِي اَلنَّاسُ أَنَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلرَّجُلِ وَحْدَهُ بِخَمْسٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ صَلاَةً فَقَالَ« صَدَقُوا» فَقُلْتُ اَلرَّجُلاَنِ يَكُونَانِ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ يَقُومُ اَلرَّجُلُ عَنْ يَمِينِ اَلْإِمَامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “What do the people narrate, that prayer in congregation is better than a man’s individual prayer by twenty-five prayers?” Imam (a.s) said: “They have spoken the truth.” I asked: “Two men, are they considered a congregation?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and the man stands to the right of the Imam.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Congregational Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and al-Fudayl, they said:
We said to him: “Is prayer in congregation an obligation?” He said: “The prayers are obligatory, but gathering (for them) is not made obligatory in all the prayers. Rather, it is a sunnah whoever abandons it out of aversion to it and to the congregation of the believers, without a valid excuse, then he has no prayer.”
arabicText: حَمَّادٌ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ اَلْفُضَيْلِ قَالاَ: قُلْنَا لَهُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَرِيضَةٌ هِيَ فَقَالَ« اَلصَّلَوَاتُ فَرِيضَةٌ وَ لَيْسَ اَلاِجْتِمَاعُ بِمَفْرُوضٍ فِي اَلصَّلَوَاتِ كُلِّهَا وَ لَكِنَّهَا سُنَّةٌ مَنْ تَرَكَهَا رَغْبَةً عَنْهَا وَ عَنْ جَمَاعَةِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah and al-Fudayl, they said:
thaqalaynMatn: We said to him: “Is prayer in congregation an obligation?” He said: “The prayers are obligatory, but gathering (for them) is not made obligatory in all the prayers. Rather, it is a sunnah whoever abandons it out of aversion to it and to the congregation of the believers, without a valid excuse, then he has no prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 27

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Congregational Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, both from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah, he said:
Zurarah was sitting one day with Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, when a man came to him and entered upon Imam (a.s). He said to Imam (a.s): “May I be your ransom, I am a man who lives next to the mosque of my people. So when I do not pray with them, they speak ill of me and say such-and-such about me.” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “If what you say is true, then indeed the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘Whoever hears the call (to prayer) and does not respond to it without a valid excuse, then he has no prayer’.” So the man left, and Imam Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: “Do not abandon the prayer with them, and (pray) behind every imam (of prayer).” When the man left, I said to Imam (a.s): “May I be your ransom, your words to this man when he asked you a legal question weighed heavily upon me. What if they are not believers?” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, laughed and said: “It seems, O’ Zurarah, that you are still here (meaning, still thinking at a surface level). What reason do you seek greater than the fact that he is not to be followed in prayer?” Then Imam (a.s) said: “O’ Zurarah, what do you think I meant?” I said: “(That you meant) Pray in your mosques and pray with your imams.” (meaning the faithful should establish their own communities of prayer led by legitimate, believing prayer leaders from among them)
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: كُنْتُ جَالِساً عِنْدَ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ إِذْ جَاءَهُ رَجُلٌ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي رَجُلٌ جَارُ مَسْجِدٍ لِقَوْمِي فَإِذَا أَنَا لَمْ أُصَلِّ مَعَهُمْ وَقَعُوا فِيَّ وَ قَالُوا هُوَ كَذَا وَ كَذَا فَقَالَ «أَمَا لَئِنْ قُلْتَ ذَلِكَ لَقَدْ قَالَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« مَنْ سَمِعَ اَلنِّدَاءَ فَلَمْ يُجِبْهُ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ فَلاَ صَلاَةَ لَهُ»» فَخَرَجَ اَلرَّجُلُ فَقَالَ لَهُ« لاَ تَدَعِ اَلصَّلاَةَ مَعَهُمْ وَ خَلْفَ كُلِّ إِمَامٍ» فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ قُلْتُ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ كَبُرَ عَلَيَّ قَوْلُكَ لِهَذَا اَلرَّجُلِ حِينَ اِسْتَفْتَاكَ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ قَالَ فَضَحِكَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ« مَا أَرَاكَ بَعْدُ إِلاَّ هَاهُنَا يَا زُرَارَةُ فَأَيَّ عِلَّةٍ تُرِيدُ أَعْظَمَ مِنْ أَنَّهُ لاَ يُؤْتَمُّ بِهِ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« يَا زُرَارَةُ مَا تَرَانِي» قُلْتُ صَلُّوا فِي مَسَاجِدِكُمْ وَ صَلُّوا مَعَ أَئِمَّتِكُمْ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and from Muhammad ibn Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, both from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Zurarah was sitting one day with Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, when a man came to him and entered upon Imam (a.s). He said to Imam (a.s): “May I be your ransom, I am a man who lives next to the mosque of my people. So when I do not pray with them, they speak ill of me and say such-and-such about me.” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “If what you say is true, then indeed the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, said: ‘Whoever hears the call (to prayer) and does not respond to it without a valid excuse, then he has no prayer’.” So the man left, and Imam Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: “Do not abandon the prayer with them, and (pray) behind every imam (of prayer).” When the man left, I said to Imam (a.s): “May I be your ransom, your words to this man when he asked you a legal question weighed heavily upon me. What if they are not believers?” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, laughed and said: “It seems, O’ Zurarah, that you are still here (meaning, still thinking at a surface level). What reason do you seek greater than the fact that he is not to be followed in prayer?” Then Imam (a.s) said: “O’ Zurarah, what do you think I meant?” I said: “(That you meant) Pray in your mosques and pray with your imams.” (meaning the faithful should establish their own communities of prayer led by legitimate, believing prayer leaders from among them)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 27

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Congregational Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The prayer in congregation surpasses every individual prayer by twenty-four degrees making it twenty-five prayers.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ تَفْضُلُ عَلَى كُلِّ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَرْدِ بِأَرْبَعٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ دَرَجَةً تَكُونُ خَمْساً وَ عِشْرِينَ صَلاَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The prayer in congregation surpasses every individual prayer by twenty-four degrees making it twenty-five prayers.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 28

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Congregational Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
I heard Imam (a.s) say: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed the dawn prayer. Then, He (saws) turned his face to his companions and asked about some people, mentioning them by their names. Prophet (saws) said: ‘Did they attend the prayer?’ They (companions) said: ‘No, O’ Messenger of Allah (swt).’ Prophet (saws) said: ‘Are they absent?’ They said: ‘No.’ Prophet (saws) said: ‘Indeed, there is no prayer more burdensome upon the hypocrites than this (Fajr) prayer and the evening prayer. And if they knew what virtue is in them, they would come to them even if crawling.’”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« صَلَّى رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ اَلْفَجْرَ فَأَقْبَلَ بِوَجْهِهِ عَلَى أَصْحَابِهِ فَسَأَلَ عَنْ أُنَاسٍ يُسَمِّيهِمْ بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ فَقَالَ« هَلْ حَضَرُوا اَلصَّلاَةَ» فَقَالُوا لاَ يَارَسُولَ اَللَّهِ فَقَالَ« أَغُيَّبٌ هُمْ» فَقَالُوا لاَ فَقَالَ« أَمَا إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ صَلاَةٍ أَشَدَّ عَلَى اَلْمُنَافِقِينَ مِنْ هَذِهِ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءِ وَ لَوْ عَلِمُوا أَيُّ فَضْلٍ فِيهِمَا لَأَتَوْهُمَا وَ لَوْ حَبْواً»»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Imam (a.s) say: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed the dawn prayer. Then, He (saws) turned his face to his companions and asked about some people, mentioning them by their names. Prophet (saws) said: ‘Did they attend the prayer?’ They (companions) said: ‘No, O’ Messenger of Allah (swt).’ Prophet (saws) said: ‘Are they absent?’ They said: ‘No.’ Prophet (saws) said: ‘Indeed, there is no prayer more burdensome upon the hypocrites than this (Fajr) prayer and the evening prayer. And if they knew what virtue is in them, they would come to them even if crawling.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 28

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Congregational Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
I heard Imam (a.s) say: “Indeed, there were people during the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, who were slow in attending the prayer in the mosque. So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘A time will soon come when people will abandon the prayer in the mosque, and we may command that wood be gathered and placed at their doors, then a fire would be kindled upon them, and their houses would be burned over them.’”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« إِنَّ أُنَاساً كَانُوا عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ أَبْطَئُوا عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ« لَيُوشِكُ قَوْمٌ يَدَعُونَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ أَنْ نَأْمُرَ بِحَطَبٍ فَيُوضَعَ عَلَى أَبْوَابِهِمْ فَتُوقَدَ عَلَيْهِمْ نَارٌ فَتُحْرَقَ عَلَيْهِمْ بُيُوتُهُمْ»»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Imam (a.s) say: “Indeed, there were people during the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, who were slow in attending the prayer in the mosque. So the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘A time will soon come when people will abandon the prayer in the mosque, and we may command that wood be gathered and placed at their doors, then a fire would be kindled upon them, and their houses would be burned over them.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 28

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Congregational Prayer
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from al-Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Muhammad ibn Umarah, he said:
I sent to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about a man who performs the obligatory prayer alone in the Mosque of Kufah is that better, or is his prayer in congregation better? Imam (a.s) said: “Prayer in congregation is better.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُمَارَةَ قَالَ: أَرْسَلْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةَ وَحْدَهُ فِي مَسْجِدِ اَلْكُوفَةِ أَفْضَلُ أَوْ صَلاَتُهُ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ أَفْضَلُ فَقَالَ« اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ أَفْضَلُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from al-Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Muhammad ibn Umarah, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I sent to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about a man who performs the obligatory prayer alone in the Mosque of Kufah is that better, or is his prayer in congregation better? Imam (a.s) said: “Prayer in congregation is better.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 28

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, he said:
Imam (a.s) said: “Two men, one of them leads the other in prayer, and he stands to his right. But if they are more than that, they stand behind him.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلرَّجُلاَنِ يَؤُمُّ أَحَدُهُمَا صَاحِبَهُ يَقُومُ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ فَإِنْ كَانُوا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ قَامُوا خَلْفَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Safwan from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “Two men, one of them leads the other in prayer, and he stands to his right. But if they are more than that, they stand behind him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 29

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from al-Husayn ibn Yasar al-Mada’ini:
He (al-Mada’ini) heard someone ask Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed beside another man and stood to his left without knowing what to do then he realized (the mistake) while still in the prayer. Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “He should move him to his right.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَشْيَمَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ: أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ مَنْ يَسْأَلُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى إِلَى جَانِبِ رَجُلٍ فَقَامَ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ وَ هُوَ لاَ يَعْلَمُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ ثُمَّ عَلِمَ هُوَ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« يُحَوِّلُهُ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ashyam from al-Husayn ibn Yasar al-Mada’ini:
thaqalaynMatn: He (al-Mada’ini) heard someone ask Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who prayed beside another man and stood to his left without knowing what to do then he realized (the mistake) while still in the prayer. Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “He should move him to his right.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 29

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad from Abu Mas‘ud from al-Hasan al-Sayqal from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
I asked Imam (a.s): “What is the minimum for a congregation (al-jama‘ah)?” Imam (a.s) said: “A man and a woman.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ أَبِي مَسْعُودٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّيْقَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ كَمْ أَقَلُّ مَا تَكُونُ اَلْجَمَاعَةُ قَالَ« رَجُلٌ وَ اِمْرَأَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Hammad from Abu Mas‘ud from al-Hasan al-Sayqal from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s): “What is the minimum for a congregation (al-jama‘ah)?” Imam (a.s) said: “A man and a woman.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 29

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Five individuals are never to lead the people in prayer under any circumstance; the leper, the one with vitiligo, the insane, the child of fornication, and the Bedouin.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ جَمَاعَةٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« خَمْسَةٌ لاَ يَؤُمُّونَ اَلنَّاسَ عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ اَلْمَجْذُومُ وَ اَلْأَبْرَصُ وَ اَلْمَجْنُونُ وَ وَلَدُ اَلزِّنَا وَ اَلْأَعْرَابِيُّ»
thaqalaynSanad: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
