chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Indeed, I enter the mosque and find that the imam (of prayer) has already bowed in rukuh and the people have bowed as well, and I am not able to make the adhan, or the iqamah, or to say the takbir (to begin the prayer).” So Imam (a.s) said to me: “When that happens, then enter with them in the rak’ah and count it as part of your prayer, for it is one of the most virtuous of your rak’ahs.” Ishaq then narrated: “So when I heard the adhan of Maghrib while I was sitting at my doorstep, I said to the servant, ‘Look and see, has the prayer been established?’” So he (the servant) came back to me and said: “Yes.” So I got up quickly and entered the mosque and found the people had already bowed, so I bowed with the first row that I caught and I counted it as part of my prayer. Then, after the prayer was concluded, I prayed four rak’ahs. Then I departed, and behold, five or six of my neighbors from among the Makhzumis and the Umayyads approached me. They sat me down and then said: “O Aba Hashim, may Allah (swt) reward you well on behalf of yourself, for by Allah (swt), we have seen the opposite of what we had assumed about you and what was said regarding you.” I asked: “And what is that?” They said: “We followed you when you rose for the prayer, and we used to think that you did not follow the prayer with us. But now we found that you counted the prayer with us and prayed our prayer. May Allah (swt) be pleased with you and reward you with goodness.” I said to them: “Glory be to Allah (swt)! Is such a thing said about someone like me?” Then I realized that Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, had not commanded me except because he feared this and things like it for me.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُصَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي أَدْخُلُ اَلْمَسْجِدَ فَأَجِدُ اَلْإِمَامَ قَدْ رَكَعَ وَ قَدْ رَكَعَ اَلْقَوْمُ فَلاَ يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أُؤَذِّنَ وَ أُقِيمَ وَ أُكَبِّرَ فَقَالَ لِي« فَإِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ فَادْخُلْ مَعَهُمْ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ وَ اِعْتَدَّ بِهَا فَإِنَّهَا مِنْ أَفْضَلِ رَكَعَاتِكَ» قَالَ إِسْحَاقُ فَلَمَّا سَمِعْتُ أَذَانَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ أَنَا عَلَى بَابِي قَاعِدٌ قُلْتُ لِلْغُلاَمِ اُنْظُرْ أُقِيمَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَجَاءَنِي فَقَالَ نَعَمْ فَقُمْتُ مُبَادِراً فَدَخَلْتُ اَلْمَسْجِدَ فَوَجَدْتُ اَلنَّاسَ قَدْ رَكَعُوا فَرَكَعْتُ مَعَ أَوَّلِ صَفٍّ أَدْرَكْتُهُ وَ اِعْتَدَدْتُ بِهَا ثُمَّ صَلَّيْتُ بَعْدَ اَلاِنْصِرَافِ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ ثُمَّ اِنْصَرَفْتُ فَإِذَا خَمْسَةٌ أَوْ سِتَّةٌ مِنْ جِيرَانِي قَدْ قَامُوا إِلَيَّ مِنَ اَلْمَخْزُومِيِّينَ وَ اَلْأُمَوِيِّينَ فَأَقْعَدُونِي ثُمَّ قَالُوا يَا أَبَا هَاشِمٍ جَزَاكَ اَللَّهُ عَنْ نَفْسِكَ خَيْراً فَقَدْ وَ اَللَّهِ رَأَيْنَا خِلاَفَ مَا ظَنَنَّا بِكَ وَ مَا قِيلَ فِيكَ فَقُلْتُ وَ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ ذَلِكَ قَالُوا اِتَّبَعْنَاكَ حِينَ قُمْتَ إِلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ نَحْنُ نَرَى أَنَّكَ لاَ تَقْتَدِي بِالصَّلاَةِ مَعَنَا فَقَدْ وَجَدْنَاكَ قَدِ اِعْتَدَدْتَ بِالصَّلاَةِ مَعَنَا وَ صَلَّيْتَ بِصَلاَتِنَا فَرَضِيَ اَللَّهُ عَنْكَ وَ جَزَاكَ خَيْراً قَالَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُمْ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ أَ لِمِثْلِي يُقَالُ هَذَا قَالَ فَعَلِمْتُ أَنَّ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لَمْ يَأْمُرْنِي إِلاَّ وَ هُوَ يَخَافُ عَلَيَّ هَذَا وَ شِبْهَهُ
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “Indeed, I enter the mosque and find that the imam (of prayer) has already bowed in rukuh and the people have bowed as well, and I am not able to make the adhan, or the iqamah, or to say the takbir (to begin the prayer).” So Imam (a.s) said to me: “When that happens, then enter with them in the rak’ah and count it as part of your prayer, for it is one of the most virtuous of your rak’ahs.” Ishaq then narrated: “So when I heard the adhan of Maghrib while I was sitting at my doorstep, I said to the servant, ‘Look and see, has the prayer been established?’” So he (the servant) came back to me and said: “Yes.” So I got up quickly and entered the mosque and found the people had already bowed, so I bowed with the first row that I caught and I counted it as part of my prayer. Then, after the prayer was concluded, I prayed four rak’ahs. Then I departed, and behold, five or six of my neighbors from among the Makhzumis and the Umayyads approached me. They sat me down and then said: “O Aba Hashim, may Allah (swt) reward you well on behalf of yourself, for by Allah (swt), we have seen the opposite of what we had assumed about you and what was said regarding you.” I asked: “And what is that?” They said: “We followed you when you rose for the prayer, and we used to think that you did not follow the prayer with us. But now we found that you counted the prayer with us and prayed our prayer. May Allah (swt) be pleased with you and reward you with goodness.” I said to them: “Glory be to Allah (swt)! Is such a thing said about someone like me?” Then I realized that Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, had not commanded me except because he feared this and things like it for me.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Abi Shubah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “I am with the imam (of prayer), and I finish before he finishes his recitation.” Imam (a.s) said: “Then complete the Surah and glorify Allah (swt) and praise Him (azj) until he finishes.”
arabicText: رَوَى اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي شُعْبَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أَكُونُ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَأَفْرُغُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَفْرُغَ مِنْ قِرَاءَتِهِ قَالَ« فَأَتِمَّ اَلسُّورَةَ وَ مَجِّدِ اَللَّهَ وَ أَثْنِ عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Umar ibn Abi Shubah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “I am with the imam (of prayer), and I finish before he finishes his recitation.” Imam (a.s) said: “Then complete the Surah and glorify Allah (swt) and praise Him (azj) until he finishes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 42

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about being with the imam (of prayer) and finishing my recitation before he finishes. Imam (a.s) said: “Then withhold one verse, and glorify Allah (swt) and praise Him (azj). When he finishes, then recite the verse and bow.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْإِمَامِ أَكُونُ مَعَهُ فَأَفْرُغُ مِنَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَفْرُغَ قَالَ« فَأَمْسِكْ آيَةً وَ مَجِّدِ اَللَّهَ وَ أَثْنِ عَلَيْهِ فَإِذَا فَرَغَ فَاقْرَأِ اَلْآيَةَ وَ اِرْكَعْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about being with the imam (of prayer) and finishing my recitation before he finishes. Imam (a.s) said: “Then withhold one verse, and glorify Allah (swt) and praise Him (azj). When he finishes, then recite the verse and bow.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr; and al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, who said:
Hamzah ibn Humran asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who led us in prayer during travel while he was in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity), and he knew (of his condition) while we did not know. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem.” (meaning those who prayed behind him are not required to repeat it)
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ حَمْزَةُ بْنُ حُمْرَانَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَمَّنَا فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَ هُوَ جُنُبٌ وَ قَدْ عَلِمَ وَ نَحْنُ لاَ نَعْلَمُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr; and al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Hamzah ibn Humran asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who led us in prayer during travel while he was in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity), and he knew (of his condition) while we did not know. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem.” (meaning those who prayed behind him are not required to repeat it)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 43

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s) about a man who leads a group in prayer while he is without ritual purity, and he does not realize it until after his prayer is finished. Imam (a.s) said: “He must repeat (his prayer), but those behind him do not need to repeat theirs, even if he informs them that he was without ritual purity.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَؤُمُّ اَلْقَوْمَ وَ هُوَ عَلَى غَيْرِ طُهْرٍ فَلاَ يَعْلَمُ حَتَّى تَنْقَضِيَ صَلاَتُهُ فَقَالَ «يُعِيدُ وَ لاَ يُعِيدُ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ وَ إِنْ أَعْلَمَهُمْ أَنَّهُ عَلَى غَيْرِ طُهْرٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Ala’ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s) about a man who leads a group in prayer while he is without ritual purity, and he does not realize it until after his prayer is finished. Imam (a.s) said: “He must repeat (his prayer), but those behind him do not need to repeat theirs, even if he informs them that he was without ritual purity.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdillah ibn Muskan, from Abdillah ibn Abi Yafur, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who led a group in prayer while he was without ablution. Imam (a.s) said: “It is not obligatory on them to repeat prayer, but he himself repeats it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَمَّ قَوْماً وَ هُوَ عَلَى غَيْرِ وُضُوءٍ فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِعَادَةٌ وَ عَلَيْهِ هُوَ أَنْ يُعِيدَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abdillah ibn Muskan, from Abdillah ibn Abi Yafur, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who led a group in prayer while he was without ablution. Imam (a.s) said: “It is not obligatory on them to repeat prayer, but he himself repeats it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 43

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s) about a group whose imam (of prayer) led them in prayer while he was not in a state of purity does their prayer remain valid, or must they repeat it? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no repetition upon them; their prayer is complete. But he (prayer leader) must repeat it himself, and he is not required to inform them. This is established from him.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ صَلَّى بِهِمْ إِمَامُهُمْ وَهُوَ غَيْرُ طَاهِرٍ أَ تَجُوزُ صَلاَتُهُمْ أَمْ يُعِيدُونَهَا فَقَالَ« لاَ إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِمْ تَمَّتْ صَلاَتُهُمْ وَعَلَيْهِ هُوَ اَلْإِعَادَةُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعْلِمَهُمْ هَذَا عَنْهُ مَوْضُوعٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s) about a group whose imam (of prayer) led them in prayer while he was not in a state of purity does their prayer remain valid, or must they repeat it? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no repetition upon them; their prayer is complete. But he (prayer leader) must repeat it himself, and he is not required to inform them. This is established from him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 43

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Arzami, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, once led the people in prayer while not in a state of purity, and it was the Dhuhr prayer. Then Imam (a.s) entered (his house), and his (prayer) caller came out and announced: ‘Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, led the prayer without purity, so repeat (the prayer), and let those present inform those who are absent.’”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْعَرْزَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلَّى عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِالنَّاسِ عَلَى غَيْرِ طُهْرٍ وَ كَانَتِ اَلظُّهْرُ ثُمَّ دَخَلَ فَخَرَجَ مُنَادِيهِ أَنَّ أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ صَلَّى عَلَى غَيْرِ طُهْرٍ فَأَعِيدُوا وَ لْيُبَلِّغِ اَلشَّاهِدُ اَلْغَائِبَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Arzami, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, once led the people in prayer while not in a state of purity, and it was the Dhuhr prayer. Then Imam (a.s) entered (his house), and his (prayer) caller came out and announced: ‘Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, led the prayer without purity, so repeat (the prayer), and let those present inform those who are absent.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 43

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding a group who had departed from Khurasan or from some of the mountainous regions, and a man was leading them in prayer. When they reached Kufah, they came to know that he was a Jew. Imam (a.s) said: “They do not have to repeat (their prayers).”
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْمٍ خَرَجُوا مِنْ خُرَاسَانَ أَوْ بَعْضِ اَلْجِبَالِ وَ كَانَ يَؤُمُّهُمْ رَجُلٌ فَلَمَّا صَارُوا إِلَى اَلْكُوفَةِ عَلِمُوا أَنَّهُ يَهُودِيٌّ قَالَ« لاَ يُعِيدُونَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding a group who had departed from Khurasan or from some of the mountainous regions, and a man was leading them in prayer. When they reached Kufah, they came to know that he was a Jew. Imam (a.s) said: “They do not have to repeat (their prayers).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 44

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abdillah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said regarding a man who leads a group in prayer, then comes to know that he had led them facing other than the qiblah. Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon them to repeat.”
arabicText: رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي رَجُلٍ يُصَلِّي بِالْقَوْمِ ثُمَّ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى بِهِمْ إِلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِعَادَةُ شَيْءٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abdillah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said regarding a man who leads a group in prayer, then comes to know that he had led them facing other than the qiblah. Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon them to repeat.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 44

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man entered with a group in their prayer while he did not intend it as prayer, then their imam (of prayer) became invalidated (entered a state of hadath), so the imam (of prayer) took the hand of that man and placed him forward, and he led them in prayer. Does their prayer count when he was leading them without having intended it as prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “It is not appropriate for a man to enter with a group in their prayer while he does not intend it as prayer. Rather, he should intend it as prayer. So if he had already prayed, then for him it will count as another prayer, and if not, then he should not enter with them. As for the group, their prayer may be valid even if he had not intended it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ جَمِيعاً عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ دَخَلَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ فِي صَلاَتِهِمْ وَ هُوَ لاَ يَنْوِيهَا صَلاَةً فَأَحْدَثَ إِمَامُهُمْ فَأَخَذَ بِيَدِ ذَلِكَ اَلرَّجُلِ فَقَدَّمَهُ فَصَلَّى بِهِمْ أَيُجْزِيهِمْ صَلاَتُهُمْ بِصَلاَتِهِ وَ هُوَ لاَ يَنْوِيهَا صَلاَةً فَقَالَ« لاَ يَنْبَغِي لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ فِي صَلاَتِهِمْ وَ هُوَ لاَ يَنْوِيهَا صَلاَةً بَلْ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَنْوِيَهَا صَلاَةً فَإِنْ كَانَ قَدْ صَلَّى فَإِنَّ لَهُ صَلاَةً أُخْرَى وَ إِلاَّ فَلاَ يَدْخُلْ مَعَهُمْ قَدْ تُجْزِي عَنِ اَلْقَوْمِ صَلاَتُهُمْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَنْوِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, both from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “A man entered with a group in their prayer while he did not intend it as prayer, then their imam (of prayer) became invalidated (entered a state of hadath), so the imam (of prayer) took the hand of that man and placed him forward, and he led them in prayer. Does their prayer count when he was leading them without having intended it as prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “It is not appropriate for a man to enter with a group in their prayer while he does not intend it as prayer. Rather, he should intend it as prayer. So if he had already prayed, then for him it will count as another prayer, and if not, then he should not enter with them. As for the group, their prayer may be valid even if he had not intended it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 45

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who comes to the mosque while they are already in prayer, and the imam (of prayer) has preceded him by a rak’ah or more. Then the imam (of prayer) becomes unable to continue, so he takes the hand of that man who is the nearest of the people to him and places him forward. Imam (a.s) said: “He should complete the prayer with the people, then sit. And when they finish the tashahhud, he should gesture with his hand to them to the right and to the left and that gesture with his hand to them is (considered) the taslim and conclusion of their prayer. Then he should complete what had passed or remained upon him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَأْتِي اَلْمَسْجِدَ وَهُمْ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَقَدْ سَبَقَهُ اَلْإِمَامُ بِرَكْعَةٍ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ فَيَعْتَلُّ اَلْإِمَامُ فَيَأْخُذُ بِيَدِهِ وَ يَكُونُ أَدْنَى اَلْقَوْمِ إِلَيْهِ فَيُقَدِّمُهُ فَقَالَ« يُتِمُّ اَلصَّلاَةَ بِالْقَوْمِ ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ حَتَّى إِذَا فَرَغُوا مِنَ اَلتَّشَهُّدِ أَوْمَى بِيَدِهِ إِلَيْهِمْ عَنِ اَلْيَمِينِ وَ عَنِ اَلشِّمَالِ وَ كَانَ اَلَّذِي أَوْمَى بِيَدِهِ إِلَيْهِمُ اَلتَّسْلِيمَ وَ اِنْقِضَاءَ صَلاَتِهِمْ وَ أَتَمَّ هُوَ مَا كَانَ فَاتَهُ أَوْ بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who comes to the mosque while they are already in prayer, and the imam (of prayer) has preceded him by a rak’ah or more. Then the imam (of prayer) becomes unable to continue, so he takes the hand of that man who is the nearest of the people to him and places him forward. Imam (a.s) said: “He should complete the prayer with the people, then sit. And when they finish the tashahhud, he should gesture with his hand to them to the right and to the left and that gesture with his hand to them is (considered) the taslim and conclusion of their prayer. Then he should complete what had passed or remained upon him.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya by al-Abbas ibn Maruf by Ibn Sinan by Talhah ibn Zayd by Imam Ja’far (a.s):
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who led a group in prayer and then experienced a nosebleed after having prayed one or two rak’ahs, and he appointed a man from among them who had missed one or two rak’ahs. Imam (a.s) said: “He completes the prayer with them, then appoints another man to give the taslim with them, and he (the original deputy) stands up and completes the remainder of his prayer.”
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ طَلْحَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَمَّ قَوْماً فَأَصَابَهُ رُعَافٌ بَعْدَ مَا صَلَّى رَكْعَةً أَوْ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقَدَّمَ رَجُلاً مِمَّنْ قَدْ فَاتَهُ رَكْعَةٌ أَوْ رَكْعَتَانِ قَالَ« يُتِمُّ بِهِمُ اَلصَّلاَةَ ثُمَّ يُقَدِّمُ رَجُلاً فَيُسَلِّمُ بِهِمْ وَ يَقُومُ هُوَ فَيُتِمُّ بَقِيَّةَ صَلاَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya by al-Abbas ibn Maruf by Ibn Sinan by Talhah ibn Zayd by Imam Ja’far (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who led a group in prayer and then experienced a nosebleed after having prayed one or two rak’ahs, and he appointed a man from among them who had missed one or two rak’ahs. Imam (a.s) said: “He completes the prayer with them, then appoints another man to give the taslim with them, and he (the original deputy) stands up and completes the remainder of his prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 46

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Muawiyah ibn Shurayh, who said:
I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “If the imam (of prayer) becomes invalidated (enters a state of hadath) during the prayer, then no one should step forward except one who was present at the iqamah. So when the mu’adhdhin says, 'Qad qamatis-salah' (the prayer has been established), it is proper for those in the mosque to rise to their feet and appoint one among them, and not to wait for the imam (of prayer).” He (Ibn Shurayh) said: “I asked, ‘Even if the imam (of prayer) is the one who gave the adhan?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Even if he is, they should not wait for him and should appoint one among them.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنِ اَلْحَكَمِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ شُرَيْحٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا أَحْدَثَ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ لَمْ يَنْبَغِ أَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ إِلاَّ مَنْ شَهِدَ اَلْإِقَامَةَ فَإِذَا قَالَ اَلْمُؤَذِّنُ قَدْ قَامَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ يَنْبَغِي لِمَنْ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ أَنْ يَقُومُوا عَلَى أَرْجُلِهِمْ وَ يُقَدِّمُوا بَعْضَهُمْ وَلاَ يَنْتَظِرُوا اَلْإِمَامَ» قَالَ قُلْتُ وَإِنْ كَانَ اَلْإِمَامُ هُوَ اَلْمُؤَذِّنَ قَالَ« وَإِنْ كَانَ فَلاَ يَنْتَظِرُونَهُ وَيُقَدِّمُوا بَعْضَهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Muawiyah ibn Shurayh, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “If the imam (of prayer) becomes invalidated (enters a state of hadath) during the prayer, then no one should step forward except one who was present at the iqamah. So when the mu’adhdhin says, 'Qad qamatis-salah' (the prayer has been established), it is proper for those in the mosque to rise to their feet and appoint one among them, and not to wait for the imam (of prayer).” He (Ibn Shurayh) said: “I asked, ‘Even if the imam (of prayer) is the one who gave the adhan?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Even if he is, they should not wait for him and should appoint one among them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 46

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from al-Nadr, from Hisham, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who is leading the people in prayer, then becomes invalidated (enters a state of hadath), and he appoints a man who had missed a rak’ah what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: “He should not appoint a man who had missed a rak’ah, but rather he should take the hand of someone else and appoint him.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ هِشَامٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَؤُمُّ اَلْقَوْمَ فَيُحْدِثُ وَ يُقَدِّمُ رَجُلاً قَدْ سُبِقَ بِرَكْعَةٍ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ فَقَالَ« لاَ يُقَدِّمُ رَجُلاً قَدْ سُبِقَ بِرَكْعَةٍ وَ لَكِنْ يَأْخُذُ بِيَدِ غَيْرِهِ فَيُقَدِّمُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from al-Nadr, from Hisham, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who is leading the people in prayer, then becomes invalidated (enters a state of hadath), and he appoints a man who had missed a rak’ah what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: “He should not appoint a man who had missed a rak’ah, but rather he should take the hand of someone else and appoint him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 46

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said regarding a man who led a group in prayer and prayed one rak’ah with them, then died. Imam (a.s) said: “They should appoint another man, count the rak’ah (that was prayed), lay the deceased behind them, and whoever touched him must perform ghusl (ritual washing).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ أَمَّ قَوْماً فَصَلَّى بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ مَاتَ قَالَ« يُقَدِّمُونَ رَجُلاً آخَرَ وَ يَعْتَدُّونَ بِالرَّكْعَةِ وَ يَطْرَحُونَ اَلْمَيِّتَ خَلْفَهُمْ وَ يَغْتَسِلُ مَنْ مَسَّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said regarding a man who led a group in prayer and prayed one rak’ah with them, then died. Imam (a.s) said: “They should appoint another man, count the rak’ah (that was prayed), lay the deceased behind them, and whoever touched him must perform ghusl (ritual washing).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 47

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said to me: “If you do not catch the people before the imam (of prayer) says the takbir for the rukuh, then do not join them in that rak’ah.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ لِي:« إِنْ لَمْ تُدْرِكِ اَلْقَوْمَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُكَبِّرَ اَلْإِمَامُ لِلرَّكْعَةِ فَلاَ تَدْخُلْ مَعَهُمْ فِي تِلْكَ اَلرَّكْعَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said to me: “If you do not catch the people before the imam (of prayer) says the takbir for the rukuh, then do not join them in that rak’ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 47

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Safwan, from al-Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Do not count the rak’ah in which you did not witness the takbir with the imam (of prayer)” (meaning do not count it as a completed rak’ah)
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ تَعْتَدَّ بِالرَّكْعَةِ اَلَّتِي لَمْ تَشْهَدْ تَكْبِيرَهَا مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Safwan, from al-Ala’, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Do not count the rak’ah in which you did not witness the takbir with the imam (of prayer)” (meaning do not count it as a completed rak’ah)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 47

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr, from Asim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “If you catch the takbir before the imam (of prayer) bows into rukuh, then you have caught the prayer.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ عَاصِمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَدْرَكْتَ اَلتَّكْبِيرَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ اَلْإِمَامُ فَقَدْ أَدْرَكْتَ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Asim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “If you catch the takbir before the imam (of prayer) bows into rukuh, then you have caught the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 47

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And as for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said regarding a man who catches the imam (of prayer) while he is in rukuh, and the man says the takbir while standing upright, then bows before the imam (of prayer) raises his head indeed, he has caught the rak’ah.”
arabicText: وَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« فِي اَلرَّجُلِ إِذَا أَدْرَكَ اَلْإِمَامَ وَ هُوَ رَاكِعٌ فَكَبَّرَ اَلرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ مُقِيمٌ صُلْبَهُ ثُمَّ رَكَعَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ اَلْإِمَامُ رَأْسَهُ فَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ اَلرَّكْعَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And as for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said regarding a man who catches the imam (of prayer) while he is in rukuh, and the man says the takbir while standing upright, then bows before the imam (of prayer) raises his head indeed, he has caught the rak’ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 47

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you reach the imam (of prayer) and he has already bowed, and you say the takbir and bow before the imam (of prayer) raises his head, then you have caught the rak’ah. But if the imam (of prayer) raises his head before you bow, then you have missed the rak’ah.”
arabicText: وَ مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَدْرَكْتَ اَلْإِمَامَ وَ قَدْ رَكَعَ فَكَبَّرْتَ وَ رَكَعْتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ رَأْسَهُ فَقَدْ أَدْرَكْتَ اَلرَّكْعَةَ وَ إِنْ رَفَعَ اَلْإِمَامُ رَأْسَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَرْكَعَ فَقَدْ فَاتَتْكَ اَلرَّكْعَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you reach the imam (of prayer) and he has already bowed, and you say the takbir and bow before the imam (of prayer) raises his head, then you have caught the rak’ah. But if the imam (of prayer) raises his head before you bow, then you have missed the rak’ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 48

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
Imam (a.s) was asked about a man who enters the mosque and fears that he will miss the rak’ah. Imam (a.s) said: “He should bow before reaching the group and walk while in the state of rukuh until he joins them.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَدْخُلُ اَلْمَسْجِدَ فَيَخَافُ أَنْ تَفُوتَهُ اَلرَّكْعَةُ فَقَالَ« يَرْكَعُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَبْلُغَ اَلْقَوْمَ وَ يَمْشِي وَ هُوَ رَاكِعٌ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about a man who enters the mosque and fears that he will miss the rak’ah. Imam (a.s) said: “He should bow before reaching the group and walk while in the state of rukuh until he joins them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 49

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you enter the mosque and the imam (of prayer) is in rukuh, and you think that if you walk to him, he will raise his head before you catch him, then say the takbir and bow. If he raises his head (before you reach him), then prostrate where you are. When he stands, join the row; and if he sits, then sit where you are. When he stands again, join the row.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا دَخَلْتَ اَلْمَسْجِدَ وَ اَلْإِمَامُ رَاكِعٌ فَظَنَنْتَ أَنَّكَ إِنْ مَشَيْتَ إِلَيْهِ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُدْرِكَهُ فَكَبِّرْ وَ اِرْكَعْ فَإِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ فَاسْجُدْ مَكَانَكَ فَإِذَا قَامَ فَالْحَقْ بِالصَّفِّ وَ إِذَا جَلَسَ فَاجْلِسْ مَكَانَكَ فَإِذَا قَامَ فَالْحَقْ بِالصَّفِّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you enter the mosque and the imam (of prayer) is in rukuh, and you think that if you walk to him, he will raise his head before you catch him, then say the takbir and bow. If he raises his head (before you reach him), then prostrate where you are. When he stands, join the row; and if he sits, then sit where you are. When he stands again, join the row.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And in the narration of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, he said:
I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say and he mentioned the same (as above).
arabicText: وَفِي رِوَايَةِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: وَ ذَكَرَ مِثْلَهُ.
thaqalaynSanad: And in the narration of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas ibn Maruf, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, he said:

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ubaydullah ibn Muawiyah ibn Shurayh, from his father, who said:
I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “If a man comes quickly and the imam (of prayer) is in rukuh, then one takbir suffices for him both to enter the prayer and to join in the ruku.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ شُرَيْحٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا جَاءَ اَلرَّجُلُ مُبَادِراً وَ اَلْإِمَامُ رَاكِعٌ أَجْزَأَتْهُ تَكْبِيرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ لِدُخُولِهِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ اَلرُّكُوعِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from Ubaydullah ibn Muawiyah ibn Shurayh, from his father, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “If a man comes quickly and the imam (of prayer) is in rukuh, then one takbir suffices for him both to enter the prayer and to join in the ruku.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “If a man catches part of the prayer and misses part of it behind an imam (of prayer), and he counts the prayer behind him as valid, then he should consider the first part that he catches as the beginning of his own prayer. If he catches two rak’ahs from Dhuhr, or Asr, or Isha, and misses two rak’ahs, then in each rak’ah that he catches behind the imam (of prayer), he should recite Surah al-Fatihah and another surah to himself. But if he is not able to complete the surah, then Surah al-Fatihah suffices him. So when the imam (of prayer) finishes with the taslim, he (the follower) stands and prays two rak’ahs in which he does not recite, because recitation in the prayer is only in the first two rak’ahs of any prayer with Surah al-Fatihah and a surah. And in the last two rak’ahs, there is no recitation; rather, it is glorification (tasbih), exaltation (takbir), declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and supplication. There is no recitation in them. And if he caught one rak’ah, then he should recite in it, behind the imam (of prayer). Then when the imam (of prayer) performs the taslim, he stands and recites Surah al-Fatihah and a surah, then sits and recites the tashahhud. Then he stands and prays two rak’ahs in which there is no recitation.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَدْرَكَ اَلرَّجُلُ بَعْضَ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ فَاتَهُ بَعْضٌ خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ يَحْتَسِبُ بِالصَّلاَةِ خَلْفَهُ جَعَلَ أَوَّلَ مَا أَدْرَكَ أَوَّلَ صَلاَتِهِ إِنْ أَدْرَكَ مِنَ اَلظُّهْرِ أَوْ مِنَ اَلْعَصْرِ أَوْ مِنَ اَلْعِشَاءِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ فَاتَتْهُ رَكْعَتَانِ قَرَأَ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ مِمَّا أَدْرَكَ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فِي نَفْسِهِ بِأُمِّ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ سُورَةٍ فَإِنْ لَمْ يُدْرِكِ اَلسُّورَةَ تَامَّةً أَجْزَأَتْهُ أُمُّ اَلْكِتَابِ فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ اَلْإِمَامُ قَامَ فَصَلَّى فِيهَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ لاَ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا لِأَنَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ إِنَّمَا يُقْرَأُ فِيهَا فِي اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ مِنْ كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ بِأُمِّ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ سُورَةٍ وَ فِي اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ لاَ يُقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا إِنَّمَا هُوَ تَسْبِيحٌ وَ تَكْبِيرٌ وَ تَهْلِيلٌ وَ دُعَاءٌ لَيْسَ فِيهِمَا قِرَاءَةٌ وَ إِنْ أَدْرَكَ رَكْعَةً قَرَأَ فِيهَا خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ اَلْإِمَامُ قَامَ فَقَرَأَ بِأُمِّ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ سُورَةٍ ثُمَّ قَعَدَ فَتَشَهَّدَ ثُمَّ قَامَ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ لَيْسَ فِيهِمَا قِرَاءَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “If a man catches part of the prayer and misses part of it behind an imam (of prayer), and he counts the prayer behind him as valid, then he should consider the first part that he catches as the beginning of his own prayer. If he catches two rak’ahs from Dhuhr, or Asr, or Isha, and misses two rak’ahs, then in each rak’ah that he catches behind the imam (of prayer), he should recite Surah al-Fatihah and another surah to himself. But if he is not able to complete the surah, then Surah al-Fatihah suffices him. So when the imam (of prayer) finishes with the taslim, he (the follower) stands and prays two rak’ahs in which he does not recite, because recitation in the prayer is only in the first two rak’ahs of any prayer with Surah al-Fatihah and a surah. And in the last two rak’ahs, there is no recitation; rather, it is glorification (tasbih), exaltation (takbir), declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and supplication. There is no recitation in them. And if he caught one rak’ah, then he should recite in it, behind the imam (of prayer). Then when the imam (of prayer) performs the taslim, he stands and recites Surah al-Fatihah and a surah, then sits and recites the tashahhud. Then he stands and prays two rak’ahs in which there is no recitation.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who catches the second rak’ah of the prayer with the imam (of prayer), and it is his (the follower's) first rak’ah what should he do when the imam (of prayer) sits? Imam (a.s) said: “He should keep himself raised and not fully settle into the sitting posture. Then, when it is the third rak’ah for the imam (of prayer) and the second for him, he should delay a little after the imam (of prayer) rises enough to recite the tashahhud and then catch up with the imam (of prayer).” He (ibn al-Hajjaj) said: “I also asked Imam (a.s) about a man who catches the last two rak’ahs of the prayer what should he do regarding the recitation?” Imam (a.s) said: “Recite in them, for they are your first two rak’ahs. Do not make the beginning of your prayer its end.”

thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who catches the second rak’ah of the prayer with the imam (of prayer), and it is his (the follower's) first rak’ah what should he do when the imam (of prayer) sits? Imam (a.s) said: “He should keep himself raised and not fully settle into the sitting posture. Then, when it is the third rak’ah for the imam (of prayer) and the second for him, he should delay a little after the imam (of prayer) rises enough to recite the tashahhud and then catch up with the imam (of prayer).” He (ibn al-Hajjaj) said: “I also asked Imam (a.s) about a man who catches the last two rak’ahs of the prayer what should he do regarding the recitation?” Imam (a.s) said: “Recite in them, for they are your first two rak’ahs. Do not make the beginning of your prayer its end.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from a man, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said to me: “What do these people say about a man who has missed two rak’ahs with the imam (of prayer)?” I said: “They say he should recite ‘al-Hamd’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and a surah in the two rak’ahs.” Imam (a.s) said: “This one reverses his prayer he makes its beginning into its end.” So I asked: “Then what should he do?” Imam (a.s) said: “He should recite Surah al-Fatihah in each rak’ah.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مَرْوَكِ بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي« أَيَّ شَيْءٍ يَقُولُ هَؤُلاَءِ فِي اَلرَّجُلِ إِذَا فَاتَتْهُ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ رَكْعَتَانِ» قَالَ يَقُولُونَ يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ بِالْحَمْدِ وَ سُورَةٍ فَقَالَ« هَذَا يَقْلِبُ صَلاَتَهُ فَيَجْعَلُ أَوَّلَهَا آخِرَهَا» فَقُلْتُ فَكَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« يَقْرَأُ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah narrated from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from a man, from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said to me: “What do these people say about a man who has missed two rak’ahs with the imam (of prayer)?” I said: “They say he should recite ‘al-Hamd’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and a surah in the two rak’ahs.” Imam (a.s) said: “This one reverses his prayer he makes its beginning into its end.” So I asked: “Then what should he do?” Imam (a.s) said: “He should recite Surah al-Fatihah in each rak’ah.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from Abu Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam Ali (a.s) said: “A man counts what he has caught with the imam (of prayer) as the beginning of his prayer.” Imam Ja’far (al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: “And we do not say as the fools say.” (meaning the opponents)
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ طَلْحَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَجْعَلُ اَلرَّجُلُ مَا أَدْرَكَ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ أَوَّلَ صَلاَتِهِ» قَالَ جَعْفَرٌ« وَ لَيْسَ نَقُولُ كَمَا يَقُولُ اَلْحَمْقَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from Abu Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) said: “A man counts what he has caught with the imam (of prayer) as the beginning of his prayer.” Imam Ja’far (al-Sadiq (a.s)) said: “And we do not say as the fools say.” (meaning the opponents)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 52

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiyah ibn Wahb, he said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who catches the end of the prayer of the imam (of prayer), while it is the beginning of the man's own prayer, and the imam (of prayer) does not give him enough time to recite (the opening, al-Fatiha), so he completes the recitation at the end of his prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُدْرِكُ آخِرَ صَلاَةِ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ هِيَ أَوَّلُ صَلاَةِ اَلرَّجُلِ فَلاَ يُمْهِلُهُ حَتَّى يَقْرَأَ فَيَقْضِي اَلْقِرَاءَةَ فِي آخِرِ صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiyah ibn Wahb, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who catches the end of the prayer of the imam (of prayer), while it is the beginning of the man's own prayer, and the imam (of prayer) does not give him enough time to recite (the opening, al-Fatiha), so he completes the recitation at the end of his prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 52

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Ashari from his father from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s) about someone who performed rukuh with an imam (of prayer) whom he follows, then raised his head before the imam. Imam (a.s) said: “He should repeat his rukuh along with him.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَهْلٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَمَّنْ رَكَعَ مَعَ إِمَامٍ يَقْتَدِي بِهِ ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ قَبْلَ اَلْإِمَامِ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ رُكُوعَهُ مَعَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Ashari from his father from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s) about someone who performed rukuh with an imam (of prayer) whom he follows, then raised his head before the imam. Imam (a.s) said: “He should repeat his rukuh along with him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 52

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And as for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, he said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who raises his head from rukuh before the imam (of prayer); should he return and perform rukuh again if the imam (of prayer) delays, so that he may raise his head along with him? Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ غِيَاثِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَرْفَعُ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ قَبْلَ اَلْإِمَامِ أَ يَعُودُ فَيَرْكَعُ إِذَا أَبْطَأَ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ يَرْفَعُ رَأْسَهُ مَعَهُ قَالَ لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And as for what was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who raises his head from rukuh before the imam (of prayer); should he return and perform rukuh again if the imam (of prayer) delays, so that he may raise his head along with him? Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 53

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This was narrated by Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hammad ibn Uthman and Khalaf ibn Hammad from Ribi from Abdullah ibn al-Jarud and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
We asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who prayed with an imam (of prayer) whom he follows, and he raised his head from sujud before the imam (of prayer) raised his head from sujud. Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him prostrate (again). And whoever catches the imam (of prayer) after he has raised his head from rukuh, let him prostrate with him, but he should not count that sujud (as part of his own prayer).”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ وَ خَلَفِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ رِبْعِيٍّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْجَارُودِ وَ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالاَ: سَأَلْنَاهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى مَعَ إِمَامٍ يَأْتَمُّ بِهِ فَرَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ اَلْإِمَامُ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ قَالَ« فَلْيَسْجُدْ وَ مَنْ أَدْرَكَ اَلْإِمَامَ وَ قَدْ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ فَلْيَسْجُدْ مَعَهُ وَ لاَ يَعْتَدَّ بِذَلِكَ اَلسُّجُودِ»
thaqalaynSanad: This was narrated by Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hammad ibn Uthman and Khalaf ibn Hammad from Ribi from Abdullah ibn al-Jarud and al-Fudayl ibn Yasar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: We asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who prayed with an imam (of prayer) whom he follows, and he raised his head from sujud before the imam (of prayer) raised his head from sujud. Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him prostrate (again). And whoever catches the imam (of prayer) after he has raised his head from rukuh, let him prostrate with him, but he should not count that sujud (as part of his own prayer).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 53

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Abbas ibn Maruf from Safwan from Abu Uthman from Mualla ibn Khunays from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If the imam (of prayer) precedes you by a rak’ah, and you catch up with him after he has raised his head (from rukuh), then prostrate with him, but do not count that (rak’ah).”
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ خُنَيْسٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا سَبَقَكَ اَلْإِمَامُ بِرَكْعَةٍ فَأَدْرَكْتَهُ وَ قَدْ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ فَاسْجُدْ مَعَهُ وَ لاَ تَعْتَدَّ بِهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Abbas ibn Maruf from Safwan from Abu Uthman from Mualla ibn Khunays from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If the imam (of prayer) precedes you by a rak’ah, and you catch up with him after he has raised his head (from rukuh), then prostrate with him, but do not count that (rak’ah).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 54

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Marwak ibn Ubayd from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz from Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir al-Jufi who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “I lead a group in prayer, and I go into rukuh, and people enter while I am in rukuh how long should I wait?” Imam (a.s) said: “How amazing is your question, O’ Jabir! Wait for the duration of two of your rukus. If they (stop entering), then raise your head; otherwise, continue.”
arabicText: رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مَرْوَكِ بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلنَّضْرِ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ اَلْجُعْفِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي أَؤُمُّ قَوْماً فَأَرْكَعُ فَيَدْخُلُ اَلنَّاسُ وَ أَنَا رَاكِعٌ فَكَمْ أَنْتَظِرُ قَالَ« مَا أَعْجَبَ مَا تَسْأَلُ عَنْهُ يَا جَابِرُ اِنْتَظِرْ مِثْلَيْ رُكُوعِكَ فَإِنِ اِنْقَطَعُوا وَ إِلاَّ فَارْفَعْ رَأْسَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Marwak ibn Ubayd from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz from Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir al-Jufi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “I lead a group in prayer, and I go into rukuh, and people enter while I am in rukuh how long should I wait?” Imam (a.s) said: “How amazing is your question, O’ Jabir! Wait for the duration of two of your rukus. If they (stop entering), then raise your head; otherwise, continue.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 54

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “I lead a group in prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: “Say the taslim once, and do not turn your head. Say: ‘Peace be upon you, O’ Prophet, and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His (azj) blessings. Peace be upon you all.’”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنِّي أُصَلِّي بِقَوْمٍ فَقَالَ« سَلِّمْ وَاحِدَةً وَ لاَ تَلْتَفِتْ قُلِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا اَلنَّبِيُّ وَ رَحْمَةُ اَللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “I lead a group in prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: “Say the taslim once, and do not turn your head. Say: ‘Peace be upon you, O’ Prophet, and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His (azj) blessings. Peace be upon you all.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 54

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
I heard Imam (a.s) say: “It is not proper for the imam (of prayer) to stand up (and leave) after the prayer until everyone behind him has completed what they missed of the prayer.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْخَالِقِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« لاَ يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَقُومَ إِذَا صَلَّى حَتَّى يَقْضِيَ كُلُّ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ مَا فَاتَهُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Imam (a.s) say: “It is not proper for the imam (of prayer) to stand up (and leave) after the prayer until everyone behind him has completed what they missed of the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 54

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hajjal from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “It is proper for the imam (of prayer) to make audible to those behind him everything he says, and it is not proper for those behind him to make anything they say audible to him.”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ كُلَّ مَا يَقُولُ وَ لاَ يَنْبَغِي لِمَنْ خَلْفَهُ أَنْ يُسْمِعَهُ شَيْئاً مِمَّا يَقُولُ»
thaqalaynSanad: This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hajjal from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “It is proper for the imam (of prayer) to make audible to those behind him everything he says, and it is not proper for those behind him to make anything they say audible to him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 54

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sulaym al-Farra, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who is the mu’adhdhin for a group and their imam (of prayer) is (away) on the road to Mecca or elsewhere, so he leads them in Asr prayer at its proper time. Then a man enters who does not know (the situation) and assumes that it is Dhuhr, does it suffice him that it was actually Asr? Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سُلَيْمٍ اَلْفَرَّاءِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ مُؤَذِّنَ قَوْمٍ وَ إِمَامَهُمْ يَكُونُ فِي طَرِيقِ مَكَّةَ وَ غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمُ اَلْعَصْرَ فِي وَقْتِهَا فَيَدْخُلُ اَلرَّجُلُ اَلَّذِي لاَ يَعْرِفُ فَيَرَى أَنَّهَا اَلْأُولَى أَ فَتُجْزِيهِ أَنَّهَا اَلْعَصْرُ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sulaym al-Farra, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who is the mu’adhdhin for a group and their imam (of prayer) is (away) on the road to Mecca or elsewhere, so he leads them in Asr prayer at its proper time. Then a man enters who does not know (the situation) and assumes that it is Dhuhr, does it suffice him that it was actually Asr? Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Uthman, he said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a group in prayer, and he is praying Asr, while for them it is Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: “It is valid for him, and it is valid for them.”
arabicText: وَ أَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَؤُمُّ بِقَوْمٍ فَيُصَلِّي اَلْعَصْرَ وَ هِيَ لَهُمُ اَلظُّهْرُ قَالَ« أَجْزَأَتْ عَنْهُ وَ أَجْزَأَتْ عَنْهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Said from Hammad ibn Uthman, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a group in prayer, and he is praying Asr, while for them it is Dhuhr. Imam (a.s) said: “It is valid for him, and it is valid for them.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Ali ibn Ja’far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, about an imam (of prayer) who was in the Dhuhr prayer, and his wife stood facing him to pray with him, thinking that it was Asr. Does that invalidate the prayer of the congregation? And what is the ruling of the woman in her prayer with them, given that she had already performed Dhuhr? Imam (a.s) said: “That does not invalidate the prayer of the congregation, but the woman must repeat her prayer.”
arabicText: وَ سَأَلَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ أَخَاهُ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ:
thaqalaynMatn: Ali ibn Ja’far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, about an imam (of prayer) who was in the Dhuhr prayer, and his wife stood facing him to pray with him, thinking that it was Asr. Does that invalidate the prayer of the congregation? And what is the ruling of the woman in her prayer with them, given that she had already performed Dhuhr? Imam (a.s) said: “That does not invalidate the prayer of the congregation, but the woman must repeat her prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Buzay, who said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “I attend the mosques with my neighbors and others, and they ask me to lead them in prayer, while I have already prayed before coming to them. Sometimes those who follow my prayer include those who imitate my actions in prayer, the weak, and the ignorant, and I dislike to step forward (as imam of prayer) having already prayed, due to the state of those who follow me in prayer from among those I have mentioned to you. So command me in this matter with your instruction, that I may follow it and act upon it, if Allah (swt) wills.” So Imam (a.s) wrote back: “Pray with them.”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنِّي أَحْضُرُ اَلْمَسَاجِدَ مَعَ جِيرَتِي وَ غَيْرِهِمْ فَيَأْمُرُونِّي بِالصَّلاَةِ بِهِمْ وَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتُ قَبْلَ أَنْ آتِيَهُمْ فَرُبَّمَا صَلَّى خَلْفِي مَنْ يَقْتَدِي بِصَلاَتِي وَاَلْمُسْتَضْعَفُ وَاَلْجَاهِلُ وَ أَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَتَقَدَّمَ وَقَدْ صَلَّيْتُ لِحَالِ مَنْ يُصَلِّي بِصَلاَتِي مِمَّنْ سَمَّيْتُ لَكَ فَأْمُرْنِي فِي ذَلِكَ بِأَمْرِكَ أَنْتَهِي إِلَيْهِ وَ أَعْمَلُ بِهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ فَكَتَبَ« صَلِّ بِهِمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Buzay, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, saying: “I attend the mosques with my neighbors and others, and they ask me to lead them in prayer, while I have already prayed before coming to them. Sometimes those who follow my prayer include those who imitate my actions in prayer, the weak, and the ignorant, and I dislike to step forward (as imam of prayer) having already prayed, due to the state of those who follow me in prayer from among those I have mentioned to you. So command me in this matter with your instruction, that I may follow it and act upon it, if Allah (swt) wills.” So Imam (a.s) wrote back: “Pray with them.”
