chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who performs the obligatory prayer, then finds a group of people praying in congregation is it permissible for him to repeat the prayer with them? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and it is better.” I said: “And if he does not do it?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي اَلْفَرِيضَةَ ثُمَّ يَجِدُ قَوْماً يُصَلُّونَ جَمَاعَةً أَ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يُعِيدَ اَلصَّلاَةَ مَعَهُمْ قَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ هُوَ أَفْضَلُ» قُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ قَالَ« لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who performs the obligatory prayer, then finds a group of people praying in congregation is it permissible for him to repeat the prayer with them? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and it is better.” I said: “And if he does not do it?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 56

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhturi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said regarding a man who performs the prayer alone, then finds a group (praying in congregation). Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray with them and count it as the obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ جَمِيعاً عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي اَلصَّلاَةَ وَحْدَهُ ثُمَّ يَجِدُ جَمَاعَةً قَالَ« يُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ وَ يَجْعَلُهَا اَلْفَرِيضَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhturi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said regarding a man who performs the prayer alone, then finds a group (praying in congregation). Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray with them and count it as the obligatory prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 56

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama’ah, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who had begun to pray, and the imam (of prayer) came out while the man had already prayed one rak’ah of the obligatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “If the imam (of prayer) is just, then let him complete another rak’ah and end the prayer, and count it as a supererogatory (nafl) prayer, and then enter into prayer with the imam (of prayer). But if the imam (of prayer) is not just, then let him continue his own prayer as it is, and perform another rak’ah with the imam (of prayer), and remain seated for the duration it takes to say: ‘I bear witness that there is no God but Allah (swt), alone with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His (azj) servant and His (azj) messenger’. Then let him complete his prayer with the imam (of prayer) to the best of his ability. Indeed, taqiyyah is expansive, and there is no act of taqiyyah except that the one who performs it is rewarded for it, if Allah (swt) wills.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ كَانَ يُصَلِّي فَخَرَجَ اَلْإِمَامُ وَقَدْ صَلَّى اَلرَّجُلُ رَكْعَةً مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ إِمَاماً عَدْلاً فَلْيُصَلِّ أُخْرَى وَ يَنْصَرِفُ وَ يَجْعَلُهَا تَطَوُّعاً وَ لْيَدْخُلْ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فِي صَلاَتِهِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ إِمَامَ عَدْلٍ فَلْيَبْنِ عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ كَمَا هُوَ وَ يُصَلِّي رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى مَعَهُ وَ يَجْلِسُ قَدْرَ مَا يَقُولُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ ثُمَّ لْيُتِمَّ صَلاَتَهُ مَعَهُ عَلَى مَا اِسْتَطَاعَ فَإِنَّ اَلتَّقِيَّةَ وَاسِعَةٌ وَ لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ مِنَ اَلتَّقِيَّةِ إِلاَّ وَ صَاحِبُهَا مَأْجُورٌ عَلَيْهَا إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama’ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who had begun to pray, and the imam (of prayer) came out while the man had already prayed one rak’ah of the obligatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “If the imam (of prayer) is just, then let him complete another rak’ah and end the prayer, and count it as a supererogatory (nafl) prayer, and then enter into prayer with the imam (of prayer). But if the imam (of prayer) is not just, then let him continue his own prayer as it is, and perform another rak’ah with the imam (of prayer), and remain seated for the duration it takes to say: ‘I bear witness that there is no God but Allah (swt), alone with no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad (saws) is His (azj) servant and His (azj) messenger’. Then let him complete his prayer with the imam (of prayer) to the best of his ability. Indeed, taqiyyah is expansive, and there is no act of taqiyyah except that the one who performs it is rewarded for it, if Allah (swt) wills.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 56

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The congregational prayer is being established while I have already prayed.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray, and count it for what you have missed.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ سَلَمَةَ صَاحِبِ اَلسَّابِرِيِّ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ تُقَامُ اَلصَّلاَةُ وَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتُ فَقَالَ« صَلِّ وَ اِجْعَلْهَا لِمَا فَاتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The congregational prayer is being established while I have already prayed.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray, and count it for what you have missed.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 57

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Said ibn Abdillah al-Araj, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who enters the mosque to pray with the imam (of prayer) and finds the row crowded with people, so he stands alone until the imam (of prayer) finishes the prayer, is that permissible for him? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is no harm in it.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْأَعْرَجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَدْخُلُ اَلْمَسْجِدَ لِيُصَلِّيَ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَيَجِدُ اَلصَّفَّ مُتَضَايِقاً بِأَهْلِهِ فَيَقُومُ وَحْدَهُ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ اَلْإِمَامُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ أَ يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ لَهُ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Said ibn Abdillah al-Araj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who enters the mosque to pray with the imam (of prayer) and finds the row crowded with people, so he stands alone until the imam (of prayer) finishes the prayer, is that permissible for him? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 57

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “I do not see any harm in standing between the columns (for prayer).”
arabicText: رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ أَرَى بِالْوُقُوفِ بَيْنَ اَلْأَسَاطِينِ بَأْساً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “I do not see any harm in standing between the columns (for prayer).”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Nakhai from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I pray in the ‘taq’ meaning the ‘mihrab’.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm if you have enough space in it.”
arabicText: رَوَى سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ اَلنَّخَعِيِّ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي أُصَلِّي فِي اَلطَّاقِ يَعْنِي اَلْمِحْرَابَ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ إِذَا كُنْتَ تَتَوَسَّعُ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Nakhai from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I pray in the ‘taq’ meaning the ‘mihrab’.” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm if you have enough space in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “If a group prays while there is between them and the imam (of prayer) a distance that cannot be stepped over, then that imam (of prayer) is not an imam (of prayer) for them. And any row whose people are praying behind an imam (of prayer), but between them and the row in front of them there is a distance that cannot be stepped over, then that is not considered a prayer for them. And if there is a curtain or a wall between them, then that is not a valid prayer for them except for the one who is directly opposite the door.” Zurarah said, and Imam Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, also said: “These enclosed chambers (maqasir) did not exist in the time of any of the people; they were only introduced by the tyrants. And the one who prays behind them, following the prayer of someone within them, his prayer is not valid.” Zurarah said and Imam Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, also said: “The rows ought to be complete and continuous, connected to one another, and there should not be between two rows a space that cannot be stepped over the extent of that being the space where a human body would fall.”
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنْ صَلَّى قَوْمٌ وَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَ بَيْنَ اَلْإِمَامِ مَالاَ يُتَخَطَّى فَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ اَلْإِمَامُ لَهُمْ بِإِمَامٍ وَ أَيُّ صَفٍّ كَانَ أَهْلُهُ يُصَلُّونَ بِصَلاَةِ إِمَامٍ وَبَيْنَهُمْ وَبَيْنَ اَلصَّفِّ اَلَّذِي يَتَقَدَّمُهُمْ قَدْرُ مَالاَ يُتَخَطَّى فَلَيْسَ تِلْكَ لَهُمْ بِصَلاَةٍ فَإِنْ كَانَ بَيْنَهُمْ سُتْرَةٌ أَوْ جِدَارٌ فَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ لَهُمْ بِصَلاَةٍ إِلاَّ مَنْ كَانَ بِحِيَالِ اَلْبَابِ» قَالَ وَ قَالَ« هَذِهِ اَلْمَقَاصِيرُ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِي زَمَنِ أَحَدٍ مِنَ اَلنَّاسِ وَ إِنَّمَا أَحْدَثَهَا اَلْجَبَّارُونَ وَ لَيْسَ لِمَنْ صَلَّى خَلْفَهَا مُقْتَدِياً بِصَلاَةِ مَنْ فِيهَا صَلاَةٌ» قَالَ وَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تَكُونَ اَلصُّفُوفُ تَامَّةً مُتَوَاصِلَةً بَعْضُهَا إِلَى بَعْضٍ وَ لاَ يَكُونَ بَيْنَ اَلصَّفَّيْنِ مَالاَ يُتَخَطَّى يَكُونُ قَدْرُ ذَلِكَ مَسْقَطَ جَسَدِ اَلْإِنْسَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “If a group prays while there is between them and the imam (of prayer) a distance that cannot be stepped over, then that imam (of prayer) is not an imam (of prayer) for them. And any row whose people are praying behind an imam (of prayer), but between them and the row in front of them there is a distance that cannot be stepped over, then that is not considered a prayer for them. And if there is a curtain or a wall between them, then that is not a valid prayer for them except for the one who is directly opposite the door.” Zurarah said, and Imam Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, also said: “These enclosed chambers (maqasir) did not exist in the time of any of the people; they were only introduced by the tyrants. And the one who prays behind them, following the prayer of someone within them, his prayer is not valid.” Zurarah said and Imam Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, also said: “The rows ought to be complete and continuous, connected to one another, and there should not be between two rows a space that cannot be stepped over the extent of that being the space where a human body would fall.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 58

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a group in prayer while behind him there is a house in which there are women is it permissible for them to pray behind him? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, if the imam (of prayer) is lower than them.” I asked: “What if there is a wall or a path between them and him?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي بِالْقَوْمِ وَ خَلْفَهُ دَارٌ فِيهَا نِسَاءٌ هَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُنَّ أَنْ يُصَلِّينَ خَلْفَهُ قَالَ« نَعَمْ إِنْ كَانَ اَلْإِمَامُ أَسْفَلَ مِنْهُنَّ» قُلْتُ فَإِنَّ بَيْنَهُنَّ وَ بَيْنَهُ حَائِطاً أَوْ طَرِيقاً فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a group in prayer while behind him there is a house in which there are women is it permissible for them to pray behind him? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, if the imam (of prayer) is lower than them.” I asked: “What if there is a wall or a path between them and him?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 59

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim in a ‘marfu’ (elevated) chain said:
I saw Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, leading a group in prayer, and Imam (a.s) was in a corner of a house near the wall, and all of them were to his right, and there was no one to his left.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ رَفَعَهُ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُصَلِّي بِقَوْمٍ وَ هُوَ إِلَى زَاوِيَةٍ فِي بَيْتٍ بِقُرْبِ اَلْحَائِطِ وَ كُلُّهُمْ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ لَيْسَ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ أَحَدٌ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim in a ‘marfu’ (elevated) chain said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, leading a group in prayer, and Imam (a.s) was in a corner of a house near the wall, and all of them were to his right, and there was no one to his left.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 59

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who leads a group in prayer while they are in a place lower than the place where he is praying. Imam (a.s) said: “If the imam (of prayer) is on something like a platform (dukkan) or on a spot higher than their spot, their prayer is not valid.” (al-Sabbati asked) “But if he is higher than them by the measure of a finger, or whether it is more or less, if the elevation is by the measure of a span (shibr), then if it is flat ground and there happens to be an elevated spot from which the imam (of prayer) stands and those behind him stand below him, and the ground is flat except that they are in a sloped area” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.” Imam (a.s) was also asked: “And if the imam (of prayer) is in a position lower than that of those praying behind him?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.” And Imam (a.s) said: “And if a man is on top of a roof or anything similar a platform or something else and the imam (of prayer) is praying on the ground below him, it is permissible for the man to pray behind him and follow his prayer, even if he is significantly higher than him.”
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِدْرِيسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي بِقَوْمٍ وَ هُمْ فِي مَوْضِعٍ أَسْفَلَ مِنْ مَوْضِعِهِ اَلَّذِي يُصَلِّي فِيهِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ اَلْإِمَامُ عَلَى شِبْهِ اَلدُّكَّانِ أَوْ عَلَى مَوْضِعٍ أَرْفَعَ مِنْ مَوْضِعِهِمْ لَمْ تُجْزِ صَلاَتُهُمْ» وَ إِنْ كَانَ أَرْفَعَ مِنْهُمْ بِقَدْرِ إِصْبَعٍ أَوْ كَانَ أَكْثَرَ أَوْ أَقَلَّ إِذَا كَانَ اَلاِرْتِفَاعُ مِنْهُمْ بِقَدْرِ شِبْرٍ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ أَرْضاً مَبْسُوطَةً وَ كَانَ فِي مَوْضِعٍ مِنْهَا اِرْتِفَاعٌ فَقَامَ اَلْإِمَامُ فِي اَلْمَوْضِعِ اَلْمُرْتَفِعِ وَ قَامَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ أَسْفَلَ مِنْهُ وَ اَلْأَرْضُ مَبْسُوطَةٌ إِلاَّ أَنَّهُمْ فِي مَوْضِعٍ مُنْحَدِرٍ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ» قَالَ وَ سُئِلَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ اَلْإِمَامُ فِي أَسْفَلَ مِنْ مَوْضِعِ مَنْ يُصَلِّي خَلْفَهُ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ» وَقَالَ« وَإِنْ كَانَ رَجُلٌ فَوْقَ سَطْحٍ أَوْ غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ دُكَّاناً أَوْ غَيْرَهُ وَكَانَ اَلْإِمَامُ يُصَلِّي عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ أَسْفَلَ مِنْهُ جَازَ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ خَلْفَهُ وَ يَقْتَدِيَ بِصَلاَتِهِ إِنْ كَانَ أَرْفَعَ مِنْهُ بِشَيْءٍ كَثِيرٍ» وإذا صلى نفسان فذكر كل واحد منهما انه كان اماما كانت صلاتهما تامة
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ahmad ibn Idris from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who leads a group in prayer while they are in a place lower than the place where he is praying. Imam (a.s) said: “If the imam (of prayer) is on something like a platform (dukkan) or on a spot higher than their spot, their prayer is not valid.” (al-Sabbati asked) “But if he is higher than them by the measure of a finger, or whether it is more or less, if the elevation is by the measure of a span (shibr), then if it is flat ground and there happens to be an elevated spot from which the imam (of prayer) stands and those behind him stand below him, and the ground is flat except that they are in a sloped area” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.” Imam (a.s) was also asked: “And if the imam (of prayer) is in a position lower than that of those praying behind him?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.” And Imam (a.s) said: “And if a man is on top of a roof or anything similar a platform or something else and the imam (of prayer) is praying on the ground below him, it is permissible for the man to pray behind him and follow his prayer, even if he is significantly higher than him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 59

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This was narrated by Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, said regarding two men who disagreed (in leading prayer); one of them said, “I was your imam (of prayer),” and the other said, “I was your imam (of prayer).” Imam (a.s) said: “Their prayers are valid.” I asked: “And if each of them says, ‘I was following you (in prayer)’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Their prayers are invalid; they must begin (their prayers) again.”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلَيْنِ اِخْتَلَفَا فَقَالَ أَحَدُهُمَا كُنْتُ إِمَامَكَ وَقَالَ اَلْآخَرُ كُنْتُ أَنَا إِمَامَكَ فَقَالَ« صَلاَتُهُمَا تَامَّةٌ» قُلْتُ فَإِنْ قَالَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمَا كُنْتُ أَئْتَمُّ بِكَ قَالَ« فَصَلاَتُهُمَا فَاسِدَةٌ لِيَسْتَأْنِفَا»
thaqalaynSanad: This was narrated by Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from a man from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about an imam (of prayer) who is leading four or five people in prayer. Then two of them do tasbih (declare the imam of prayer has prayed three rak’ahs), and three of them do tasbih that they have prayed four rak’ahs. The two say: “Stand up,” and the three say: “Sit down,” while the imam (of prayer) inclines toward one of the groups or is uncertain and neutral in his doubt what is obligatory upon him? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no sahw (prostration of forgetfulness) upon the imam (of prayer) if those behind him have preserved his error with certainty. And there is no sahw upon those behind the imam (of prayer), if the imam (of prayer) did not err. And there is no sahw in sahw (no prostration for doubting whether one made a mistake). And there is no sahw in the Maghrib and Fajr prayers, nor in the first two rak’ahs of any prayer, and there is no sahw in supererogatory (nafilah) prayers. But if those behind the imam (of prayer) differ among themselves, then it is obligatory upon him and upon them, by way of precaution, to repeat the prayer and to act upon certainty.”
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْإِمَامِ يُصَلِّي بِأَرْبَعَةِ أَنْفُسٍ أَوْ خَمْسَةِ أَنْفُسٍ فَيُسَبِّحُ اِثْنَانِ عَلَى أَنَّهُمْ صَلَّوْا ثَلاَثاً وَ يُسَبِّحُ ثَلاَثَةٌ عَلَى أَنَّهُمْ صَلَّوْا أَرْبَعَةً يَقُولُونَ هَؤُلاَءِ قُومُوا وَ يَقُولُونَ هَؤُلاَءِ اُقْعُدُوا وَ اَلْإِمَامُ مَائِلٌ مَعَ أَحَدِهِمَا أَوْ مُعْتَدِلُ اَلْوَهْمِ فَمَا يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ« لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلْإِمَامِ سَهْوٌ إِذَا حَفِظَ عَلَيْهِ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ سَهْوَهُ بِإِيقَانٍ مِنْهُمْ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَى مَنْ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ سَهْوٌ إِذَا لَمْ يَسْهُ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ لاَ سَهْوَ فِي سَهْوٍ وَ لَيْسَ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْفَجْرِ سَهْوٌ وَ لاَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ مِنْ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ وَ لاَ سَهْوَ فِي نَافِلَةٍ فَإِذَا اِخْتَلَفَ عَلَى اَلْإِمَامِ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ فَعَلَيْهِ وَ عَلَيْهِمْ فِي اَلاِحْتِيَاطِ اَلْإِعَادَةُ وَ اَلْأَخْذُ بِالْجَزْمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from a man from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about an imam (of prayer) who is leading four or five people in prayer. And there is no sahw upon those behind the imam (of prayer), if the imam (of prayer) did not err. And there is no sahw in sahw (no prostration for doubting whether one made a mistake). And there is no sahw in the Maghrib and Fajr prayers, nor in the first two rak’ahs of any prayer, and there is no sahw in supererogatory (nafilah) prayers. But if those behind the imam (of prayer) differ among themselves, then it is obligatory upon him and upon them, by way of precaution, to repeat the prayer and to act upon certainty.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about a man who is praying behind an imam (of prayer) whom he is following, and the imam (of prayer) goes into rukuh while the man forgets and he is behind him and does not perform rukuh until the imam (of prayer) has raised his head and gone down into sujud. Should he perform rukuh and then catch up with the imam (of prayer) and the people while they are in sujud? Or what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: “Let him perform rukuh, then go down (to sujud), and complete his prayer with them. Nothing is required of him.”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي مَعَ إِمَامٍ يَقْتَدِي بِهِ فَرَكَعَ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ سَهَا اَلرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ خَلْفَهُ لَمْ يَرْكَعْ حَتَّى رَفَعَ اَلْإِمَامُ رَأْسَهُ وَ اِنْحَطَّ لِلسُّجُودِ أَ يَرْكَعُ ثُمَّ يَلْحَقُ بِالْإِمَامِ وَ اَلْقَوْمُ فِي سُجُودِهِمْ أَوْ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« يَرْكَعُ ثُمَّ يَنْحَطُّ وَ يُتِمُّ صَلاَتَهُ مَعَهُمْ وَ لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about a man who is praying behind an imam (of prayer) whom he is following, and the imam (of prayer) goes into rukuh while the man forgets and he is behind him and does not perform rukuh until the imam (of prayer) has raised his head and gone down into sujud. Imam (a.s) said: “Let him perform rukuh, then go down (to sujud), and complete his prayer with them. Nothing is required of him.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated, [saying]: Abu al-Miza from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said concerning a man who is praying behind an imam (of prayer) and gives the taslim before the imam (of prayer). Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that.”
arabicText: رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ أَبُو اَلْمِعْزَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ فَيُسَلِّمُ قَبْلَ اَلْإِمَامِ قَالَ« لَيْسَ بِذَلِكَ بَأْسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated, [saying]: Abu al-Miza from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said concerning a man who is praying behind an imam (of prayer) and gives the taslim before the imam (of prayer). Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
This was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Said from Abu Ali, who said:
We were with Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, when a man came to Imam (a.s) and said: “May I be your ransom. We prayed the Fajr prayer in the mosque, and some of us left while others remained seated in tasbih. Then a man entered the mosque and gave the adhan, so we prevented him and pushed him away from doing that.” Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “You did well. Push him away from that and prevent him with the strongest prevention.” I asked: “If they enter and wish to pray in congregation in it?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then let them stand in a corner of the mosque, and no imam (of prayer) should step forward among them.” I said to Imam (a.s): “May I be your ransom. We have an imam (of prayer) who is opposed (to us), and he hates all of our companions.” Imam (a.s) said: “What concern do you have for what he says? By Allah (swt), if you are truthful, then you have more right to the mosque than he does. So be the first to enter and the last to leave, and display good character with the people and speak well.” Then a man asked: “May I be your ransom, the saying of Allah (swt), the Exalted: ‘And speak kindly to people’ (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:83), is that meant for all people?” Imam Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, laughed and said: “No, what is meant is, ‘Say: (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) is the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family.’”
arabicText: رَوَى ذَلِكَ أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيٍّ قَالَ: كُنَّا عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَأَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ صَلَّيْنَا فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْفَجْرَ وَ اِنْصَرَفَ بَعْضُنَا وَ جَلَسَ بَعْضٌ فِي اَلتَّسْبِيحِ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْنَا رَجُلٌ اَلْمَسْجِدَ فَأَذَّنَ فَمَنَعْنَاهُ وَ دَفَعْنَاهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« أَحْسَنْتَ اِدْفَعْهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ وَ اِمْنَعْهُ أَشَدَّ اَلْمَنْعِ» فَقُلْتُ فَإِنْ دَخَلُوا فَأَرَادُوا أَنْ يُصَلُّوا فِيهِ جَمَاعَةً قَالَ« يَقُومُونَ فِي نَاحِيَةِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ وَ لاَ يَبْدُرْ بِهِمْ إِمَامٌ» فَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَنَا جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنَّ لَنَا إِمَاماً مُخَالِفاً وَ هُوَ يُبْغِضُ أَصْحَابَنَا كُلَّهُمْ فَقَالَ« مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ وَ اَللَّهِ لَئِنْ كُنْتَ صَادِقاً لَأَنْتَ أَحَقُّ بِالْمَسْجِدِ مِنْهُ فَكُنْ أَوَّلَ دَاخِلٍ وَآخِرَ خَارِجٍ وَأَحْسِنْ خُلُقَكَ مَعَ اَلنَّاسِ وَقُلْ خَيْراً» فَقَالَ رَجُلٌ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ قَوْلُ اَللَّهِ تَعَالَى« وَقُولُوا لِلنّٰاسِ حُسْناً» هُوَ لِلنَّاسِ جَمِيعاً فَضَحِكَ وَقَالَ« لاَ عَنَى قُولُوا مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ عَلَى أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ»

thaqalaynMatn: We were with Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, when a man came to Imam (a.s) and said: “May I be your ransom. We prayed the Fajr prayer in the mosque, and some of us left while others remained seated in tasbih. Then a man entered the mosque and gave the adhan, so we prevented him and pushed him away from doing that.” Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “You did well. author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Abu Ja’far from Abu al-Jawza from al-Husayn ibn Alwan from Amru ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn Ali from his forefathers (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
Two men entered the mosque after Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, had already led the people in prayer. Imam Ali (a.s) said to them: “If you wish, then let one of you lead the other in prayer but do not give the adhan or the iqamah.”
arabicText: مَا رَوَاهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْجَوْزَاءِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُلْوَانَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« دَخَلَ رَجُلاَنِ اَلْمَسْجِدَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّى عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِالنَّاسِ فَقَالَ لَهُمَا «إِنْ شِئْتُمَا فَلْيَؤُمَّ أَحَدُكُمَا صَاحِبَهُ وَ لاَ يُؤَذِّنُ وَ لاَ يُقِيمُ»»

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ishaq from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Give the adhan behind the one whom you recited behind.”
arabicText: رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَذِّنْ خَلْفَ مَنْ قَرَأْتَ خَلْفَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Ishaq from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Give the adhan behind the one whom you recited behind.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 63

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abu al-Bukhturi from Imam Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Indeed, Imam Ali (a.s), said: ‘The child stands to the right of the man in prayer if the row is properly formed that is considered congregation. And the seated sick person sits to the right of the child that is also considered congregation.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَ قَالَ إِنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلصَّبِيُّ عَنْ يَمِينِ اَلرَّجُلِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ إِذَا ضَبَطَ اَلصَّفَّ جَمَاعَةٌ وَ اَلْمَرِيضُ اَلْقَاعِدُ عَنْ يَمِينِ اَلصَّبِيِّ جَمَاعَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abu al-Bukhturi from Imam Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Indeed, Imam Ali (a.s), said: ‘The child stands to the right of the man in prayer if the row is properly formed that is considered congregation. And the seated sick person sits to the right of the child that is also considered congregation.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 63

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Abbas ibn Amir al-Qasabani and Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Sufyan al-Jariri, from al-‘Arzami, from his father, to Prophet:
Prophet Muhammad (saws) said: “Whoever leads a group in prayer while there is among them someone more knowledgeable than him, their affair will continuously decline until the Day of Resurrection.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ اَلْقَصَبَانِيِّ وَ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ اَلْحُصَيْنِ عَنْ سُفْيَانَ اَلْجَرِيرِيِّ عَنِ اَلْعَرْزَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ رَفَعَ اَلْحَدِيثَ إِلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَالَ:« مَنْ أَمَّ قَوْماً وَ فِيهِمْ مَنْ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مِنْهُ لَمْ يَزَلْ أَمْرُهُمْ إِلَى اَلسَّفَالِ إِلَى يَوْمِ اَلْقِيَامَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Abbas ibn Amir al-Qasabani and Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Sufyan al-Jariri, from al-‘Arzami, from his father, to Prophet:
thaqalaynMatn: Prophet Muhammad (saws) said: “Whoever leads a group in prayer while there is among them someone more knowledgeable than him, their affair will continuously decline until the Day of Resurrection.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 63

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughirah from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam Ali (a.s) used to say: “When a man enters the mosque and its people have already prayed, then he should not give the adhan, nor should he give the iqamah, and he should not perform supererogatory prayers until he begins with the obligatory prayer. And he should not leave it (the mosque) for another place until he has prayed in it.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ بُنَانِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا دَخَلَ اَلرَّجُلُ اَلْمَسْجِدَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّى أَهْلُهُ فَلاَ يُؤَذِّنَنَّ وَ لاَ يُقِيمَنَّ وَ لاَ يَتَطَوَّعُ حَتَّى يَبْدَأَ بِصَلاَةِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ لاَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ إِلَى غَيْرِهِ حَتَّى يُصَلِّيَ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Bunan ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughirah from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) used to say: “When a man enters the mosque and its people have already prayed, then he should not give the adhan, nor should he give the iqamah, and he should not perform supererogatory prayers until he begins with the obligatory prayer. And he should not leave it (the mosque) for another place until he has prayed in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 64

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ayyub, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar and Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said:
Imam (a.s) asked about a man who missed one rak’ah of Maghrib prayer with the imam (of prayer), and he caught the other two; the first of those two is his first rak‘ah, and the second is the second rak‘ah for the group in which they perform the tashahhud. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “And the second one as well?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “All of them?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and it is only a blessing.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ اَلْمُخْتَارِ وَ دَاوُدَ بْنِ اَلْحُصَيْنِ قَالَ: سَأَلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ فَاتَتْهُ رَكْعَةٌ مِنَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَأَدْرَكَ اَلثِّنْتَيْنِ فَهِيَ اَلْأُولَى لَهُ وَ اَلثَّانِيَةُ لِلْقَوْمِ يَتَشَهَّدُ فِيهَا قَالَ« نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ وَ اَلثَّانِيَةَ أَيْضاً قَالَ« نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ كُلَّهُنَّ قَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ إِنَّمَا هِيَ بَرَكَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ayyub, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar and Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) asked about a man who missed one rak’ah of Maghrib prayer with the imam (of prayer), and he caught the other two; the first of those two is his first rak‘ah, and the second is the second rak‘ah for the group in which they perform the tashahhud. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “And the second one as well?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I asked: “All of them?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and it is only a blessing.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 64

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Congregational Prayer (the Minimum Number for Congregational Prayer, the Description of the Imam, Who Is to Be Followed and Who Is Not to Be Followed, Recitation Behind Both of Them, the Rulings of Those Led in Prayer, and Other Such Rulings Related to It)
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Nasr from Asim from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “When is a person considered to have caught the prayer with the imam (of prayer)?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he catches the imam (of prayer) while he is in the final prostration of his prayer, then he has attained the merit of praying with the imam (of prayer).”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ عَاصِمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ مَتَى يَكُونُ يُدْرِكُ اَلصَّلاَةَ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ قَالَ« إِذَا أَدْرَكَ اَلْإِمَامَ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلسَّجْدَةِ اَلْأَخِيرَةِ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ فَهُوَ مُدْرِكٌ لِفَضْلِ اَلصَّلاَةِ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Nasr from Asim from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “When is a person considered to have caught the prayer with the imam (of prayer)?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he catches the imam (of prayer) while he is in the final prostration of his prayer, then he has attained the merit of praying with the imam (of prayer).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 64

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of the Month of Ramadan and the Prayers Within It in Addition to the Recommended Prayers Mentioned in the Other Months
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub al-Zarrad from Abu Ayyub from Abu al-Ward from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, delivered a sermon to the people on the last Friday of Shaban. Prophet (saws) praised Allah (swt) and glorified Him (azj), then said: “O people, indeed there has come upon you a month in which there is a night that is ‘better than a thousand months’. It is the Month of Ramadan. Allah (swt) has made its fasting obligatory and made standing in prayer during one of its nights in voluntary prayer equal to one who has offered prayer on seventy nights outside of it in other months. And whoever performs in it, one act of goodness or righteousness voluntarily, it will be as the reward of one who has fulfilled an obligation among the obligations of Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted. And whoever fulfills in it, an obligatory act among the obligations of Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted, it will be as if he has fulfilled seventy obligatory acts in other months. And it is the month of patience (sabr), and indeed the reward of patience is Paradise. And it is the month of compassion, and it is the month in which Allah (swt) increases the sustenance of the believers. And whoever provides iftar to a fasting believer in it, it will be for him with Allah (swt) the reward of freeing a slave and forgiveness for his past sins.” It was said to the Prophet (saws): “O Messenger of Allah (swt), not all of us are able to provide iftar to a fasting person.” So Prophet (saws) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, is Generous. He (azj) gives this reward even to the one who is only able to offer a sip of milk with which a fasting person breaks his fast, or a drink of fresh water, or a single date if he is unable to give more than that. And whoever lightens the burden on his servant during this month, Allah (swt) will lighten his reckoning for him. And it is a month its beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is acceptance and freedom from the Fire. And you have no need in this month to do without four qualities; two by which you please Allah (swt), and two which you cannot do without. As for the two by which you please Allah (swt), (it is) the testimony that there is ‘no God but Allah (swt)’, and that ‘I (Prophet Muhammad (saws) am the Messenger of Allah (swt)’. And as for the two which you cannot do without, you ask Allah (swt) for your needs and for Paradise, and you ask Him (azj) for well-being and seek refuge with Him (azj) from the Fire.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ اَلزَّرَّادِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْوَرْدِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «خَطَبَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ اَلنَّاسَ فِي آخِرِ جُمُعَةٍ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ فَحَمِدَ اَللَّهَ وَ أَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ« أَيُّهَا اَلنَّاسُ إِنَّهُ قَدْ أَظَلَّكُمْ شَهْرٌ فِيهِ لَيْلَةٌ« خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ» وَ هُوَ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ فَرَضَ اَللَّهُ صِيَامَهُ وَ جَعَلَ قِيَامَ لَيْلَةٍ فِيهِ بِتَطَوُّعِ صَلاَةٍ كَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ بِصَلاَةِ سَبْعِينَ لَيْلَةً فِيمَا سِوَاهُ مِنَ اَلشُّهُورِ وَ جَعَلَ لِمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ فِيهِ بِخَصْلَةٍ مِنْ خِصَالِ اَلْخَيْرِ وَ اَلْبِرِّ كَأَجْرِ مَنْ أَدَّى فَرِيضَةً مِنْ فَرَائِضِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ مَنْ أَدَّى فِيهِ فَرِيضَةً مِنْ فَرَائِضِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ كَانَ كَمَنْ أَدَّى سَبْعِينَ فَرِيضَةً مِنْ فَرَائِضِ اَللَّهِ فِيمَا سِوَاهُ مِنَ اَلشُّهُورِ وَ هُوَ شَهْرُ اَلصَّبْرِ وَ إِنَّ اَلصَّبْرَ ثَوَابُهُ اَلْجَنَّةُ وَ هُوَ شَهْرُ اَلْمُوَاسَاةِ وَ هُوَ شَهْرٌ يَزِيدُ اَللَّهُ فِي رِزْقِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ مَنْ فَطَّرَ فِيهِ مُؤْمِناً صَائِماً كَانَ لَهُ عِنْدَ اَللَّهِ بِذَلِكَ عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ وَ مَغْفِرَةٌ لِذُنُوبِهِ فِيمَا مَضَى» فَقِيلَ لَهُ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ لَيْسَ كُلُّنَا يَقْدِرُ أَنْ يُفَطِّرَ صَائِماً فَقَالَ« إِنَّ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى كَرِيمٌ يُعْطِي هَذَا اَلثَّوَابَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ إِلاَّ عَلَى مَذْقَةٍ مِنْ لَبَنٍ يُفَطِّرُ بِهَا مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَوْ شَرْبَةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ عَذْبٍ أَوْ تَمْرَةٍ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَ مَنْ خَفَّفَ فِيهِ عَنْ مَمْلُوكِهِ خَفَّفَ اَللَّهُ عَنْهُ حِسَابَهُ وَ هُوَ شَهْرٌ أَوَّلُهُ رَحْمَةٌ وَ وَسَطُهُ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَ آخِرُهُ إِجَابَةٌ وَ اَلْعِتْقُ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ وَ لاَ غَنَاءَ بِكُمْ فِيهِ عَنْ أَرْبَعِ خِصَالٍ خَصْلَتَيْنِ تُرْضُونَ اَللَّهَ بِهِمَا وَ خَصْلَتَيْنِ لاَ غَنَاءَ بِكُمْ عَنْهُمَا أَمَّا اَللَّتَانِ تُرْضُونَ اَللَّهَ بِهِمَا فَشَهَادَةُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ أَنِّي رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ وَ أَمَّا اَللَّتَانِ لاَ غَنَاءَ بِكُمْ عَنْهُمَا فَتَسْأَلُونَ اَللَّهَ فِيهِ حَوَائِجَكُمْ وَ اَلْجَنَّةَ وَ تَسْأَلُونَ اَلْعَافِيَةَ وَ تَتَعَوَّذُونَ بِهِ مِنَ اَلنَّارِ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub al-Zarrad from Abu Ayyub from Abu al-Ward from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, delivered a sermon to the people on the last Friday of Shaban. Prophet (saws) praised Allah (swt) and glorified Him (azj), then said: “O people, indeed there has come upon you a month in which there is a night that is ‘better than a thousand months’. It is the Month of Ramadan. Allah (swt) has made its fasting obligatory and made standing in prayer during one of its nights in voluntary prayer equal to one who has offered prayer on seventy nights outside of it in other months. And whoever performs in it, one act of goodness or righteousness voluntarily, it will be as the reward of one who has fulfilled an obligation among the obligations of Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted. And whoever fulfills in it, an obligatory act among the obligations of Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted, it will be as if he has fulfilled seventy obligatory acts in other months. And it is the month of patience (sabr), and indeed the reward of patience is Paradise. And it is the month of compassion, and it is the month in which Allah (swt) increases the sustenance of the believers. And whoever provides iftar to a fasting believer in it, it will be for him with Allah (swt) the reward of freeing a slave and forgiveness for his past sins.” It was said to the Prophet (saws): “O Messenger of Allah (swt), not all of us are able to provide iftar to a fasting person.” So Prophet (saws) said: “Indeed, Allah (swt), the Exalted, is Generous. He (azj) gives this reward even to the one who is only able to offer a sip of milk with which a fasting person breaks his fast, or a drink of fresh water, or a single date if he is unable to give more than that. And whoever lightens the burden on his servant during this month, Allah (swt) will lighten his reckoning for him. And it is a month its beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is acceptance and freedom from the Fire. And you have no need in this month to do without four qualities; two by which you please Allah (swt), and two which you cannot do without. As for the two by which you please Allah (swt), (it is) the testimony that there is ‘no God but Allah (swt)’, and that ‘I (Prophet Muhammad (saws) am the Messenger of Allah (swt)’. And as for the two which you cannot do without, you ask Allah (swt) for your needs and for Paradise, and you ask Him (azj) for well-being and seek refuge with Him (azj) from the Fire.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 64

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of the Month of Ramadan and the Prayers Within It in Addition to the Recommended Prayers Mentioned in the Other Months
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hasan, from Zurah, from Sama’ah, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said to me (Sama’ah): “Pray on the night of the twenty-first and the night of the twenty-third of the Month of Ramadan; in each of these nights, if you have the strength; one hundred rak’ahs, aside from the thirteen (regular) rak’ahs (meaning salat al layl). And stay awake during them until morning, for it is recommended that you remain in prayer, supplication, and humble entreaty, for it is hoped that one of them will be the Night of Qadr. And ‘The Night of Qadr is better than a thousand months.’” (Surah Al-Qadr 97:3). So I said to Imam (a.s): “How is it better than a thousand months?” Imam (a.s) said: “The deeds performed during it are better than deeds performed over a thousand months, and in those (other) months there is no ‘Night of Qadr’. It occurs only in the Month of Ramadan. And (as Allah (swt) says): ‘In it every wise matter is decreed.’” (Surah Al-Qadr 97:4) I asked: “And how is that?” Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever will occur in the year is decreed during it and in it is written those who will go as pilgrims to Mecca.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي« صَلِّ فِي لَيْلَةِ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ وَ لَيْلَةِ ثَلاَثٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ فِي كُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا إِنْ قَوِيتَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ مِائَةَ رَكْعَةٍ سِوَى اَلثَّلاَثَ عَشْرَةَ وَ اِسْهَرْ فِيهِمَا حَتَّى تُصْبِحَ فَإِنَّهُ يُسْتَحَبُّ أَنْ تَكُونَ فِي صَلاَةٍ وَ دُعَاءٍ وَ تَضَرُّعٍ فَإِنَّهُ يُرْجَى أَنْ تَكُونَ لَيْلَةُ اَلْقَدْرِ فِي إِحْدَاهُمَا وَ« لَيْلَةُ اَلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ»» فَقُلْتُ لَهُ كَيْفَ هِيَ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ قَالَ« اَلْعَمَلُ فِيهَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ اَلْعَمَلِ فِي أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ وَ لَيْسَ فِي هَذِهِ اَلْأَشْهُرِ لَيْلَةُ اَلْقَدْرِ وَ هِيَ تَكُونُ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ« فِيهٰا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ»» فَقُلْتُ وَ كَيْفَ ذَاكَ فَقَالَ «مَا يَكُونُ فِي اَلسَّنَةِ وَ فِيهَا يُكْتَبُ اَلْوَفْدُ إِلَى مَكَّةَ»

thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said to me (Sama’ah): “Pray on the night of the twenty-first and the night of the twenty-third of the Month of Ramadan; in each of these nights, if you have the strength; one hundred rak’ahs, aside from the thirteen (regular) rak’ahs (meaning salat al layl). And stay awake during them until morning, for it is recommended that you remain in prayer, supplication, and humble entreaty, for it is hoped that one of them will be the Night of Qadr. And ‘The Night of Qadr is better than a thousand months.’” (Surah Al-Qadr 97:3). So I said to Imam (a.s): “How is it better than a thousand months?” Imam (a.s) said: “The deeds performed during it are better than deeds performed over a thousand months, and in those (other) months there is no ‘Night of Qadr’. It occurs only in the Month of Ramadan. And (as Allah (swt) says): ‘In it every wise matter is decreed.’” (Surah Al-Qadr 97:4) I asked: “And how is that?” Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever will occur in the year is decreed during it and in it is written those who will go as pilgrims to Mecca.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of the Month of Ramadan and the Prayers Within It in Addition to the Recommended Prayers Mentioned in the Other Months
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s) about the ‘Night of Qadr’. Imam (a.s) said: “It is the night of the twenty-first or the twenty-third (of the Month of Ramadan).” I asked: “Is it not just one night?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, indeed.” I asked: “Then inform me which one it is.” Imam (a.s) said: “What harm is there upon you in doing good on both nights?”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ لَيْلَةِ اَلْقَدْرِ قَالَ« هِيَ لَيْلَةُ إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ أَوْ ثَلاَثٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ» قُلْتُ أَ لَيْسَ إِنَّمَا هِيَ لَيْلَةٌ قَالَ« بَلَى» قُلْتُ فَأَخْبِرْنِي بِهَا فَقَالَ« وَ مَا عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَفْعَلَ خَيْراً فِي لَيْلَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s) about the ‘Night of Qadr’. Imam (a.s) said: “It is the night of the twenty-first or the twenty-third (of the Month of Ramadan).” I asked: “Is it not just one night?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, indeed.” I asked: “Then inform me which one it is.” Imam (a.s) said: “What harm is there upon you in doing good on both nights?”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of the Month of Ramadan and the Prayers Within It in Addition to the Recommended Prayers Mentioned in the Other Months
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali, who said:
I was with Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and Abu Basir said to Imam (a.s): “The night in which that which is hoped for is to be hoped which night is it?” Imam (a.s) said: “The twenty-first or the twenty-third (of the Month of Ramadan).” He (Abu Basir) asked: “And if I do not have the strength for both of them?” Imam (a.s) said: “How easy are two nights for what you seek!” I asked: “Sometimes we see the new moon in our region, then someone comes to us from another land informing us of something different.” Imam (a.s) said: “How easy it is to seek it over four nights!” I asked: “May I be your ransom, is the twenty-third night, ‘the night of al-Juhaniyy’?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is indeed said.” I asked: “Sulayman ibn Khalid narrated that on the nineteenth [of Month of Ramadan], the names of the pilgrims are written.” Imam (a.s) said: “O Aba Muhammad, the names of the pilgrims are written on the ‘Night of Qadr’, along with (the decrees of) death, trials, provisions, and all that will occur until the same time the following year. So seek it on the twenty-first and the twenty-third (of the Month of Ramadan). Pray one hundred rak’ahs on each of them, and keep them alive (with worship) if you are able.” I asked: “And if I am not able?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then there is no harm in applying a little sleep to your eyes at the start of the night. Indeed, the gates of the heavens are opened in (month of) Ramadan, the devils are chained, and the deeds of the believers are accepted. What a blessed month Ramadan is! It used to be called, in the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, ‘al-Marzuq’ (the blessed and provisioned one).”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ قَالَ: كُنْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ اَللَّيْلَةُ اَلَّتِي يُرْجَى فِيهَا مَا يُرْجَى فَقَالَ« فِي إِحْدَى وَ عِشْرِينَ أَوْ ثَلاَثٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ» قَالَ فَإِنْ لَمْ أَقْوَ عَلَى كِلْتَيْهِمَا فَقَالَ« مَا أَيْسَرَ لَيْلَتَيْنِ فِيمَا تَطْلُبُ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَرُبَّمَا رَأَيْنَا اَلْهِلاَلَ عِنْدَنَا وَجَاءَنَامَنْ يُخْبِرُ نَابِخِلاَفِ ذَلِكَ فِي أَرْضٍ أُخْرَى فَقَالَ« مَا أَيْسَرَ أَرْبَعَ لَيَالٍ تَطْلُبُهَا فِيهَا» قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ لَيْلَةُ ثَلاَثٍ وَ عِشْرِينَ لَيْلَةُ اَلْجُهَنِيِّ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَيُقَالُ» قُلْتُ إِنَّ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنَ خَالِدٍ رَوَى فِي تِسْعَ عَشْرَةَ يُكْتَبُ وَفْدُ اَلْحَاجِّ فَقَالَ« يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ يُكْتَبُ وَفْدُ اَلْحَاجِّ فِي لَيْلَةِ اَلْقَدْرِ وَاَلْمَنَايَا وَاَلْبَلاَيَا وَاَلْأَرْزَاقُ وَمَا يَكُونُ إِلَى مِثْلِهَا فِي قَابِلٍ فَاطْلُبْهَا فِي إِحْدَى وَ ثَلاَثٍ وَ صَلِّ فِي كُلِّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا مِائَةَ رَكْعَةٍ وَأَحْيِهِمَا إِنِ اِسْتَطَعْتَ» قُلْتُ فَإِنْ لَمْ أَسْتَطِعْ قَالَ« فَلاَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَكْتَحِلَ فِي أَوَّلِ اَللَّيْلِ بِشَيْءٍ مِنَ اَلنَّوْمِ إِنَّ أَبْوَابَ اَلسَّمَاءِ تُفَتَّحُ فِي رَمَضَانَ وَ تُصَفَّدُ اَلشَّيَاطِينُ وَ تُقْبَلُ أَعْمَالُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ نِعْمَ اَلشَّهْرُ رَمَضَانُ كَانَ يُسَمَّى عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ اَلْمَرْزُوقَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I was with Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and Abu Basir said to Imam (a.s): “The night in which that which is hoped for is to be hoped which night is it?” Imam (a.s) said: “The twenty-first or the twenty-third (of the Month of Ramadan).” He (Abu Basir) asked: “And if I do not have the strength for both of them?” Imam (a.s) said: “How easy are two nights for what you seek!” I asked: “Sometimes we see the new moon in our region, then someone comes to us from another land informing us of something different.” Imam (a.s) said: “How easy it is to seek it over four nights!” I asked: “May I be your ransom, is the twenty-third night, ‘the night of al-Juhaniyy’?” Imam (a.s) said: “That is indeed said.” I asked: “Sulayman ibn Khalid narrated that on the nineteenth [of Month of Ramadan], the names of the pilgrims are written.” Imam (a.s) said: “O Aba Muhammad, the names of the pilgrims are written on the ‘Night of Qadr’, along with (the decrees of) death, trials, provisions, and all that will occur until the same time the following year. So seek it on the twenty-first and the twenty-third (of the Month of Ramadan). Pray one hundred rak’ahs on each of them, and keep them alive (with worship) if you are able.” I asked: “And if I am not able?” Imam (a.s) said: “Then there is no harm in applying a little sleep to your eyes at the start of the night. Indeed, the gates of the heavens are opened in (month of) Ramadan, the devils are chained, and the deeds of the believers are accepted. What a blessed month Ramadan is! It used to be called, in the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, ‘al-Marzuq’ (the blessed and provisioned one).”
