chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja’far from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Eid prayer with the (just) imam is a sunnah, and there is no prayer before it nor after it on that day until midday (zawal).”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« صَلاَةُ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ سُنَّةٌ وَ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَهَا صَلاَةٌ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ إِلَى اَلزَّوَالِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja’far from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Eid prayer with the (just) imam is a sunnah, and there is no prayer before it nor after it on that day until midday (zawal).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 146

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Uthman from Sama’ah from Abi Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There is no (prescribed) prayer on the two Eids except with the (just) imam. But if you pray alone, then there is no harm.” And I asked Imam (a.s) about eating before going out on the day of Eid. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes and if you do not eat, then there is no harm.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ صَلاَةَ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ إِلاَّ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ إِنْ صَلَّيْتَ وَحْدَكَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْأَكْلِ قَبْلَ اَلْخُرُوجِ يَوْمَ اَلْعِيدِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَأْكُلْ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Uthman from Sama’ah from Abi Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There is no (prescribed) prayer on the two Eids except with the (just) imam. But if you pray alone, then there is no harm.” And I asked Imam (a.s) about eating before going out on the day of Eid. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes and if you do not eat, then there is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 146

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Muawiyah ibn Hakim from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah who said: Some of our companions narrated to me. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the prayer of al-Fitr and al-Adha. Imam (a.s) said: “Pray them as two rak’ahs, whether in congregation or individually, and say takbir seven times (in the first unit) and five times (in the second unit).”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْفِطْرِ وَ اَلْأَضْحَى فَقَالَ« صَلِّهِمَا رَكْعَتَيْنِ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ وَ غَيْرِ جَمَاعَةٍ وَ كَبِّرْ سَبْعاً وَ خَمْساً»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Muawiyah ibn Hakim from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah who said: Some of our companions narrated to me. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the prayer of al-Fitr and al-Adha. Imam (a.s) said: “Pray them as two rak’ahs, whether in congregation or individually, and say takbir seven times (in the first unit) and five times (in the second unit).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 147

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Abi al-Bakhtari from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever misses the Eid prayer, let him pray four (rak’ahs).”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ فَاتَتْهُ صَلاَةُ اَلْعِيدِ فَلْيُصَلِّ أَرْبَعاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Abi al-Bakhtari from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them both, from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever misses the Eid prayer, let him pray four (rak’ahs).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 147

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from al-Ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the prayer on the Day of Fitr and the Day of Adha. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no prayer except with the Imam.”
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن صفوان عن العلا عن محمد بن مسلم عن أحدهما قال سألته عن الصلاة يوم الفطر والاضحى فقال ليس صلاة إلا مع الامام
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from al-Ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two (Imams (a.s)), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about the prayer on the Day of Fitr and the Day of Adha. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no prayer except with the Imam.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 147

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Hatim from al-Husayn ibn Ali from his father from Fadalah from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever does not attend the public congregation of people on the two Eids, let him perform ghusl, and apply fragrance with whatever he finds, and let him pray alone, just as he would pray in congregation.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Take your adornment at every masjid” (Surah Al-A’raf 7:31), And Imam (a.s) said: “(this applies to) The two Eids and Jumu’ah (Friday).”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنْ لَمْ يَشْهَدْ جَمَاعَةَ اَلنَّاسِ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ فَلْيَغْتَسِلْ وَ يَتَطَيَّبُ بِمَا وَجَدَ وَ لْيُصَلِّ وَحْدَهُ كَمَا يُصَلِّي فِي اَلْجَمَاعَةِ» وَ قَالَ«« خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِنْدَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ»» قَالَ« اَلْعِيدَانِ وَ اَلْجُمُعَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Hatim from al-Husayn ibn Ali from his father from Fadalah from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever does not attend the public congregation of people on the two Eids, let him perform ghusl, and apply fragrance with whatever he finds, and let him pray alone, just as he would pray in congregation.” And Imam (a.s) said: “Take your adornment at every masjid” (Surah Al-A’raf 7:31), And Imam (a.s) said: “(this applies to) The two Eids and Jumu’ah (Friday).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 147

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: (A similar narration)
And Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) added, saying: “On the Day of Arafah, they gather without an Imam in the cities ('amsar') to supplicate to Allah (swt), the Exalted, the Mighty and Majestic.”
arabicText: وَرَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: مِثْلَهُ وَ زَادَ وَ قَالَ« فِي يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ يَجْتَمِعُونَ بِغَيْرِ إِمَامٍ فِي اَلْأَمْصَارِ يَدْعُونَ اَللَّهَ تَعَالَى عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: (A similar narration)
thaqalaynMatn: And Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) added, saying: “On the Day of Arafah, they gather without an Imam in the cities ('amsar') to supplicate to Allah (swt), the Exalted, the Mighty and Majestic.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who does not go out on the Day of Fitr and the Day of Adha, does he have to pray alone? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ لاَ يَخْرُجُ يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ وَ اَلْأَضْحَى أَ عَلَيْهِ صَلاَةٌ وَحْدَهُ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, was asked about a man who does not go out on the Day of Fitr and the Day of Adha, does he have to pray alone? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Umar ibn Ja’far who said: Abdillah ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Yaqub from Mansur from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “My father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) became ill on the Day of Adha, so he prayed two rak’ahs in his house, then offered the sacrifice.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَرِضَ أَبِي يَوْمَ اَلْأَضْحَى فَصَلَّى فِي بَيْتِهِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ ضَحَّى»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Umar ibn Ja’far who said: Abdillah ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yunus ibn Yaqub from Mansur from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “My father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) became ill on the Day of Adha, so he prayed two rak’ahs in his house, then offered the sacrifice.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I (Zurarah) asked: “(If) I caught the imam (of prayer) while he was delivering the sermon.” Imam (a.s) said: “You sit until he (imam of prayer)) finishes his sermon, then you stand and pray.” I asked: “Should I begin with making up the prayer (qadah) or start with my own prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather start with your own prayer and this ruling applies only in this prayer.” I asked: “Then what if I catch part of the obligatory prayer with the imam (of prayer) and then complete the rest afterward?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for what you catch from the obligatory prayer, it is the beginning of your prayer, and what you make up is its end.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ أَدْرَكْتُ اَلْإِمَامَ عَلَى اَلْخُطْبَةِ قَالَ قَالَ« تَجْلِسُ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ مِنْ خُطْبَتِهِ ثُمَّ تَقُومُ فَتُصَلِّي» قُلْتُ اَلْقَضَاءُ أَوَّلُ صَلاَتِي أَوْ آخِرُهَا قَالَ« لاَ بَلْ أَوَّلُهَا وَ لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ فِي هَذِهِ اَلصَّلاَةِ» قُلْتُ فَمَا أَدْرَكْتُ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ مِنَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ مَا قَضَيْتُ قَالَ« أَمَّا مَا أَدْرَكْتَ مِنَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَهُوَ أَوَّلُ صَلاَتِكَ وَ مَا قَضَيْتَ فَآخِرُهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (Zurarah) asked: “(If) I caught the imam (of prayer) while he was delivering the sermon.” Imam (a.s) said: “You sit until he (imam of prayer)) finishes his sermon, then you stand and pray.” I asked: “Should I begin with making up the prayer (qadah) or start with my own prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather start with your own prayer and this ruling applies only in this prayer.” I asked: “Then what if I catch part of the obligatory prayer with the imam (of prayer) and then complete the rest afterward?” Imam (a.s) said: “As for what you catch from the obligatory prayer, it is the beginning of your prayer, and what you make up is its end.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr from Asim from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) narrates: “The people said to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, ‘Will you not appoint a man to lead the prayer on the two Eids?’” Imam Ali (a.s) said: “I will not go against the Sunnah.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ عَاصِمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« قَالَ اَلنَّاسُ لِأَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ لاَ تُخَلِّفُ رَجُلاً يُصَلِّي فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ فَقَالَ« لاَ أُخَالِفُ اَلسُّنَّةَ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr from Asim from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) narrates: “The people said to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, ‘Will you not appoint a man to lead the prayer on the two Eids?’” Imam Ali (a.s) said: “I will not go against the Sunnah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 148

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama’ah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “To eat before going out on the day of Eid is permissible and if you do not eat, there is no harm.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْأَ كْلُ قَبْلَ اَلْخُرُوجِ يَوْمَ اَلْعِيدِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَأْكُلْ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama’ah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “To eat before going out on the day of Eid is permissible and if you do not eat, there is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 149

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kallub from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), peace be upon them:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: ‘When two Eids coincide for the people on the same day, it is appropriate for the Imam to say in his first sermon: ‘Two Eids have come together for you today, so I will pray them both together. Whoever's dwelling is far and wishes to leave after one of them, I have granted him permission to do so.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلْخَشَّابِ عَنْ غِيَاثِ بْنِ كَلُّوبٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا اِجْتَمَعَ عِيدَانِ لِلنَّاسِ فِي يَوْمٍ وَاحِدٍ فَإِنَّهُ يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ فِي خُطْبَتِهِ اَلْأُولَى أَنَّهُ قَدِ اِجْتَمَعَ لَكُمْ عِيدَانِ فَأَنَا أُصَلِّيهِمَا جَمِيعاً فَمَنْ كَانَ مَكَانُهُ قَاصِياً فَأَحَبَّ أَنْ يَنْصَرِفَ عَنِ اَلْآخَرِ فَقَدْ أَذِنْتُ لَهُ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kallub from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: ‘When two Eids coincide for the people on the same day, it is appropriate for the Imam to say in his first sermon: ‘Two Eids have come together for you today, so I will pray them both together. Whoever's dwelling is far and wishes to leave after one of them, I have granted him permission to do so.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 149

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from al-Nawfali from al-Sukuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, forbade that weapons be brought out on the two Eids, except in the case of an evident enemy.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« نَهَى اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ اَلسِّلاَحُ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ عَدُوٌّ ظَاهِرٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from al-Nawfali from al-Sukuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s) from his father (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, forbade that weapons be brought out on the two Eids, except in the case of an evident enemy.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban ibn Uthman from Salamah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Two Eids coincided during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, so Imam Ali (a.s) addressed the people and said: ‘This is a day in which two Eids have come together. So whoever wishes to perform the congregational prayer with us, let him do so, and whoever does not, then indeed there is a concession for him’ (meaning whoever is staying at a distance).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَلَمَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اِجْتَمَعَ عِيدَانِ عَلَى عَهْدِ أَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَخَطَبَ اَلنَّاسَ فَقَالَ« هَذَا يَوْمٌ اِجْتَمَعَ فِيهِ عِيدَانِ فَمَنْ أَحَبَّ أَنْ يُجَمِّعَ مَعَنَا فَلْيَفْعَلْ وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ فَإِنَّ لَهُ رُخْصَةً» يَعْنِي مَنْ كَانَ مُتَنَحِّياً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban ibn Uthman from Salamah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Two Eids coincided during the time of the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, so Imam Ali (a.s) addressed the people and said: ‘This is a day in which two Eids have come together. So whoever wishes to perform the congregational prayer with us, let him do so, and whoever does not, then indeed there is a concession for him’ (meaning whoever is staying at a distance).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 149

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who raised it (in isnad) to Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Sunnah for the people of the cities is that they should go out from their cities on the two Eids, except for the people of Makkah, for they perform the prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلسُّنَّةُ عَلَى أَهْلِ اَلْأَمْصَارِ أَنْ يَبْرُزُوا مِنْ أَمْصَارِهِمْ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ إِلاَّ أَهْلَ مَكَّةَ فَإِنَّهُمْ يُصَلُّونَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرَامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya, who raised it (in isnad) to Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Sunnah for the people of the cities is that they should go out from their cities on the two Eids, except for the people of Makkah, for they perform the prayer in al-Masjid al-Haram.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 150

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There are two rak’ahs from the Sunnah which are not performed in any place except in Madinah.” Imam (a.s) said: “They are performed in the Mosque of the Messenger (saws), peace be upon him and his family, on Eid, before one goes out to the place of prayer. This is not (done) except in Madinah, because the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, did it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« رَكْعَتَانِ مِنَ اَلسُّنَّةِ لَيْسَ يُصَلَّيَانِ فِي مَوْضِعٍ إِلاَّ بِالْمَدِينَةِ» قَالَ «يُصَلَّى فِي مَسْجِدِ اَلرَّسُولِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فِي اَلْعِيدِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ إِلَى اَلْمُصَلَّى لَيْسَ ذَلِكَ إِلاَّ بِالْمَدِينَةِ لِأَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَعَلَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There are two rak’ahs from the Sunnah which are not performed in any place except in Madinah.” Imam (a.s) said: “They are performed in the Mosque of the Messenger (saws), peace be upon him and his family, on Eid, before one goes out to the place of prayer. This is not (done) except in Madinah, because the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, did it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 150

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Eat on the day of al-Fitr, before you go out to the place of prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اِطْعَمْ يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَخْرُجَ إِلَى اَلْمُصَلَّى»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Eat on the day of al-Fitr, before you go out to the place of prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 150

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Jarrah al-Mada’ini, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Eat on the day of al-Fitr before you pray, and do not eat on the day of al-Adha, until the Imam has finished and departed.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ جَرَّاحٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« اِطْعَمْ يَوْمَ اَلْفِطْرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ وَ لاَ تَطْعَمْ يَوْمَ اَلْأَضْحَى حَتَّى يَنْصَرِفَ اَلْإِمَامُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from a group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Said, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Jarrah al-Mada’ini, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Eat on the day of al-Fitr before you pray, and do not eat on the day of al-Adha, until the Imam has finished and departed.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 150

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Said al-Naqqash, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: “Indeed, there is Takbir (proclamation of 'Allahu Akbar') in al-Fitr, but it is Sunnah (recommended).” He (al-Naqqash) said: “I asked, ‘And when is it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “On the night of al-Fitr, in (the prayers of) Maghrib and the final Isha, and in the prayer of Fajr and the prayer of Eid, then it is discontinued.” He (al-Naqqash) said: “I asked, ‘How should I say it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “You say: ‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illa Allah (swt), wa-Allahu Akbar wa lillahi al-hamd, Allahu Akbar ala ma hadana’, And this is the saying of Allah (swt): ‘So that you may complete the prescribed period and glorify Allah (swt) for guiding you’. (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185)”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِاَ للَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ خَلَفِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ سَعِيدٍ اَلنَّقَّاشِ قَالَ: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لِي« أَمَا إِنَّ فِي اَلْفِطْرِ تَكْبِيراً وَ لَكِنَّهُ مَسْنُونٌ» قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ أَيْنَ هُوَ قَالَ« فِي لَيْلَةِ اَلْفِطْرِ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ وَ اَلْعِشَاءِ اَلْآخِرَةِ وَ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ وَ صَلاَةِ اَلْعِيدِ ثُمَّ يُقْطَعُ» قَالَ قُلْتُ كَيْفَ أَقُولُ قَالَ تَقُولُ« اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَ لِلَّهِ اَلْحَمْدُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ عَلَى مَا هَدَانَا وَ هُوَ قَوْلُ اَللَّهِ« وَ لِتُكْمِلُوا اَلْعِدَّةَ وَ لِتُكَبِّرُوا اَللّٰهَ عَلىٰ مٰا هَدٰاكُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Said al-Naqqash, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: “Indeed, there is Takbir (proclamation of 'Allahu Akbar') in al-Fitr, but it is Sunnah (recommended).” He (al-Naqqash) said: “I asked, ‘And when is it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “On the night of al-Fitr, in (the prayers of) Maghrib and the final Isha, and in the prayer of Fajr and the prayer of Eid, then it is discontinued.” He (al-Naqqash) said: “I asked, ‘How should I say it?’” Imam (a.s) said: “You say: ‘Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar, la ilaha illa Allah (swt), wa-Allahu Akbar wa lillahi al-hamd, Allahu Akbar ala ma hadana’, And this is the saying of Allah (swt): ‘So that you may complete the prescribed period and glorify Allah (swt) for guiding you’. (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185)”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 150

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “And remember Allah (swt) during the appointed days” (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:203). Imam (a.s) said: “The Takbir (proclamation of 'Allahu Akbar') is during the Days of Tashriq, from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer on the third day. And in the cities, it is for ten prayers. So when one departs (from Mina) after the first (departure), the people of the cities stop. And whoever remains in Mina and performs the Dhuhr and Asr prayers there, then let him proclaim the Takbir.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ« وَاُذْكُرُوا اَللّٰهَ فِي أَيّٰامٍ مَعْدُودٰاتٍ» قَالَ« اَلتَّكْبِيرُ فِي أَيَّامِ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ صَلاَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ مِنْ يَوْمِ اَلنَّحْرِ إِلَى صَلاَةِ اَلْفَجْرِ يَوْمَ اَلثَّالِثِ وَ فِي اَلْأَمْصَارِ عَشْرَ صَلَوَاتٍُ فَإِذَا نَفَرَ بَعْدَ اَلْأُولَى أَمْسَكَ أَهْلُ اَلْأَمْصَارِ وَ مَنْ أَقَامَ بِمِنًى فَصَلَّى بِهَا اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ فَلْيُكَبِّرْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “And remember Allah (swt) during the appointed days” (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:203). Imam (a.s) said: “The Takbir (proclamation of 'Allahu Akbar') is during the Days of Tashriq, from the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice until the Fajr prayer on the third day. And in the cities, it is for ten prayers. So when one departs (from Mina) after the first (departure), the people of the cities stop. And whoever remains in Mina and performs the Dhuhr and Asr prayers there, then let him proclaim the Takbir.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, said:
I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the Takbir during the Days of Tashriq after the prayers. Imam (a.s) said: “The Takbir in Mina is after fifteen prayers, and in the other cities (amsar), it is after ten prayers. The first of the Takbir is after the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr). You say in it; ‘Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest for what He has guided us to, Allah (swt) is the Greatest for what He has provided us from the beast of cattle.’ And the reason the Takbir was made for ten prayers in the other cities (amsar), is that when the people depart in the first departure (al-nafr al-awwal), the people of the cities cease from the Takbir, while the people of Mina continue to proclaim the Takbir as long as they remain in Mina, until the final departure (al-nafr al-akhir).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلتَّكْبِيرُ فِي أَيَّامِ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ فِي دُبُرِ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ فَقَالَ« اَلتَّكْبِيرُ بِمِنًى فِي دُبُرِ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ صَلاَةً وَ فِي سَائِرِ اَلْأَمْصَارِ فِي دُبُرِ عَشْرِ صَلَوَاتٍُ أَوَّلُ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فِي دُبُرِ صَلاَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ يَوْمَ اَلنَّحْرِ تَقُولُ فِيهِ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَاَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ عَلَى مَا هَدَانَا اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ عَلَى مَا رَزَقَنَا مِنْ بَهِيمَةِ اَلْأَنْعَامِ وَ إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ فِي سَائِرِ اَلْأَمْصَارِ فِي دُبُرِ عَشْرِ صَلَوَاتٍُ اَلتَّكْبِيرُ أَنَّهُ إِذَا نَفَرَ اَلنَّاسُ فِي اَلنَّفْرِ اَلْأَوَّلِ أَمْسَكَ أَهْلُ اَلْأَمْصَارِ عَنِ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ وَ كَبَّرَ أَهْلُ مِنًى مَا دَامُوا بِمِنًى إِلَى اَلنَّفْرِ اَلْأَخِيرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurarah, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the Takbir during the Days of Tashriq after the prayers. Imam (a.s) said: “The Takbir in Mina is after fifteen prayers, and in the other cities (amsar), it is after ten prayers. The first of the Takbir is after the Dhuhr prayer on the Day of Sacrifice (Yawm al-Nahr). You say in it; ‘Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest, there is no god but Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) is the Greatest, Allah (swt) is the Greatest for what He has guided us to, Allah (swt) is the Greatest for what He has provided us from the beast of cattle.’ And the reason the Takbir was made for ten prayers in the other cities (amsar), is that when the people depart in the first departure (al-nafr al-awwal), the people of the cities cease from the Takbir, while the people of Mina continue to proclaim the Takbir as long as they remain in Mina, until the final departure (al-nafr al-akhir).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Hatim from Sulayman al-Zurari from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sadan ibn Muslim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Abi Mansur from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “You say between every two Takbirs in the Eid prayers: ‘O’ Allah (swt), Possessor of Majesty and Greatness, Possessor of Generosity and Might, Possessor of Forgiveness and Mercy, Possessor of God-consciousness and forgiveness. I ask You (azj) on this day which You (azj) have made a festival for the Muslims and a treasure and increase for (Prophet) Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, that You (azj) send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), with the best of what You (azj) have sent upon any servant from among Your servants, and that You (azj) send blessings upon Your nearest angels and Your messengers, and that You forgive the believing men and believing women, and the Muslim men and Muslim women, those among them who are living and those who are deceased. O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) for the best of what Your sent servants have asked You (azj) for, and I seek refuge in You (azj) from the evil of that from which Your sent servants sought refuge.’”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ حَاتِمٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ اَلزُّرَارِيِّ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ سَعْدَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ أَبِي مَنْصُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« تَقُولُ بَيْنَ كُلِّ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ اَللَّهُمَّ أَهْلَ اَلْكِبْرِيَاءِ وَ اَلْعَظَمَةِ وَ أَهْلَ اَلْجُودِ وَ اَلْجَبَرُوتِ وَ أَهْلَ اَلْعَفْوِ وَ اَلرَّحْمَةِ وَ أَهْلَ اَلتَّقْوَى وَ اَلْمَغْفِرَةِ أَسْأَلُكَ فِي هَذَا اَلْيَوْمِ اَلَّذِي جَعَلْتَهُ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ عِيداً وَ لِمُحَمَّدٍ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ذُخْراً وَ مَزِيداً أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ كَأَفْضَلِ مَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى عَبْدٍ مِنْ عِبَادِكَ وَ صَلِّ عَلَى مَلاَئِكَتِكَ اَلْمُقَرَّبِينَ وَ رُسُلِكَ وَ اِغْفِرْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ اَلْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ اَلْمُسْلِمَاتِ اَلْأَحْيَاءِ مِنْهُمْ وَ اَلْأَمْوَاتِ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِ مَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادُكَ اَلْمُرْسَلُونَ وَ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا عَاذَ بِكَ مِنْهُ عِبَادُكَ اَلْمُرْسَلُونَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Hatim from Sulayman al-Zurari from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sadan ibn Muslim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Abi Mansur from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “You say between every two Takbirs in the Eid prayers: ‘O’ Allah (swt), Possessor of Majesty and Greatness, Possessor of Generosity and Might, Possessor of Forgiveness and Mercy, Possessor of God-consciousness and forgiveness. I ask You (azj) on this day which You (azj) have made a festival for the Muslims and a treasure and increase for (Prophet) Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, that You (azj) send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), with the best of what You (azj) have sent upon any servant from among Your servants, and that You (azj) send blessings upon Your nearest angels and Your messengers, and that You forgive the believing men and believing women, and the Muslim men and Muslim women, those among them who are living and those who are deceased. O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) for the best of what Your sent servants have asked You (azj) for, and I seek refuge in You (azj) from the evil of that from which Your sent servants sought refuge.’”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abi Jamilah from Jabir from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “When the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, used to pronounce the Takbir during the two Eids, He (a.s) would say between every two Takbirs; ‘I bear witness that there is no God but Allah (swt), alone, without partner, and I bear witness that (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) is His (azj) servant and His (azj) messenger, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. O’ Allah (swt), Possessor of Majesty’” And Imam (a.s) mentioned the supplication to its end, as previously stated.
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا كَبَّرَ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ قَالَ بَيْنَ كُلِّ تَكْبِيرَتَيْنِ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ اَللَّهُمَّ أَهْلَ اَلْكِبْرِيَاءِ»» وَ ذَكَرَ اَلدُّعَاءَ إِلَى آخِرِهِ مِثْلَهُ
thaqalaynSanad: And Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abi Jamilah from Jabir from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “When the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, used to pronounce the Takbir during the two Eids, He (a.s) would say between every two Takbirs; ‘I bear witness that there is no God but Allah (swt), alone, without partner, and I bear witness that (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) is His (azj) servant and His (azj) messenger, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. O’ Allah (swt), Possessor of Majesty’” And Imam (a.s) mentioned the supplication to its end, as previously stated.

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Two Eids
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn Atiyyah from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Supplicate on the two Eids and on the day of Jumu’ah, when you have prepared yourself to go out, with this supplication: “O’ Allah (swt), whoever has made preparations, and mobilized himself, and prepared and readied himself for an arrival before a created being, hoping for his gifts, seeking his bounty, his rewards, his generosity, and his surplus offerings then my arrival, O’ my Master, is to You (azj); And my preparation, and my readiness, and my equipping, and my preparation again, are for You (azj), hoping for Your gifts, Your rewards, and Your generous offerings. So do not disappoint my hope today, O’ You (azj) in Whom no supplicant is ever disappointed, and Whose bestowal is never diminished, I have not come to You (azj) today with a righteous deed that I have sent forward, nor with the intercession of a created being, in whom I placed hope. Rather, I have come to You (azj) acknowledging my wrongdoing and misdeeds. I have no proof and no excuse. So I ask You (azj), O’ my Lord (azj), to grant me my request, to return me with what I seek, and not to turn me back disappointed or deprived. O’ Great One! O’ Great One! O’ Great One! I beseech You (azj) by the Great, I ask You (azj), O’ Great One, to forgive me the great (sins). There is no God, but You (azj). O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and grant me the good of this day which You (azj) have honored and magnified. Cleanse me on it from all my sins and misdeeds, and increase me from Your bounty. ‘Indeed, You are the Bestower’. (Surah Sa’ad 38:35)”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مَالِكِ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ اَلثُّمَالِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اُدْعُ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ وَ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ إِذَا تَهَيَّأْتَ لِلْخُرُوجِ بِهَذَا اَلدُّعَاءِ اَللَّهُمَّ مَنْ تَهَيَّأَ وَ تَعَبَّأَ وَأَعَدَّ وَاِسْتَعَدَّ لِوِفَادَةٍ إِلَى مَخْلُوقٍ رَجَاءَ رِفْدِهِ وَطَلَبَ نَائِلِهِ وَجَوَائِزِهِ وَفَوَاضِلِهِ وَنَوَافِلِهِ فَإِلَيْكَ يَا سَيِّدِي وِفَادَتِي وَ تَهْيِئَتِي وَ تَعْبِئَتِي وَ إِعْدَادِي وَ اِسْتِعْدَادِي رَجَاءَ رِفْدِكَ وَ جَوَائِزِكَ وَ نَوَافِلِكَ فَلاَ تُخَيِّبِ اَلْيَوْمَ رَجَائِي يَا مَنْ لاَ يَخِيبُ عَلَيْهِ سَائِلٌ وَ لاَ يَنْقُصُهُ نَائِلٌ فَإِنِّي لَمْ آتِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ بِعَمَلٍ صَالِحٍ قَدَّمْتُهُ وَ لاَ شَفَاعَةِ مَخْلُوقٍ رَجَوْتُهُ وَ لَكِنْ أَتَيْتُكَ مُقِرّاً بِالظُّلْمِ وَ اَلْإِسَاءَةِ لاَ حُجَّةَ لِي وَ لاَ عُذْرَ فَأَسْأَلُكَ يَا رَبِّ أَنْ تُعْطِيَنِي مَسْأَلَتِي وَ تَقْلِبَنِي بِرَغْبَتِي وَ لاَ تَرُدَّنِي مَجْبُوهاً وَ لاَ خَائِباً يَا عَظِيمُ يَا عَظِيمُ يَا عَظِيمُ أَرْجُوكَ لِلْعَظِيمِ أَسْأَلُكَ يَا عَظِيمُ أَنْ تَغْفِرَ لِيَ اَلْعَظِيمَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ اَللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَاُرْزُقْنِي خَيْرَ هَذَا اَلْيَوْمِ اَلَّذِي شَرَّفْتَهُ وَعَظَّمْتَهُ وَ تَغْسِلَنِي فِيهِ مِنْ جَمِيعِ ذُنُوبِي وَ خَطَايَايَ وَ زِدْنِي مِنْ فَضْلِكَ« إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَلْوَهّٰابُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Malik ibn Atiyyah from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Supplicate on the two Eids and on the day of Jumu’ah, when you have prepared yourself to go out, with this supplication: “O’ Allah (swt), whoever has made preparations, and mobilized himself, and prepared and readied himself for an arrival before a created being, hoping for his gifts, seeking his bounty, his rewards, his generosity, and his surplus offerings then my arrival, O’ my Master, is to You (azj); And my preparation, and my readiness, and my equipping, and my preparation again, are for You (azj), hoping for Your gifts, Your rewards, and Your generous offerings. So do not disappoint my hope today, O’ You (azj) in Whom no supplicant is ever disappointed, and Whose bestowal is never diminished, I have not come to You (azj) today with a righteous deed that I have sent forward, nor with the intercession of a created being, in whom I placed hope. Rather, I have come to You (azj) acknowledging my wrongdoing and misdeeds. I have no proof and no excuse. So I ask You (azj), O’ my Lord (azj), to grant me my request, to return me with what I seek, and not to turn me back disappointed or deprived. O’ Great One! O’ Great One! O’ Great One! I beseech You (azj) by the Great, I ask You (azj), O’ Great One, to forgive me the great (sins). There is no God, but You (azj). O’ Allah (swt), send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and grant me the good of this day which You (azj) have honored and magnified. Cleanse me on it from all my sins and misdeeds, and increase me from Your bounty. ‘Indeed, You are the Bestower’. (Surah Sa’ad 38:35)”
