chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Ghadir
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hamadhani narrated to us; he said: Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti narrated to us; he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Abdi narrated to us; he said:
I heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Fasting on the day of Ghadir Khumm, equals the fasting of the lifetime of the world, if a person were to live and fast for as long as the world lasts, the reward of that would be for him. And its fasting equals, in the sight of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, in every year, one hundred accepted Hajj and one hundred accepted Umrah. And it is the greatest Eid of Allah (swt), and Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has never sent any prophet except that he celebrated Eid on this day, recognized its sanctity, and knew its name. In the heavens it is called the ‘Day of the Promised Covenant’, and on the earth it is the ‘Day of the Taken Pledge’ and the ‘Witnessed Gathering’. Whoever prays two rak‘ahs on this day having performed ghusl (ritual bathing) at the time of the sun's zenith, half an hour before it begins to decline and supplicates to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and in each rak‘ah recites Surah al-Hamd (once), and ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) ten times, and Ayat al-Kursi (ten times), and ‘Inna anzalnahu’ (ten times); it would equal, in the sight of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, one hundred thousand Hajj and one hundred thousand Umrah. And he would not ask Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, for any need from among the needs of this world or the Hereafter, except that it would be fulfilled whatever that need may be. And if you missed the two rak’ahs and the supplication, you may perform them later. And whoever gives iftar (breaks the fast) of a believer on this day, it would be as if he had fed an army, and an army, and an army (and Imam (a.s) kept counting until he reached ten with his hand).” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Do you know how many are in an army (fiam)?” I said: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “One hundred thousand. Each army would carry the reward of one who fed the same number from among the Prophets, the Truthful, and the Martyrs in the Sacred Sanctuary of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and gave them drink ‘on a day of severe hunger’. And a dirham (spent) on this day is equal to a million dirhams.” Imam (a.s) said: “Perhaps you think that Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has created a day more sacred than this? No, by Allah (swt)! No, by Allah (swt)! No, by Allah (swt)!” Then Imam (a.s) said: “And let it be from your words when you meet one another that you say: ‘All praise is due to Allah (swt), who honoured us with this day and made us among those who fulfill His (azj) covenant with us, and His (azj) pledge which He (azj) bound us to concerning the guardianship of the leaders of His (azj) command and the ones who uphold His (azj) justice and did not make us among the deniers and rejecters of the Day of Judgement.’” Then Imam (a.s) said: “And let it be from your supplication after these two rak’ahs that you say: ‘Our Lord (azj), indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, saying: ‘Believe in your Lord (azj),’ so we believed. Our Lord (azj), forgive us our sins, and expiate from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous. Our Lord (azj), and grant us what You (azj) promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You (azj) do not break the promise.’” (Imam (a.s) then continued) “Then you say after that; ‘O’ Allah (swt), I call You (azj) to witness and You (azj) are sufficient as a witness and I call to witness Your angels, the bearers of Your Throne, the inhabitants of Your heavens and Your earth, that indeed You (azj) are Allah (swt), there is no God but You (azj), the One to be worshipped. There is no being from beneath Your Throne to the depths of Your earth, that is rightfully worshipped besides You (azj); anything else that is worshipped is false and perishing, apart from Your Noble Face. There is no God but You (azj), the One to be worshipped; so none is worthy of worship besides You (azj). Exalted are You (azj) above what the wrongdoers say, with great exaltation. And I bear witness that (Prophet) Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, is Your servant and Your Messenger (saws). And I bear witness that Imam Ali (a.s), may Allah’s blessings be upon him, is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), and their guardian and their master. Our Lord (azj), indeed we heard the call and believed in the caller the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when he proclaimed a proclamation from You (azj) concerning that which You (azj) commanded him to convey, that he should deliver what had been revealed to him regarding the guardianship of the authority-holder appointed by You (azj). And You (azj) warned him and threatened him that if he did not convey it, You (azj) would be displeased with him. And You (azj) promised him that if he conveyed Your messages, You (azj) would protect him from the people. So He (saws) called out, delivering Your revelation and Your messages: ‘Indeed, whomever I am his master (mawla), then Ali (a.s) is his master; And whomever I am his guardian, then Ali (a.s) is his guardian; And whomever I am his Prophet (saws), then Ali (a.s) is his commander.’ Our Lord (azj), we have responded to Your caller, the warner and one who gave warning, (Prophet) Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, Your servant and Your Messenger, to (follow) Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him, the one whom You (azj) favored and made an example for the Children of Israel. Truly, he is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), their master and their guardian until the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Judgement. For indeed You (azj) said: ‘He is but a servant upon whom We bestowed Our favor and made him an example for the Children of Israel.’ (Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:59) Our Lord (azj), we have believed and followed our master, our guardian, our guide, our summoner, the summoner of all creation, And Your straight and upright path, and Your proof, and Your way, the one who calls to You (azj) with clear insight, he and those who follow him. “Glory be to Allah (swt) above what they associate (with Him)” (Surah Al-Tawbah 9:31) by his guardianship and against what they deviate by taking guardians besides him. So I bear witness, O’ my God, that Imam Ali (a.s) is the guiding, directing, And the rightly-guided Imam Ali (a.s), the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), the one You (azj) mentioned in Your Book, when You (azj) said: ‘And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and full of wisdom.’ (Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:4). I do not associate any Imam alongside him, nor do I take any guardian besides him. O’ Allah (swt), indeed we bear witness that he is Your servant, the guide after Your Prophet (saws), the warner, the one who gives warning, and Your straight path, And the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), the leader of the radiant ones with shining foreheads and limbs, Your conclusive proof, and Your tongue that speaks on Your behalf among Your creation, and the one who upholds justice after Your Prophet (saws), the executor of Your religion, And the keeper of Your knowledge, the place of Your secret, the repository of Your knowledge, and Your trusted trustee, And the one whose covenant was taken along with the covenant of Your Messenger (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, from all of Your creation and beings, A testimony of sincerity to You (azj) in affirming Your oneness; That indeed You are Allah (swt), there is no God but You (azj), and that (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) is Your servant and Your Messenger, and that Imam Ali (a.s) is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s). And that acknowledgment of his guardianship, is the completion of Your tawhid (Divine Unity), and sincerity in Your oneness, And the perfection of Your religion, and the completion of Your favor, and Your bounty upon all of Your creation and beings. For indeed You (azj) said and Your word is the truth: ‘This day I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as your religion.’ (Surah Al-Ma’idah 5:3) O’ Allah (swt), to You (azj) belongs all praise for what You (azj) have bestowed upon us, the sincerity to You (azj) in Your Oneness when You (azj) guided us to the guardianship of Your friend, the guide after Your Prophet (saws), the warner. And You (azj) were pleased for us that Islam be our religion through our loyalty to him, And You (azj) completed upon us Your blessing, that by which You (azj) renewed for us Your covenant and Your pledge, and reminded us of it, And made us among the people of sincerity and affirmation of Your covenant and Your pledge, and among those who fulfill it. And You (azj) did not make us among the breakers (of the covenant), nor among the rejecters, nor among those who deny the Day of Judgement. And You (azj) did not make us among the followers of those who alter and distort, And those who deviate and split, And those who mutilate the ears of cattle, And those who alter the creation of Allah (swt), and among those over whom ‘Satan has taken control, so he made them forget the remembrance of Allah (swt)’ (Surah Al-Mujadilah 58:19), And (Satan) diverted them from the path and from the straight path.” (Imam (a.s) then continued) “And frequently say in your day and your night: ‘O’ Allah (swt), curse the rejecters, the breakers (of the covenant), the distorters, and those who deny the Day of Judgment from the first to the last. O’ Allah (swt), to You (azj) belongs all praise for Your favor upon us, in guiding us to guardianship of the authorities over our affairs, after Your Prophet (saws), the guiding and rightly-guided Imams (a.s), those whom You (azj) have made pillars of Your oneness, banners of guidance, beacons of piety, the firmest handhold, the perfection of Your religion, and the completion of Your favor. So to You (azj) belongs all praise. We have believed in You (azj), affirmed Your Prophet (saws), followed after him the warner and one who gives warning, allied ourselves with his guardian, opposed his enemy, and disassociated ourselves from the rejecters, the breakers, and the deniers until the Day of Judgement. O’ Allah (swt), just as is Your way, O’ You (azj) who are true to Your promise, O’ You (azj) who ‘never break Your promise.’ (Surah Al Imran 3:9)” O’ You (azj) who, every day, are in a new affair, You (azj) who bestowed upon us the favor of loyalty to Your friends, the very loyalty about which Your servants will be questioned. For indeed You (azj) said and Your word is the truth: ‘Then, on that Day, you shall surely be questioned about the blessing.’ (Surah At-Takathur 102:8) And You (azj) said: ‘And stop them, for indeed they will be questioned.’ (Surah As-Saffat 37:24) And You (azj) have granted us the favor of bearing witness to the sincerity of loyalty to You (azj), through devotion to Your guiding friends after the warner who warned, and the radiant lamp. And You (azj) perfected the religion through their loyalty and disassociation from their enemies, And completed Your blessing upon us, the same blessing by which You (azj) renewed Your covenant with us, And reminded us of Your pledge, which was taken from us at the beginning of our creation. And You (azj) made us among those who responded, And You (azj) reminded us of the covenant and the pledge, And You (azj) did not cause us to forget Your remembrance. For indeed You (azj) said: ‘And (mention) when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their loins their descendants and made them testify about themselves: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes, we bear witness.’ (Surah Al-A’raf 7:172) O’ Allah (swt), yes we have borne witness, by Your grace and Your kindness, that indeed You (azj) are Allah (swt), there is no God but You (azj), our Lord (azj); And Muhammad (saws) is Your servant and Your Messenger (saws), our Prophet (saws); And Imam Ali (a.s) is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), the supreme proof, Your greatest sign, and the tremendous announcement ‘about which they differ.’ (Surah An-Naba’ 78:3) O’ Allah (swt), just as it has been Your way, that You (azj) bestowed upon us the guidance to know them, let it be of Your way to send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), And to bless for us this day of ours the day on which You (azj) reminded us of Your covenant and Your pledge, And perfected our religion, And completed Your blessing upon us, And made us among the people of response and sincerity in affirming Your oneness, And among the people of faith and affirmation of the guardianship of Your friends, And disassociation from Your enemies and the enemies of Your friends the deniers, those who reject the Day of Judgement. And that You (azj) do not place us among the misguided, nor join us with those who deny the Day of Judgement. And grant us a firm footing of truth with the Prophets, and appoint for us with the righteous a leader, until the Day of Judgement the Day when “every people shall be called by their Imam.” (Surah Al-Isra 17:71) And gather us among the group of the guided and rightly guided ones, and let us live for as long as You (azj) give us life, upon loyalty to Your covenant and Your pledge, which was taken from us and upon us for You (azj). And make for us a path with the Messenger (saws), and establish for us a firm footing of truth in emigration (hijrah). O’ Allah (swt), make our life the best of lives, and our death the best of deaths, and our return, the best of returns, until You (azj) take us to Yourself while You (azj) are pleased with us. And You (azj) have made obligatory for us entrance into Your Paradise by Your mercy, and abiding in Your abode, And returning to the place of permanence by Your bounty “wherein no fatigue shall touch us, and no weariness shall touch us.” (Surah Fatir 35:35) Our Lord (azj), indeed You (azj) have commanded us to obey the guardians of Your command, and You (azj) have commanded us to be with the truthful, as You (azj) said: ‘Obey Allah (swt) and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you,’ (Surah An-Nisa 4:59) And You (azj) said: “Fear Allah (swt) and be with the truthful.” (Surah At-Tawbah 9:119) So we have heard and obeyed, our Lord (azj). So ‘make firm our steps’ (Surah Al Imran 3:147) and ‘cause us to die as Muslims,’ (Surah Al-A’raf 7:126) affirming Your friends. And ‘do not cause our hearts to deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself indeed, You are the Bestower.’ (Surah Al Imran 3:8) O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) by the right which You (azj) have placed with them, and by that with which You (azj) have favored them, over all the worlds, that You (azj) bless for us this day of ours, the day in which You (azj) have honored us, And that You (azj) complete Your blessing upon us, and make it a lasting gift for us, never to be taken away, and never make it a temporary deposit. For indeed You (azj) said: “Then, (there is) a place of settlement and a place of deposit.” (Surah Al-An’am 6:98) So make it for us a place of settlement and do not make it a place of deposit. And grant us the victory of Your religion, with a guided and supported guardian from the family of Your Prophet (saws), and place us with him, under his banner, as witnesses and truthful ones in Your path and in the support of Your religion.” (Imam (a.s) then continued) “Then after that, ask for your needs of this world and the Hereafter for by Allah (swt), they are surely granted on this day.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِيُّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُوسَى اَلْهَمْدَانِيُّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ حَسَّانَ اَلْوَاسِطِيُّ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ اَلْعَبْدِيُّ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلصَّادِقَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« صِيَامُ يَوْمِ غَدِيرِ خُمٍّ يَعْدِلُ صِيَامَ عُمُرِ اَلدُّنْيَا لَوْ عَاشَ إِنْسَانٌ ثُمَّ صَامَ مَا عَمَرَتِ اَلدُّنْيَا لَكَانَ لَهُ ثَوَابُ ذَلِكَ وَ صِيَامُهُ يَعْدِلُ عِنْدَ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِي كُلِّ عَامٍ مِائَةَ حَجَّةٍ وَ مِائَةَ عُمْرَةٍ مَبْرُورَاتٍ مُتَقَبَّلاَتٍ وَ هُوَ عِيدُ اَللَّهِ اَلْأَكْبَرُ وَ مَا بَعَثَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ نَبِيّاً قَطُّ إِلاَّ وَ تَعَيَّدَ فِي هَذَا اَلْيَوْمِ وَ عَرَفَ حُرْمَتَهُ وَ اِسْمُهُ فِي اَلسَّمَاءِ يَوْمُ اَلْعَهْدِ اَلْمَعْهُودِ وَ فِي اَلْأَرْضِ يَوْمُ اَلْمِيثَاقِ اَلْمَأْخُوذِ وَ اَلْجَمْعِ اَلْمَشْهُودِ مَنْ صَلَّى فِيهِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ يَغْتَسِلُ عِنْدَ زَوَالِ اَلشَّمْسِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَزُولَ مِقْدَارَ نِصْفِ سَاعَةٍ يَسْأَلُ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقْرَأُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ سُورَةَ اَلْحَمْدِ مَرَّةً وَ عَشْرَ مَرَّاتٍ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ عَشْرَ مَرَّاتٍ آيَةَ اَلْكُرْسِيِّ وَ عَشْرَ مَرَّاتٍ« إِنّٰا أَنْزَلْنٰاهُ» عَدَلَتْ عِنْدَ اَللَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ مِائَةَ أَلْفِ حَجَّةٍ وَمِائَةَ أَلْفِ عُمْرَةٍ وَمَا سَأَلَ اَللَّهَ عَزَّوَجَلَّ حَاجَةً مِنْ حَوَائِجِ اَلدُّنْيَا وَ حَوَائِجِ اَلْآخِرَةِ إِلاَّ قُضِيَتْ كَائِنَةً مَا كَانَتِ اَلْحَاجَةُ وَ إِنْ فَاتَتْكَ اَلرَّكْعَتَانِ وَ اَلدُّعَاءُ قَضَيْتَهُمَا بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ وَ مَنْ فَطَّرَ فِيهِ مُؤْمِناً كَانَ كَمَنْ أَطْعَمَ فِئَاماً وَ فِئَاماً وَ فِئَاماً فَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَعُدُّ إِلَى أَنْ عَقَدَ بِيَدِهِ عَشْراً» ثُمَّ قَالَ« أَتَدْرِي كَمِ اَلْفِئَامُ» قُلْتُ لاَ قَالَ« مِائَةُ أَلْفٍ كُلُّ فِئَامٍ كَانَ لَهُ ثَوَابُ مَنْ أَطْعَمَ بِعَدَدِهَا« مِنَ اَلنَّبِيِّينَ وَاَلصِّدِّيقِينَ وَ اَلشُّهَدٰاءِ» فِي حَرَمِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ سَقَاهُمْ« فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ» وَ اَلدِّرْهَمُ فِيهِ بِأَلْفِ أَلْفِ دِرْهَمٍ» قَالَ« لَعَلَّكَ تَرَى أَنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ خَلَقَ يَوْماً أَعْظَمَ حُرْمَةً مِنْهُ لاَ وَ اَللَّهِ لاَ وَ اَللَّهِ لاَ وَ اَللَّهِ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« وَ لْيَكُنْ مِنْ قَوْلِكُمْ إِذَا اِلْتَقَيْتُمْ أَنْ تَقُولُوا اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي أَكْرَمَنَا بِهَذَا اَلْيَوْمِ وَجَعَلَنَا مِنَ اَلْمُوفِينَ بِعَهْدِهِ إِلَيْنَا وَمِيثَاقِهِ اَلَّذِي وَاثَقَنَا بِهِ مِنْ وَلاَيَةِ وُلاَةِ أَمْرِهِ وَاَلْقُوَّامِ بِقِسْطِهِ وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنَا مِنَ اَلْجَاحِدِينَ وَاَلْمُكَذِّبِينَ بِيَوْمِ اَلدِّينِ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« وَلْيَكُنْ مِنْ دُعَائِكَ فِي دُبُرِ هَاتَيْنِ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ أَنْ تَقُولَ« رَبَّنٰا إِنَّنٰا سَمِعْنٰا مُنٰادِياً يُنٰادِي لِلْإِيمٰانِ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ فَآمَنّٰا رَبَّنٰا فَاغْفِرْ لَنٰا ذُنُوبَنٰا وَ كَفِّرْ عَنّٰا سَيِّئٰاتِنٰا وَ تَوَفَّنٰا مَعَ اَلْأَبْرٰارِ` رَبَّنٰا وَ آتِنٰا مٰا وَعَدْتَنٰا عَلىٰ رُسُلِكَ وَلاٰ تُخْزِنٰا يَوْمَ اَلْقِيٰامَةِ إِنَّكَ لاٰ تُخْلِفُ اَلْمِيعٰادَ» ثُمَّ تَقُولُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أُشْهِدُكَ وَ كَفَى بِكَ شَهِيداً وَ أُشْهِدُ مَلاَئِكَتَكَ وَ حَمَلَةَ عَرْشِكَ وَ سُكَّانَ سَمَاوَاتِكَ وَ أَرْضِكَ بِأَنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَللَّهُ اَلَّذِي لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ اَلْمَعْبُودُ اَلَّذِي لَيْسَ مِنْ لَدُنْ عَرْشِكَ إِلَى قَرَارِ أَرْضِكَ مَعْبُودٌ يُعْبَدُ سِوَاكَ إِلاَّ بَاطِلٌ مُضْمَحِلٌّ غَيْرُ وَجْهِكَ اَلْكَرِيمِ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ اَلْمَعْبُودُ فَلاَ مَعْبُودَ سِوَاكَ تَعَالَيْتَ عَمَّا يَقُولُ اَلظَّالِمُونَ عُلُوّاً كَبِيراً وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ عَبْدُكَ وَ رَسُولُكَ وَ أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ عَلِيّاً صَلَوَاتُُ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ وَلِيُّهُمْ وَ مَوْلاَهُمْ رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا بِالنِّدَاءِ وَ صَدَّقْنَا اَلْمُنَادِيَ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِذَا نَادَى بِنِدَاءٍ عَنْكَ بِالَّذِي أَمَرْتَهُ بِهِ أَنْ يُبَلِّغَ مَا أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ وَلاَيَةِ وَلِيِّ أَمْرِكَ فَحَذَّرْتَهُ وَ أَنْذَرْتَهُ إِنْ لَمْ يُبَلِّغْ أَنْ تَسْخَطَ عَلَيْهِ وَ أَنَّهُ إِنْ بَلَّغَ رِسَالاَتِكَ عَصَمْتَهُ مِنَ اَلنَّاسِ فَنَادَى مُبَلِّغاً وَحْيَكَ وَ رِسَالاَتِكَ أَلاَ مَنْ كُنْتُ مَوْلاَهُ فَعَلِيٌّ مَوْلاَهُ وَ مَنْ كُنْتُ وَلِيَّهُ فَعَلِيٌّ وَلِيُّهُ وَ مَنْ كُنْتُ نَبِيَّهُ فَعَلِيٌّ أَمِيرُهُ رَبَّنَا فَقَدْ أَجَبْنَا دَاعِيَكَ اَلنَّذِيرَ اَلْمُنْذِرَ مُحَمَّداً صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ عَبْدَكَ وَ رَسُولَكَ إِلَى عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ اَلَّذِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ وَ جَعَلْتَهُ مَثَلاً لِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ إِنَّهُ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ مَوْلاَهُمْ وَ وَلِيُّهُمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ اَلْقِيَامَةِ يَوْمِ اَلدِّينِ فَإِنَّكَ قُلْتَ« إِنْ هُوَ إِلاّٰ عَبْدٌ أَنْعَمْنٰا عَلَيْهِ وَ جَعَلْنٰاهُ مَثَلاً لِبَنِي إِسْرٰائِيلَ» رَبَّنَا آمَنَّا وَ اِتَّبَعْنَا مَوْلاَنَا وَ وَلِيَّنَا وَ هَادِيَنَا وَ دَاعِيَنَا وَ دَاعِيَ اَلْأَنَامِ وَ صِرَاطَكَ اَلْمُسْتَقِيمَ اَلسَّوِيَّ وَ حُجَّتَكَ وَ سَبِيلَكَ اَلدَّاعِيَ إِلَيْكَ عَلَى بَصِيرَةٍ هُوَ وَ مَنِ اِتَّبَعَهُ وَ« سُبْحٰانَ اَللّٰهِ عَمّٰا يُشْرِكُونَ» بِوَلاَيَتِهِ وَ بِمَا يُلْحِدُونَ بِاتِّخَاذِ اَلْوَلاَئِجِ دُونَهُ فَأَشْهَدُ يَا إِلَهِي أَنَّهُ اَلْإِمَامُ اَلْهَادِي اَلْمُرْشِدُ اَلرَّشِيدُ عَلِيٌّ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ اَلَّذِي ذَكَرْتَهُ فِي كِتَابِكَ فَقُلْتَ« وَ إِنَّهُ فِي أُمِّ اَلْكِتٰابِ لَدَيْنٰا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ» لاَ أُشْرِكُ مَعَهُ إِمَاماً وَ لاَ أَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِهِ وَلِيجَةً اَللَّهُمَّ فَإِنَّا نَشْهَدُ أَنَّهُ عَبْدُكَ اَلْهَادِي مِنْ بَعْدِ نَبِيِّكَ اَلنَّذِيرُ اَلْمُنْذِرُ وَ صِرَاطُكَ اَلْمُسْتَقِيمُ وَأَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَقَائِدُ اَلْغُرِّ اَلْمُحَجَّلِينَ وَ حُجَّتُكَ اَلْبَالِغَةُ وَ لِسَانُكَ اَلْمُعَبِّرُ عَنْكَ فِي خَلْقِكَ وَ اَلْقَائِمُ بِالْقِسْطِ مِنْ بَعْدِ نَبِيِّكَ وَ دَيَّانُ دِينِكَ وَ خَازِنُ عِلْمِكَ وَ مَوْضِعُ سِرِّكَ وَ عَيْبَةُ عِلْمِكَ وَ أَمِينُكَ اَلْمَأْمُونُ اَلْمَأْخُوذُ مِيثَاقُهُ مَعَ مِيثَاقِ رَسُولِكَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ مِنْ جَمِيعِ خَلْقِكَ وَ بَرِيَّتِكَ شَهَادَةً بِالْإِخْلاَصِ لَكَ بِالْوَحْدَانِيَّةِ بِأَنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَللَّهُ اَلَّذِي لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ وَ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً عَبْدُكَ وَ رَسُولُكَ وَ عَلِيّاً أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ أَنَّ اَلْإِقْرَارَ بِوَلاَيَتِهِ تَمَامُ تَوْحِيدِكَ وَ اَلْإِخْلاَصُ بِوَحْدَانِيَّتِكَ وَ كَمَالُ دِينِكَ وَ تَمَامُ نِعْمَتِكَ وَ فَضْلِكَ عَلَى جَمِيعِ خَلْقِكَ وَ بَرِيَّتِكَ فَإِنَّكَ قُلْتَ وَ قَوْلُكَ اَلْحَقُّ« اَلْيَوْمَ أَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِينَكُمْ وَ أَتْمَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعْمَتِي وَ رَضِيتُ لَكُمُ اَلْإِسْلاٰمَ دِيناً» اَللَّهُمَّ فَلَكَ اَلْحَمْدُ عَلَى مَا مَنَنْتَ بِهِ عَلَيْنَا مِنَ اَلْإِخْلاَصِ لَكَ بِوَحْدَانِيَّتِكَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا لِمُوَالاَةِ وَلِيِّكَ اَلْهَادِي مِنْ بَعْدِ نَبِيِّكَ اَلْمُنْذِرِ وَ رَضِيتَ لَنَا اَلْإِسْلاَمَ دِيناً بِمُوَالاَتِهِ وَ أَتْمَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا نِعْمَتَكَ اَلَّتِي جَدَّدْتَ لَنَا عَهْدَكَ وَ مِيثَاقَكَ وَ ذَكَّرْتَنَا ذَلِكَ وَ جَعَلْتَنَا مِنْ أَهْلِ اَلْإِخْلاَصِ وَ اَلتَّصْدِيقِ بِعَهْدِكَ وَ مِيثَاقِكَ وَ مِنْ أَهْلِ اَلْوَفَاءِ بِذَلِكَ وَ لَمْ تَجْعَلْنَا مِنَ اَلنَّاكِثِينَ وَ اَلْجَاحِدِينَ وَ اَلْمُكَذِّبِينَ بِيَوْمِ اَلدِّينِ وَ لَمْ تَجْعَلْنَا مِنْ أَتْبَاعِ اَلْمُغَيِّرِينَ وَ اَلْمُبَدِّلِينَ وَ اَلْمُنْحَرِفِينَ وَ اَلْمُبَتِّكِينَ آذَانَ اَلْأَنْعَامِ وَ اَلْمُغَيِّرِينَ خَلْقَ اَللَّهِ وَ مِنَ اَلَّذِينَ« اِسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلشَّيْطٰانُ فَأَنْسٰاهُمْ ذِكْرَ اَللّٰهِ» وَ صَدَّهُمْ عَنِ اَلسَّبِيلِ وَ عَنِ اَلصِّرَاطِ اَلْمُسْتَقِيمِ وَ أَكْثِرْ مِنْ قَوْلِكَ فِي يَوْمِكَ وَ لَيْلَتِكَ أَنْ تَقُولَ اَللَّهُمَّ اِلْعَنِ اَلْجَاحِدِينَ وَاَلنَّاكِثِينَ وَاَلْمُغَيِّرِينَ وَاَلْمُكَذِّبِينَ بِيَوْمِ اَلدِّينِ مِنَ اَلْأَوَّلِينَ وَاَلْآخِرِينَ اَللَّهُمَّ فَلَكَ اَلْحَمْدُ عَلَى إِنْعَامِكَ عَلَيْنَا بِالَّذِي هَدَيْتَنَا إِلَى وَلاَيَةِ وُلاَةِ أَمْرِكَ مِنْ بَعْدِ نَبِيِّكَ اَلْأَئِمَّةِ اَلْهُدَاةِ اَلرَّاشِدِينَ اَلَّذِينَ جَعَلْتَهُمْ أَرْكَاناً لِتَوْحِيدِكَ وَ أَعْلاَمَ اَلْهُدَى وَ مَنَارَ اَلتَّقْوَى وَ اَلْعُرْوَةَ اَلْوُثْقَى وَ كَمَالَ دِينِكَ وَ تَمَامَ نِعْمَتِكَ فَلَكَ اَلْحَمْدُ آمَنَّا بِكَ وَ صَدَّقْنَا بِنَبِيِّكَ وَ اِتَّبَعْنَا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ اَلنَّذِيرَ اَلْمُنْذِرَ وَ وَالَيْنَا وَلِيَّهُمْ وَ عَادَيْنَا عَدُوَّهُمْ وَ بَرِئْنَا مِنَ اَلْجَاحِدِينَ وَ اَلنَّاكِثِينَ وَ اَلْمُكَذِّبِينَ إِلَى يَوْمِ اَلدِّينِ اَللَّهُمَّ فَكَمَا كَانَ مِنْ شَأْنِكَ يَا صَادِقَ اَلْوَعْدِ يَا مَنْ« لاٰ يُخْلِفُ اَلْمِيعٰادَ» يَا مَنْ هُوَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ فِي شَأْنٍ أَنْ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا بِمُوَالاَةِ أَوْلِيَائِكَ اَلْمَسْئُولِ عَنْهَا عِبَادُكَ فَإِنَّكَ قُلْتَ وَ قَوْلُكَ اَلْحَقُّ« ثُمَّ لَتُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ اَلنَّعِيمِ» وَ قُلْتَ« وَ قِفُوهُمْ إِنَّهُمْ مَسْؤُلُونَ» وَ مَنَنْتَ عَلَيْنَا بِشَهَادَةِ اَلْإِخْلاَصِ لَكَ بِمُوَالاَةِ أَوْلِيَائِكَ اَلْهُدَاةِ مِنْ بَعْدِ اَلنَّذِيرِ اَلْمُنْذِرِ وَ اَلسِّرَاجِ اَلْمُنِيرِ وَ أَكْمَلْتَ اَلدِّينَ بِمُوَالاَتِهِمْ وَ اَلْبَرَاءَةِ مِنْ عَدُوِّهِمْ وَ أَتْمَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا اَلنِّعْمَةَ اَلَّتِي جَدَّدْتَ لَنَا عَهْدَكَ وَ ذَكَّرْتَنَا مِيثَاقَكَ اَلْمَأْخُوذَ مِنَّا فِي مُبْتَدَإِ خَلْقِكَ إِيَّانَا وَجَعَلْتَنَا مِنْ أَهْلِ اَلْإِجَابَةِ وَ ذَكَّرْتَنَا اَلْعَهْدَ وَاَلْمِيثَاقَ وَ لَمْ تُنْسِنَا ذِكْرَكَ فَإِنَّكَ قُلْتَ« وَ إِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَنِي آدَمَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَ أَشْهَدَ هُمْ عَلىٰ أَنْفُسِهِمْ أَ لَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قٰالُوا بَلىٰ» اَللَّهُمَّ بَلَى شَهِدْنَا بِمَنِّكَ وَ لُطْفِكَ بِأَنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَللَّهُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ رَبُّنَا وَ مُحَمَّدٌ عَبْدُكَ وَ رَسُولُكَ نَبِيُّنَا وَ عَلِيٌّ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ اَلْحُجَّةُ اَلْعُظْمَى وَ آيَتُكَ اَلْكُبْرَى وَ اَلنَّبَأُ اَلْعَظِيمُ« اَلَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ» اَللَّهُمَّ فَكَمَا كَانَ مِنْ شَأْنِكَ أَنْ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا بِالْهِدَايَةِ إِلَى مَعْرِفَتِهِمْ فَلْيَكُنْ مِنْ شَأْنِكَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَنْ تُبَارِكَ لَنَا فِي يَوْمِنَا هَذَا اَلَّذِي ذَكَّرْتَنَا فِيهِ عَهْدَكَ وَ مِيثَاقَكَ وَ أَكْمَلْتَ دِينَنَا وَ أَتْمَمْتَ عَلَيْنَا نِعْمَتَكَ وَ جَعَلْتَنَا مِنْ أَهْلِ اَلْإِجَابَةِ وَ اَلْإِخْلاَصِ بِوَحْدَانِيَّتِكَ وَ مِنْ أَهْلِ اَلْإِيمَانِ وَ اَلتَّصْدِيقِ بِوَلاَيَةِ أَوْلِيَائِكَ وَ اَلْبَرَاءَةِ مِنْ أَعْدَائِكَ وَ أَعْدَاءِ أَوْلِيَائِكَ اَلْجَاحِدِينَ اَلْمُكَذِّبِينَ بِيَوْمِ اَلدِّينِ وَ أَنْ لاَ تَجْعَلَنَا مِنَ اَلْغَاوِينَ وَ لاَ تُلْحِقَنَا بِالْمُكَذِّبِينَ بِيَوْمِ اَلدِّينِ وَ اِجْعَلْ لَنَا قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ مَعَ اَلنَّبِيِّينَ وَ تَجْعَلُ لَنَا مَعَ اَلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَاماً إِلَى يَوْمِ اَلدِّينِ يَوْمَ يُدْعَى كُلُّ« أُنٰاسٍ بِإِمٰامِهِمْ» وَاُحْشُرْنَا فِي زُمْرَةِ اَلْهُدَاةِ اَلْمَهْدِيِّينَ وَ أَحْيِنَا مَا أَحْيَيْتَنَا عَلَى اَلْوَفَاءِ بِعَهْدِكَ وَ مِيثَاقِكَ اَلْمَأْخُوذِ مِنَّا وَ عَلَيْنَا لَكَ وَ اِجْعَلْ لَنَا مَعَ اَلرَّسُولِ سَبِيلاً وَ ثَبِّتْ لَنَا قَدَمَ صِدْقٍ فِي اَلْهِجْرَةِ اَللَّهُمَّ وَ اِجْعَلْ مَحْيَانَا خَيْرَ اَلْمَحْيَا وَ مَمَاتَنَا خَيْرَ اَلْمَمَاتِ وَ مُنْقَلَبَنَا خَيْرَ اَلْمُنْقَلَبِ حَتَّى تَوَفَّانَا وَ أَنْتَ عَنَّا رَاضٍ قَدْ أَوْجَبْتَ لَنَا حُلُولَ جَنَّتِكَ بِرَحْمَتِكَ وَ اَلْمَثْوَى فِي دَارِكَ وَ اَلْإِنَابَةَ إِلَى دَارِ اَلْمُقَامَةِ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ« لاٰ يَمَسُّنٰا فِيهٰا نَصَبٌ وَ لاٰ يَمَسُّنٰا فِيهٰا لُغُوبٌ» رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ أَمَرْتَنَا بِطَاعَةِ وُلاَةِ أَمْرِكَ وَ أَمَرْتَنَا أَنْ نَكُونَ مَعَ اَلصَّادِقِينَ فَقُلْتَ« أَطِيعُوا اَللّٰهَ وَ أَطِيعُوا اَلرَّسُولَ وَ أُولِي اَلْأَمْرِ مِنْكُمْ» وَ قُلْتَ« اِتَّقُوا اَللّٰهَ وَ كُونُوا مَعَ اَلصّٰادِقِينَ» فَسَمِعْنَا وَ أَطَعْنَا رَبَّنَا فَ«ثَبِّتْ أَقْدٰامَنٰا» وَ «تَوَفَّنٰا مُسْلِمِينَ» مُصَدِّقِينَ لِأَوْلِيَائِكَ وَ «لاٰ تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنٰا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنٰا وَ هَبْ لَنٰا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَلْوَهّٰابُ» اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ بِالْحَقِّ اَلَّذِي جَعَلْتَهُ عِنْدَهُمْ وَ بِالَّذِي فَضَّلْتَهُمْ عَلَى اَلْعَالَمِينَ جَمِيعاً أَنْ تُبَارِكَ لَنَا فِي يَوْمِنَا هَذَا اَلَّذِي أَكْرَمْتَنَا فِيهِ وَأَنْ تُتِمَّ عَلَيْنَا نِعْمَتَكَ وَ تَجْعَلَهُ عِنْدَنَا مُسْتَقَرّاً وَ لاَ تَسْلُبَنَاهُ أَبَداً وَ لاَ تَجْعَلَهُ مُسْتَوْدَعاً فَإِنَّكَ قُلْتَ «فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ وَ مُسْتَوْدَعٌ فَاجْعَلْهُ مُسْتَقَرّاً وَ لاَ تَجْعَلْهُ مُسْتَوْدَعاً وَ اُرْزُقْنَا نَصْرَ دِينِكَ مَعَ وَلِيٍّ هَادٍ مَنْصُورٍ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَيْتِ نَبِيِّكَ وَ اِجْعَلْنَا مَعَهُ وَ تَحْتَ رَايَتِهِ شُهَدَاءَ صِدِّيقِينَ فِي سَبِيلِكَ وَ عَلَى نُصْرَةِ دِينِكَ ثُمَّ تَسْأَلُ بَعْدَهَا حَاجَتَكَ لِلدُّنْيَا وَ اَلْآخِرَةِ فَإِنَّهَا وَ اَللَّهِ مَقْضِيَّةٌ فِي هَذَا اَلْيَوْمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Husayni said: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Hamadhani narrated to us; he said: Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti narrated to us; he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Abdi narrated to us; he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Aba Abdillah al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Fasting on the day of Ghadir Khumm, equals the fasting of the lifetime of the world, if a person were to live and fast for as long as the world lasts, the reward of that would be for him. And its fasting equals, in the sight of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, in every year, one hundred accepted Hajj and one hundred accepted Umrah. And it is the greatest Eid of Allah (swt), and Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has never sent any prophet except that he celebrated Eid on this day, recognized its sanctity, and knew its name. In the heavens it is called the ‘Day of the Promised Covenant’, and on the earth it is the ‘Day of the Taken Pledge’ and the ‘Witnessed Gathering’. Whoever prays two rak‘ahs on this day having performed ghusl (ritual bathing) at the time of the sun's zenith, half an hour before it begins to decline and supplicates to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and in each rak‘ah recites Surah al-Hamd (once), and ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) ten times, and Ayat al-Kursi (ten times), and ‘Inna anzalnahu’ (ten times); it would equal, in the sight of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, one hundred thousand Hajj and one hundred thousand Umrah. And he would not ask Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, for any need from among the needs of this world or the Hereafter, except that it would be fulfilled whatever that need may be. And if you missed the two rak’ahs and the supplication, you may perform them later. And whoever gives iftar (breaks the fast) of a believer on this day, it would be as if he had fed an army, and an army, and an army (and Imam (a.s) kept counting until he reached ten with his hand).” Then Imam (a.s) said: “Do you know how many are in an army (fiam)?” I said: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “One hundred thousand. Each army would carry the reward of one who fed the same number from among the Prophets, the Truthful, and the Martyrs in the Sacred Sanctuary of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, and gave them drink ‘on a day of severe hunger’. And a dirham (spent) on this day is equal to a million dirhams.” Imam (a.s) said: “Perhaps you think that Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has created a day more sacred than this? No, by Allah (swt)! No, by Allah (swt)! No, by Allah (swt)!” Then Imam (a.s) said: “And let it be from your words when you meet one another that you say: ‘All praise is due to Allah (swt), who honoured us with this day and made us among those who fulfill His (azj) covenant with us, and His (azj) pledge which He (azj) bound us to concerning the guardianship of the leaders of His (azj) command and the ones who uphold His (azj) justice and did not make us among the deniers and rejecters of the Day of Judgement.’” Then Imam (a.s) said: “And let it be from your supplication after these two rak’ahs that you say: ‘Our Lord (azj), indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, saying: ‘Believe in your Lord (azj),’ so we believed. Our Lord (azj), forgive us our sins, and expiate from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous. Our Lord (azj), and grant us what You (azj) promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You (azj) do not break the promise.’” (Imam (a.s) then continued) “Then you say after that; ‘O’ Allah (swt), I call You (azj) to witness and You (azj) are sufficient as a witness and I call to witness Your angels, the bearers of Your Throne, the inhabitants of Your heavens and Your earth, that indeed You (azj) are Allah (swt), there is no God but You (azj), the One to be worshipped. There is no being from beneath Your Throne to the depths of Your earth, that is rightfully worshipped besides You (azj); anything else that is worshipped is false and perishing, apart from Your Noble Face. There is no God but You (azj), the One to be worshipped; so none is worthy of worship besides You (azj). Exalted are You (azj) above what the wrongdoers say, with great exaltation. And I bear witness that (Prophet) Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, is Your servant and Your Messenger (saws). And I bear witness that Imam Ali (a.s), may Allah’s blessings be upon him, is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), and their guardian and their master. Our Lord (azj), indeed we heard the call and believed in the caller the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when he proclaimed a proclamation from You (azj) concerning that which You (azj) commanded him to convey, that he should deliver what had been revealed to him regarding the guardianship of the authority-holder appointed by You (azj). And You (azj) warned him and threatened him that if he did not convey it, You (azj) would be displeased with him. And You (azj) promised him that if he conveyed Your messages, You (azj) would protect him from the people. So He (saws) called out, delivering Your revelation and Your messages: ‘Indeed, whomever I am his master (mawla), then Ali (a.s) is his master; And whomever I am his guardian, then Ali (a.s) is his guardian; And whomever I am his Prophet (saws), then Ali (a.s) is his commander.’ Our Lord (azj), we have responded to Your caller, the warner and one who gave warning, (Prophet) Muhammad (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, Your servant and Your Messenger, to (follow) Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him, the one whom You (azj) favored and made an example for the Children of Israel. Truly, he is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), their master and their guardian until the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Judgement. For indeed You (azj) said: ‘He is but a servant upon whom We bestowed Our favor and made him an example for the Children of Israel.’ (Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:59) Our Lord (azj), we have believed and followed our master, our guardian, our guide, our summoner, the summoner of all creation, And Your straight and upright path, and Your proof, and Your way, the one who calls to You (azj) with clear insight, he and those who follow him. “Glory be to Allah (swt) above what they associate (with Him)” (Surah Al-Tawbah 9:31) by his guardianship and against what they deviate by taking guardians besides him. So I bear witness, O’ my God, that Imam Ali (a.s) is the guiding, directing, And the rightly-guided Imam Ali (a.s), the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), the one You (azj) mentioned in Your Book, when You (azj) said: ‘And indeed it is, in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and full of wisdom.’ (Surah Az-Zukhruf 43:4). I do not associate any Imam alongside him, nor do I take any guardian besides him. O’ Allah (swt), indeed we bear witness that he is Your servant, the guide after Your Prophet (saws), the warner, the one who gives warning, and Your straight path, And the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), the leader of the radiant ones with shining foreheads and limbs, Your conclusive proof, and Your tongue that speaks on Your behalf among Your creation, and the one who upholds justice after Your Prophet (saws), the executor of Your religion, And the keeper of Your knowledge, the place of Your secret, the repository of Your knowledge, and Your trusted trustee, And the one whose covenant was taken along with the covenant of Your Messenger (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, from all of Your creation and beings, A testimony of sincerity to You (azj) in affirming Your oneness; That indeed You are Allah (swt), there is no God but You (azj), and that (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) is Your servant and Your Messenger, and that Imam Ali (a.s) is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s). And that acknowledgment of his guardianship, is the completion of Your tawhid (Divine Unity), and sincerity in Your oneness, And the perfection of Your religion, and the completion of Your favor, and Your bounty upon all of Your creation and beings. For indeed You (azj) said and Your word is the truth: ‘This day I have perfected for you your religion, and completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as your religion.’ (Surah Al-Ma’idah 5:3) O’ Allah (swt), to You (azj) belongs all praise for what You (azj) have bestowed upon us, the sincerity to You (azj) in Your Oneness when You (azj) guided us to the guardianship of Your friend, the guide after Your Prophet (saws), the warner. And You (azj) were pleased for us that Islam be our religion through our loyalty to him, And You (azj) completed upon us Your blessing, that by which You (azj) renewed for us Your covenant and Your pledge, and reminded us of it, And made us among the people of sincerity and affirmation of Your covenant and Your pledge, and among those who fulfill it. And You (azj) did not make us among the breakers (of the covenant), nor among the rejecters, nor among those who deny the Day of Judgement. And You (azj) did not make us among the followers of those who alter and distort, And those who deviate and split, And those who mutilate the ears of cattle, And those who alter the creation of Allah (swt), and among those over whom ‘Satan has taken control, so he made them forget the remembrance of Allah (swt)’ (Surah Al-Mujadilah 58:19), And (Satan) diverted them from the path and from the straight path.” (Imam (a.s) then continued) “And frequently say in your day and your night: ‘O’ Allah (swt), curse the rejecters, the breakers (of the covenant), the distorters, and those who deny the Day of Judgment from the first to the last. O’ Allah (swt), to You (azj) belongs all praise for Your favor upon us, in guiding us to guardianship of the authorities over our affairs, after Your Prophet (saws), the guiding and rightly-guided Imams (a.s), those whom You (azj) have made pillars of Your oneness, banners of guidance, beacons of piety, the firmest handhold, the perfection of Your religion, and the completion of Your favor. So to You (azj) belongs all praise. We have believed in You (azj), affirmed Your Prophet (saws), followed after him the warner and one who gives warning, allied ourselves with his guardian, opposed his enemy, and disassociated ourselves from the rejecters, the breakers, and the deniers until the Day of Judgement. O’ Allah (swt), just as is Your way, O’ You (azj) who are true to Your promise, O’ You (azj) who ‘never break Your promise.’ (Surah Al Imran 3:9)” O’ You (azj) who, every day, are in a new affair, You (azj) who bestowed upon us the favor of loyalty to Your friends, the very loyalty about which Your servants will be questioned. For indeed You (azj) said and Your word is the truth: ‘Then, on that Day, you shall surely be questioned about the blessing.’ (Surah At-Takathur 102:8) And You (azj) said: ‘And stop them, for indeed they will be questioned.’ (Surah As-Saffat 37:24) And You (azj) have granted us the favor of bearing witness to the sincerity of loyalty to You (azj), through devotion to Your guiding friends after the warner who warned, and the radiant lamp. And You (azj) perfected the religion through their loyalty and disassociation from their enemies, And completed Your blessing upon us, the same blessing by which You (azj) renewed Your covenant with us, And reminded us of Your pledge, which was taken from us at the beginning of our creation. And You (azj) made us among those who responded, And You (azj) reminded us of the covenant and the pledge, And You (azj) did not cause us to forget Your remembrance. For indeed You (azj) said: ‘And (mention) when your Lord took from the children of Adam from their loins their descendants and made them testify about themselves: ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes, we bear witness.’ (Surah Al-A’raf 7:172) O’ Allah (swt), yes we have borne witness, by Your grace and Your kindness, that indeed You (azj) are Allah (swt), there is no God but You (azj), our Lord (azj); And Muhammad (saws) is Your servant and Your Messenger (saws), our Prophet (saws); And Imam Ali (a.s) is the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), the supreme proof, Your greatest sign, and the tremendous announcement ‘about which they differ.’ (Surah An-Naba’ 78:3) O’ Allah (swt), just as it has been Your way, that You (azj) bestowed upon us the guidance to know them, let it be of Your way to send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), And to bless for us this day of ours the day on which You (azj) reminded us of Your covenant and Your pledge, And perfected our religion, And completed Your blessing upon us, And made us among the people of response and sincerity in affirming Your oneness, And among the people of faith and affirmation of the guardianship of Your friends, And disassociation from Your enemies and the enemies of Your friends the deniers, those who reject the Day of Judgement. And that You (azj) do not place us among the misguided, nor join us with those who deny the Day of Judgement. And grant us a firm footing of truth with the Prophets, and appoint for us with the righteous a leader, until the Day of Judgement the Day when “every people shall be called by their Imam.” (Surah Al-Isra 17:71) And gather us among the group of the guided and rightly guided ones, and let us live for as long as You (azj) give us life, upon loyalty to Your covenant and Your pledge, which was taken from us and upon us for You (azj). And make for us a path with the Messenger (saws), and establish for us a firm footing of truth in emigration (hijrah). O’ Allah (swt), make our life the best of lives, and our death the best of deaths, and our return, the best of returns, until You (azj) take us to Yourself while You (azj) are pleased with us. And You (azj) have made obligatory for us entrance into Your Paradise by Your mercy, and abiding in Your abode, And returning to the place of permanence by Your bounty “wherein no fatigue shall touch us, and no weariness shall touch us.” (Surah Fatir 35:35) Our Lord (azj), indeed You (azj) have commanded us to obey the guardians of Your command, and You (azj) have commanded us to be with the truthful, as You (azj) said: ‘Obey Allah (swt) and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you,’ (Surah An-Nisa 4:59) And You (azj) said: “Fear Allah (swt) and be with the truthful.” (Surah At-Tawbah 9:119) So we have heard and obeyed, our Lord (azj). So ‘make firm our steps’ (Surah Al Imran 3:147) and ‘cause us to die as Muslims,’ (Surah Al-A’raf 7:126) affirming Your friends. And ‘do not cause our hearts to deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself indeed, You are the Bestower.’ (Surah Al Imran 3:8) O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) by the right which You (azj) have placed with them, and by that with which You (azj) have favored them, over all the worlds, that You (azj) bless for us this day of ours, the day in which You (azj) have honored us, And that You (azj) complete Your blessing upon us, and make it a lasting gift for us, never to be taken away, and never make it a temporary deposit. For indeed You (azj) said: “Then, (there is) a place of settlement and a place of deposit.” (Surah Al-An’am 6:98) So make it for us a place of settlement and do not make it a place of deposit. And grant us the victory of Your religion, with a guided and supported guardian from the family of Your Prophet (saws), and place us with him, under his banner, as witnesses and truthful ones in Your path and in the support of Your religion.” (Imam (a.s) then continued) “Then after that, ask for your needs of this world and the Hereafter for by Allah (swt), they are surely granted on this day.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer for Seeking Rain
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When four things become widespread, four things will appear. When fornication becomes widespread, earthquakes will appear. When zakat is withheld, livestock will perish. When judges act unjustly in rulings, rain from the sky will be withheld. And when the covenant (with God (azj) and His (azj) creation) is violated, the polytheists will be granted victory over the Muslims.”
arabicText: رَوَى عَبْدُ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ كَثِيرٍ عَنِ اَلصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« إِذَا فَشَتْ أَرْبَعَةٌ ظَهَرَتْ أَرْبَعَةٌ إِذَا فَشَا اَلزِّنَا ظَهَرَتِ اَلزَّلاَزِلُ وَ إِذَا أُمْسِكَتِ اَلزَّكَاةُ هَلَكَتِ اَلْمَاشِيَةُ وَ إِذَا جَارَ اَلْحُكَّامُ فِي اَلْقَضَاءِ أُمْسِكَ اَلْقَطْرُ مِنَ اَلسَّمَاءِ وَ إِذَا خُفِرَتِ اَلذِّمَّةُ نُصِرَ اَلْمُشْرِكُونَ عَلَى اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When four things become widespread, four things will appear. When fornication becomes widespread, earthquakes will appear. When zakat is withheld, livestock will perish. When judges act unjustly in rulings, rain from the sky will be withheld. And when the covenant (with God (azj) and His (azj) creation) is violated, the polytheists will be granted victory over the Muslims.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 161

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer for Seeking Rain
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And it is narrated from the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, that He (saws) said:
Prophet Muhammad (saws) said: “When Allah (swt), the Exalted, becomes angry with a nation, yet does not send punishment upon it, their prices rise, their lifespans become short, their merchants do not profit, their fruits do not increase, their rivers lose sweetness, their rains are withheld, and their wicked ones are given authority over them.”
arabicText: وَ رُوِيَ عَنِ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« إِذَا غَضِبَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَى أُمَّةٍ ثُمَّ لَمْ يُنْزِلْ بِهَا اَلْعَذَابَ غَلَتْ أَسْعَارُهَا وَقَصُرَتْ أَعْمَارُهَا وَ لَمْ تَرْبَحْ تُجَّارُهَا وَ لَمْ تَزْكُ ثِمَارُهَا وَ لَمْ تَعْذُبْ أَنْهَارُهَا وَحُبِسَ عَنْهَا أَمْطَارُهَا وَسُلِّطَ عَلَيْهَا أَشْرَارُهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And it is narrated from the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, that He (saws) said:
thaqalaynMatn: Prophet Muhammad (saws) said: “When Allah (swt), the Exalted, becomes angry with a nation, yet does not send punishment upon it, their prices rise, their lifespans become short, their merchants do not profit, their fruits do not increase, their rivers lose sweetness, their rains are withheld, and their wicked ones are given authority over them.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer for Seeking Rain
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Hammad al-Sarraj:
Muhammad ibn Khalid sent me to Abu Abdillah (a.s), to ask Imam (a.s): “The people have persistently asked me regarding seeking rain (istisqa), what is your opinion about going out tomorrow (to seek rain)?” So I conveyed this to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. Imam (a.s) said: “Say to him (ibn Khalid); This is not how istisqa is to be done. Say to him (ibn Khalid); He should go out and deliver a sermon to the people and command them to fast today and tomorrow and then on the third day, he should go out with them, while they are fasting.” He (al-Sarraj) said: “So I went to Muhammad (ibn Khalid) and informed him of the words of Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. So he (ibn Khalid) went and delivered a sermon to the people and commanded them to fast, just as Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, had said. Then, on the third day, he (ibn Khalid) sent to Imam (a.s) asking: “What is your opinion about going out (today)?”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَمَّادٍ اَلسَّرَّاجِ قَالَ: أَرْسَلَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَقُولُ لَهُ إِنَّ اَلنَّاسَ قَدْ أَكْثَرُوا عَلَيَّ فِي اَلاِسْتِسْقَاءِ فَمَا رَأْيُكَ فِي اَلْخُرُوجِ غَداً فَقُلْتُ ذَلِكَ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ لِي« قُلْ لَهُ لَيْسَ اَلاِسْتِسْقَاءُ هَكَذَا فَقُلْ لَهُ يَخْرُجُ فَيَخْطُبُ اَلنَّاسَ وَ يَأْمُرُهُمْ بِالصِّيَامِ اَلْيَوْمَ وَ غَداً وَ يَخْرُجُ بِهِمُ اَلْيَوْمَ اَلثَّالِثَ وَ هُمْ صِيَامٌ» قَالَ فَأَتَيْتُ مُحَمَّداً فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ بِمَقَالَةِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَجَاءَ فَخَطَبَ اَلنَّاسَ وَأَمَرَهُمْ بِالصِّيَامِ كَمَا قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَلَمَّا كَانَ فِي اَلْيَوْمِ اَلثَّالِثِ أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْهِ مَا رَأْيُكَ فِي اَلْخُرُوجِ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Hammad al-Sarraj:
thaqalaynMatn: Muhammad ibn Khalid sent me to Abu Abdillah (a.s), to ask Imam (a.s): “The people have persistently asked me regarding seeking rain (istisqa), what is your opinion about going out tomorrow (to seek rain)?” So I conveyed this to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. Imam (a.s) said: “Say to him (ibn Khalid); This is not how istisqa is to be done. Say to him (ibn Khalid); He should go out and deliver a sermon to the people and command them to fast today and tomorrow and then on the third day, he should go out with them, while they are fasting.” He (al-Sarraj) said: “So I went to Muhammad (ibn Khalid) and informed him of the words of Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. So he (ibn Khalid) went and delivered a sermon to the people and commanded them to fast, just as Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, had said. Then, on the third day, he (ibn Khalid) sent to Imam (a.s) asking: “What is your opinion about going out (today)?”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer for Seeking Rain
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say regarding istisqa (the prayer for seeking rain); “He prays two rak’ahs, then turns his cloak placing what is on his right side to his left, and what is on his left side to his right and he supplicates to Allah (swt) and seeks rain.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: فِي اَلاِسْتِسْقَاءِ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَقْلِبُ رِدَاءَهُ اَلَّذِي عَلَى يَمِينِهِ فَيَجْعَلُهُ عَلَى يَسَارِهِ وَ اَلَّذِي عَلَى يَسَارِهِ عَلَى يَمِينِهِ وَ يَدْعُو اَللَّهَ فَيَسْتَسْقِي»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan, from Abdillah ibn Bukayr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say regarding istisqa (the prayer for seeking rain); “He prays two rak’ahs, then turns his cloak placing what is on his right side to his left, and what is on his left side to his right and he supplicates to Allah (swt) and seeks rain.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer for Seeking Rain
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, all from Murrah, the mawla (client) of Khalid, who said:
The people of Madinah cried out to Muhammad ibn Khalid concerning istisqa (seeking rain), so Khalid said to me (Murrah): “Go to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and ask Imam (a.s); ‘What is your opinion? For these people have turned to me.’” So I came to Imam (a.s) and conveyed to him what Khalid said to me. Imam (a.s) said to me: “Say to Khalid; ‘Let him go out.’” I asked Imam (a.s): “When should he go out, may I be your ransom?” Imam (a.s) said: “On Monday.” I asked Imam (a.s): “How should he do it?” Imam (a.s) said: “He should bring out the pulpit, then he should go out walking, just as he goes out on the two Eids, with the callers to prayer (mu’adhdhins) going before him, holding their staffs in their hands. When he reaches the place of prayer (musalla), he should lead the people in two rak’ahs, without any adhan or iqamah. Then he should ascend the pulpit and turn his cloak, placing what is on his right side to his left, and what is on his left to his right. Then he should face the qiblah and proclaim ‘Allahu Akbar’ one hundred times, raising his voice with it. Then he should turn to the people on his right and proclaim ‘SubhanAllah’ one hundred times, raising his voice. Then he should turn to the people on his left and proclaim ‘La ilaha illa Allah’ one hundred times, raising his voice. Then he should face the people and praise Allah (swt) (‘Alhamdulillah’) one hundred times. Then he should raise his hands and supplicate, and then the people should supplicate. For indeed, I hope that they will not be disappointed.” He (the narrator) said: “So Khalid did as instructed. And when we returned, the people said: ‘This is from the teachings of Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَامِرٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ جَمِيعاً عَنْ مُرَّةَ مَوْلَى خَالِدٍ قَالَ: صَاحَ أَهْلُ اَلْمَدِينَةِ إِلَى مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ فِي اَلاِسْتِسْقَاءِ فَقَالَ لِي اِنْطَلِقْ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَسَلْهُ مَا رَأْيُكَ فَإِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ قَدْ صَاحُوا إِلَيَّ فَأَتَيْتُهُ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ مَا قَالَ لِي فَقَالَ لِي« قُلْ لَهُ فَلْيَخْرُجْ» قُلْتُ لَهُ مَتَى يَخْرُجُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ قَالَ« يَوْمَ اَلْإِثْنَيْنِ» قُلْتُ لَهُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« يُخْرِجُ اَلْمِنْبَرَ ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُ يَمْشِي كَمَا يَخْرُجُ يَوْمَ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ وَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ اَلْمُؤَذِّنُونَ فِي أَيْدِيهِمْ عَنَزُهُمْ حَتَّى إِذَا اِنْتَهَى إِلَى اَلْمُصَلَّى صَلَّى بِالنَّاسِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ بِلاَ أَذَانٍ وَ لاَ إِقَامَةٍ ثُمَّ يَصْعَدُ اَلْمِنْبَرَ فَيَقْلِبُ رِدَاءَهُ فَيَجْعَلُ اَلَّذِي عَلَى يَمِينِهِ عَلَى يَسَارِهِ وَ اَلَّذِي عَلَى يَسَارِهِ عَلَى يَمِينِهِ ثُمَّ يَسْتَقْبِلُ اَلْقِبْلَةَ فَيُكَبِّرُ اَللَّهَ مِائَةَ تَكْبِيرَةٍ رَافِعاً بِهَا صَوْتَهُ ثُمَّ يَلْتَفِتُ إِلَى اَلنَّاسِ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ فَيُسَبِّحُ اَللَّهَ مِائَةَ تَسْبِيحَةٍ رَافِعاً بِهَا صَوْتَهُ ثُمَّ يَلْتَفِتُ إِلَى اَلنَّاسِ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ فَيُهَلِّلُ اَللَّهَ مِائَةَ تَهْلِيلَةٍ رَافِعاً بِهَا صَوْتَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَقْبِلُ اَلنَّاسَ فَيَحْمَدُ اَللَّهَ مِائَةَ تَحْمِيدَةٍ ثُمَّ يَرْفَعُ يَدَيْهِ فَيَدْعُو ثُمَّ يَدْعُونَ فَإِنِّي لَأَرْجُو أَنْ لاَ يَخِيبُوا» قَالَ فَفَعَلَ فَلَمَّا رَجَعْنَا قَالُوا هَذَا مِنْ تَعْلِيمِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Ahmad ibn Sulayman, all from Murrah, the mawla (client) of Khalid, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The people of Madinah cried out to Muhammad ibn Khalid concerning istisqa (seeking rain), so Khalid said to me (Murrah): “Go to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and ask Imam (a.s); ‘What is your opinion? For these people have turned to me.’” So I came to Imam (a.s) and conveyed to him what Khalid said to me. Imam (a.s) said to me: “Say to Khalid; ‘Let him go out.’” I asked Imam (a.s): “When should he go out, may I be your ransom?” Imam (a.s) said: “On Monday.” I asked Imam (a.s): “How should he do it?” Imam (a.s) said: “He should bring out the pulpit, then he should go out walking, just as he goes out on the two Eids, with the callers to prayer (mu’adhdhins) going before him, holding their staffs in their hands. When he reaches the place of prayer (musalla), he should lead the people in two rak’ahs, without any adhan or iqamah. Then he should ascend the pulpit and turn his cloak, placing what is on his right side to his left, and what is on his left to his right. Then he should face the qiblah and proclaim ‘Allahu Akbar’ one hundred times, raising his voice with it. Then he should turn to the people on his right and proclaim ‘SubhanAllah’ one hundred times, raising his voice. Then he should turn to the people on his left and proclaim ‘La ilaha illa Allah’ one hundred times, raising his voice. Then he should face the people and praise Allah (swt) (‘Alhamdulillah’) one hundred times. Then he should raise his hands and supplicate, and then the people should supplicate. For indeed, I hope that they will not be disappointed.” He (the narrator) said: “So Khalid did as instructed. And when we returned, the people said: ‘This is from the teachings of Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him.’”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer for Seeking Rain
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the prayer of ‘al-Istisqa’ (the prayer for rain). Imam (a.s) said: “It is like the (prayer of) two Eid prayers. In both of them, recitation is done and takbirs are pronounced. The Imam goes out and appears in a clean place with calmness, dignity, humility, and supplication. The people go out with him. Then he praises Allah (swt), glorifies Him (azj), and extols Him (azj), and strives earnestly in supplication and increases in tasbih (‘Subhanallah’), tahlil (‘La ilaha illallah’), and takbir (‘Allahu Akbar’). Then he performs a prayer like the Eid prayer, two rak’ahs with supplication, entreaty, and striving (in prayer). Then when the Imam finishes (with salam), he turns his garment inside out and places the side that was on the right shoulder onto the left shoulder, and the one that was on the left shoulder onto the right shoulder for indeed the Prophet (saws), peace be upon him and his family, did so.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلاِسْتِسْقَاءِ قَالَ« مِثْلُ صَلاَةِ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ يُقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا وَ يُكَبَّرُ فِيهِمَا يَخْرُجُ اَلْإِمَامُ فَيَبْرُزُ إِلَى مَكَانٍ نَظِيفٍ فِي سَكِينَةٍ وَ وَقَارٍ وَ خُشُوعٍ وَ مَسْأَلَةٍ وَ يَبْرُزُ مَعَهُ اَلنَّاسُ فَيَحْمَدُ اَللَّهَ وَ يُمَجِّدُهُ وَ يُثْنِي عَلَيْهِ وَ يَجْتَهِدُ فِي اَلدُّعَاءِ وَ يُكْثِرُ مِنَ اَلتَّسْبِيحِ وَاَلتَّهْلِيلِ وَاَلتَّكْبِيرِ وَ يُصَلِّي مِثْلَ صَلاَةِ اَلْعِيدَيْنِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فِي دُعَاءٍ وَمَسْأَلَةٍ وَاِجْتِهَادٍ فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ اَلْإِمَامُ قَلَبَ ثَوْبَهُ وَ جَعَلَ اَلْجَانِبَ اَلَّذِي عَلَى اَلْمَنْكِبِ اَلْأَيْمَنِ عَلَى اَلْمَنْكِبِ اَلْأَيْسَرِ وَ اَلَّذِي عَلَى اَلْأَيْسَرِ عَلَى اَلْأَيْمَنِ فَإِنَّ اَلنَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ كَذَلِكَ صَنَعَ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the prayer of ‘al-Istisqa’ (the prayer for rain). Imam (a.s) said: “It is like the (prayer of) two Eid prayers. In both of them, recitation is done and takbirs are pronounced. The Imam goes out and appears in a clean place with calmness, dignity, humility, and supplication. The people go out with him. Then he praises Allah (swt), glorifies Him (azj), and extols Him (azj), and strives earnestly in supplication and increases in tasbih (‘Subhanallah’), tahlil (‘La ilaha illallah’), and takbir (‘Allahu Akbar’). Then he performs a prayer like the Eid prayer, two rak’ahs with supplication, entreaty, and striving (in prayer). Then when the Imam finishes (with salam), he turns his garment inside out and places the side that was on the right shoulder onto the left shoulder, and the one that was on the left shoulder onto the right shoulder for indeed the Prophet (saws), peace be upon him and his family, did so.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 163

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer for Seeking Rain
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi, from Muhammad ibn Sufyan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, turning his cloak inside out when He (saws) prayed for rain (istisqa). Imam (a.s) said: “It was a sign between Him (saws) and his companions, by which drought would be turned into abundance.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلصَّيْرَفِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُفْيَانَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ تَحْوِيلِ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ رِدَاءَهُ إِذَا اِسْتَسْقَى قَالَ« عَلاَمَةٌ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ أَصْحَابِهِ يُحَوَّلُ اَلْجَدْبُ خِصْباً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Sayrafi, from Muhammad ibn Sufyan, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, turning his cloak inside out when He (saws) prayed for rain (istisqa). Imam (a.s) said: “It was a sign between Him (saws) and his companions, by which drought would be turned into abundance.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer for Seeking Rain
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
Imam Ali (a.s) said: “The established Sunnah is that the prayer for rain (istisqa) is not performed except in open lands, where people can look towards the sky, and it is not performed in mosques except in Mecca.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« مَضَتِ اَلسُّنَّةُ أَنَّهُ لاَ يُسْتَسْقَى إِلاَّ بِالْبَرَارِي حَيْثُ يَنْظُرُ اَلنَّاسُ إِلَى اَلسَّمَاءِ وَلاَ يُسْتَسْقَى فِي اَلْمَسَاجِدِ إِلاَّ بِمَكَّةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) said: “The established Sunnah is that the prayer for rain (istisqa) is not performed except in open lands, where people can look towards the sky, and it is not performed in mosques except in Mecca.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer for Seeking Rain
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan, who informed me: Musa ibn Bakr or Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed two rak’ahs for al-Istisqa (the prayer for rain), and He (saws) began with the prayer before the sermon. He (saws) pronounced takbir seven times and then five times, and He (saws) recited aloud.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ أَخْبَرَنِي مُوسَى بْنُ بَكْرٍ أَوْ عَبْدُ اَللَّهِ بْنُ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ طَلْحَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ صَلَّى لِلاِسْتِسْقَاءِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ بَدَأَ بِالصَّلاَةِ قَبْلَ اَلْخُطْبَةِ وَ كَبَّرَ سَبْعاً وَ خَمْساً وَ جَهَرَ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Safwan, who informed me: Musa ibn Bakr or Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed two rak’ahs for al-Istisqa (the prayer for rain), and He (saws) began with the prayer before the sermon. He (saws) pronounced takbir seven times and then five times, and He (saws) recited aloud.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer for Seeking Rain
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The sermon in the prayer for rain (al-Istisqa) is before the prayer, and he pronounces takbir seven times in the first rak’ah and five times in the second.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْخُطْبَةُ فِي اَلاِسْتِسْقَاءِ قَبْلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ يُكَبِّرُ فِي اَلْأُولَى سَبْعاً وَ فِي اَلْأُخْرَى خَمْساً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The sermon in the prayer for rain (al-Istisqa) is before the prayer, and he pronounces takbir seven times in the first rak’ah and five times in the second.”
