chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Ala ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them:
Imam (a.s) was asked concerning a man who returns from a journey and the time of prayer enters upon him. Imam (a.s) said: “If he does not fear that the time will end, then let him enter and perform it in full. But if he fears that the time will expire before he enters, then let him pray and shorten (the prayer).”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ رَزِينٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَقْدَمُ مِنَ اَلْغَيْبَةِ فَيَدْخُلُ عَلَيْهِ وَقْتُ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ لاَ يَخَافُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ اَلْوَقْتُ فَلْيَدْخُلْ فَلْيُتِمَّ وَ إِنْ كَانَ يَخَافُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ اَلْوَقْتُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ فَلْيُصَلِّ وَ لْيُقَصِّرْ» فرغب عليه السلام بهذا الخبر في ان من لم يخف فوت الوقت في تأخير الصلاة حتى يدخل البيت يؤخرها حتى يؤديها على التمام فلولا ان فوت الوقت كان مراعى في هذا الباب لم يكن لتقييد الاتمام بهذه الحال معنى
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan ibn Yahya and Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Ala ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked concerning a man who returns from a journey and the time of prayer enters upon him. Imam (a.s) said: “If he does not fear that the time will end, then let him enter and perform it in full. But if he fears that the time will expire before he enters, then let him pray and shorten (the prayer).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 180

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja’far from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “A resident should not lead a traveller in prayer, nor should a traveller lead a resident. But if one is put in a situation where this occurs, and he (the traveller) leads a group of residents in prayer, then when he completes two rak’ahs, he should give salam and then take the hand of one of them and bring him forward to lead them. And if a traveller prays behind a group of residents, he should complete his prayer as two rak’ahs and give salam. And if he prays Dhuhr with them, then let him consider the first two rak’ahs as Dhuhr and the latter two as Asr.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ اَلْحُصَيْنِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْعَبَّاسِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يَؤُمُّ اَلْحَضَرِيُّ اَلْمُسَافِرَ وَ لاَ اَلْمُسَافِرُ اَلْحَضَرِيَّ فَإِنِ اُبْتُلِيَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَأَمَّ قَوْماً حَاضِرِينَ فَإِذَا أَتَمَّ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ سَلَّمَ ثُمَّ أَخَذَ بِيَدِ بَعْضِهِمْ فَقَدَّمَهُ فَأَمَّهُمْ وَإِذَا صَلَّى اَلْمُسَافِرُ خَلْفَ قَوْمٍ حُضُورٍ فَلْيُتِمَّ صَلاَتَهُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يُسَلِّمُ وَ إِنْ صَلَّى مَعَهُمُ اَلظُّهْرَ فَلْيَجْعَلِ اَلْأُولَيَيْنِ اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْأُخْرَيَيْنِ اَلْعَصْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Abu Ja’far from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Dawud ibn al-Husayn from Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “A resident should not lead a traveller in prayer, nor should a traveller lead a resident. But if one is put in a situation where this occurs, and he (the traveller) leads a group of residents in prayer, then when he completes two rak’ahs, he should give salam and then take the hand of one of them and bring him forward to lead them. And if a traveller prays behind a group of residents, he should complete his prayer as two rak’ahs and give salam. And if he prays Dhuhr with them, then let him consider the first two rak’ahs as Dhuhr and the latter two as Asr.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 180

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lului from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abu al-Miza Humayd ibn al-Muthanna from Imran from Muhammad ibn Ali:
(Muhammad ibn Ali) asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a traveller who enters into prayer with residents. Imam (a.s) said: “Let him perform his (own) prayer, then give salam, and make the last two (rak’ahs) supererogatory (nafila) prayer.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ اَللُّؤْلُؤِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْمِعْزَى حُمَيْدِ بْنِ اَلْمُثَنَّى عَنْ عِمْرَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ اَلْمُسَافِرِ إِذَا دَخَلَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ مَعَ اَلْمُقِيمِينَ قَالَ «فَلْيُصَلِّ صَلاَتَهُ ثُمَّ لْيُسَلِّمْ وَ لْيَجْعَلِ اَلْأُخْرَيَيْنِ سُبْحَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lului from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Abu al-Miza Humayd ibn al-Muthanna from Imran from Muhammad ibn Ali:
thaqalaynMatn: (Muhammad ibn Ali) asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a traveller who enters into prayer with residents. Imam (a.s) said: “Let him perform his (own) prayer, then give salam, and make the last two (rak’ahs) supererogatory (nafila) prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 181

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a traveller who prays behind a resident. Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray two rak’ahs and then go wherever he wishes.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمُسَافِرِ يُصَلِّي خَلْفَ اَلْمُقِيمِ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَمْضِي حَيْثُ شَاءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a traveller who prays behind a resident. Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray two rak’ahs and then go wherever he wishes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 181

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Husayn ibn Uthman from Abdillah ibn Muskan from Abu Basir. He said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The traveller should not pray with the resident. But if he does pray, then let him leave after two rak’ahs.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« لاَ يُصَلِّي اَلْمُسَافِرُ مَعَ اَلْمُقِيمِ فَإِنْ صَلَّى فَلْيَنْصَرِفْ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Husayn ibn Uthman from Abdillah ibn Muskan from Abu Basir. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The traveller should not pray with the resident. But if he does pray, then let him leave after two rak’ahs.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 181

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mualla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha from Aban ibn Uthman from Umar ibn Yazid. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a traveller who prays with the imam (of prayer) and catches two rak’ahs of the prayer. Does that suffice him? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمُسَافِرِ يُصَلِّي مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَيُدْرِكُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ أَ يُجْزِي ذَلِكَ عَنْهُ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mualla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha from Aban ibn Uthman from Umar ibn Yazid. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a traveller who prays with the imam (of prayer) and catches two rak’ahs of the prayer. Does that suffice him? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 181

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Abbas ibn Maruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdillah ibn Muskan and Muhammad ibn al-Numan al-Ahwal from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If a traveller joins a group of residents in their prayer, then if it is the first (Dhuhr) prayer, let him make the obligatory prayer in the first two rak’ahs. And if it is the Asr prayer, let him make the first two (rak’ahs) supererogatory and the last two obligatory.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ اَلْأَحْوَلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا دَخَلَ اَلْمُسَافِرُ مَعَ أَقْوَامٍ حَاضِرِينَ فِي صَلاَتِهِمْ فَإِنْ كَانَتِ اَلْأُولَى فَلْيَجْعَلِ اَلْفَرِيضَةَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ وَإِنْ كَانَتِ اَلْعَصْرُ فَلْيَجْعَلِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ نَافِلَةً وَاَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ فَرِيضَةً» وفقه هذا الحديث انه انما قال ان كانت الظهر فليجعل الفريضة في الركعتين الاولتين لانه متى فعل ذلك جاز له ان يجعل الركعتين الاخيرتين صلاة العصر وإذا كان صلاة العصر انما يجعل الركعتين الاخيرتين صلاته لانه يكره الصلاة بعد صلاة العصر إلا على جهة القضاء ومن صلى على ما قلناه لم يبق عليه شئ ويحتسب به من النوافل
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Abbas ibn Maruf from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdillah ibn Muskan and Muhammad ibn al-Numan al-Ahwal from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If a traveller joins a group of residents in their prayer, then if it is the first (Dhuhr) prayer, let him make the obligatory prayer in the first two rak’ahs. And if it is the Asr prayer, let him make the first two (rak’ahs) supererogatory and the last two obligatory.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 182

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abbad ibn Suhayb. He said:
I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “A person performing tayammum should not lead a group who have performed wudu.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبَّادِ بْنِ صُهَيْبٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« لاَ يُصَلِّي اَلْمُتَيَمِّمُ بِقَوْمٍ مُتَوَضِّئِينَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abbad ibn Suhayb. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “A person performing tayammum should not lead a group who have performed wudu.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 182

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Bunan ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughirah from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them, said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “A person who performs tayammum should not lead those who have performed wudu, and a person afflicted with paralysis (al-falij) should not lead those who are healthy.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ بُنَانِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يَؤُمُّ صَاحِبُ اَلتَّيَمُّمِ اَلْمُتَوَضِّئِينَ وَ لاَ يَؤُمُّ صَاحِبُ اَلْفَالِجِ اَلْأَصِحَّاءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Bunan ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughirah from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father Imam al-Baqir (a.s), peace be upon them, said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “A person who performs tayammum should not lead those who have performed wudu, and a person afflicted with paralysis (al-falij) should not lead those who are healthy.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 183

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Abu Usamah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said concerning a man who enters a state of janabah (major ritual impurity) and has no water, and he is the imam (of prayer) of the people. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, he performs tayammum and leads them in prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يُجْنِبُ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ مَاءٌ وَ هُوَ إِمَامُ اَلْقَوْمِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ يَتَيَمَّمُ وَ يَؤُمُّهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu Jamilah from Abu Usamah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said concerning a man who enters a state of janabah (major ritual impurity) and has no water, and he is the imam (of prayer) of the people. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, he performs tayammum and leads them in prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 183

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And among them is what was narrated by Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abdillah ibn Bukayr. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s) about a man who entered a state of janabah, then performed tayammum and led us in prayer while we were in a state of full purity. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”
arabicText: وَ مِنْهُ مَا رَوَاهُ سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَجْنَبَ ثُمَّ تَيَمَّمَ فَأَمَّنَا وَ نَحْنُ طَهُورٌ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And among them is what was narrated by Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Abdillah ibn Bukayr. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s) about a man who entered a state of janabah, then performed tayammum and led us in prayer while we were in a state of full purity. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 183

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj. They said:
I said to Aba Abdillah (a.s): “An imam (of prayer) of a group, who becomes junub (ritually impure due to major impurity) during travel, and does not have enough water for ghusl, should someone among them who has wudu lead them in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No. Rather, the one in a state of janabah should perform tayammum and lead them in prayer, for Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted, has made the earth a purifier.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حُمْرَانَ وَجَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِمَامُ قَوْمٍ أَصَابَتْهُ جَنَابَةٌ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُ مِنَ اَلْمَاءِ مَا يَكْفِيهِ لِلْغُسْلِ أَ يَتَوَضَّأُ بَعْضُهُمْ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ فَقَالَ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ تَيَمَّمَ اَلْجُنُبُ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ فَإِنَّ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ جَعَلَ اَلتُّرَابَ طَهُوراً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Humran and Jamil ibn Darraj. They said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Aba Abdillah (a.s): “An imam (of prayer) of a group, who becomes junub (ritually impure due to major impurity) during travel, and does not have enough water for ghusl, should someone among them who has wudu lead them in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No. Rather, the one in a state of janabah should perform tayammum and lead them in prayer, for Allah (swt), Mighty and Exalted, has made the earth a purifier.”

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Abu Ja’far from his father from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “A man led a group in prayer while he was in a state of janabah and had performed tayammum, while they were in a state of full purification (taharah).” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ أَمَّ قَوْماً وَ هُوَ جُنُبٌ وَ قَدْ تَيَمَّمَ وَ هُمْ عَلَى طَهُورٍ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Abu Ja’far from his father from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “A man led a group in prayer while he was in a state of janabah and had performed tayammum, while they were in a state of full purification (taharah).” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 183

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amru ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about a man who repeats a prayer does he also repeat the adhan and the iqamah? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ إِذَا أَعَادَ اَلصَّلاَةَ هَلْ يُعِيدُ اَلْأَذَانَ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةَ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amru ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about a man who repeats a prayer does he also repeat the adhan and the iqamah? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 184

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Fadalah from Muawiyah ibn Ammar. He said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me (Ibn Ammar): “Make up what you missed of the daytime prayer during the day, and what you missed of the night prayer during the night.” I asked: “Should I make up two witr prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, always make up the witr prayer.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« اِقْضِ مَا فَاتَكَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ بِالنَّهَارِ وَ مَا فَاتَكَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَللَّيْلِ بِاللَّيْلِ» قُلْتُ أَقْضِي وَتْرَيْنِ فِي لَيْلَةٍ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ اِقْضِ وَتْراً أَبَداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Fadalah from Muawiyah ibn Ammar. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me (Ibn Ammar): “Make up what you missed of the daytime prayer during the day, and what you missed of the night prayer during the night.” I asked: “Should I make up two witr prayers in one night?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, always make up the witr prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 184

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan from Fadalah and al-Hasan from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Make up the daytime prayer at whatever hour you wish whether by night or by day all of that is the same.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ وَ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اِقْضِ صَلاَةَ اَلنَّهَارِ أَيَّ سَاعَةٍ شِئْتَ مِنْ لَيْلٍ أَوْ نَهَارٍ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ سَوَاءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan from Fadalah and al-Hasan from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Ala from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Make up the daytime prayer at whatever hour you wish whether by night or by day all of that is the same.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 184

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habib. He said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “I have missed the supererogatory prayers (nafilah), when should I make them up?” So Imam al-Ridha (a.s) wrote: “Whenever you wish by night or by day.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى بْنِ حَبِيبٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ تَكُونُ عَلَيَّ اَلصَّلاَةُ اَلنَّافِلَةُ مَتَى أَقْضِيهَا فَكَتَبَ« أَيَّ سَاعَةٍ شِئْتَ مِنْ لَيْلٍ أَوْ نَهَارٍ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habib. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “I have missed the supererogatory prayers (nafilah), when should I make them up?” So Imam al-Ridha (a.s) wrote: “Whenever you wish by night or by day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 184

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The prayer during travel is two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them nor after them, except for Maghrib. For after Maghrib, are four rak’ahs; do not leave them out whether in residence or travel. And there is no make-up upon you for the daytime prayers, but pray the night prayer and make it up (if missed).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَ بِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ رَكْعَتَانِ لَيْسَ قَبْلَهُمَا وَ لاَ بَعْدَ هُمَا شَيْءٌ إِلاَّ اَلْمَغْرِبَ فَإِنَّ بَعْدَهَا أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ لاَ تَدَعْهُنَّ فِي حَضَرٍ وَ لاَ سَفَرٍ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاءُ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ صَلِّ صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ وَ اِقْضِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The prayer during travel is two rak’ahs, there is nothing before them nor after them, except for Maghrib. For after Maghrib, are four rak’ahs; do not leave them out whether in residence or travel. And there is no make-up upon you for the daytime prayers, but pray the night prayer and make it up (if missed).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 185

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-Is ibn al-Qasim. He said:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who was traveling and performed the prayer in full. Imam (a.s) said: “If it is still within the time (of the prayer), then he should repeat it. But if the time has already passed, then no (he does not need to repeat it).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعِيصِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى وَ هُوَ مُسَافِرٌ فَأَتَمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَلْيُعِدْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ اَلْوَقْتُ قَدْ مَضَى فَلاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from al-Is ibn al-Qasim. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who was traveling and performed the prayer in full. Imam (a.s) said: “If it is still within the time (of the prayer), then he should repeat it. But if the time has already passed, then no (he does not need to repeat it).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 185

chapter: Chapter on the Rulings of Missed Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Numan from Suwayd al-Qalla from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who forgets and prays four rak’ahs while traveling. Imam (a.s) said: “If he remembers on the same day, then let him repeat (the prayer). But if he does not remember until that day has passed, then there is no repetition upon him.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ سُوَيْدٍ اَلْقَلاَّءِ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى فَيُصَلِّي فِي اَلسَّفَرِ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ قَالَ« إِنْ كَانَ ذَكَرَ فِي ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمِ فَلْيُعِدْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَذْكُرْ حَتَّى يَمْضِيَ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمُ فَلاَ إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Numan from Suwayd al-Qalla from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who forgets and prays four rak’ahs while traveling. Imam (a.s) said: “If he remembers on the same day, then let him repeat (the prayer). But if he does not remember until that day has passed, then there is no repetition upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 186

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa. He said:
I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, being asked about prayer on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “If you are able to go out onto dry land, then go out. But if you are not able, then pray standing, and if you cannot, then pray sitting. And strive to face the qiblah.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُسْأَلُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فَيَقُولُ« إِنِ اِسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَنْ تَخْرُجُوا إِلَى اَلْجَدَدِ فَاخْرُجُوا وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَقْدِرُوا فَصَلُّوا قِيَاماً وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِيعُوا فَصَلُّوا قُعُوداً وَ تَحَرَّوُا اَلْقِبْلَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, being asked about prayer on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “If you are able to go out onto dry land, then go out. But if you are not able, then pray standing, and if you cannot, then pray sitting. And strive to face the qiblah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 186

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Ibrahim said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about prayer on a boat. Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray while sitting if he is unable to stand in the boat, and he should not pray in the boat if he is able to reach the shore.” And Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray in the boat, turning his face towards the qiblah, then he may continue the prayer however the boat turns.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْجَوْهَرِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ إِذَا لَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ اَلْقِيَامُ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ وَ لاَ يُصَلِّي فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ وَ هُوَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى اَلشَّطِّ» وَ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ يُحَوِّلُ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي كَيْفَ مَا دَارَتْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari from Ibn Abi Hamzah from Ali ibn Ibrahim said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about prayer on a boat. Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray while sitting if he is unable to stand in the boat, and he should not pray in the boat if he is able to reach the shore.” And Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray in the boat, turning his face towards the qiblah, then he may continue the prayer however the boat turns.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “We were afflicted with a situation, and we were on a boat, and evening came upon us while we were unable to find a place where we could disembark.” So Imam (a.s) said: “The people of the boat do not pray during the day, as long as they hope to disembark.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “My father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) used to say: ‘That is the prayer of Nuh (a.s), peace be upon him.’ And are you not pleased to pray the prayer of Nuh (a.s)?” I said: “Yes, may I be your ransom.” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not let your heart be constricted, for Nuh (a.s) prayed on the boat.” I asked: “While standing or sitting?” Imam (a.s) said: “Rather, (it was whilst) standing.” I asked: “Sometimes I face the qiblah, then the boat turns.” Imam (a.s) said: “Strive to face the qiblah with the best of your effort.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّا اُبْتُلِينَا وَ كُنَّا فِي سَفِينَةٍ فَأَمْسَيْنَا وَ لَمْ نَقْدِرْ عَلَى مَكَانٍ نَخْرُجُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ« أَصْحَابُ اَلسَّفِينَةِ لَيْسَ نُصَلِّي يَوْمَنَا مَادُمْنَا نَطْمَعُ فِي اَلْخُرُوجِ» فَقَالَ «إِنَّ أَبِي كَانَ يَقُولُ« تِلْكَ صَلاَةُ نُوحٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» أَ وَ مَا تَرْضَى أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ صَلاَةَ نُوحٍ» فَقُلْتُ بَلَى جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ قَالَ« لاَ يَضِيقَنَّ صَدْرُكَ فَإِنَّ نُوحاً قَدْ صَلَّى فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ قَائِماً أَوْ قَاعِداً قَالَ« بَلْ قَائِماً» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنِّي رُبَّمَا اِسْتَقْبَلْتُ اَلْقِبْلَةَ فَدَارَتِ اَلسَّفِينَةُ قَالَ« تَحَرَّ اَلْقِبْلَةَ بِجُهْدِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “We were afflicted with a situation, and we were on a boat, and evening came upon us while we were unable to find a place where we could disembark.” So Imam (a.s) said: “The people of the boat do not pray during the day, as long as they hope to disembark.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “My father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) used to say: ‘That is the prayer of Nuh (a.s), peace be upon him.’ And are you not pleased to pray the prayer of Nuh (a.s)?” I said: “Yes, may I be your ransom.” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not let your heart be constricted, for Nuh (a.s) prayed on the boat.” I asked: “While standing or sitting?” Imam (a.s) said: “Rather, (it was whilst) standing.” I asked: “Sometimes I face the qiblah, then the boat turns.” Imam (a.s) said: “Strive to face the qiblah with the best of your effort.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid.
He (Sulayman) said: “I asked Imam (a.s) about prayer on a boat.” Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray while standing, and if he is unable to stand, then let him sit and pray while facing the qiblah. If the boat turns, then let him turn with the qiblah if he is able to do so, and if he is not able to do so, then let him remain in his place and strive to face the qiblah with the best of his effort.” And Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray the supererogatory prayer facing the front of the boat, while he is facing the qiblah when he says the takbir, and it does not harm him wherever the boat turns afterward.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ« يُصَلِّي قَائِماً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعِ اَلْقِيَامَ فَلْيَجْلِسْ وَ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ مُسْتَقْبِلُ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَإِنْ دَارَتِ اَلسَّفِينَةُ فَلْيَدُرْ مَعَ اَلْقِبْلَةِ إِنْ قَدَرَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ فَلْيَثْبُتْ عَلَى مَقَامِهِ وَ لْيَتَحَرَّ اَلْقِبْلَةَ بِجُهْدِهِ» وَ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي اَلنَّافِلَةَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ صَدْرِ اَلسَّفِينَةِ وَ هُوَ مُسْتَقْبِلُ اَلْقِبْلَةِ إِذَا كَبَّرَ ثُمَّ لاَ يَضُرُّهُ حَيْثُ دَارَتْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid.
thaqalaynMatn: He (Sulayman) said: “I asked Imam (a.s) about prayer on a boat.” Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray while standing, and if he is unable to stand, then let him sit and pray while facing the qiblah. If the boat turns, then let him turn with the qiblah if he is able to do so, and if he is not able to do so, then let him remain in his place and strive to face the qiblah with the best of his effort.” And Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray the supererogatory prayer facing the front of the boat, while he is facing the qiblah when he says the takbir, and it does not harm him wherever the boat turns afterward.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about prayer on a boat. Imam (a.s) said: “If it is loaded and heavy, such that when you stand in it, it does not sway, then pray standing. But if it is light and sways, then pray sitting.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ حَمْزَةَ اَلْغَنَوِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَتْ مُحَمَّلَةً ثَقِيلَةً إِذَا قُمْتَ فِيهَا لَمْ تَتَحَرَّكْ فَصَلِّ قَائِماً وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ خَفِيفَةً تَكَفَّأُ فَصَلِّ قَاعِداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Yazid ibn Ishaq from Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about prayer on a boat. Imam (a.s) said: “If it is loaded and heavy, such that when you stand in it, it does not sway, then pray standing. But if it is light and sways, then pray sitting.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the prayer of fear. Imam (a.s) said: “The imam (of prayer) stands, and a group from among his companions comes and stands behind him, while another group positions themselves facing the enemy. Then the imam (of prayer) leads that group in one rak’ah, then he stands and they stand with him, and he remains standing while they complete the second rak’ah. Then they give salam to one another and depart, and they go to take the place of their companions. Then the others come and stand behind the imam (of prayer), and he leads them in the second rak’ah, then the imam (of prayer) sits, and they (the second group) stand and pray another rak’ah, then he gives salam to them, and they depart with one taslimah.” Imam (a.s) said: “And in Maghrib, it is similar to that; the imam (of prayer) stands, and a group comes and stands behind him, and he leads them in prayer. Then he stands and they stand, and the imam (of prayer) remains standing, and they pray two rak’ahs, then recite the tashahhud and give salam to one another. Then they depart and go to the position of their companions, and the others come and take the place of their companions behind the imam (of prayer). Then he prays one rak’ah with them, reciting in it, then he sits and recites the tashahhud. Then he stands and they stand with him, and he prays with them another rak’ah. Then he sits, and they stand and pray another rak’ah, then he gives salam to them.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْخَوْفِ قَالَ« يَقُومُ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ يَجِيءُ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِهِ فَيَقُومُونَ خَلْفَهُ وَطَائِفَةٌ بِإِزَاءِ اَلْعَدُوِّ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمُ اَلْإِمَامُ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ يَقُومُ وَ يَقُومُونَ مَعَهُ فَيَمْثُلُ قَائِماً وَ يُصَلُّونَ هُمُ اَلرَّكْعَةَ اَلثَّانِيَةَ ثُمَّ يُسَلِّمُ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ ثُمَّ يَنْصَرِفُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ فِي مَقَامِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَ يَجِيءُ اَلْآخَرُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمُ اَلرَّكْعَةَ اَلثَّانِيَةَ ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ يَقُومُونَ هُمْ فَيُصَلُّونَ رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ يُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْهِمْ فَيَنْصَرِفُونَ بِتَسْلِيمَةٍ» قَالَ« وَ فِي اَلْمَغْرِبِ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ يَقُومُ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ تَجِيءُ طَائِفَةٌ فَيَقُومُونَ خَلْفَهُ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ وَ يَقُومُونَ فَيَمْثُلُ اَلْإِمَامُ قَائِماً وَ يُصَلُّونَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُونَ وَ يُسَلِّمُ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ ثُمَّ يَنْصَرِفُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ فِي مَوْقِفِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَ يَجِيءُ اَلْآخَرُونَ فَيَقُومُونَ فِي مَوْقِفِ أَصْحَابِهِمْ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَيُصَلِّي بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً يَقْرَأُ فِيهَا ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يَقُومُ وَ يَقُومُونَ مَعَهُ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ وَ يَقُومُونَ هُمْ فَيُصَلُّونَ رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ يُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْهِمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Aba Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the prayer of fear. Imam (a.s) said: “The imam (of prayer) stands, and a group from among his companions comes and stands behind him, while another group positions themselves facing the enemy. Then the imam (of prayer) leads that group in one rak’ah, then he stands and they stand with him, and he remains standing while they complete the second rak’ah. Then they give salam to one another and depart, and they go to take the place of their companions. Then the others come and stand behind the imam (of prayer), and he leads them in the second rak’ah, then the imam (of prayer) sits, and they (the second group) stand and pray another rak’ah, then he gives salam to them, and they depart with one taslimah.” Imam (a.s) said: “And in Maghrib, it is similar to that; the imam (of prayer) stands, and a group comes and stands behind him, and he leads them in prayer. Then he stands and they stand, and the imam (of prayer) remains standing, and they pray two rak’ahs, then recite the tashahhud and give salam to one another. Then they depart and go to the position of their companions, and the others come and take the place of their companions behind the imam (of prayer). Then he prays one rak’ah with them, reciting in it, then he sits and recites the tashahhud. Then he stands and they stand with him, and he prays with them another rak’ah. Then he sits, and they stand and pray another rak’ah, then he gives salam to them.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him.
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) with his companions in the expedition of Dhat al-Riqa. Prophet (saws) divided his companions into two groups; He (saws) placed one group facing the enemy, and the other group behind him. He (saws) said the takbir, and they said the takbir, then He (saws) recited and they listened. Then He (saws) bowed and they bowed, and He (saws) prostrated and they prostrated. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, stood upright, and they completed one rak’ah for themselves. Then some of them gave salam to others, then they went to their companions and stood facing the enemy, And their companions came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. Then Prophet (saws) prayed one rak’ah with them, then recited the tashahhud and gave salam to them. Then they stood and completed one rak’ah for themselves and gave salam to one another.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلَّى رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِأَصْحَابِهِ فِي غَزَاةِ ذَاتِ اَلرِّقَاعِ صَلاَةَ اَلْخَوْفِ فَفَرَّقَ أَصْحَابَهُ فِرْقَتَيْنِ أَقَامَ فِرْقَةً بِإِزَاءِ اَلْعَدُوِّ وَ فِرْقَةً خَلْفَهُ فَكَبَّرَ وَ كَبَّرُوا فَقَرَأَ وَ أَنْصَتُوا فَرَكَعَ وَ رَكَعُوا وَ سَجَدَ فَسَجَدُوا ثُمَّ اِسْتَتَمَّ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَائِماً وَ صَلَّوْا لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ ثُمَّ خَرَجُوا إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَأَقَامُوا بِإِزَاءِ اَلْعَدُوِّ وَجَاءَ أَصْحَابُهُمْ فَقَامُوا خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ فَصَلَّى بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ تَشَهَّدَ وَ سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَامُوا فَصَلَّوْا لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ رَكْعَةً وَ سَلَّمَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him.
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, prayed the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) with his companions in the expedition of Dhat al-Riqa. Prophet (saws) divided his companions into two groups; He (saws) placed one group facing the enemy, and the other group behind him. He (saws) said the takbir, and they said the takbir, then He (saws) recited and they listened. Then He (saws) bowed and they bowed, and He (saws) prostrated and they prostrated. Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, stood upright, and they completed one rak’ah for themselves. Then some of them gave salam to others, then they went to their companions and stood facing the enemy, And their companions came and stood behind the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. Then Prophet (saws) prayed one rak’ah with them, then recited the tashahhud and gave salam to them. Then they stood and completed one rak’ah for themselves and gave salam to one another.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 188

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Hammad from Abu Basir. He said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “If you are in a land of fear and you fear a thief or a wild beast, then pray the obligatory prayer while you are on your mount.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِنْ كُنْتَ فِي أَرْضِ مَخَافَةٍ فَخَشِيتَ لِصّاً أَوْ سَبُعاً فَصَلِّ اَلْفَرِيضَةَ وَ أَنْتَ عَلَى دَابَّتِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Hammad from Abu Basir. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “If you are in a land of fear and you fear a thief or a wild beast, then pray the obligatory prayer while you are on your mount.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 189

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who fears a wild beast or a thief, how should he pray? Imam (a.s) said: “He should say the takbir and gesture with his head.”
arabicText: وَعَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَخَافُ مِنْ سَبُعٍ أَوْ لِصٍّ كَيْفَ يُصَلِّي قَالَ« يُكَبِّرُ وَ يُومِئُ بِرَأْسِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who fears a wild beast or a thief, how should he pray? Imam (a.s) said: “He should say the takbir and gesture with his head.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 189

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sadd from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah. He said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The one who fears thieves and wild beasts should perform the prayer of those in dangerous situations, by gesturing while on his mount.” I (Zurarah) asked: “What if the person in such a situation, is not in a state of ablution and is unable to dismount, what should he do?” Imam (a.s) said: “He performs tayammum from the felt of his saddle or from his mount or from the mane of his mount, for there is dust in it, and he performs the prayer, and makes his prostration lower than his bowing. He does not turn toward the qibla, but rather wherever his mount turns except that he must face the qibla for the first takbirah when he begins the prayer.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ وَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« اَلَّذِي يَخَافُ اَللُّصُوصَ وَ اَلسَّبُعَ يُصَلِّي صَلاَةَ اَلْمُوَاقَفَةِ إِيمَاءً عَلَى دَابَّتِهِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ أَ رَأَيْتَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنِ اَلْمُوَاقِفُ عَلَى وُضُوءٍ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ وَ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى اَلنُّزُولِ قَالَ« يَتَيَمَّمُ مِنْ لِبْدِ سَرْجِهِ أَوْ دَابَّتِهِ أَوْ مِنْ مَعْرَفَةِ دَابَّتِهِ فَإِنَّ فِيهَا غُبَاراً وَ يُصَلِّي وَ يَجْعَلُ اَلسُّجُودَ أَخْفَضَ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ وَ لاَ يَدُورُ إِلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَ لَكِنْ أَيْنَمَا دَارَتْ دَابَّتُهُ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ يَسْتَقْبِلُ اَلْقِبْلَةَ بِأَوَّلِ تَكْبِيرَةٍ حِينَ يَتَوَجَّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sadd from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Zurarah. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The one who fears thieves and wild beasts should perform the prayer of those in dangerous situations, by gesturing while on his mount.” I (Zurarah) asked: “What if the person in such a situation, is not in a state of ablution and is unable to dismount, what should he do?” Imam (a.s) said: “He performs tayammum from the felt of his saddle or from his mount or from the mane of his mount, for there is dust in it, and he performs the prayer, and makes his prostration lower than his bowing. He does not turn toward the qibla, but rather wherever his mount turns except that he must face the qibla for the first takbirah when he begins the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 189

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer During Pursuit and Sword Fighting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, Fudayl, and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “In the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) during pursuit, skirmishes, and the intensification of fighting, each person among them should pray by gesturing, wherever his face is. But when there is close combat, grappling, and intense fighting, then indeed the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, on the night of Siffin and it was the night of al-Harir, had not led them in Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha at the time of each prayer; except with takbir (‘Allahu Akbar’), tahlil (‘La ilaha illa Allah’), tasbih (‘SubhanAllah’), tamjid (‘Al-hamdu lillah’), and supplication. So that was their prayer, and Imam Ali (a.s) did not command them to make up the prayer.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ فُضَيْلٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْخَوْفِ عِنْدَ اَلْمُطَارَدَةِ وَ اَلْمُنَاوَشَةِ وَ تَلاَحُمِ اَلْقِتَالِ فَإِنَّهُ يُصَلِّي كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ مِنْهُمْ بِالْإِيمَاءِ حَيْثُ كَانَ وَجْهُهُ فَإِذَا كَانَتِ اَلْمُسَايَفَةُ وَ اَلْمُعَانَقَةُ وَ تَلاَحُمُ اَلْقِتَالِ فَإِنَّ أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لَيْلَةَ صِفِّينَ وَ هِيَ لَيْلَةُ اَلْهَرِيرِ لَمْ يَكُنْ صَلَّى بِهِمُ اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ وَ اَلْمَغْرِبَ وَ اَلْعِشَاءَ عِنْدَ وَقْتِ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ إِلاَّ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ وَ اَلتَّهْلِيلِ وَ اَلتَّسْبِيحِ وَ اَلتَّمْجِيدِ وَ اَلدُّعَاءِ فَكَانَتْ تِلْكَ صَلاَتَهُمْ وَ لَمْ يَأْمُرْهُمْ بِإِعَادَةِ اَلصَّلاَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah, Fudayl, and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “In the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) during pursuit, skirmishes, and the intensification of fighting, each person among them should pray by gesturing, wherever his face is. But when there is close combat, grappling, and intense fighting, then indeed the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, on the night of Siffin and it was the night of al-Harir, had not led them in Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha at the time of each prayer; except with takbir (‘Allahu Akbar’), tahlil (‘La ilaha illa Allah’), tasbih (‘SubhanAllah’), tamjid (‘Al-hamdu lillah’), and supplication. So that was their prayer, and Imam Ali (a.s) did not command them to make up the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 190

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer During Pursuit and Sword Fighting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur’ah, from Sama’ah. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the prayer during combat. Imam (a.s) said: “When they meet and engage in fighting, then at that time, the prayer is only with takbir. And if they are standing still, then the prayer is by gesturing.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْقِتَالِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا اِلْتَقَوْا فَاقْتَتَلُوا فَإِنَّمَا اَلصَّلاَةُ حِينَئِذٍ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ وَ إِذَا كَانُوا وُقُوفاً فَالصَّلاَةُ إِيمَاءً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Zur’ah, from Sama’ah. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the prayer during combat. Imam (a.s) said: “When they meet and engage in fighting, then at that time, the prayer is only with takbir. And if they are standing still, then the prayer is by gesturing.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 191

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer During Pursuit and Sword Fighting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sadd from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The prayer during a march (of war), is performed at noon with gesturing by your head and with takbir, And during sword fighting, it is with takbir along with gesturing, And during pursuit it is by gesturing each man prays individually in his position.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَلاَةُ اَلزَّحْفِ عَلَى اَلظَّهْرِ إِيمَاءٌ بِرَأْسِكَ وَ تَكْبِيرٌ وَ اَلْمُسَايَفَةُ تَكْبِيرٌ مَعَ إِيمَاءٍ وَ اَلْمُطَارَدَةُ إِيمَاءٌ يُصَلِّي كُلُّ رَجُلٍ عَلَى حِيَالِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sadd from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The prayer during a march (of war), is performed at noon with gesturing by your head and with takbir, And during sword fighting, it is with takbir along with gesturing, And during pursuit it is by gesturing each man prays individually in his position.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 191

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer During Pursuit and Sword Fighting
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, and from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah. He said: One of our companions narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The minimum that suffices in the case of close combat (musayafah), in terms of takbir, is two takbirs for each prayer except for the Maghrib prayer, for it requires three.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ وَ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي بَعْضُ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَقَلُّ مَا يُجْزِي فِي حَدِّ اَلْمُسَايَفَةِ مِنَ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ تَكْبِيرَتَانِ لِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ إِلاَّ صَلاَةَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فَإِنَّ لَهَا ثَلاَثاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, and from Ayyub ibn Nuh from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah. He said: One of our companions narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The minimum that suffices in the case of close combat (musayafah), in terms of takbir, is two takbirs for each prayer except for the Maghrib prayer, for it requires three.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 191

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir. He said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever is in a place where he is unable to reach the ground, should gesture with indications.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ هِلاَلٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: «مَنْ كَانَ فِي مَكَانٍ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَلْيُومِ إِيمَاءً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Hilal from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever is in a place where he is unable to reach the ground, should gesture with indications.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who gestures in the obligatory and supererogatory prayers, when he does not find anything to prostrate upon and does not have a place in which he can perform prostration. Imam (a.s) said: “If it is like that, then let him gesture throughout the entire prayer.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُومِئُ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ وَ اَلنَّوَافِلِ إِذَا لَمْ يَجِدْ مَا يَسْجُدُ عَلَيْهِ وَ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ مَوْضِعٌ يَسْجُدُ فِيهِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ هَكَذَا فَلْيُومِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ كُلِّهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar ibn Musa from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who gestures in the obligatory and supererogatory prayers, when he does not find anything to prostrate upon and does not have a place in which he can perform prostration. Imam (a.s) said: “If it is like that, then let him gesture throughout the entire prayer.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And with this same chain of transmission, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who is caught in the rain, while in a place where he is unable to prostrate, due to mud and does not find a dry spot. Imam (a.s) said: “He should begin the prayer, and when he bows, let him bow as he would normally do in prayer. And when he raises his head from the bowing, let him gesture for the prostration while standing. He should continue in this manner until he completes the prayer, perform the tashahhud while standing, and give the salam.”
arabicText: وَ بِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ ع قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصِيبُهُ اَلْمَطَرُ وَ هُوَ فِي مَوْضِعٍ لاَ يَقْدِرُ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ فِيهِ مِنَ اَلطِّينِ وَ لاَ يَجِدُ مَوْضِعاً جَافّاً قَالَ« يَفْتَتِحُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَإِذَا رَكَعَ فَلْيَرْكَعْ كَمَا يَرْكَعُ إِذَا صَلَّى وَ إِذَا رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ فَلْيُومِ بِالسُّجُودِ إِيمَاءً وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ يُسَلِّمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And with this same chain of transmission, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who is caught in the rain, while in a place where he is unable to prostrate, due to mud and does not find a dry spot. Imam (a.s) said: “He should begin the prayer, and when he bows, let him bow as he would normally do in prayer. And when he raises his head from the bowing, let him gesture for the prostration while standing. He should continue in this manner until he completes the prayer, perform the tashahhud while standing, and give the salam.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Zur’ah from Sama’ah. He said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a prisoner taken captive by the polytheists, and the time of prayer comes, while the one who captured him, prevents him from performing it. Imam (a.s) said: “He should gesture with indications.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْأَسِيرِ يَأْسِرُهُ اَلْمُشْرِكُونَ فَتَحْضُرُهُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَيَمْنَعُهُ اَلَّذِي أَسَرَهُ مِنْهَا قَالَ« يُومِئُ إِيمَاءً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Zur’ah from Sama’ah. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a prisoner taken captive by the polytheists, and the time of prayer comes, while the one who captured him, prevents him from performing it. Imam (a.s) said: “He should gesture with indications.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If the sick person is unable to pray sitting, then he should pray however he is able, either by being positioned and gesturing with indications.” And Imam (a.s) said: “He should be positioned as a man is positioned in his grave, and lie on his right side, then gesture for the prayer. If he is unable to lie on his right side, then however he is able, it is permissible for him. He should face the qibla with his face, then gesture for the prayer by indication.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْمَرِيضُ إِذَا لَمْ يَقْدِرْ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ قَاعِداً كَيْفَ قَدَرَ صَلَّى إِمَّا أَنْ يُوَجَّهَ فَيُومِئُ إِيمَاءً» وَ قَالَ« يُوَجَّهُ كَمَا يُوَجَّهُ اَلرَّجُلُ فِي لَحْدِهِ وَ يَنَامُ عَلَى جَنْبِهِ اَلْأَيْمَنِ ثُمَّ يُومِئُ بِالصَّلاَةِ فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ أَنْ يَنَامَ عَلَى جَنْبِهِ اَلْأَيْمَنِ فَكَيْفَ مَا قَدَرَ فَإِنَّهُ لَهُ جَائِزٌ وَ يَسْتَقْبِلُ بِوَجْهِهِ اَلْقِبْلَةَ ثُمَّ يُومِئُ بِالصَّلاَةِ إِيمَاءً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Said from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If the sick person is unable to pray sitting, then he should pray however he is able, either by being positioned and gesturing with indications.” And Imam (a.s) said: “He should be positioned as a man is positioned in his grave, and lie on his right side, then gesture for the prayer. If he is unable to lie on his right side, then however he is able, it is permissible for him. He should face the qibla with his face, then gesture for the prayer by indication.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn al-Qasim from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from someone who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The sick person prays standing, and if he is unable to do that, he prays sitting. If he is unable to do that, he prays lying on his back he pronounces the takbir, then recites. When he wishes to bow, he closes his eyes, then glorifies (‘SubhanAllah’). When he has glorified, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes is considered his rising from bowing. When he wishes to prostrate, he closes his eyes, then glorifies. When he has glorified, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes is considered his rising from prostration. Then he recites the tashahhud and ends the prayer.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُصَلِّي اَلْمَرِيضُ قَائِماً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ صَلَّى جَالِساً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ صَلَّى مُسْتَلْقِياً يُكَبِّرُ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ اَلرُّكُوعَ غَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُسَبِّحُ فَإِذَا سَبَّحَ فَتَحَ عَيْنَيْهِ فَيَكُونُ فَتْحُهُ عَيْنَيْهِ رَفْعَهُ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ فَإِذَا أَرَادَ أَنْ يَسْجُدَ غَمَّضَ عَيْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُسَبِّحُ فَإِذَا سَبَّحَ فَتَحَ عَيْنَيْهِ فَيَكُونُ فَتْحُهُ عَيْنَيْهِ رَفْعَهُ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلسُّجُودِ ثُمَّ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn al-Qasim from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim from someone who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The sick person prays standing, and if he is unable to do that, he prays sitting. If he is unable to do that, he prays lying on his back he pronounces the takbir, then recites. When he wishes to bow, he closes his eyes, then glorifies (‘SubhanAllah’). When he has glorified, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes is considered his rising from bowing. When he wishes to prostrate, he closes his eyes, then glorifies. When he has glorified, he opens his eyes, and the opening of his eyes is considered his rising from prostration. Then he recites the tashahhud and ends the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 192

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Do not hold your turban while you are praying, and do not lean against a wall unless you are ill.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ تُمْسِكْ بِخَمَرِكَ وَ أَنْتَ تُصَلِّي وَ لاَ تَسْتَنِدْ إِلَى جِدَارٍ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَكُونَ مَرِيضاً»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Nadr from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Do not hold your turban while you are praying, and do not lean against a wall unless you are ill.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ali ibn Mahziyar. He said:
I asked Imam al-Hadi (a.s) about a person who falls unconscious for a day or more than that, does he make up the prayers he missed? Imam (a.s) wrote: “He does not make up the fasts, nor does he make up the prayers.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ يَوْماً أَوْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ هَلْ يَقْضِي مَا فَاتَهُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَكَتَبَ« لاَ يَقْضِي اَلصَّوْمَ وَ لاَ يَقْضِي اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Ali ibn Mahziyar. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Hadi (a.s) about a person who falls unconscious for a day or more than that, does he make up the prayers he missed? Imam (a.s) wrote: “He does not make up the fasts, nor does he make up the prayers.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 193

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub by Ali from his father from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Hamzah by Abu Ja’far (a.s):
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) was asked regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “Those who remember Allah (swt) standing” (Surah Aal Imran 3:191) Imam (a.s) said: “The healthy one prays ‘standing’. ‘And sitting’ (Surah Aal Imran 3:191), for the sick person prays sitting. ‘And on their sides’ (Surah Aal Imran 3:191), for the one who is weaker than the sick person who prays sitting.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« اَلَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اَللّٰهَ قِيٰاماً» قَالَ« اَلصَّحِيحُ يُصَلِّي قَائِماً« وَ قُعُوداً» اَلْمَرِيضُ يُصَلِّي جَالِساً« وَ عَلىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ» اَلَّذِي يَكُونُ أَضْعَفَ مِنَ اَلْمَرِيضِ اَلَّذِي يُصَلِّي جَالِساً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub by Ali from his father from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Hamzah by Abu Ja’far (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) was asked regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “Those who remember Allah (swt) standing” (Surah Aal Imran 3:191) Imam (a.s) said: “The healthy one prays ‘standing’. ‘And sitting’ (Surah Aal Imran 3:191), for the sick person prays sitting. ‘And on their sides’ (Surah Aal Imran 3:191), for the one who is weaker than the sick person who prays sitting.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Husayn from Sama’ah from Abu Basir. He said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a sick person, can a woman hold something for him to prostrate upon? Imam (a.s) said: “No, unless he is in a state of necessity, having no one else with him and nothing else available. There is nothing that Allah (swt) has forbidden except that He (azj) has made it permissible, for the one who is compelled to it.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حُسَيْنٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرِيضِ هَلْ تُمْسِكُ لَهُ اَلْمَرْأَةُ شَيْئاً يَسْجُدُ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ« لاَ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُضْطَرّاً لَيْسَ عِنْدَهُ غَيْرُهَا وَ لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ مِمَّا حَرَّمَ اَللَّهُ إِلاَّ وَ قَدْ أَحَلَّهُ لِمَنِ اُضْطُرَّ إِلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Fadalah from Husayn from Sama’ah from Abu Basir. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a sick person, can a woman hold something for him to prostrate upon? Imam (a.s) said: “No, unless he is in a state of necessity, having no one else with him and nothing else available. There is nothing that Allah (swt) has forbidden except that He (azj) has made it permissible, for the one who is compelled to it.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s) about the (prayer of a) sick person. Imam (a.s) said: “He should prostrate on the ground, or on a fan, or on a tooth-stick (siwak), something he raises up that is better than gesturing. Those who disliked prostration on a fan, only disliked it because of the idols that used to be worshipped besides Allah (swt). And we have never worshipped anyone other than Allah (swt), ever. So prostrate on a fan, or on a tooth-stick, or on a piece of wood.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرِيضِ قَالَ «يَسْجُدُ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ أَوْ عَلَى مِرْوَحَةٍ أَوْ عَلَى سِوَاكٍ يَرْفَعُهُ هُوَ أَفْضَلُ مِنَ اَلْإِيمَاءِ إِنَّمَا كَرِهَ مَنْ كَرِهَ اَلسُّجُودَ عَلَى اَلْمِرْوَحَةِ مِنْ أَجْلِ اَلْأَوْثَانِ اَلَّتِي كَانَتْ تُعْبَدُ مِنْ دُونِ اَللَّهِ وَ إِنَّا لَمْ نَعْبُدْ غَيْرَ اَللَّهِ قَطُّ فَاسْجُدْ عَلَى اَلْمِرْوَحَةِ أَوْ عَلَى سِوَاكٍ أَوْ عَلَى عُودٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s) about the (prayer of a) sick person. Imam (a.s) said: “He should prostrate on the ground, or on a fan, or on a tooth-stick (siwak), something he raises up that is better than gesturing. Those who disliked prostration on a fan, only disliked it because of the idols that used to be worshipped besides Allah (swt). And we have never worshipped anyone other than Allah (swt), ever. So prostrate on a fan, or on a tooth-stick, or on a piece of wood.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from someone who informed him from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) was asked: “What is the degree of illness that compels its sufferer, and what is the illness in which its sufferer should leave off praying while standing?” Imam (a.s) said: “Rather, man is a witness against himself.” (Surah Al Qiyamah 75:14) Imam (a.s) said: “That is up to him, he is more knowledgeable about himself.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَمَّنْ أَخْبَرَهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ مَا حَدُّ اَلْمَرَضِ اَلَّذِي يُضْطَرُّ صَاحِبُهُ وَ اَلْمَرَضِ اَلَّذِي يَدَعُ صَاحِبُهُ فِيهِ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَائِماً قَالَ«« بَلِ اَلْإِنْسٰانُ عَلىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ» قَالَ ذَاكَ إِلَيْهِ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِنَفْسِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from someone who informed him from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) was asked: “What is the degree of illness that compels its sufferer, and what is the illness in which its sufferer should leave off praying while standing?” Imam (a.s) said: “Rather, man is a witness against himself.” (Surah Al Qiyamah 75:14) Imam (a.s) said: “That is up to him, he is more knowledgeable about himself.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Jamil, and from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil. He said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “What is the degree of illness for which a person should pray sitting?” Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, a man may suffer fever or be wounded, but he knows himself best. If he has the strength, then let him stand (for prayer).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ وَ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا حَدُّ اَلْمَرَضِ اَلَّذِي يُصَلِّي صَاحِبُهُ قَاعِداً فَقَالَ« إِنَّ اَلرَّجُلَ لَيُوعَكُ وَ يُجْرَحُ وَ لَكِنَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِنَفْسِهِ إِذَا قَوِيَ فَلْيَقُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Jamil, and from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “What is the degree of illness for which a person should pray sitting?” Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, a man may suffer fever or be wounded, but he knows himself best. If he has the strength, then let him stand (for prayer).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf from Bakkar. He said:
My father, spoke to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and asked Imam (a.s) while I (Bakkar) was listening: “What is the degree of illness in which fasting is to be abandoned?” Imam (a.s) said: “When he is unable to partake in the pre-dawn meal (suhur).”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفٍ عَنْ بَكَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَهُ أَبِي يَعْنِي أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ أَنَا أَسْمَعُ مَا حَدُّ اَلْمَرَضِ اَلَّذِي يُتْرَكُ فِيهِ اَلصَّوْمُ قَالَ« إِذَا لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ أَنْ يَتَسَحَّرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf from Bakkar. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: My father, spoke to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and asked Imam (a.s) while I (Bakkar) was listening: “What is the degree of illness in which fasting is to be abandoned?” Imam (a.s) said: “When he is unable to partake in the pre-dawn meal (suhur).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Drowning Person, the One Who Is Alone, and the One in Necessity, and Other Such Cases
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi. He said:
The Jurist (Faqih), Imam al-Hadi (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The sick person is to pray sitting only when he reaches the condition, in which he is unable to walk the length of his prayer, from beginning to end while standing.”
arabicText: اَلصَّفَّارُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ حَفْصٍ اَلْمَرْوَزِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ اَلْفَقِيهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« اَلْمَرِيضُ إِنَّمَا يُصَلِّي قَاعِداً إِذَا صَارَ بِالْحَالِ اَلَّتِي لاَ يَقْدِرُ فِيهَا أَنْ يَمْشِيَ مِقْدَارَ صَلاَتِهِ إِلَى أَنْ يَفْرُغَ قَائِماً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Sulayman ibn Hafs al-Marwazi. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Jurist (Faqih), Imam al-Hadi (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The sick person is to pray sitting only when he reaches the condition, in which he is unable to walk the length of his prayer, from beginning to end while standing.”
