chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Naked
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah. He said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s): “A man comes out of a ship naked, or his clothes have been taken from him, and he does not find anything to pray in, what should he do?” Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray by gesturing. If it is a woman, she should place her hand over her private part, and if it is a man, he should place his hand over his private part. Then they should both sit and gesture with indications. They should neither bow nor prostrate, as what is behind them (anus) would become exposed. Their prayer should be by gesturing with their heads.” Imam (a.s) said: “And if they are in water or in a deep sea, they should not prostrate in it, and the requirement of facing the qibla is lifted from them in that case. They should gesture therein with indications, their lifting is counted as turning toward the qibla, and their lowering (is considered) likewise.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَجُلٌ خَرَجَ مِنْ سَفِينَةٍ عُرْيَاناً أَوْ سُلِبَ ثِيَابُهُ وَ لَمْ يَجِدْ شَيْئاً يُصَلِّي فِيهِ فَقَالَ« يُصَلِّي إِيمَاءً وَ إِنْ كَانَتِ اِمْرَأَةً جَعَلَتْ يَدَهَا عَلَى فَرْجِهَا وَ إِنْ كَانَ رَجُلاً وَضَعَ يَدَهُ عَلَى سَوْأَتِهِ ثُمَّ يَجْلِسَانِ فَيُومِيَانِ إِيمَاءً وَ لاَ يَرْكَعَانِ وَ لاَ يَسْجُدَانِ فَيَبْدُوَ مَا خَلْفَهُمَا تَكُونُ صَلاَتُهُمَا إِيمَاءً بِرُءُوسِهِمَا» قَالَ« وَإِنْ كَانَا فِي مَاءٍ أَوْ بَحْرٍ لُجِّيٍّ لَمْ يَسْجُدَا عَلَيْهِ وَ مَوْضُوعٌ عَنْهُمَا اَلتَّوَجُّهُ فِيهِ يُومِيَانِ فِي ذَلِكَ إِيمَاءً رَفْعُهُمَا تَوَجُّهٌ وَ وَضْعُهُمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s): “A man comes out of a ship naked, or his clothes have been taken from him, and he does not find anything to pray in, what should he do?” Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray by gesturing. If it is a woman, she should place her hand over her private part, and if it is a man, he should place his hand over his private part. Then they should both sit and gesture with indications. They should neither bow nor prostrate, as what is behind them (anus) would become exposed. Their prayer should be by gesturing with their heads.” Imam (a.s) said: “And if they are in water or in a deep sea, they should not prostrate in it, and the requirement of facing the qibla is lifted from them in that case. They should gesture therein with indications, their lifting is counted as turning toward the qibla, and their lowering (is considered) likewise.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Naked
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a group of people who prayed in congregation, while they were naked. Imam (a.s) said: “The imam (of prayer) should go before them on his knees and lead them in prayer sitting, while he is also sitting.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ صَلَّوْا جَمَاعَةً وَ هُمْ عُرَاةٌ قَالَ« يَتَقَدَّمُهُمُ اَلْإِمَامُ بِرُكْبَتَيْهِ وَ يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ جُلُوساً وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a group of people who prayed in congregation, while they were naked. Imam (a.s) said: “The imam (of prayer) should go before them on his knees and lead them in prayer sitting, while he is also sitting.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 196

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Naked
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ayyub ibn Nuh from one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The naked person, who has no garment, if he finds a pit, he should enter it and perform his prostration and bowing in it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْعَارِي اَلَّذِي لَيْسَ لَهُ ثَوْبٌ إِذَا وَجَدَ حُفْرَةً دَخَلَهَا فَسَجَدَ فِيهَا وَ رَكَعَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ayyub ibn Nuh from one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The naked person, who has no garment, if he finds a pit, he should enter it and perform his prostration and bowing in it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 196

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Naked
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Marwan ibn Muslim from Ammar al-Sabati. He said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “What do you say about a group of people, who were on a journey walking along the shore of the sea, when suddenly they came upon a dead man; naked, whom the sea had cast ashore. These group of people are themselves naked, having only a waist wrap or a cloak. How should they pray over him (the deceased), while they are naked and have no extra garment to shroud him with?” Imam (a.s) said: “A grave should be dug for him, and he should be placed in his burial niche (lahd), and bricks should be placed over his private parts, so that his private area is covered with the bricks and stones. Then the prayer should be performed over him, and then he should be buried.” I asked: “So, the prayer is not to be performed over him, if he has already been buried?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, the prayer is not performed over the deceased after he has been buried, nor is it performed over him while he is naked, until his private parts are covered.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ مَرْوَانَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي قَوْمٍ كَانُوا فِي سَفَرٍ لَهُمْ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى سَاحِلِ اَلْبَحْرِ فَإِذَا هُمْ بِرَجُلٍ مَيِّتٍ عُرْيَانٍ قَدْ لَفَظَهُ اَلْبَحْرُ وَ هُمْ عُرَاةٌ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِلاَّ إِزَارٌ أَوْ رِدَاءٌ كَيْفَ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَيْهِ وَ هُمْ عُرَاةٌ لَيْسَ مَعَهُمْ فَضْلُ ثَوْبٍ يُكَفِّنُونَهُ بِهِ قَالَ« يُحْفَرُ لَهُ وَ يُوضَعُ فِي لَحْدِهِ وَ يُوضَعُ اَللَّبِنُ عَلَى عَوْرَتِهِ فَيُسْتَرُ بِاللَّبِنِ وَ بِالْحَجَرِ ثُمَّ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُدْفَنُ» قُلْتُ فَلاَ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ إِذَا دُفِنَ قَالَ« لاَ يُصَلَّى عَلَى اَلْمَيِّتِ بَعْدَمَا يُدْفَنُ وَ لاَ يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ وَ هُوَ عُرْيَانٌ حَتَّى تُوَارَى عَوْرَتُهُ»

thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “What do you say about a group of people, who were on a journey walking along the shore of the sea, when suddenly they came upon a dead man; naked, whom the sea had cast ashore. These group of people are themselves naked, having only a waist wrap or a cloak. How should they pray over him (the deceased), while they are naked and have no extra garment to shroud him with?” Imam (a.s) said: “A grave should be dug for him, and he should be placed in his burial niche (lahd), and bricks should be placed over his private parts, so that his private area is covered with the bricks and stones. Then the prayer should be performed over him, and then he should be buried.” I asked: “So, the prayer is not to be performed over him, if he has already been buried?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, the prayer is not performed over the deceased after he has been buried, nor is it performed over him while he is naked, until his private parts are covered.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Seeking Guidance
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from Amr ibn Hurayth. He said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Pray two rak’ahs and seek guidance (istikharah) from Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, for by Allah (swt), no Muslim ever seeks guidance from Allah (swt) except that Allah (swt) surely grants him the best outcome.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ بْنِ سُوَيْدٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ حُرَيْثٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« صَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ اِسْتَخِرِ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَوَاَللَّهِ مَا اِسْتَخَارَ اَللَّهَ مُسْلِمٌ إِلاَّ خَارَ اَللَّهُ لَهُ اَلْبَتَّةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from Amr ibn Hurayth. He said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Pray two rak’ahs and seek guidance (istikharah) from Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, for by Allah (swt), no Muslim ever seeks guidance from Allah (swt) except that Allah (swt) surely grants him the best outcome.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Seeking Guidance
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Uthman ibn Isa from ‘Amru ibn Shimr from Jabir from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “When Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, intended to perform the Hajj, or the ‘Umrah, or to engage in buying, or selling, or manumission (of a slave); Imam al-Husayn (a.s) would perform ablution, then he would pray the two units (rak‘ahs) of the prayer of Istikharah, in which He (a.s) would recite Surah al-Hashr and Surah al-Rahman. Then He (a.s) would recite ‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (the two chapters of refuge) and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas). Then Imam al-Husayn (a.s) would say: “O’ Allah (swt), if such and such a matter is good for me in my religion, my worldly life, my hereafter, my immediate affairs, and my future ones, then facilitate it for me in the best and most beautiful manner. O’ Allah (swt), and if such and such a matter is bad for me in my religion, my worldly life, my hereafter, my immediate affairs, and my future ones, then turn it away from me in the best manner. My Lord (swt), determine for me what is right, even if I dislike it or my soul refuses it.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ إِذَا هَمَّ بِأَمْرِ حَجٍّ أَوْ عُمْرَةٍ أَوْ بَيْعٍ أَوْ شِرَاءٍ أَوْ عِتْقٍ تَطَهَّرَ ثُمَّ صَلَّى رَكْعَتَيِ اَلاِسْتِخَارَةِ يَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا سُورَةَ اَلْحَشْرِ وَ سُورَةَ اَلرَّحْمَنِ ثُمَّ يَقْرَأُ اَلْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ« اَللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كَانَ كَذَا وَ كَذَا خَيْراً لِي فِي دِينِي وَ دُنْيَايَ وَ آخِرَتِي وَ عَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَ آجِلِهِ فَيَسِّرْهُ لِي عَلَى أَحْسَنِ اَلْوُجُوهِ وَ أَجْمَلِهَا اَللَّهُمَّ وَإِنْ كَانَ كَذَا وَ كَذَا شَرّاً لِي فِي دِينِي وَ دُنْيَايَ وَآخِرَتِي وَعَاجِلِ أَمْرِي وَآجِلِهِ فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي عَلَى أَحْسَنِ اَلْوُجُوهِ رَبِّ اِعْزِمْ لِي عَلَى رُشْدِي وَ إِنْ كَرِهْتُ ذَلِكَ أَوْ أَبَتْهُ نَفْسِي»»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Uthman ibn Isa from ‘Amru ibn Shimr from Jabir from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “When Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, intended to perform the Hajj, or the ‘Umrah, or to engage in buying, or selling, or manumission (of a slave); Imam al-Husayn (a.s) would perform ablution, then he would pray the two units (rak‘ahs) of the prayer of Istikharah, in which He (a.s) would recite Surah al-Hashr and Surah al-Rahman. Then He (a.s) would recite ‘al-Mu‘awwidhatayn’ (the two chapters of refuge) and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas). Then Imam al-Husayn (a.s) would say: “O’ Allah (swt), if such and such a matter is good for me in my religion, my worldly life, my hereafter, my immediate affairs, and my future ones, then facilitate it for me in the best and most beautiful manner. O’ Allah (swt), and if such and such a matter is bad for me in my religion, my worldly life, my hereafter, my immediate affairs, and my future ones, then turn it away from me in the best manner. My Lord (swt), determine for me what is right, even if I dislike it or my soul refuses it.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Seeking Guidance
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal, who said:
Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm asked Aba al-Hasan (a.s) on behalf of Ibn Asbat. He (Al-Hasan) said to Imam (a.s): “What do you see for him?”, and Ibn Asbat was present, and we were all together, (Al-Hasan asked) “Should he (ibn Asbat) travel by sea or by land to Egypt?” Then he (Al-Hasan) informed Imam (a.s) about the condition of the land route. Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Go to the mosque at a time other than the time of obligatory prayer. Then pray two units (rak‘ahs) and seek the guidance of Allah (swt) (istikharah) one hundred times. Then look at what settles in your heart, and act upon it.” Al-Hasan said to Imam (a.s): “The land route is more beloved to me for him (ibn Asbat).” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “And to me as well.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ قَالَ: سَأَلَ اَلْحَسَنُ بْنُ اَلْجَهْمِ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لاِبْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ فَقَالَ لَهُ مَا تَرَى لَهُ وَ اِبْنُ أَسْبَاطٍ حَاضِرٌ وَ نَحْنُ جَمِيعاً يَرْكَبُ اَلْبَحْرَ أَوِ اَلْبَرَّ إِلَى مِصْرَ وَ أَخْبَرَهُ بِخَبَرِ طَرِيقِ اَلْبَرِّ فَقَالَ« فَأْتِ اَلْمَسْجِدَ فِي غَيْرِ وَقْتِ صَلاَةٍ فَرِيضَةٍ فَصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ اِسْتَخِرِ اَللَّهَ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ ثُمَّ اُنْظُرْ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ يَقَعُ فِي قَلْبِكَ فَاعْمَلْ بِهِ» قَالَ لَهُ اَلْحَسَنُ اَلْبَرُّ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ لَهُ قَالَ« وَ إِلَيَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm asked Aba al-Hasan (a.s) on behalf of Ibn Asbat. He (Al-Hasan) said to Imam (a.s): “What do you see for him?”, and Ibn Asbat was present, and we were all together, (Al-Hasan asked) “Should he (ibn Asbat) travel by sea or by land to Egypt?” Then he (Al-Hasan) informed Imam (a.s) about the condition of the land route. Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Go to the mosque at a time other than the time of obligatory prayer. Then pray two units (rak‘ahs) and seek the guidance of Allah (swt) (istikharah) one hundred times. Then look at what settles in your heart, and act upon it.” Al-Hasan said to Imam (a.s): “The land route is more beloved to me for him (ibn Asbat).” Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “And to me as well.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Seeking Guidance
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Murazim said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When one of you intends something, let him pray two units (rak’ahs), then praise Allah (swt) and commend Him (azj), then send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and his family (a.s), and then say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), if this matter is good for me in my religion and my worldly life, then facilitate it for me and ordain it for me; and if it is otherwise, then turn it away from me.’” I asked Imam (a.s): “What should I recite in them (the two rak’ahs)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Recite in them whatever you wish, and if you wish, you may recite ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) and ‘Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ مُرَازِمٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ :«إِذَا أَرَادَ أَحَدُكُمْ شَيْئاً فَلْيُصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ لْيَحْمَدِ اَللَّهَ وَ لْيُثْنِ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِهِ وَ يَقُولُ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كَانَ هَذَا اَلْأَمْرُ خَيْراً لِي فِي دِينِي وَ دُنْيَايَ فَيَسِّرْهُ لِي وَقَدِّرْهُ وَإِنْ كَانَ عَلَى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي» فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ أَقْرَأُ فِيهِمَا فَقَالَ« اِقْرَأْ فِيهِمَا مَا شِئْتَ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ قَرَأْتَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Murazim said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When one of you intends something, let him pray two units (rak’ahs), then praise Allah (swt) and commend Him (azj), then send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and his family (a.s), and then say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), if this matter is good for me in my religion and my worldly life, then facilitate it for me and ordain it for me; and if it is otherwise, then turn it away from me.’” I asked Imam (a.s): “What should I recite in them (the two rak’ahs)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Recite in them whatever you wish, and if you wish, you may recite ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) and ‘Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Seeking Guidance
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Amru ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “At times I intend to do something, but two thoughts arise within me; one commands me to proceed, and the other forbids me.” Imam (a.s) said: “When you are in such a situation, then pray two units (rak‘ahs) and seek Allah’s (swt) guidance (istikharah) one hundred and one times. Then look to whichever of the two matters is more prudent for you, and do it, for indeed the good is in it, if Allah (swt) wills. And let your istikharah be in a state of well-being, for indeed it may happen that a man’s best outcome lies in cutting off of his hand, death of his child, or loss of wealth.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ خَلَفِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رُبَّمَا أَرَدْتُ اَلْأَمْرَ فَيَفْرُقُ مِنِّي فَرِيقَانِ أَحَدُهُمَا يَأْمُرُنِي وَ اَلْآخَرُ يَنْهَانِي فَقَالَ« إِذَا كُنْتَ كَذَلِكَ فَصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ اِسْتَخِرِ اَللَّهَ مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ وَ مَرَّةً ثُمَّ اُنْظُرْ أَحْزَمَ اَلْأَمْرَيْنِ لَكَ فَافْعَلْهُ فَإِنَّ اَلْخَيْرَ فِيهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ وَ لْتَكُنِ اِسْتِخَارَتُكَ فِي عَافِيَةٍ فَإِنَّهُ رُبَّمَا خِيرَ لِلرَّجُلِ فِي قَطْعِ يَدِهِ وَ مَوْتِ وَلَدِهِ وَ ذَهَابِ مَالِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Isa, from Amru ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “At times I intend to do something, but two thoughts arise within me; one commands me to proceed, and the other forbids me.” Imam (a.s) said: “When you are in such a situation, then pray two units (rak‘ahs) and seek Allah’s (swt) guidance (istikharah) one hundred and one times. Then look to whichever of the two matters is more prudent for you, and do it, for indeed the good is in it, if Allah (swt) wills. And let your istikharah be in a state of well-being, for indeed it may happen that a man’s best outcome lies in cutting off of his hand, death of his child, or loss of wealth.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Seeking Guidance
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from more than one person, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Hashimi, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When you intend to undertake a matter, take six slips (of paper). Write on three of them: ‘In the Name of Allah (swt), the All-Beneficent, the All-Merciful. A choice (khirah) from Allah (swt), the Mighty, the Wise, for (so-and-so) son of (so-and-so): Do it.’ And on the other three write: ‘In the Name of Allah (swt), the All-Beneficent, the All-Merciful. A choice (khirah) from Allah (swt), the Mighty, the Wise, for (so-and-so) son of (so-and-so): Do not do it.’ Then place them beneath your prayer mat. When you finish, perform a prostration and say in it one hundred times: ‘I seek the best (khirah) from Allah (swt) through His (azj) mercy a choice in well-being.’ Then sit upright and say: “O’ Allah (swt), choose for me in all of my affairs with ease from You (azj) and with well-being.” Then reach your hand toward the slips, mix them up thoroughly, and draw one out. If three consecutive slips come out that say ‘Do it,’ then proceed with the matter you intended. And if three consecutive slips come out that say ‘Do not do it,’ then do not proceed with it. And if one says ‘Do it’ and the other says ‘Do not do it,’ then continue drawing from the slips until you have drawn five. Then look at the majority among them and act according to it. Leave the sixth; you do not need it.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْبَصْرِيِّ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ خَارِجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَرَدْتَ أَمْراً فَخُذْسِتَّ رِقَاعٍ فَاكْتُبْ فِي ثَلاَثٍ مِنْهَا« بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ» خِيَرَةٌ« مِنَ اَللّٰهِ اَلْعَزِيزِ اَلْحَكِيمِ» لِفُلاَنِ بْنِ فُلاَنَةَ اِفْعَلْهُ وَ فِي ثَلاَثٍ مِنْهَا «بِسْمِ اَللّٰهِ اَلرَّحْمٰنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ» خِيَرَةٌ« مِنَ اَللّٰهِ اَلْعَزِيزِ اَلْحَكِيمِ» لِفُلاَنِ بْنِ فُلاَنَةَ لاَ تَفْعَلْ ثُمَّ ضَعْهَا تَحْتَ مُصَلاَّكَ فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَاسْجُدْ سَجْدَةً وَ قُلْ فِيهَا مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ أَسْتَخِيرُ اَللَّهَ بِرَحْمَتِهِ خِيَرَةً فِي عَافِيَةٍ ثُمَّ اِسْتَوِ جَالِساً وَ قُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ خِرْ لِي فِي جَمِيعِ أُمُورِي فِي يُسْرٍ مِنْكَ وَ عَافِيَةٍ ثُمَّ اِضْرِبْ بِيَدِكَ إِلَى اَلرِّقَاعِ فَشَوِّشْهَا وَ أَخْرِجْ وَاحِدَةً فَإِنْ خَرَجَ ثَلاَثٌ مُتَوَالِيَاتٌ اِفْعَلْ فَافْعَلْ ذَلِكَ اَلْأَمْرَ اَلَّذِي تُرِيدُهُ وَ إِنْ خَرَجَ ثَلاَثٌ مُتَوَالِيَاتٌ لاَ تَفْعَلْ فَلاَ تَفْعَلْهُ وَ إِنْ خَرَجَتْ وَاحِدَةٌ اِفْعَلْ وَ اَلْأُخْرَى لاَ تَفْعَلْ فَأَخْرِجْ مِنَ اَلرِّقَاعِ إِلَى خَمْسٍ فَانْظُرْ أَكْثَرَهَا فَاعْمَلْ بِهِ وَ دَعِ اَلسَّادِسَةَ لاَ تَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهَا»

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Seeking Guidance
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, who transmitted it with a raised chain from the Imams (a.s):
Imam (a.s) said to one of his companions, who had asked Imam (a.s) about a matter he wished to proceed in, but could not find anyone to consult so what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: “Consult your Lord (azj).” He said to Imam (a.s): “How?” Imam (a.s) replied: “Intend the need within yourself, and write two slips on one write ‘No’ and on the other write ‘Yes.’ Place them into two pellets of clay. Then pray two units (rak’ahs) and place the two pellets beneath your prayer garment, and say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), I consult You (azj) regarding this matter of mine, and You (azj) are the best of those who are consulted and who give counsel. So guide me to that which contains righteousness and a good outcome.’ Then insert your hand (into the pellets). If the one you draw says ‘Yes’, then proceed with it. And if it says ‘No’, then do not proceed. This is how you consult your Lord (azj).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ رَفَعَهُ عَنْهُمْ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ قَالَ لِبَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ وَ قَدْ سَأَلَهُ عَنِ اَلْأَمْرِ يَمْضِي فِيهِ وَ لاَ يَجِدُ أَحَداً يُشَاوِرُهُ فَكَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ« شَاوِرْ رَبَّكَ» قَالَ فَقَالَ لَهُ كَيْفَ قَالَ« اِنْوِ اَلْحَاجَةَ فِي نَفْسِكَ وَ اُكْتُبْ رُقْعَتَيْنِ فِي وَاحِدَةٍ لاَ وَ فِي وَاحِدَةٍ نَعَمْ وَ اِجْعَلْهُمَا فِي بُنْدُقَتَيْنِ مِنْ طِينٍ ثُمَّ صَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ اِجْعَلْهُمَا تَحْتَ ذَيْلِكَ وَ قُلْ يَا اَللَّهُ إِنِّي أُشَاوِرُكَ فِي أَمْرِي هَذَا وَ أَنْتَ خَيْرُ مُسْتَشَارٍ وَ مُشِيرٍ فَأَشِرْ عَلَيَّ مَا فِيهِ صَلاَحٌ وَ حُسْنُ عَاقِبَةٍ ثُمَّ أَدْخِلْ يَدَكَ فَإِنْ كَانَ فِيهَا نَعَمْ فَافْعَلْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ فِيهَا لاَ لاَ تَفْعَلْ هَكَذَا تُشَاوِرُ رَبَّكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, who transmitted it with a raised chain from the Imams (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said to one of his companions, who had asked Imam (a.s) about a matter he wished to proceed in, but could not find anyone to consult so what should he do? Imam (a.s) said: “Consult your Lord (azj).” He said to Imam (a.s): “How?” Imam (a.s) replied: “Intend the need within yourself, and write two slips on one write ‘No’ and on the other write ‘Yes.’ Place them into two pellets of clay. Then pray two units (rak’ahs) and place the two pellets beneath your prayer garment, and say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), I consult You (azj) regarding this matter of mine, and You (azj) are the best of those who are consulted and who give counsel. So guide me to that which contains righteousness and a good outcome.’ Then insert your hand (into the pellets). If the one you draw says ‘Yes’, then proceed with it. And if it says ‘No’, then do not proceed. This is how you consult your Lord (azj).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Seeking Guidance
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muawiyah ibn Mayasrah narrated from Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “No servant seeks Allah’s (swt) guidance (istikharah) seventy times, with this form of istikharah, except Allah (swt) directs him toward what is good. He (the seeker) should say: ‘O’ Most Seeing of those who see, O’ Most Hearing of those who hear, O’ Swiftest of those who take account, O’ Most Merciful of the merciful, O’ Wisest of those who judge, send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the people of his household, and choose for me in such and such matter.’”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« مَا اِسْتَخَارَ اَللَّهَ عَبْدٌ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً بِهَذِهِ اَلاِسْتِخَارَةِ إِلاَّ رَمَاهُ اَللَّهُ بِالْخَيْرِ يَقُولُ يَا أَبْصَرَ اَلنَّاظِرِينَ وَ يَا أَسْمَعَ اَلسَّامِعِينَ وَ يَا أَسْرَعَ اَلْحَاسِبِينَ وَ يَا أَرْحَمَ اَلرَّاحِمِينَ وَ يَا أَحْكَمَ اَلْحَاكِمِينَ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ وَ خِرْ لِي فِي كَذَا وَ كَذَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Muawiyah ibn Mayasrah narrated from Imam (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “No servant seeks Allah’s (swt) guidance (istikharah) seventy times, with this form of istikharah, except Allah (swt) directs him toward what is good. He (the seeker) should say: ‘O’ Most Seeing of those who see, O’ Most Hearing of those who hear, O’ Swiftest of those who take account, O’ Most Merciful of the merciful, O’ Wisest of those who judge, send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the people of his household, and choose for me in such and such matter.’”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Needs
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sama’ah ibn Mihran narrated from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Indeed, when one of you falls ill, he calls for the physician and gives him (payment), and when he has a need from a ruler, he bribes the doorkeeper and gives him something. But if one of you, when a matter becomes overwhelming for him, Were to turn to your Lord (swt), the Exalted, performing purification, giving charity whether little or much, then entering the mosque and praying two units (rak’ahs), praising Allah (swt) and commending Him (azj), and sending blessings upon the Prophet (saws) and his family, and then said: ‘O’ Allah (swt), if You (azj) grant me recovery from my illness, or return me safely from my journey, or protect me from that which I fear such and such then You (azj) will surely grant me that,’ Allah (swt) would indeed grant it to him. And this is the binding oath, and it is what Allah (swt), the Exalted, has made obligatory upon him in gratitude.”
arabicText: رَوَى سَمَاعَةُ بْنُ مِهْرَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ إِذَا مَرِضَ دَعَا اَلطَّبِيبَ وَأَعْطَاهُ وَ إِذَا كَانَ لَهُ حَاجَةٌ إِلَى سُلْطَانٍ رَشَا اَلْبَوَّابَ وَ أَعْطَاهُ وَ لَوْ أَنَّ أَحَدَكُمْ إِذَا فَدَحَهُ أَمْرٌ فَزِعَ إِلَى اَللَّهِ تَعَالَى فَتَطَهَّرَ وَ تَصَدَّقَ بِصَدَقَةٍ قَلَّتْ أَوْ كَثُرَتْ ثُمَّ دَخَلَ اَلْمَسْجِدَ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَحَمِدَ اَللَّهَ وَ أَثْنَى عَلَيْهِ وَ صَلَّى عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ وَ أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنْ عَافَيْتَنِي مِنْ مَرَضِي أَوْ رَدَدْتَنِي مِنْ سَفَرِي أَوْ عَافَيْتَنِي مِمَّا أَخَافُ مِنْ كَذَا وَكَذَا إِلاَّ آتَاهُ اَللَّهُ ذَلِكَ وَ هِيَ اَلْيَمِينُ اَلْوَاجِبَةُ وَ مَا جَعَلَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ فِي اَلشُّكْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sama’ah ibn Mihran narrated from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Indeed, when one of you falls ill, he calls for the physician and gives him (payment), and when he has a need from a ruler, he bribes the doorkeeper and gives him something. But if one of you, when a matter becomes overwhelming for him, Were to turn to your Lord (swt), the Exalted, performing purification, giving charity whether little or much, then entering the mosque and praying two units (rak’ahs), praising Allah (swt) and commending Him (azj), and sending blessings upon the Prophet (saws) and his family, and then said: ‘O’ Allah (swt), if You (azj) grant me recovery from my illness, or return me safely from my journey, or protect me from that which I fear such and such then You (azj) will surely grant me that,’ Allah (swt) would indeed grant it to him. And this is the binding oath, and it is what Allah (swt), the Exalted, has made obligatory upon him in gratitude.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Needs
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Suhayl from their shaykhs, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When you are faced with an important need before Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, then fast for three consecutive days; Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. When it is Friday, Allah (swt) willing, perform ghusl and wear a new garment, then ascend to the highest room in your house and pray two units (rak’ahs) therein. Then raise your hands toward the sky and say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), I have come to Your courtyard, Acknowledging Your Oneness and Your Self-Sufficiency, And knowing that none is capable of fulfilling my need besides You (azj). And You (azj) know, O’ my Lord (azj), that every time Your blessings increase upon me, my neediness toward You (azj) intensifies. A worry (such-and-such) has struck me, You (azj) are aware of its removal without being taught, all-encompassing without effort. So I ask You (azj) by Your Name which, when You (azj) placed it upon the mountains, they were crushed; And when You (azj) placed it upon the sky, it split; And when You (azj) placed it upon the stars, they scattered; And when You (azj) placed it upon the earth, it was spread out. And I ask You (azj) by the truth which You (azj) have placed with (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the Imams (a.s) (and you name them to their end), I ask that You (azj) send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and his family (a.s), And that You (azj) fulfill my need, And ease its difficulty for me, And suffice me in its concern. So if You (azj) do so, then to You (azj) belongs all praise; And if You (azj) do not do so, then to You (azj) belongs all praise, You (azj) are neither unjust in Your judgment, nor accused in Your decree, nor feared in Your justice.’” (Imam (a.s) then continued) “Then place your cheek on the ground and say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), indeed Yunus son of Matta, Your servant, called upon You (a.s) from within the belly of the whale, and he was Your servant, and You (a.s) answered him. And I am Your servant; I call upon You (a.s), so answer me.’” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When I have a need, I supplicate with this supplication, and whilst I return, it has already been fulfilled.”
arabicText: رَوَى مُوسَى بْنُ اَلْقَاسِمِ اَلْبَجَلِيُّ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ بْنِ يَحْيَى وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُهَيْلٍ عَنْ أَشْيَاخِهِمَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا حَضَرَتْ لَكَ حَاجَةٌ مُهِمَّةٌ إِلَى اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَصُمْ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ مُتَوَالِيَةٍ اَلْأَرْبِعَاءَ وَ اَلْخَمِيسَ وَ اَلْجُمُعَةَ فَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ اَلْجُمُعَةِ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ فَاغْتَسِلْ وَ اِلْبَسْ ثَوْباً جَدِيداً ثُمَّ اِصْعَدْ إِلَى أَعْلَى بَيْتٍ فِي دَارِكَ وَ صَلِّ فِيهِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ اِرْفَعْ يَدَيْكَ إِلَى اَلسَّمَاءِ ثُمَّ قُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي حَلَلْتُ بِسَاحَتِكَ لِمَعْرِفَتِي بِوَحْدَانِيَّتِكَ وَ صَمَدَانِيَّتِكَ وَ أَنَّهُ لاَ قَادِرَ عَلَى قَضَاءِ حَاجَتِي غَيْرُكَ وَ قَدْ عَلِمْتَ يَا رَبِّ أَنَّهُ كُلَّمَا تَظَاهَرَتْ نِعَمُكَ عَلَيَّ اِشْتَدَّتْ فَاقَتِي إِلَيْكَ وَ قَدْ طَرَقَنِي هَمُّ كَذَا وَ أَنْتَ بِكَشْفِهِ عَالِمٌ غَيْرُ مُعَلَّمٍ وَاسِعٌ غَيْرُ مُتَكَلِّفٍ فَأَسْأَلُكَ بِاسْمِكَ اَلَّذِي وَضَعْتَهُ عَلَى اَلْجِبَالِ فَنُسِفَتْ وَ وَضَعْتَهُ عَلَى اَلسَّمَاءِ فَانْشَقَّتْ وَ عَلَى اَلنُّجُومِ فَانْتَشَرَتْ وَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَسُطِحَتْ وَ أَسْأَلُكَ بِالْحَقِّ اَلَّذِي جَعَلْتَهُ عِنْدَ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ اَلْأَئِمَّةِ وَ تُسَمِّيهِمْ إِلَى آخِرِهِمْ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ وَ أَنْ تَقْضِيَ حَاجَتِي وَ أَنْ تُيَسِّرَ لِي عُسْرَهَا وَ تَكْفِيَنِي مُهِمَّهَا فَإِنْ فَعَلْتَ فَلَكَ اَلْحَمْدُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ فَلَكَ اَلْحَمْدُ غَيْرَ جَائِرٍ فِي حُكْمِكَ وَ لاَ مُتَّهَمٍ فِي قَضَائِكَ وَ لاَ حَائِفٍ فِي عَدْلِكَ وَ تُلْصِقُ خَدَّكَ بِالْأَرْضِ وَ تَقُولُ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنَّ يُونُسَ بْنَ مَتَّى عَبْدُكَ دَعَاكَ فِي بَطْنِ اَلْحُوتِ وَ هُوَ عَبْدُكَ فَاسْتَجَبْتَ لَهُ وَ أَنَا عَبْدُكَ أَدْعُوكَ فَاسْتَجِبْ لِي» ثُمَّ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ «إِذَا كَانَتْ لِيَ اَلْحَاجَةُ فَأَدْعُو بِهَذَا اَلدُّعَاءِ فَأَرْجِعُ وَ قَدْ قُضِيَتْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Musa ibn al-Qasim al-Bajali narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Suhayl from their shaykhs, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When you are faced with an important need before Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, then fast for three consecutive days; Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. When it is Friday, Allah (swt) willing, perform ghusl and wear a new garment, then ascend to the highest room in your house and pray two units (rak’ahs) therein. Then raise your hands toward the sky and say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), I have come to Your courtyard, Acknowledging Your Oneness and Your Self-Sufficiency, And knowing that none is capable of fulfilling my need besides You (azj). And You (azj) know, O’ my Lord (azj), that every time Your blessings increase upon me, my neediness toward You (azj) intensifies. A worry (such-and-such) has struck me, You (azj) are aware of its removal without being taught, all-encompassing without effort. So I ask You (azj) by Your Name which, when You (azj) placed it upon the mountains, they were crushed; And when You (azj) placed it upon the sky, it split; And when You (azj) placed it upon the stars, they scattered; And when You (azj) placed it upon the earth, it was spread out. And I ask You (azj) by the truth which You (azj) have placed with (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the Imams (a.s) (and you name them to their end), I ask that You (azj) send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and his family (a.s), And that You (azj) fulfill my need, And ease its difficulty for me, And suffice me in its concern. So if You (azj) do so, then to You (azj) belongs all praise; And if You (azj) do not do so, then to You (azj) belongs all praise, You (azj) are neither unjust in Your judgment, nor accused in Your decree, nor feared in Your justice.’” (Imam (a.s) then continued) “Then place your cheek on the ground and say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), indeed Yunus son of Matta, Your servant, called upon You (a.s) from within the belly of the whale, and he was Your servant, and You (a.s) answered him. And I am Your servant; I call upon You (a.s), so answer me.’” Then Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When I have a need, I supplicate with this supplication, and whilst I return, it has already been fulfilled.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Needs
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Duwail from Muqatil, who said:
I said to Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, teach me a supplication for the fulfillment of needs.” Imam (a.s) said: “When you have an important need from Allah (swt), perform ghusl (ritual bathing), wear your cleanest clothes, and apply some perfume. Then go out under the open sky and pray two units (rak’ahs) of prayer. Begin the prayer by reciting the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) fifteen times. Then bow (for rukuh) and recite it fifteen times in the same manner as the prayer of al-Tasbih, except that the recitation is fifteen times. When you finish with salam, recite it again (Surah Ikhlas) fifteen times. Then go into prostration (sujud) and say in your prostration: ‘O’ Allah (swt), every object of worship from beneath Your Throne to the depth of Your earth is false except You (azj), for indeed You (azj) are Allah (swt), the True, the Clear. Fulfill for me the need of such and such this very hour, this very hour!’ And be insistent in what you seek.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ دُوَيْلٍ عَنْ مُقَاتِلٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ عَلِّمْنِي دُعَاءً لِقَضَاءِ اَلْحَوَائِجِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَتْ لَكَ حَاجَةٌ إِلَى اَللَّهِ مُهِمَّةٌ فَاغْتَسِلْ وَاِلْبَسْ أَنْظَفَ ثِيَابِكَ وَ شَمَّ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلطِّيبِ ثُمَّ اُبْرُزْ تَحْتَ اَلسَّمَاءِ فَصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ تَفْتَتِحُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَتَقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ قُلْ هُوَ اَللَّهُ أَحَدٌ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ مَرَّةً ثُمَّ تَرْكَعُ فَتَقْرَأُ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ مَرَّةً عَلَى مِثَالِ صَلاَةِ اَلتَّسْبِيحِ غَيْرَ أَنَّ اَلْقِرَاءَةَ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ مَرَّةً فَإِذَا سَلَّمْتَ فَاقْرَأْهَا خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ مَرَّةً ثُمَّ تَسْجُدُ وَ تَقُولُ فِي سُجُودِكَ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنَّ كُلَّ مَعْبُودٍ مِنْ لَدُنْ عَرْشِكَ إِلَى قَرَارِ أَرْضِكَ فَهُوَ بَاطِلٌ سِوَاكَ فَإِنَّكَ أَنْتَ اَللَّهُ اَلْحَقُّ اَلْمُبِينُ اِقْضِ لِي حَاجَةَ كَذَا وَ كَذَا اَلسَّاعَةَ اَلسَّاعَةَ وَ تُلِحُّ فِيمَا أَرَدْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Duwail from Muqatil, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, teach me a supplication for the fulfillment of needs.” Imam (a.s) said: “When you have an important need from Allah (swt), perform ghusl (ritual bathing), wear your cleanest clothes, and apply some perfume. Then go out under the open sky and pray two units (rak’ahs) of prayer. Begin the prayer by reciting the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) fifteen times. Then bow (for rukuh) and recite it fifteen times in the same manner as the prayer of al-Tasbih, except that the recitation is fifteen times. When you finish with salam, recite it again (Surah Ikhlas) fifteen times. Then go into prostration (sujud) and say in your prostration: ‘O’ Allah (swt), every object of worship from beneath Your Throne to the depth of Your earth is false except You (azj), for indeed You (azj) are Allah (swt), the True, the Clear. Fulfill for me the need of such and such this very hour, this very hour!’ And be insistent in what you seek.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Gratitude
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj from Harun ibn Kharijah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said to me regarding the ‘Prayer of Gratitude’ (salat al-shukr): “When Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, bestows a blessing upon you, then pray two units (rak’ahs). In the first, recite the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) And in the second (rak’ah), recite the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun). In the first rak’ah, during your bowing (rukuh) and prostration (sujud), say: ‘All praise is due to Allah (swt) thanks, thanks, and praise.’ And in the second rak’ah, during your bowing and prostration, say: ‘All praise is due to Allah (swt) who answered my supplication and granted me my request.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْمَاعِيلَ اَلسَّرَّاجِ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ خَارِجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي فِي صَلاَةِ اَلشُّكْرِ« إِذَا أَنْعَمَ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَيْكَ بِنِعْمَةٍ فَصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ تَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْأُولَى بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ تَقْرَأُ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ «قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ» وَ تَقُولُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى فِي رُكُوعِكَ وَ سُجُودِكَ: اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ شُكْراً شُكْراً وَ حَمْداً وَ تَقُولُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ فِي رُكُوعِكَ وَ سُجُودِكَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ اَلَّذِي اِسْتَجَابَ دُعَائِي وَ أَعْطَانِي مَسْأَلَتِي»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ismail from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj from Harun ibn Kharijah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said to me regarding the ‘Prayer of Gratitude’ (salat al-shukr): “When Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, bestows a blessing upon you, then pray two units (rak’ahs). In the first, recite the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) And in the second (rak’ah), recite the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Qul Ya Ayyuha al-Kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun). In the first rak’ah, during your bowing (rukuh) and prostration (sujud), say: ‘All praise is due to Allah (swt) thanks, thanks, and praise.’ And in the second rak’ah, during your bowing and prostration, say: ‘All praise is due to Allah (swt) who answered my supplication and granted me my request.’”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Day of Mab‘ath and the Night of the Middle of Sha‘ban
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Muhammad, who transmitted it with a raised chain from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When it is the night of the middle of Shaban, pray four rak’ahs. In each rak’ah, recite ‘al-Hamd’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) one hundred times. When you have finished, say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), indeed I am in need before You (azj), And I seek refuge in You (azj), And I fear from You (azj), And I seek protection through You (azj). My Lord (azj), do not change my name, And do not alter my body. My Lord (azj), do not burden me with severe trials, And do not let my enemies gloat over me. I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, And I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, And I seek refuge in Your mercy from Your chastisement, And I seek refuge in You (azj), from You (azj). Exalted is Your praise. You (azj) are as You (azj) have praised Yourself, and above what those who speak may say.’” He (Ibn Muhammad) said “And Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, also said: ‘On the twenty-seventh day of Rajab, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was commissioned (nubbi’a - received revelation for the first time). Whoever prays on that day, at any time he wishes, twelve rak‘ahs; reciting in each rak‘ah the ‘Umm al-Kitab’ (Surah Al Fatihah) and any surah that is easy for him, And when he finishes and gives the salam, he remains seated in his place. Then recites the ‘Umm al-Kitab’ (Surah Al Fatihah), (four times). And the three chapters of seeking refuge (al-Mu‘awwidhat: ‘Qul A‘udhu bi-Rabbi al-Falaq’ (Surah al-Falaq), (four times). And ‘Qul A‘udhu bi-Rabbi al-Nas’ (Surah an-Nas)), (four times). Then, while still seated, he says: ‘There is no God but Allah (swt), Allah (swt) is the Greatest, (four times). praise be to Allah (swt), glory be to Allah (swt), (four times). And there is no power and no strength except with Allah (swt)’ (four times). Then he says: ‘Allah (swt), Allah (swt) is my Lord (azj), and I do not associate anything with Him (azj)’, (four times). Then he supplicates, and he will not ask for anything except that he will be answered in every need, unless he prays for a calamity upon a people or for the severing of family ties.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ رَفَعَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كَانَ لَيْلَةُ اَلنِّصْفِ مِنْ شَعْبَانَ فَصَلِّ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ تَقْرَأُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ فَإِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَقُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي إِلَيْكَ فَقِيرٌ وَ إِنِّي عَائِذٌ بِكَ وَ مِنْكَ خَائِفٌ وَ بِكَ مُسْتَجِيرٌ رَبِّ لاَ تُبَدِّلِ اِسْمِي وَ لاَ تُغَيِّرْ جِسْمِي رَبِّ لاَ تُجْهِدْ بَلاَئِي وَ لاَ تُشْمِتْ بِي أَعْدَائِي أَعُوذُ بِعَفْوِكَ مِنْ عِقَابِكَ وَ أَعُوذُ بِرِضَاكَ مِنْ سَخَطِكَ وَ أَعُوذُ بِرَحْمَتِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِكَ وَ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْكَ جَلَّ ثَنَاؤُكَ أَنْتَ كَمَا أَثْنَيْتَ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ وَ فَوْقَ مَا يَقُولُ اَلْقَائِلُونَ» قَالَ وَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَوْمُ سَبْعَةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ مِنْ رَجَبٍ نُبِّئَ فِيهِ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ مَنْ صَلَّى فِيهِ أَيَّ وَقْتٍ شَاءَ اِثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً يَقْرَأُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ بِأُمِّ اَلْقُرْآنِ وَسُورَةٍ مِمَّا تَيَسَّرَ فَإِذَا فَرَغَ وَ سَلَّمَ جَلَسَ مَكَانَهُ ثُمَّ قَرَأَ أُمَّ اَلْقُرْآنِ أَرْبَعَ مَرَّاتٍ وَ اَلْمُعَوِّذَاتِ اَلثَّلاَثَ كُلَّ وَاحِدَةٍ أَرْبَعَ مَرَّاتٍ فَإِذَا فَرَغَ وَ هُوَ فِي مَكَانِهِ قَالَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ وَ لاَ حَوْلَ وَ لاَ قُوَّةَ إِلاَّ بِاللَّهِ أَرْبَعَ مَرَّاتٍ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ اَللَّهُ اَللَّهُ رَبِّي وَ لاَ أُشْرِكُ بِهِ شَيْئاً أَرْبَعَ مَرَّاتٍ ثُمَّ يَدْعُو فَلاَ يَدْعُو بِشَيْءٍ إِلاَّ اُسْتُجِيبَ لَهُ فِي كُلِّ حَاجَةٍ إِلاَّ أَنْ يَدْعُوَ فِي جَائِحَةِ قَوْمٍ أَوْ قَطِيعَةِ رَحِمٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Muhammad, who transmitted it with a raised chain from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When it is the night of the middle of Shaban, pray four rak’ahs. In each rak’ah, recite ‘al-Hamd’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas) one hundred times. When you have finished, say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), indeed I am in need before You (azj), And I seek refuge in You (azj), And I fear from You (azj), And I seek protection through You (azj). My Lord (azj), do not change my name, And do not alter my body. My Lord (azj), do not burden me with severe trials, And do not let my enemies gloat over me. I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, And I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, And I seek refuge in Your mercy from Your chastisement, And I seek refuge in You (azj), from You (azj). Exalted is Your praise. You (azj) are as You (azj) have praised Yourself, and above what those who speak may say.’” He (Ibn Muhammad) said “And Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, also said: ‘On the twenty-seventh day of Rajab, the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, was commissioned (nubbi’a - received revelation for the first time). Whoever prays on that day, at any time he wishes, twelve rak‘ahs; reciting in each rak‘ah the ‘Umm al-Kitab’ (Surah Al Fatihah) and any surah that is easy for him, And when he finishes and gives the salam, he remains seated in his place. Then recites the ‘Umm al-Kitab’ (Surah Al Fatihah), (four times). And the three chapters of seeking refuge (al-Mu‘awwidhat: ‘Qul A‘udhu bi-Rabbi al-Falaq’ (Surah al-Falaq), (four times). And ‘Qul A‘udhu bi-Rabbi al-Nas’ (Surah an-Nas)), (four times). Then, while still seated, he says: ‘There is no God but Allah (swt), Allah (swt) is the Greatest, (four times). praise be to Allah (swt), glory be to Allah (swt), (four times). And there is no power and no strength except with Allah (swt)’ (four times). Then he says: ‘Allah (swt), Allah (swt) is my Lord (azj), and I do not associate anything with Him (azj)’, (four times). Then he supplicates, and he will not ask for anything except that he will be answered in every need, unless he prays for a calamity upon a people or for the severing of family ties.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Tasbih and Other Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Bistam from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
A man said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “May I be your ransom, is it proper for a man to embrace his brother?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. Indeed, when the Messenger of Allah (swt), blessings on him and his family, conquered Khaybar, the news came to Him (saws) that Ja’far (a.s) had arrived. So Prophet (saws) said: ‘By Allah (swt), I do not know which of the two gladdens me more; the arrival of Ja’far (a.s) or the conquest of Khaybar’.” Imam (a.s) continued: “It was not long before Ja’far (a.s) arrived. So the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, leapt up, embraced him, and kissed him between his eyes.” The man then said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “The four rak‘ahs, which I have heard the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, commanded Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, to pray?” Imam (a.s) said: “When Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, arrived, Prophet (saws) said to Imam (a.s): ‘O Ja’far, shall I not give you something? Shall I not grant you something? Shall I not bestow something upon you?’” Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) continued: “So the people (around the Prophet (saws)) became attentive, thinking that He (saws) was going to give Ja’far (a.s) gold or silver. Ja’far (a.s) said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah (swt).' Prophet (saws) said: 'Pray four rak‘ahs, whenever you pray them, whatever is between them will be forgiven for you. If you are able to perform them every day, then do so. Otherwise, every two days, or every Friday, or every month, or every year. For indeed, what is between them will be forgiven for you.' Ja’far (a.s) asked: 'How do I pray them?' Prophet (saws) said: 'You begin the prayer, then recite, then say fifteen times while standing: ‘Subhana Allah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu Akbar.’ Then when you bow, say that ten times. And when you raise your head from the bowing, ten times. And when you prostrate, ten times. And when you raise your head from the prostration, ten times. And when you prostrate the second time, ten times. And when you raise your head, ten times. That makes seventy-five (times per rak‘ah), which totals three hundred in four rak‘ahs, and that is one thousand and two hundred. And you recite in every rak‘ah: ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) and ‘Qul Ya ayyuhal-Kafirun’ (Surah al-Kafirun)”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ بِسْطَامَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أَيَلْتَزِمُ اَلرَّجُلُ أَخَاهُ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يَوْمَ اِفْتَتَحَ خَيْبَرَ أَتَاهُ اَلْخَبَرُ أَنَّ جَعْفَراً قَدْ قَدِمَ فَقَالَ« وَ اَللَّهِ مَا أَدْرِي بِأَيِّهِمَا أَنَا أَشَدُّ سُرُوراً أَبِقُدُومِ جَعْفَرٍ أَوْ بِفَتْحِ خَيْبَرَ»» قَالَ« فَلَمْ يَلْبَثْ أَنْ جَاءَ جَعْفَرٌ» قَالَ« فَوَثَبَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَالْتَزَمَهُ وَ قَبَّلَ مَا بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ» قَالَ فَقَالَ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ اَلْأَرْبَعُ اَلرَّكَعَاتِ اَلَّتِي بَلَغَنِي أَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ أَمَرَ جَعْفَراً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَهَا فَقَالَ« لَمَّا قَدِمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ لَهُ« يَا جَعْفَرُ أَ لاَ أُعْطِيكَ أَ لاَ أَمْنَحُكَ أَ لاَ أَحْبُوكَ»» قَالَ« فَتَشَوَّفَ اَلنَّاسُ وَ رَأَوْا أَنَّهُ يُعْطِيهِ ذَهَباً أَوْ فِضَّةً قَالَ بَلَى يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ قَالَ« صَلِّ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ مَتَى مَا صَلَّيْتَهُنَّ غُفِرَ لَكَ مَا بَيْنَهُنَّ إِنِ اِسْتَطَعْتَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ وَ إِلاَّ فَكُلَّ يَوْمَيْنِ أَوْ كُلَّ جُمُعَةٍ أَوْ كُلَّ شَهْرٍ أَوْ كُلَّ سَنَةٍ فَإِنَّهُ يُغْفَرُ لَكَ مَا بَيْنَهُمَا» قَالَ كَيْفَ أُصَلِّيهَا قَالَ« تَفْتَتِحُ اَلصَّلاَةَ ثُمَّ تَقْرَأُ ثُمَّ تَقُولُ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ مَرَّةً وَ أَنْتَ قَائِمٌ سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ فَإِذَا رَكَعْتَ قُلْتَ ذَلِكَ عَشْراً وَ إِذَا رَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ فَعَشْراً وَ إِذَا سَجَدْتَ فَعَشْراً فَإِذَا رَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ فَعَشْراً وَ إِذَا سَجَدْتَ اَلثَّانِيَةَ عَشْراً وَ إِذَا رَفَعْتَ رَأْسَكَ عَشْراً فَذَلِكَ خَمْسٌ وَ سَبْعُونَ يَكُونُ ثَلاَثُمِائَةٍ فِي أَرْبَعِ رَكَعَاتٍ فَهُنَّ أَلْفٌ وَ مِائَتَانِ وَ تَقْرَأُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ بِ «قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَ« قُلْ يٰا أَيُّهَا اَلْكٰافِرُونَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Bistam from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Tasbih and Other Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Ali ibn Asbat from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said:
I (Ibrahim) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “What is the merit for one who performs the ‘Prayer of Ja’far (a.s)’?” Imam (a.s) said: “If his sins were as numerous as the sand of Alij and the foam of the sea, Allah (swt) would forgive them for him.” Ibrahim asked: “Is this for us?” Imam (a.s) said: “And for whom else is it for, if not for you, specifically?” Imam (a.s) said: “And So what should be recited in it?” Ibrahim said: “I alternate through the Qur'an.” Imam (a.s) said: “No. Recite in it: ‘Idha zulzilati al-ardu’ (Surah al-Zalzalah), ‘Idha jaa nasrullah’ (Surah al-Nasr), ‘Inna anzalnahu fi laylat al-qadr’ (Surah al-Qadr), and ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْبِلاَدِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ لِمَنْ صَلَّى صَلاَةَ جَعْفَرٍ قَالَ« لَوْ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ مِثْلُ رَمْلِ عَالِجٍ وَ زَبَدِ اَلْبَحْرِ ذُنُوباً لَغَفَرَ اَللَّهُ لَهُ» قُلْتُ هَذِهِ لَنَا قَالَ« فَلِمَنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ لَكُمْ خَاصَّةً» قَالَ« فَأَيُّ شَيْءٍ تَقْرَأُ فِيهَا» قُلْتُ أَعْتَرِضُ اَلْقُرْآنَ قَالَ «لاَ اِقْرَأْ فِيهَا« إِذٰا زُلْزِلَتِ اَلْأَرْضُ» وَ« إِذٰا جٰاءَ نَصْرُ اَللّٰهِ» وَ« إِنّٰا أَنْزَلْنٰاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ اَلْقَدْرِ» وَ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Ali ibn Asbat from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I (Ibrahim) asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “What is the merit for one who performs the ‘Prayer of Ja’far (a.s)’?” Imam (a.s) said: “If his sins were as numerous as the sand of Alij and the foam of the sea, Allah (swt) would forgive them for him.” Ibrahim asked: “Is this for us?” Imam (a.s) said: “And for whom else is it for, if not for you, specifically?” Imam (a.s) said: “And So what should be recited in it?” Ibrahim said: “I alternate through the Qur'an.” Imam (a.s) said: “No. Recite in it: ‘Idha zulzilati al-ardu’ (Surah al-Zalzalah), ‘Idha jaa nasrullah’ (Surah al-Nasr), ‘Inna anzalnahu fi laylat al-qadr’ (Surah al-Qadr), and ‘Qul huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Tasbih and Other Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Dhurayh, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you wish, perform the ‘Prayer of Tasbih’ (Salat Ja’far al-Tayyar) at night, and if you wish, during the day. And if you wish, while traveling. And if you wish, make it part of your recommended (nafl) prayers. And if you wish, make it as the makeup (qadah) of an obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ عِمْرَانَ عَنْ ذَرِيحٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِنْ شِئْتَ صَلِّ صَلاَةَ اَلتَّسْبِيحِ بِاللَّيْلِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ بِالنَّهَارِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فِي اَلسَّفَرِ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ جَعَلْتَهَا فِي نَوَافِلِكَ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ جَعَلْتَهَا مِنْ قَضَاءِ صَلاَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Yahya ibn Imran, from Dhurayh, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you wish, perform the ‘Prayer of Tasbih’ (Salat Ja’far al-Tayyar) at night, and if you wish, during the day. And if you wish, while traveling. And if you wish, make it part of your recommended (nafl) prayers. And if you wish, make it as the makeup (qadah) of an obligatory prayer.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And in the narration of Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) said: “In the first rak’ah, ‘Idha zulzilati’ (Surah al-Zalzalah) is recited; in the second, recite ‘al-Adiyat’ (Surah Al-'Adiyat); in the third, recite ‘Idha jaa nasrullah’ (Surah al-Nasr); and in the fourth, recite ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas).” I asked: “What is its reward?” Imam (a.s) said: “If his sins were as numerous as the sand of Alij, Allah (swt) would forgive them for him.” Then Imam (a.s) looked at me and said: “This is only for you and your companions.” (meaning our Shia)

thaqalaynSanad: And in the narration of Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him:

Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Muhassin ibn Ahmad from Aban, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “Whoever is in a hurry, may pray the ‘Prayer of Ja’far’ in its basic form, then complete the tasbih (the prescribed glorifications) while he is going about his needs.” (meaning away from the prayer mat)
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ مُحَسِّنِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« مَنْ كَانَ مُسْتَعْجِلاً يُصَلِّي صَلاَةَ جَعْفَرٍ مُجَرَّدَةً ثُمَّ يَقْضِي اَلتَّسْبِيحَ وَ هُوَ ذَاهِبٌ فِي حَوَائِجِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Muhassin ibn Ahmad from Aban, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s) say: “Whoever is in a hurry, may pray the ‘Prayer of Ja’far’ in its basic form, then complete the tasbih (the prescribed glorifications) while he is going about his needs.” (meaning away from the prayer mat)

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Tasbih and Other Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdillah ibn al-Qasim he mentioned it from someone who narrated to him from Abu Said al-Madaini, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me (al-Madaini): “Shall I teach you something to say in the ‘Prayer of Ja’far’?” I said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “When you are in the final prostration of the four rak’ahs, then say once you have completed your tasbih; ‘Glory be to the One who is clothed in might and dignity. Glory be to the One who is wrapped in majesty and ennobled by it. Glory be to the One to whom glorification is not fitting except for Him (azj). Glory be to the One whose knowledge encompasses everything. Glory be to the Possessor of bounty and blessings. Glory be to the Possessor of power and command. O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) by the stations of might in Your Throne, and the utmost of mercy in Your Book, and by Your Greatest Name, and by Your complete words which are fulfilled in truth and justice, send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and his family (a.s), and do for me (such-and-such) and (such-and-such).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ ذَكَرَهُ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ اَلْمَدَائِنِيِّ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« أَ لاَ أُعَلِّمُكَ شَيْئاً تَقُولُهُ فِي صَلاَةِ جَعْفَرٍ» فَقُلْتُ بَلَى فَقَالَ« إِذَا كُنْتَ فِي آخِرِ سَجْدَةٍ مِنَ اَلْأَرْبَعِ رَكَعَاتٍ فَقُلْ إِذَا فَرَغْتَ مِنْ تَسْبِيحِكَ سُبْحَانَ مَنْ لَبِسَ اَلْعِزَّ وَ اَلْوَقَارَ سُبْحَانَ مَنْ تَعَطَّفَ بِالْمَجْدِ وَ تَكَرَّمَ بِهِ سُبْحَانَ مَنْ لاَ يَنْبَغِي اَلتَّسْبِيحُ إِلاَّ لَهُ سُبْحَانَ مَنْ أَحْصَى كُلَّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمُهُ سُبْحَانَ ذِي اَلْمَنِّ وَ اَلنِّعَمِ سُبْحَانَ ذِي اَلْقُدْرَةِ وَ اَلْأَمْرِ اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ بِمَعَاقِدِ اَلْعِزِّ مِنْ عَرْشِكَ وَ مُنْتَهَى اَلرَّحْمَةِ مِنْ كِتَابِكَ وَ اِسْمِكَ اَلْأَعْظَمِ وَ كَلِمَاتِكَ اَلتَّامَّةِ اَلَّتِي تَمَّتْ صِدْقاً وَعَدْلاً صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ وَ اِفْعَلْ بِي كَذَا وَ كَذَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdillah ibn al-Qasim he mentioned it from someone who narrated to him from Abu Said al-Madaini, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me (al-Madaini): “Shall I teach you something to say in the ‘Prayer of Ja’far’?” I said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “When you are in the final prostration of the four rak’ahs, then say once you have completed your tasbih; ‘Glory be to the One who is clothed in might and dignity. Glory be to the One who is wrapped in majesty and ennobled by it. Glory be to the One to whom glorification is not fitting except for Him (azj). Glory be to the One whose knowledge encompasses everything. Glory be to the Possessor of bounty and blessings. Glory be to the Possessor of power and command. O’ Allah (swt), I ask You (azj) by the stations of might in Your Throne, and the utmost of mercy in Your Book, and by Your Greatest Name, and by Your complete words which are fulfilled in truth and justice, send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and his family (a.s), and do for me (such-and-such) and (such-and-such).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Tasbih and Other Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Whoever performs the ‘Prayer of Ja’far’, is it written for him the same reward as that which the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to Ja’far (a.s)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, by Allah (swt).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنِ اَلْحَكَمِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَنْ صَلَّى صَلاَةَ جَعْفَرٍ كُتِبَ لَهُ مِنَ اَلْأَجْرِ مِثْلُ مَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لِجَعْفَرٍ قَالَ« إِي وَ اَللَّهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Whoever performs the ‘Prayer of Ja’far’, is it written for him the same reward as that which the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to Ja’far (a.s)?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, by Allah (swt).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Tasbih and Other Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from Sadan from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever prays four rak’ahs, reciting in each rak’ah ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) fifty times, will not complete the prayer while there remains any sin between him and Allah (swt).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ صَلَّى أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ يَقْرَأُ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» خَمْسِينَ مَرَّةً لَمْ يَنْفَتِلْ وَ بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ اَللَّهِ ذَنْبٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from a group of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from Sadan from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever prays four rak’ahs, reciting in each rak’ah ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah al-Ikhlas) fifty times, will not complete the prayer while there remains any sin between him and Allah (swt).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Tasbih and Other Prayers
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, with his chain of narration from one of the Imams (a.s), peace be upon them:
Imam (a.s) was asked regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “Indeed, the rising at night is strongest in impression and more upright in speech” (Surah Al Muzzammil 73:6) Imam (a.s) said: “It is two rak’ahs after Maghrib in which you recite in the first rak’ah with the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ten (verses) from the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, and the verse of submission (Ayat al-Sukhrah) from His (azj) saying: ‘And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day’ up to His (azj) saying: ‘Surely in that are signs for a people who use reason.’” (Surah Al Baqarah 2:163–164). (Imam (a.s) then continued) “And (recite) fifteen times; ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas), And in the second rak’ah, recite the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah), and Ayat al-Kursi, and the end of Surah al-Baqarah from His (azj) saying: ‘To Allah (swt) belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth’ (Surah Al Baqarah 2:284) until you complete the surah. And recite fifteen times; ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas), Then supplicate after this with whatever you wish.” Imam (a.s) said: “And whoever maintains it regularly, Allah (swt) will write for him with every prayer six hundred thousand pilgrimages (hajj).”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ بِإِسْنَادِهِ عَنْ بَعْضِهِمْ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« إِنَّ نٰاشِئَةَ اَللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئاً وَ أَقْوَمُ قِيلاً» قَالَ« هِيَ رَكْعَتَانِ بَعْدَ اَلْمَغْرِبِ تَقْرَأُ فِي أَوَّلِ رَكْعَةٍ بِفَاتِحَةِ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ عَشْرٍ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَلْبَقَرَةِ وَ آيَةِ اَلسُّخْرَةِ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ« وَإِلٰهُكُمْ إِلٰهٌ وٰاحِدٌ لاٰ إِلٰهَ إِلاّٰ هُوَ اَلرَّحْمٰنُ اَلرَّحِيمُ` إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَاَلْأَرْضِ وَاِخْتِلاٰفِ اَللَّيْلِ وَاَلنَّهٰارِ» إِلَى قَوْلِهِ« لَآ يٰاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ» وَخَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ مَرَّةً« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» وَفِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ آيَةَ اَلْكُرْسِيِّ وَ آخِرَ اَلْبَقَرَةِ مِنْ قَوْلِهِ« لِلّٰهِ مٰا فِي اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَ مٰا فِي اَلْأَرْضِ» إِلَى أَنْ تَخْتِمَ اَلسُّورَةَ وَ خَمْسَ عَشْرَةَ مَرَّةً« قُلْ هُوَ اَللّٰهُ أَحَدٌ» ثُمَّ اُدْعُ بَعْدَ هَذَا بِمَا شِئْتَ» قَالَ« وَ مَنْ وَاظَبَ عَلَيْهِ كَتَبَ اَللَّهُ لَهُ بِكُلِّ صَلاَةٍ سِتَّمِائَةِ أَلْفِ حَجَّةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from Ali ibn Muhammad, with his chain of narration from one of the Imams (a.s), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “Indeed, the rising at night is strongest in impression and more upright in speech” (Surah Al Muzzammil 73:6) Imam (a.s) said: “It is two rak’ahs after Maghrib in which you recite in the first rak’ah with the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah) and ten (verses) from the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, and the verse of submission (Ayat al-Sukhrah) from His (azj) saying: ‘And your God is one God; there is no deity except Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day’ up to His (azj) saying: ‘Surely in that are signs for a people who use reason.’” (Surah Al Baqarah 2:163–164). (Imam (a.s) then continued) “And (recite) fifteen times; ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas), And in the second rak’ah, recite the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah), and Ayat al-Kursi, and the end of Surah al-Baqarah from His (azj) saying: ‘To Allah (swt) belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth’ (Surah Al Baqarah 2:284) until you complete the surah. And recite fifteen times; ‘Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad’ (Surah Ikhlas), Then supplicate after this with whatever you wish.” Imam (a.s) said: “And whoever maintains it regularly, Allah (swt) will write for him with every prayer six hundred thousand pilgrimages (hajj).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer over the Dead
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, both of them heard Aba Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, say:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “There is no prescribed recitation nor fixed supplication in the prayer over the dead, except that you may supplicate with whatever occurs to you. And the one most deserving among the dead for whom supplication should be made, is he for whom the prayer begins with the blessings upon the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ وَزُرَارَةَ أَنَّهُمَا سَمِعَا أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« لَيْسَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ عَلَى اَلْمَيِّتِ قِرَاءَةٌ وَ لاَ دُعَاءٌ مُوَقَّتٌ إِلاَّ أَنْ تَدْعُوَ بِمَا بَدَالَكَ وَ أَحَقُّ اَلْأَمْوَاتِ أَنْ يُدْعَى لَهُ أَنْ يُبْدَأَ بِالصَّلاَةِ عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurarah, both of them heard Aba Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, say:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “There is no prescribed recitation nor fixed supplication in the prayer over the dead, except that you may supplicate with whatever occurs to you. And the one most deserving among the dead for whom supplication should be made, is he for whom the prayer begins with the blessings upon the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer over the Dead
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik al-Hadrami from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, he said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “O Aba Bakr (al-Hadrami), do you know how many takbirs are in the ‘Prayer over the dead’ (Salat al-Mayyit)?” I said: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “Five takbirs. Do you know from where the five takbirs were derived?” I said: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “Five takbirs were taken from five daily prayers, one from each prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ أَتَدْرِي كَمِ اَلصَّلاَةُ عَلَى اَلْمَيِّتِ» قُلْتُ لاَ قَالَ« خَمْسُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ فَتَدْرِي مِنْ أَيْنَ أُخِذَتِ اَلْخَمْسُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ» قُلْتُ لاَ قَالَ« أُخِذَتِ اَلْخَمْسُ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ مِنِ اَلْخَمْسِ صَلَوَاتٍُ مِنْ كُلِّ صَلاَةٍ تَكْبِيرَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Uthman ibn Abd al-Malik al-Hadrami from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s) said: “O Aba Bakr (al-Hadrami), do you know how many takbirs are in the ‘Prayer over the dead’ (Salat al-Mayyit)?” I said: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “Five takbirs. Do you know from where the five takbirs were derived?” I said: “No.” Imam (a.s) said: “Five takbirs were taken from five daily prayers, one from each prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer over the Dead
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Muhajir from his mother, Umm Salamah, she said:
I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s) say: “When the Messenger of Allah (swt), prayed over a deceased person, He (saws) would pronounce the takbir and recite the tashahhud. Then Prophet (saws) would pronounce the takbir again, send blessings upon the Prophets, and supplicate. Then Prophet (saws) would pronounce the takbir and supplicate for the believers. Then Prophet (saws) would pronounce the fourth takbir and supplicate for the deceased. Then Prophet (saws) would pronounce the (final and fifth) takbir and depart. But when Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, forbade Him (saws) from praying over the hypocrites, Prophet (saws) would pronounce the takbir and recite the tashahhud. Then Prophet (saws) would pronounce the takbir and send blessings upon the Prophets (a.s), peace be upon them. Then he would pronounce the takbir and supplicate for the believers. Then he would pronounce the fourth takbir and depart, and He (saws) would not supplicate for the deceased.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُهَاجِرٍ عَنْ أُمِّهِ أُمِّ سَلَمَةَ قَالَتْ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ يَقُولُ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَ إِذَا صَلَّى عَلَى مَيِّتٍ كَبَّرَ وَ تَشَهَّدَ ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ فَصَلَّى عَلَى اَلْأَنْبِيَاءِ وَ دَعَا ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ وَ دَعَا لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ اَلرَّابِعَةَ وَ دَعَا لِلْمَيِّتِ ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ وَ اِنْصَرَفَ فَلَمَّا نَهَاهُ اَللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ عَلَى اَلْمُنَافِقِينَ كَبَّرَ وَ تَشَهَّدَ ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ فَصَلَّى عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّينَ عَ ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ وَ دَعَا لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ثُمَّ كَبَّرَ اَلرَّابِعَةَ وَ اِنْصَرَفَ وَ لَمْ يَدْعُ لِلْمَيِّتِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Muhajir from his mother, Umm Salamah, she said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Aba Abdillah (a.s) say: “When the Messenger of Allah (swt), prayed over a deceased person, He (saws) would pronounce the takbir and recite the tashahhud. Then Prophet (saws) would pronounce the takbir again, send blessings upon the Prophets, and supplicate. Then Prophet (saws) would pronounce the takbir and supplicate for the believers. Then Prophet (saws) would pronounce the fourth takbir and supplicate for the deceased. Then Prophet (saws) would pronounce the (final and fifth) takbir and depart. But when Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, forbade Him (saws) from praying over the hypocrites, Prophet (saws) would pronounce the takbir and recite the tashahhud. Then Prophet (saws) would pronounce the takbir and send blessings upon the Prophets (a.s), peace be upon them. Then he would pronounce the takbir and supplicate for the believers. Then he would pronounce the fourth takbir and depart, and He (saws) would not supplicate for the deceased.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer over the Dead
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yaqub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) said: “When you perform the prayer (of deceased) over a woman, stand at her head, and when you perform the prayer (of deceased) over a man, stand at his chest.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنْ عِدَّةٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى اَلْمَرْأَةِ فَقُمْ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهَا وَ إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى اَلرَّجُلِ فَقُمْ عِنْدَ صَدْرِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yaqub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Musa ibn Bakr from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) said: “When you perform the prayer (of deceased) over a woman, stand at her head, and when you perform the prayer (of deceased) over a man, stand at his chest.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer over the Dead
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever prays (Salat Al Mayyit) over a woman, let him not stand at her middle, but rather at the part corresponding to her chest. And if he prays (Salat Al Mayyit) over a man, then let him stand at his middle.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« مَنْ صَلَّى عَلَى اِمْرَأَةٍ فَلاَ يَقُومُ فِي وَسَطِهَا وَ يَكُونُ مِمَّا يَلِي صَدْرَهَا وَ إِذَا صَلَّى عَلَى اَلرَّجُلِ فَلْيَقُمْ فِي وَسَطِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever prays (Salat Al Mayyit) over a woman, let him not stand at her middle, but rather at the part corresponding to her chest. And if he prays (Salat Al Mayyit) over a man, then let him stand at his middle.”
