chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about one who did not catch the sermon on the day of Friday. Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray two rak‘ahs. But if he misses the prayer and does not catch it, then let him pray four (rak’ah).” And Imam (a.s) said: “If you catch the Imam before he bows in the last rak‘ah, then you have caught the prayer. But if you catch him after he has bowed, then it is the Dhuhr prayer, (which is) four rak‘ahs.”
arabicText: علي عن ابيه عن ابن ابي عمير عن حماد بن عثمان عن الحلبي قال سألت ابا عبد الله عليه السلام عمن لم يدرك الخطبة يوم الجمعة فقال يصلي ركعتين فان فاتته الصلاة فلم يدركها فليصل اربعا وقال إذا أدركت الامام قبل أن يركع الركعة الاخيرة فقد ادركت الصلاة فان انت ادركته بعد ما ركع فهي الظهر اربع
thaqalaynSanad: Ali narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s) about one who did not catch the sermon on the day of Friday. Imam (a.s) said: “He should pray two rak‘ahs. But if he misses the prayer and does not catch it, then let him pray four (rak’ah).” And Imam (a.s) said: “If you catch the Imam before he bows in the last rak‘ah, then you have caught the prayer. But if you catch him after he has bowed, then it is the Dhuhr prayer, (which is) four rak‘ahs.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 266

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Saeed narrated from al-Qasim, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir and Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If a man catches one rak‘ah, then he has caught the Friday prayer. But if he misses it, then let him pray four (rak’ahs of Dhuhr instead).”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ وَ أَبِي اَلْعَبَّاسِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْمَلِكِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَدْرَكَ اَلرَّجُلُ رَكْعَةً فَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ اَلْجُمُعَةَ وَإِنْ فَاتَتْهُ فَلْيُصَلِّ أَرْبَعاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Saeed narrated from al-Qasim, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Basir and Abu al-Abbas al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If a man catches one rak‘ah, then he has caught the Friday prayer. But if he misses it, then let him pray four (rak’ahs of Dhuhr instead).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 266

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Friday prayer is not valid except for the one who catches both sermons.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْجُمُعَةُ لاَ تَكُونُ إِلاَّ لِمَنْ أَدْرَكَ اَلْخُطْبَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Friday prayer is not valid except for the one who catches both sermons.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 266

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdur-Rahman al-Arzami, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you catch the Imam on the day of Friday and he has preceded you by one rak‘ah, then add to it another rak‘ah and recite aloud in it. But if you catch him while he is reciting the tashahhud, then pray four rak‘ahs (of Dhuhr).”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ اَلْعَرْزَمِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَدْرَكْتَ اَلْإِمَامَ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَ قَدْ سَبَقَكَ بِرَكْعَةٍ فَأَضِفْ إِلَيْهَا رَكْعَةً أُخْرَى وَ اِجْهَرْ فِيهَا فَإِنْ أَدْرَكْتَهُ وَ هُوَ يَتَشَهَّدُ فَصَلِّ أَرْبَعاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdur-Rahman al-Arzami, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you catch the Imam on the day of Friday and he has preceded you by one rak‘ah, then add to it another rak‘ah and recite aloud in it. But if you catch him while he is reciting the tashahhud, then pray four rak‘ahs (of Dhuhr).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 266

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Abu Ali al-Ash‘ari narrated from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, used to go early to the mosque on the day of Friday, when the sun had risen to the height of a spear. But if it was the Month of Ramadan, Imam (a.s) would go earlier than that, and He (a.s) used to say: “Indeed, the Fridays of the Month of Ramadan have a superiority over the Fridays of the other months, just as the Month of Ramadan has a superiority over the other months.”
arabicText: أَبُو عَلِيٍّ اَلْأَشْعَرِيُّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ قَالَ: كَانَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُبَكِّرُ إِلَى اَلْمَسْجِدِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ حِينَ تَكُونُ اَلشَّمْسُ قِيدَ رُمْحٍ فَإِذَا كَانَ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ يَكُونُ قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ وَكَانَ يَقُولُ« إِنَّ لِجُمَعِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ عَلَى جُمَعِ سَائِرِ اَلشُّهُورِ فَضْلاً كَفَضْلِ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ عَلَى سَائِرِ اَلشُّهُورِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Abu Ali al-Ash‘ari narrated from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, used to go early to the mosque on the day of Friday, when the sun had risen to the height of a spear. But if it was the Month of Ramadan, Imam (a.s) would go earlier than that, and He (a.s) used to say: “Indeed, the Fridays of the Month of Ramadan have a superiority over the Fridays of the other months, just as the Month of Ramadan has a superiority over the other months.”

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Qasri, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I fear that we may be performing the Friday prayer before the sun has passed the zenith.” So Imam (a.s) said: “This is upon the mu’adhdhins.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلصُّهْبَانِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ اَلْقَسْرِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ نَكُونَ نُصَلِّي اَلْجُمُعَةَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ قَالَ فَقَالَ« إِنَّمَا هَذَا عَلَى اَلْمُؤَذِّنِينَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Qasri, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I fear that we may be performing the Friday prayer before the sun has passed the zenith.” So Imam (a.s) said: “This is upon the mu’adhdhins.”

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu‘adh ibn Thabit, from Amr ibn Jumay‘ he raised it to Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam Ali (a.s) said: “Among the sunnah is that when the Imam ascends the pulpit, he should give the greeting of peace when he faces the people.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يُوسُفَ عَنْ مُعَاذِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ جُمَيْعٍ رَفَعَهُ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مِنَ اَلسُّنَّةِ إِذَا صَعِدَ اَلْإِمَامُ اَلْمِنْبَرَ أَنْ يُسَلِّمَ إِذَا اِسْتَقْبَلَ اَلنَّاسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Mu‘adh ibn Thabit, from Amr ibn Jumay‘ he raised it to Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) said: “Among the sunnah is that when the Imam ascends the pulpit, he should give the greeting of peace when he faces the people.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 267

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ja’far ibn Muhammad, from Abdillah ibn Maymun, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when He (saws) went out for the Friday prayer, would sit on the pulpit until the mu’adhdhins finished.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كَانَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِذَا خَرَجَ إِلَى اَلْجُمُعَةِ قَعَدَ عَلَى اَلْمِنْبَرِ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ اَلْمُؤَذِّنُونَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ja’far ibn Muhammad, from Abdillah ibn Maymun, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, when He (saws) went out for the Friday prayer, would sit on the pulpit until the mu’adhdhins finished.”

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Abbas, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib‘i, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If there are seven people on the day of Friday, then let them pray in congregation. And let him (the ‘just’ imam) wear the cloak and the turban, And lean on a bow or a staff, And let him (the ‘just’ imam) sit between the two sermons, And recite aloud, And perform qunut in the first rak‘ah, of them before the bowing.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ رِبْعِيٍّ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كَانُوا سَبْعَةً يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَلْيُصَلُّوا فِي جَمَاعَةٍ وَ لْيَلْبَسِ اَلْبُرْدَ وَ اَلْعِمَامَةَ وَ يَتَوَكَّأُ عَلَى قَوْسٍ أَوْ عَصًا وَ لْيَقْعُدْ قَعْدَةً بَيْنَ اَلْخُطْبَتَيْنِ وَ يَجْهَرُ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ وَ يَقْنُتُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى مِنْهُمَا قَبْلَ اَلرُّكُوعِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Abbas, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib‘i, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If there are seven people on the day of Friday, then let them pray in congregation. And let him (the ‘just’ imam) wear the cloak and the turban, And lean on a bow or a staff, And let him (the ‘just’ imam) sit between the two sermons, And recite aloud, And perform qunut in the first rak‘ah, of them before the bowing.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 267

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Saeed narrated from al-Hasan, from Zur’ah, from Sama’ah, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the qunut in the Friday prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “As for the (just) imam, upon him is the qunut in the first rak‘ah after he finishes the recitation, before he bows; And in the second, after he raises his head from the bowing, before the prostration. And indeed, the Friday prayer with the (just) imam is two rak‘ahs. So whoever prays without an (just) imam, alone, then it is four rak‘ahs like the Dhuhr prayer. So whoever wishes, may perform qunut in the second rak‘ah before bowing, and if he wishes, he may not perform qunut and that is if he prays alone.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْقُنُوتِ فِي اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ« أَمَّا اَلْإِمَامُ فَعَلَيْهِ اَلْقُنُوتُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلْأُولَى بَعْدَ مَا يَفْرُغُ مِنَ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ وَ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ بَعْدَ مَا يَرْفَعُ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ اَلرُّكُوعِ قَبْلَ اَلسُّجُودِ وَ إِنَّمَا صَلاَةُ اَلْجُمُعَةِ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ رَكْعَتَانِ فَمَنْ صَلَّى مِنْ غَيْرِ إِمَامٍ وَحْدَهُ فَهِيَ أَرْبَعُ رَكَعَاتٍ بِمَنْزِلَةِ اَلظُّهْرِ فَمَنْ شَاءَ قَنَتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَةِ اَلثَّانِيَةِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ لَمْ يَقْنُتْ وَ ذَلِكَ إِذَا صَلَّى وَحْدَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Saeed narrated from al-Hasan, from Zur’ah, from Sama’ah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about the qunut in the Friday prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “As for the (just) imam, upon him is the qunut in the first rak‘ah after he finishes the recitation, before he bows; And in the second, after he raises his head from the bowing, before the prostration. And indeed, the Friday prayer with the (just) imam is two rak‘ahs. So whoever prays without an (just) imam, alone, then it is four rak‘ahs like the Dhuhr prayer. So whoever wishes, may perform qunut in the second rak‘ah before bowing, and if he wishes, he may not perform qunut and that is if he prays alone.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 267

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Saeed narrated from al-Nadr, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Umar ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The voluntary prayer on the day of Friday, if you wish, from the beginning of the day and whatever you intend to pray on the day of Friday. If you wish, hasten it and pray it from the beginning of the day, whichever part of the day you wish, before the sun passes the zenith.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ حَنْظَلَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «صَلاَةُ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ إِنْ شِئْتَ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ مَا تُرِيدُ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَهُ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَإِنْ شِئْتَ عَجَّلْتَهُ فَصَلَّيْتَهُ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اَلنَّهَارِ أَيَّ اَلنَّهَارِ شِئْتَ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَزُولَ اَلشَّمْسُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Saeed narrated from al-Nadr, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Umar ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The voluntary prayer on the day of Friday, if you wish, from the beginning of the day and whatever you intend to pray on the day of Friday. If you wish, hasten it and pray it from the beginning of the day, whichever part of the day you wish, before the sun passes the zenith.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 268

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Sa’id al-A‘raj, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the nafilah (supererogatory prayer) on the day of Friday. Imam (a.s) said: “Sixteen rak‘ahs before Asr.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “And Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: ‘Whatever is added is good.’” And Imam (a.s) said: “If a man wishes, he may perform six rak‘ahs at the beginning of the day, and six rak‘ahs at midday, then pray Dhuhr and along with it four rak‘ahs, then pray Asr.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنْ سَعِيدٍ اَلْأَعْرَجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلنَّافِلَةِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ« سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً قَبْلَ اَلْعَصْرِ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« وَ كَانَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ« مَا زَادَ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ»» وَ قَالَ« إِنْ شَاءَ رَجُلٌ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ مِنْهَا سِتَّ رَكَعَاتٍ فِي صَدْرِ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ سِتَّ رَكَعَاتٍ نِصْفَ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ يُصَلِّي اَلظُّهْرَ وَ يُصَلِّي مَعَهَا أَرْبَعَةً ثُمَّ يُصَلِّي اَلْعَصْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad narrated from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Sa’id al-A‘raj, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the nafilah (supererogatory prayer) on the day of Friday. Imam (a.s) said: “Sixteen rak‘ahs before Asr.” Then Imam (a.s) said: “And Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: ‘Whatever is added is good.’” And Imam (a.s) said: “If a man wishes, he may perform six rak‘ahs at the beginning of the day, and six rak‘ahs at midday, then pray Dhuhr and along with it four rak‘ahs, then pray Asr.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 268

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about voluntary prayer on day of Friday. Imam (a.s) said: “Six rak‘ahs at the beginning of the day, six rak‘ahs before the zenith, two rak‘ahs when the sun passes the zenith, and six rak‘ahs after the Friday prayer so that is twenty rak‘ahs, besides the obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلتَّطَوُّعِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَقَالَ« سِتُّ رَكَعَاتٍ فِي صَدْرِ اَلنَّهَارِ وَ سِتُّ رَكَعَاتٍ قَبْلَ اَلزَّوَالِ وَ رَكْعَتَانِ إِذَا زَالَتْ وَ سِتُّ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَذَلِكَ عِشْرُونَ رَكْعَةً سِوَى اَلْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about voluntary prayer on day of Friday. Imam (a.s) said: “Six rak‘ahs at the beginning of the day, six rak‘ahs before the zenith, two rak‘ahs when the sun passes the zenith, and six rak‘ahs after the Friday prayer so that is twenty rak‘ahs, besides the obligatory prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 268

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Barqi, from Sa’ad ibn Sa’ad al-Ash‘ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), who said:
I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s) about the prayer on the day of Friday, how many rak‘ahs are there before the zenith? Imam (a.s) said: “Six rak‘ahs early, and six rak‘ahs after that; that makes twelve rak‘ahs. And six rak‘ahs after that; that makes eighteen rak‘ahs, And two rak‘ahs after the meridian; that makes twenty rak‘ahs. And two rak‘ahs after Asr; and that makes twenty-two rak‘ahs.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ سَعْدٍ اَلْأَشْعَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ كَمْ رَكْعَةً هِيَ قَبْلَ اَلزَّوَالِ قَالَ« سِتُّ رَكَعَاتٍ بُكْرَةً وَ سِتُّ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ اِثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً وَ سِتُّ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ ثَمَانِيَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً وَ رَكْعَتَانِ بَعْدَ اَلزَّوَالِ فَهَذِهِ عِشْرُونَ رَكْعَةً وَ رَكْعَتَانِ بَعْدَ اَلْعَصْرِ فَهَذِهِ ثِنْتَانِ وَ عِشْرُونَ رَكْعَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Barqi, from Sa’ad ibn Sa’ad al-Ash‘ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s) about the prayer on the day of Friday, how many rak‘ahs are there before the zenith? Imam (a.s) said: “Six rak‘ahs early, and six rak‘ahs after that; that makes twelve rak‘ahs. And six rak‘ahs after that; that makes eighteen rak‘ahs, And two rak‘ahs after the meridian; that makes twenty rak‘ahs. And two rak‘ahs after Asr; and that makes twenty-two rak‘ahs.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 268

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Uqbah ibn Musab, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and said: “Which is better, that I perform the rak‘ahs on the day of Friday before the obligatory prayer, or that I perform them after the obligatory prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather perform them after the obligatory prayer.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ عُقْبَةَ بْنِ مُصْعَبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ فَقُلْتُ أَيُّمَا أَفْضَلُ أُقَدِّمُ اَلرَّكَعَاتِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ أَوْ أُصَلِّيهَا بَعْدَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَلْ تُصَلِّيهَا بَعْدَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Uqbah ibn Musab, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, and said: “Which is better, that I perform the rak‘ahs on the day of Friday before the obligatory prayer, or that I perform them after the obligatory prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather perform them after the obligatory prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 269

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What do you do on the day of Friday?” Imam (a.s) said: “What do you do?” I said: “I pray in my home, then I go out and pray with them.” Imam (a.s) said: “That is what I do as well.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ اَلْحَضْرَمِيِّ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَيْفَ تَصْنَعُ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ قَالَ« كَيْفَ تَصْنَعُ أَنْتَ» قُلْتُ أُصَلِّي فِي مَنْزِلِي ثُمَّ أَخْرُجُ فَأُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ قَالَ« كَذَلِكَ أَصْنَعُ أَنَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What do you do on the day of Friday?” Imam (a.s) said: “What do you do?” I said: “I pray in my home, then I go out and pray with them.” Imam (a.s) said: “That is what I do as well.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 269

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about the nafilah that is prayed on the day of Friday, at the time of the obligatory prayer, whether it is better before the Friday prayer or after it. Imam (a.s) said: “Before the prayer.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلنَّافِلَةِ اَلَّتِي تُصَلَّى فِي يَوْمِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَقْتَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ قَبْلَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ أَفْضَلُ أَوْ بَعْدَهَا قَالَ« قَبْلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about the nafilah that is prayed on the day of Friday, at the time of the obligatory prayer, whether it is better before the Friday prayer or after it. Imam (a.s) said: “Before the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 269

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And from him, Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) said: “Pray on the day of Friday, ten rak‘ahs before the prayer, and ten rak‘ahs after it.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ قَالَ:« صَلِّ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ عَشْرَ رَكَعَاتٍ قَبْلَ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ عَشْرَ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَهَا»
thaqalaynMatn: And from him, Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) said: “Pray on the day of Friday, ten rak‘ahs before the prayer, and ten rak‘ahs after it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 269

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘If you see an old man narrating the stories of ‘the Age of Ignorance’ in the mosque on the day of Friday, then strike his head, even if it is with pebbles.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« إِذَا رَأَيْتُمُ اَلشَّيْخَ يُحَدِّثُ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ بِأَحَادِيثِ اَلْجَاهِلِيَّةِ فَارْمُوا رَأْسَهُ وَ لَوْ بِالْحَصَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘If you see an old man narrating the stories of ‘the Age of Ignorance’ in the mosque on the day of Friday, then strike his head, even if it is with pebbles.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 270

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who catches the (just) imam while he is praying four rak‘ahs, and the (just) imam has already prayed two rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: “He should begin the prayer and join with him, and recite behind him in the two rak‘ahs. He should recite in the first, ‘al-Hamd’ and whatever he catches from ‘Surah al-Jumu‘ah’, and bow with the (just) imam; and in the second, ‘al-Hamd’ and whatever he catches from ‘Surah al-Munafiqun’, and bow with the (just) imam. When the (just) imam sits for the tashahhud, he should not recite the tashahhud but should instead glorify (tasbih), and when the (just) imam says the taslim, he should stand and pray two rak‘ahs, in which he glorifies (tasbih), then recites the tashahhud and gives the taslim.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُدْرِكُ اَلْإِمَامَ وَ هُوَ يُصَلِّي أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ وَ قَدْ صَلَّى اَلْإِمَامُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ قَالَ «يَفْتَتِحُ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ يَدْخُلُ مَعَهُ وَ يَقْرَأُ خَلْفَهُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ يَقْرَأُ فِي اَلْأُولَى اَلْحَمْدَ وَ مَا أَدْرَكَ مِنْ سُورَةِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ وَ يَرْكَعُ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ مَا أَدْرَكَ مِنْ سُورَةِ اَلْمُنَافِقِينَ وَ يَرْكَعُ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَإِذَا قَعَدَ اَلْإِمَامُ لِلتَّشَهُّدِ فَلاَ يَتَشَهَّدْ وَ لَكِنْ يُسَبِّحُ فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ اَلْإِمَامُ رَكَعَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ يُسَبِّحُ فِيهِمَا وَ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ يُسَلِّمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who catches the (just) imam while he is praying four rak‘ahs, and the (just) imam has already prayed two rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: “He should begin the prayer and join with him, and recite behind him in the two rak‘ahs. He should recite in the first, ‘al-Hamd’ and whatever he catches from ‘Surah al-Jumu‘ah’, and bow with the (just) imam; and in the second, ‘al-Hamd’ and whatever he catches from ‘Surah al-Munafiqun’, and bow with the (just) imam. When the (just) imam sits for the tashahhud, he should not recite the tashahhud but should instead glorify (tasbih), and when the (just) imam says the taslim, he should stand and pray two rak‘ahs, in which he glorifies (tasbih), then recites the tashahhud and gives the taslim.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 270

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abu Ja’far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, that Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say:
Imam Ali (a.s) said: “To miss attending the Eid al-Adha, ten times, is more beloved to me than to miss attending the Friday prayer, (even) once, without an excuse.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ وَهْبٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ يَقُولُ:« لَأَنْ أَدَعَ شُهُودَ حُضُورِ اَلْأَضْحَى عَشْرَ مَرَّاتٍ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ أَدَعَ شُهُودَ حُضُورِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abu Ja’far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, that Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) said: “To miss attending the Eid al-Adha, ten times, is more beloved to me than to miss attending the Friday prayer, (even) once, without an excuse.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 270

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja’far, from his brother Imam Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about the two rak‘ahs of midday (al-zawal) on the day of Friday, Are they before the adhan or after it? Imam (a.s) said: “Before the adhan.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَكْعَتَيِ اَلزَّوَالِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ قَبْلَ اَلْأَذَانِ أَوْ بَعْدَهُ قَالَ« قَبْلَ اَلْأَذَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja’far, from his brother Imam Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about the two rak‘ahs of midday (al-zawal) on the day of Friday, Are they before the adhan or after it? Imam (a.s) said: “Before the adhan.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 271

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abu Ja’far, from his father, from Zur’ah, from Sama’ah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam Ali (a.s) was asked about a man who is in the middle of a crowd, on the day of Friday or the day of Arafah, and he experiences a hadath (state of ritual impurity) or remembers that he is not in a state of wudu. And he is unable to leave due to the intensity of the crowd. Imam (a.s) said: “He should perform tayammum and pray with them, and repeat the prayer when he returns.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَكُونُ وَسْطَ اَلزِّحَامِ يَوْمَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ أَوْ يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ فَأَحْدَثَ أَوْ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ عَلَى غَيْرِ وُضُوءٍ وَ لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُ اَلْخُرُوجَ مِنْ كَثْرَةِ اَلزِّحَامِ قَالَ« يَتَيَمَّمُ وَ يُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ وَ يُعِيدُ إِذَا هُوَ اِنْصَرَفَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abu Ja’far, from his father, from Zur’ah, from Sama’ah, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) was asked about a man who is in the middle of a crowd, on the day of Friday or the day of Arafah, and he experiences a hadath (state of ritual impurity) or remembers that he is not in a state of wudu. And he is unable to leave due to the intensity of the crowd. Imam (a.s) said: “He should perform tayammum and pray with them, and repeat the prayer when he returns.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 271

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abu Ja’far, from his father, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “There is no Friday prayer (Jumu'ah) upon the people of the villages, nor any going out on the two Eids.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ غِيَاثٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لَيْسَ عَلَى أَهْلِ اَلْقُرَى جُمُعَةٌ وَ لاَ خُرُوجٌ فِي اَلْعِيدَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abu Ja’far, from his father, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “There is no Friday prayer (Jumu'ah) upon the people of the villages, nor any going out on the two Eids.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 271

chapter: Chapter on the Deeds to Be Attained on Night of Friday and Its Day
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “About a man who is in the mosque, either on the day of Jumu'ah or on other days, and the people press him; either towards a wall or towards a pillar, and he is not able to bow (ruku) or prostrate (sujud) until the people raise their heads. So is it permissible for him to bow and prostrate alone and then align himself with the people in the row?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is no harm in that.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ إِمَّا فِي يَوْمِ جُمُعَةٍ وَإِمَّا غَيْرَ ذَلِكَ مِنَ اَلْأَيَّامِ فَيَزْحَمُهُ اَلنَّاسُ إِمَّا إِلَى حَائِطٍ وَ إِمَّا إِلَى أُسْطُوَانَةٍ فَلاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى أَنْ يَرْكَعَ وَ لاَ يَسْجُدَ حَتَّى يَرْفَعَ اَلنَّاسُ رُءُوسَهُمْ فَهَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ وَ يَسْجُدَ وَحْدَهُ ثُمَّ يَسْتَوِيَ مَعَ اَلنَّاسِ فِي اَلصَّفِّ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “About a man who is in the mosque, either on the day of Jumu'ah or on other days, and the people press him; either towards a wall or towards a pillar, and he is not able to bow (ruku) or prostrate (sujud) until the people raise their heads. So is it permissible for him to bow and prostrate alone and then align himself with the people in the row?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is no harm in that.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 271

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Sa’ad al-Iskaf from Ziyad ibn Isa from Abu al-Jarud from al-Asbagh from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam Ali (a.s) used to say: “Whoever frequents the mosque will attain one of eight things; a brother benefitted in Allah (swt), or newly acquired knowledge, or a decisive verse, or hears a word that guides him to guidance, or a mercy awaited, or a word that repels him from destruction, or he leaves a sin out of fear, or out of shame.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ سَعْدٍ اَلْإِسْكَافِ عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ أَبِي اَلْجَارُودِ عَنِ اَلْأَصْبَغِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ كَانَ يَقُولُ:« مَنِ اِخْتَلَفَ إِلَى اَلْمَسْجِدِ أَصَابَ إِحْدَى اَلثَّمَانِ أَخاً مُسْتَفَاداً فِي اَللَّهِ أَوْ عِلْماً مُسْتَطْرَفاً أَوْ آيَةً مُحْكَمَةً أَوْ سَمِعَ كَلِمَةً تَدُلُّهُ عَلَى هُدًى أَوْ رَحْمَةً مُنْتَظَرَةً أَوْ كَلِمَةً تَرُدُّهُ عَنْ رَدًى أَوْ يَتْرُكُ ذَنْباً خَشْيَةً أَوْ حَيَاءً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Sa’ad al-Iskaf from Ziyad ibn Isa from Abu al-Jarud from al-Asbagh from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) used to say: “Whoever frequents the mosque will attain one of eight things; a brother benefitted in Allah (swt), or newly acquired knowledge, or a decisive verse, or hears a word that guides him to guidance, or a mercy awaited, or a word that repels him from destruction, or he leaves a sin out of fear, or out of shame.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of his men, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Keep your mosques free from; trade and buying and selling, and the insane, and children, and legal judgments, and lost property, and the carrying out of punishments, and raising the voice.”
arabicText: وَ عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مُوسَى اَلْخَشَّابِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَسْبَاطٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ رِجَالِهِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: «جَنِّبُوا مَسَاجِدَكُمُ اَلْبَيْعَ وَ اَلشِّرَاءَ وَ اَلْمَجَانِينَ وَ اَلصِّبْيَانَ وَ اَلْأَحْكَامَ وَ اَلضَّالَّةَ وَ اَلْحُدُودَ وَ رَفْعَ اَلصَّوْتِ»
thaqalaynSanad: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from some of his men, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Keep your mosques free from; trade and buying and selling, and the insane, and children, and legal judgments, and lost property, and the carrying out of punishments, and raising the voice.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 272

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Hashimi, from al-Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja’far, from his brother Imam Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about poetry, is it proper for it to be recited in the mosque? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.” And I asked Imam (a.s) about a lost item, is it proper for it to be announced in the mosque? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ اَلْهَاشِمِيِّ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلشِّعْرِ أَ يَصْلُحُ أَنْ يُنْشَدَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلضَّالَّةِ أَ يَصْلُحُ أَنْ تُنْشَدَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Hashimi, from al-Amraki, from Ali ibn Ja’far, from his brother Imam Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about poetry, is it proper for it to be recited in the mosque? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.” And I asked Imam (a.s) about a lost item, is it proper for it to be announced in the mosque? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi from Abu Muhammad al-Razi from Isma'il ibn Abi Abdillah (a.s) from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Reclining in the mosque is the monasticism (‘rahbaniyyah’) of the Arabs, and the mosque is the gathering place for the believer, and his monastery (‘sawm'ah’) is his house.’”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَسَّانَ اَلرَّازِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ اَلرَّازِيِّ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:« اَلاِتِّكَاءُ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ رَهْبَانِيَّةُ اَلْعَرَبِ وَاَلْمُؤْمِنُ مَجْلِسُهُ مَسْجِدُهُ وَ صَوْمَعَتُهُ بَيْتُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Hassan al-Razi from Abu Muhammad al-Razi from Isma'il ibn Abi Abdillah (a.s) from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Reclining in the mosque is the monasticism (‘rahbaniyyah’) of the Arabs, and the mosque is the gathering place for the believer, and his monastery (‘sawm'ah’) is his house.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 273

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “In Kufah, there are cursed mosques and blessed mosques. As for the blessed; the ‘Mosque of Ghani’. By Allah, its qiblah is upright, and its soil is pure, and it was established by a believing man. And the world will not end until two springs burst forth at it, and there will be two gardens upon it. But its people are cursed, and it has been taken away from them. And the mosque of ‘Banu Zafar’, and that is the ‘Mosque of al-Sahlah’, and the ‘Mosque of al-Hamra’, and the ‘Mosque of Ju‘fi’ and it is not their mosque today, (and It has disappeared.)” Imam (a.s) said: “As for the cursed mosques; the ‘Mosque of Thaqif’, the ‘Mosque of al-Ash‘ath’, the ‘Mosque of Jarir ibn Abdillah al-Bajali’, the ‘Mosque of Simak’, and the ‘Mosque of al-Hamra’, it was built over the grave of a Pharaoh from among the Pharaohs.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« بِالْكُوفَةِ مَسَاجِدُ مَلْعُونَةٌ وَ مَسَاجِدُ مُبَارَكَةٌ فَأَمَّا اَلْمُبَارَكَةُ فَمَسْجِدُ غَنِيٍّ وَ اَللَّهِ إِنَّ قِبْلَتَهُ لَقَاسِطَةٌ وَإِنَّ طِينَتَهُ لَطَيِّبَةٌ وَلَقَدْ وَضَعَهُ رَجُلٌ مُؤْمِنٌ وَلاَ تَذْهَبُ اَلدُّنْيَا حَتَّى تَنْفَجِرَ عِنْدَهُ عَيْنَانِ وَتَكُونَ عَلَيْهِ جَنَّتَانِ وَ أَهْلُهُ مَلْعُونُونَ وَ هُوَ مَسْلُوبٌ مِنْهُمْ وَ مَسْجِدُ بَنِي ظَفَرٍ وَ هُوَ مَسْجِدُ اَلسَّهْلَةِ وَ مَسْجِدُ اَلْحَمْرَاءِ وَ مَسْجِدُ جُعْفِيٍّ وَلَيْسَ هُوَ مَسْجِدَ هُمُ اَلْيَوْمَ» قَالَ« دَرَسَ وَأَمَّا اَلْمَسَاجِدُ اَلْمَلْعُونَةُ فَمَسْجِدُ ثَقِيفٍ وَمَسْجِدُ اَلْأَشْعَثِ وَ مَسْجِدُ جَرِيرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْبَجَلِيِّ وَ مَسْجِدُ سِمَاكٍ وَ مَسْجِدُ اَلْحَمْرَاءِ بُنِيَ عَلَى قَبْرِ فِرْعَوْنٍ مِنَ اَلْفَرَاعِنَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “In Kufah, there are cursed mosques and blessed mosques. As for the blessed; the ‘Mosque of Ghani’. By Allah, its qiblah is upright, and its soil is pure, and it was established by a believing man. And the world will not end until two springs burst forth at it, and there will be two gardens upon it. But its people are cursed, and it has been taken away from them. And the mosque of ‘Banu Zafar’, and that is the ‘Mosque of al-Sahlah’, and the ‘Mosque of al-Hamra’, and the ‘Mosque of Ju‘fi’ and it is not their mosque today, (and It has disappeared.)” Imam (a.s) said: “As for the cursed mosques; the ‘Mosque of Thaqif’, the ‘Mosque of al-Ash‘ath’, the ‘Mosque of Jarir ibn Abdillah al-Bajali’, the ‘Mosque of Simak’, and the ‘Mosque of al-Hamra’, it was built over the grave of a Pharaoh from among the Pharaohs.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 273

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s) about the prayer in the ‘Sacred Mosque’ (al-Masjid al-Haram) and the prayer in the ‘Mosque of the Messenger’, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, are they equal in virtue? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and the prayer in between them equals one thousand prayers.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرَامِ وَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي مَسْجِدِ اَلرَّسُولِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي اَلْفَضْلِ سَوَاءٌ قَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِيمَا بَيْنَهُمَا تَعْدِلُ أَلْفَ صَلاَةٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s) about the prayer in the ‘Sacred Mosque’ (al-Masjid al-Haram) and the prayer in the ‘Mosque of the Messenger’, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, are they equal in virtue? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and the prayer in between them equals one thousand prayers.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 274

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah from Sulayman ibn Hisham from Salim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Four mosques in Kufah were renovated out of joy for the killing of Imam al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him; the ‘Mosque of al-Ash'ath’, the ‘Mosque of Jarir’, the ‘Mosque of Simak’, and the ‘Mosque of Shabath ibn Rib'i’. May Allah (swt) curse them.” (meaning may Allah (swt) curse those involved in the killing of Imam al-Husayn (a.s), those who renovated these ‘mosques’ out of joy for killing Imam al-Husayn (a.s))
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ هِشَامٍ عَنْ سَالِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« جُدِّدَتْ أَرْبَعَةُ مَسَاجِدَ بِالْكُوفَةِ فَرَحاً لِقَتْلِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَسْجِدُ اَلْأَشْعَثِ وَمَسْجِدُ جَرِيرٍ وَمَسْجِدُ سِمَاكٍ وَ مَسْجِدُ شَبَثِ بْنِ رِبْعِيٍّ لَعَنَهُمُ اَللَّهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah from Sulayman ibn Hisham from Salim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Four mosques in Kufah were renovated out of joy for the killing of Imam al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon him; the ‘Mosque of al-Ash'ath’, the ‘Mosque of Jarir’, the ‘Mosque of Simak’, and the ‘Mosque of Shabath ibn Rib'i’. May Allah (swt) curse them.” (meaning may Allah (swt) curse those involved in the killing of Imam al-Husayn (a.s), those who renovated these ‘mosques’ out of joy for killing Imam al-Husayn (a.s))

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Khazzaz from Harun ibn Kharijah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said to me: “O Harun ibn Kharijah, how far is it between you and the ‘Mosque of Kufa’? Is it a mile?” I said: “No”. Imam (a.s) said: “Then do you perform all the prayers in it?” I said: “No”. So Imam (a.s) said: “If I were present near it, I would hope that not a single prayer would pass me by in it. And do you know the merit of that place? There is not a single righteous servant nor a prophet except that he has prayed in your mosque, even the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. Indeed, when Allah (swt) caused the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, to be taken on the ‘Night Journey’ (Mi’raj), Jibra'il (a.s), said to him: ‘Do you know where you are, O’ Messenger of Allah (saws)? At this moment you are facing the ‘Mosque of Kufa’.” Prophet (saws) said: “Then ask permission from my Lord (azj), Mighty and Majestic, that I may go to it and pray two units of prayer in it.” So Jibra’il (a.s) asked Allah (swt), the Majestic, for permission, and He (azj) permitted. And indeed, its right side is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, And its center is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, And its rear is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And indeed the obligatory prayer performed in it is equal to one thousand prayers, and the supererogatory prayer in it is equal to five hundred prayers. And sitting in it without recitation or remembrance is worship. And if the people knew what was in it, they would come to it even crawling.”
arabicText: سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ خَارِجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي« يَا هَارُونَ بْنَ خَارِجَةَ كَمْ بَيْنَكَ وَ بَيْنَ مَسْجِدِ اَلْكُوفَةِ يَكُونُ مِيلاً» قُلْتُ لاَ قَالَ« أَ فَتُصَلِّي فِيهِ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ كُلَّهَا» قُلْتُ لاَ فَقَالَ« أَمَا لَوْ كُنْتُ حَاضِراً بِحَضْرَتِهِ لَرَجَوْتُ أَنْ لاَ تَفُوتَنِي فِيهِ صَلاَةٌ وَ تَدْرِي مَا فَضْلُ ذَلِكَ اَلْمَوْضِعِ مَا مِنْ عَبْدٍ صَالِحٍ وَ لاَ نَبِيٍّ إِلاَّ وَ قَدْ صَلَّى فِي مَسْجِدِكُمْ حَتَّى إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ لَمَّا أَسْرَى اَللَّهُ بِهِ قَالَ لَهُ جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَتَدْرِي أَيْنَ أَنْتَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ اَلسَّاعَةَ أَنْتَ مُقَابِلُ مَسْجِدِ كُوفَانَ قَالَ« فَاسْتَأْذِنْ لِي رَبِّي عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ حَتَّى آتِيَهُ فَأُصَلِّيَ فِيهِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ» فَاسْتَأْذَنَ اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَأَذِنَ لَهُ وَ إِنَّ مَيْمَنَتَهُ لَرَوْضَةٌ مِنْ رِيَاضِ اَلْجَنَّةِ وَإِنَّ وَسَطَهُ لَرَوْضَةٌ مِنْ رِيَاضِ اَلْجَنَّةِ وَإِنَّ مُؤَخَّرَهُ لَرَوْضَةٌ مِنْ رِيَاضِ اَلْجَنَّةِ وَإِنَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةَ فِيهِ لَتَعْدِلُ بِأَلْفِ صَلاَةٍ وَ إِنَّ اَلنَّافِلَةَ فِيهِ لَتَعْدِلُ بِخَمْسِمِائَةِ صَلاَةٍ وَ إِنَّ اَلْجُلُوسَ فِيهِ بِغَيْرِ تِلاَوَةٍ وَ لاَ ذِكْرٍ لَعِبَادَةٌ وَ لَوْ عَلِمَ اَلنَّاسُ مَا فِيهِ لَأَتَوْهُ وَ لَوْ حَبْواً»
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Abdillah al-Khazzaz from Harun ibn Kharijah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said to me: “O Harun ibn Kharijah, how far is it between you and the ‘Mosque of Kufa’? Is it a mile?” I said: “No”. Imam (a.s) said: “Then do you perform all the prayers in it?” I said: “No”. So Imam (a.s) said: “If I were present near it, I would hope that not a single prayer would pass me by in it. And do you know the merit of that place? There is not a single righteous servant nor a prophet except that he has prayed in your mosque, even the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. Indeed, when Allah (swt) caused the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, to be taken on the ‘Night Journey’ (Mi’raj), Jibra'il (a.s), said to him: ‘Do you know where you are, O’ Messenger of Allah (saws)? At this moment you are facing the ‘Mosque of Kufa’.” Prophet (saws) said: “Then ask permission from my Lord (azj), Mighty and Majestic, that I may go to it and pray two units of prayer in it.” So Jibra’il (a.s) asked Allah (swt), the Majestic, for permission, and He (azj) permitted. And indeed, its right side is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, And its center is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, And its rear is a garden from the gardens of Paradise. And indeed the obligatory prayer performed in it is equal to one thousand prayers, and the supererogatory prayer in it is equal to five hundred prayers. And sitting in it without recitation or remembrance is worship. And if the people knew what was in it, they would come to it even crawling.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 274

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Yusuf Ya'qub ibn Abdillah from the descendants of Abu Fatimah, from Isma'il ibn Zayd, the mawla of Abdillah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abdillah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, while he was in the Mosque of Kufa. He said: “Peace be upon you, O’ Commander of the Faithful (a.s), and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His (azj) blessings.” Imam Ali (a.s) returned the greeting. The man said: “May I be your ransom, I intended to go to the ‘al-Masjid al-Aqsa’, and I wanted to greet you and bid you farewell.” So Imam (a.s) said to him: “What do you intend by that?” He said: “The merit, may I be your ransom.” Imam (a.s) said “Then sell your mount and consume your provisions and pray in this mosque (Mosque of Kufa), for the obligatory prayer performed in it is (rewarded as) an accepted Hajj, and the supererogatory prayer in it is (rewarded as) an accepted Umrah. And the blessing from it extends for twelve miles. Its right side is blessed, and its left side is deception. In its center is a spring of oil, and a spring of milk, and a spring of drinking water for the believers, and a spring of purifying water for the believers. From it the Ark of Nuh (a.s), peace be upon him, set sail. And in it were (the idols) Nasr, Yaghuth, and Ya'uq. Seventy prophets and seventy successors prayed in it. I am one of them,” And Imam Ali (a.s) placed his hand upon his chest. (Imam (a.s) then continued) “No distressed person ever supplicated in it with a need among his needs except that Allah (swt) answered him and relieved him of his distress.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي يُوسُفَ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ مِنْ وُلْدِ أَبِي فَاطِمَةَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ مَوْلَى عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلْكَاهِلِيِّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلْكَاهِلِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« جَاءَ رَجُلٌ إِلَى أَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ هُوَ فِي مَسْجِدِ اَلْكُوفَةِ فَقَالَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ يَا أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ رَحْمَةُ اَللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ فَرَدَّ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ إِنِّي أَرَدْتُ اَلْمَسْجِدَ اَلْأَقْصَى فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُسَلِّمَ عَلَيْكَ وَ أُوَدِّعَكَ فَقَالَ لَهُ« فَأَيَّ شَيْءٍ أَرَدْتَ بِذَاكَ» فَقَالَ اَلْفَضْلَ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ قَالَ« فَبِعْ رَاحِلَتَكَ وَكُلْ زَادَكَ وَصَلِّ فِي هَذَا اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَإِنَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةَ فِيهِ حَجَّةٌ مَبْرُورَةٌ وَ اَلنَّافِلَةَ فِيهِ عُمْرَةٌ مَبْرُورَةٌ وَ اَلْبَرَكَةَ مِنْهُ عَلَى اِثْنَيْ عَشَرَ مِيلاً يَمِينُهُ يُمْنٌ وَ يَسَارُهُ مَكْرٌ وَ فِي وَسَطِهِ عَيْنٌ مِنْ دُهْنٍ وَ عَيْنٌ مِنْ لَبَنٍ وَ عَيْنٌ مِنْ مَاءٍ شَرَابٍ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ عَيْنٌ مِنْ مَاءٍ طُهْرٍ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْهُ سَارَتْ سَفِينَةُ نُوحٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ كَانَ فِيهِ نَسْرٌ وَ يَغُوثُ وَ يَعُوقُ صَلَّى فِيهِ سَبْعُونَ نَبِيّاً وَ سَبْعُونَ وَصِيّاً أَنَا أَحَدُهُمْ» وَقَالَ بِيَدِهِ عَلَى صَدْرِهِ« مَا دَعَا فِيهِ مَكْرُوبٌ بِمَسْأَلَةٍ فِي حَاجَةٍ مِنَ اَلْحَوَائِجِ إِلاَّ أَجَابَهُ اَللَّهُ وَ فَرَّجَ عَنْهُ كُرْبَتَهُ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Yusuf Ya'qub ibn Abdillah from the descendants of Abu Fatimah, from Isma'il ibn Zayd, the mawla of Abdillah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abdillah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, while he was in the Mosque of Kufa. He said: “Peace be upon you, O’ Commander of the Faithful (a.s), and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His (azj) blessings.” Imam Ali (a.s) returned the greeting. The man said: “May I be your ransom, I intended to go to the ‘al-Masjid al-Aqsa’, and I wanted to greet you and bid you farewell.” So Imam (a.s) said to him: “What do you intend by that?” He said: “The merit, may I be your ransom.” Imam (a.s) said “Then sell your mount and consume your provisions and pray in this mosque (Mosque of Kufa), for the obligatory prayer performed in it is (rewarded as) an accepted Hajj, and the supererogatory prayer in it is (rewarded as) an accepted Umrah. And the blessing from it extends for twelve miles. Its right side is blessed, and its left side is deception. In its center is a spring of oil, and a spring of milk, and a spring of drinking water for the believers, and a spring of purifying water for the believers. From it the Ark of Nuh (a.s), peace be upon him, set sail. And in it were (the idols) Nasr, Yaghuth, and Ya'uq. Seventy prophets and seventy successors prayed in it. I am one of them,” And Imam Ali (a.s) placed his hand upon his chest. (Imam (a.s) then continued) “No distressed person ever supplicated in it with a need among his needs except that Allah (swt) answered him and relieved him of his distress.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you enter from the second gate on the right side of the mosque, count five pillars; two of them are under the shade and three of them are in the courtyard. At the third (pillar) is the prayer place of Ibrahim (a.s) and it is the fifth from the wall.” He (Sufyan ibn al-Simt) said: “When it was the time of Abu al-Abbas, Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, entered from the ‘Gate of the Elephant’, then turned to the left as He (a.s) entered from the gate and prayed at the fourth pillar, which is opposite the fifth. So I asked him: “Is that the pillar of Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him?” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Yes.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سُفْيَانَ بْنِ اَلسِّمْطِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا دَخَلْتَ مِنَ اَلْبَابِ اَلثَّانِي فِي مَيْمَنَةِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ تَعُدُّ خَمْسَ أَسَاطِينَ ثِنْتَانِ مِنْهَا فِي اَلظِّلاَلِ وَ ثَلاَثٌ مِنْهَا فِي اَلصَّحْنِ فَعِنْدَ اَلثَّالِثَةِ مُصَلَّى إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ هِيَ اَلْخَامِسَةُ مِنَ اَلْحَائِطِ» قَالَ فَلَمَّا كَانَ أَيَّامُ أَبِي اَلْعَبَّاسِ دَخَلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مِنْ بَابِ اَلْفِيلِ فَتَيَاسَرَ حِينَ دَخَلَ مِنَ اَلْبَابِ فَصَلَّى عِنْدَ اَلْأُسْطُوَانَةِ اَلرَّابِعَةِ وَ هِيَ بِحِذَاءِ اَلْخَامِسَةِ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ تِلْكَ أُسْطُوَانَةُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ لِي« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sufyan ibn al-Simt, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s) said: “When you enter from the second gate on the right side of the mosque, count five pillars; two of them are under the shade and three of them are in the courtyard. At the third (pillar) is the prayer place of Ibrahim (a.s) and it is the fifth from the wall.” He (Sufyan ibn al-Simt) said: “When it was the time of Abu al-Abbas, Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, entered from the ‘Gate of the Elephant’, then turned to the left as He (a.s) entered from the gate and prayed at the fourth pillar, which is opposite the fifth. So I asked him: “Is that the pillar of Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him?” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from Salih ibn al-Sindi from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hadha’ from Abu Usamah from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The ‘Mosque of Kufah’ is a garden from gardens of Paradise. One thousand and seventy prophets prayed in it. Its right side is mercy, and its left side is deception. And in it is the staff of Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, And the gourd tree (shajarat yaqtin), And the ring of Sulayman (a.s), peace be upon him. And from it ‘the oven gushed forth’ (Surah Hud 11:40), and the Ark (of Nuh (a.s)) sailed. And it is the ‘navel of Babylon’ and the gathering place of the prophets (a.s).”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ اَلْحَذَّاءِ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَسْجِدُ كُوفَانَ رَوْضَةٌ مِنْ رِيَاضِ اَلْجَنَّةِ صَلَّى فِيهِ أَلْفُ نَبِيٍّ وَ سَبْعُونَ نَبِيّاً وَ مَيْمَنَتُهُ رَحْمَةٌ وَ مَيْسَرَتُهُ مَكْرٌ وَ فِيهِ عَصَا مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ شَجَرَةُ يَقْطِينٍ وَ خَاتَمُ سُلَيْمَانَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ مِنْهُ« فٰارَ اَلتَّنُّورُ» وَ جَرَتِ اَلسَّفِينَةُ وَ هِيَ صُرَّةُ بَابِلَ وَ مَجْمَعُ اَلْأَنْبِيَاءِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from Salih ibn al-Sindi from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hadha’ from Abu Usamah from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The ‘Mosque of Kufah’ is a garden from gardens of Paradise. One thousand and seventy prophets prayed in it. Its right side is mercy, and its left side is deception. And in it is the staff of Musa (a.s), peace be upon him, And the gourd tree (shajarat yaqtin), And the ring of Sulayman (a.s), peace be upon him. And from it ‘the oven gushed forth’ (Surah Hud 11:40), and the Ark (of Nuh (a.s)) sailed. And it is the ‘navel of Babylon’ and the gathering place of the prophets (a.s).”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from al-Husayn ibn Sayf from Uthman from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, mentioned the ‘Mosque of al-Sahlah’ and said: “Indeed, it is the residence of our companion (the Qa'im (ajf)), when He (ajf) rises with his family.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَيْفٍ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْأَسْوَدِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ ذَكَرَ مَسْجِدَ اَلسَّهْلَةِ فَقَالَ« أَمَا إِنَّهُ مَنْزِلُ صَاحِبِنَا إِذَا قَامَ بِأَهْلِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from al-Husayn ibn Sayf from Uthman from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, mentioned the ‘Mosque of al-Sahlah’ and said: “Indeed, it is the residence of our companion (the Qa'im (ajf)), when He (ajf) rises with his family.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Husayn ibn Bakr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “In Kufah, there is a mosque called the ‘Mosque of al-Sahlah’. If my uncle Zayd had gone to it and prayed in it and sought refuge with Allah (swt), Allah (swt) would have granted him refuge for twenty years. In it is the resting place of the ‘Rider’.” It was asked: “And who is the ‘Rider’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Al-Khidr (a.s), peace be upon him, and the house of Idris (a.s) the Prophet, peace be upon him. And no distressed person has ever come to it and prayed in it, between the two evening prayers, and supplicated to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah (swt) relieved his distress.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ حُسَيْنِ بْنِ بَكْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ اَلْخَزَّازِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ« بِالْكُوفَةِ مَسْجِدٌ يُقَالُ لَهُ مَسْجِدُ اَلسَّهْلَةِ لَوْ أَنَّ عَمِّي زَيْداً أَتَاهُ فَصَلَّى فِيهِ وَاِسْتَجَارَ اَللَّهَ لَأَجَارَ لَهُ اَللَّهُ عِشْرِينَ سَنَةً فِيهِ مُنَاخُ اَلرَّاكِبِ» قِيلَ وَ مَنِ اَلرَّاكِبُ قَالَ« اَلْخَضِرُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ بَيْتُ إِدْرِيسَ اَلنَّبِيِّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ مَا أَتَاهُ مَكْرُوبٌ قَطُّ فَصَلَّى فِيهِ مَا بَيْنَ اَلْعِشَاءَيْنِ فَدَعَا اَللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلاَّ فَرَّجَ اَللَّهُ كُرْبَتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Husayn ibn Bakr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “In Kufah, there is a mosque called the ‘Mosque of al-Sahlah’. If my uncle Zayd had gone to it and prayed in it and sought refuge with Allah (swt), Allah (swt) would have granted him refuge for twenty years. In it is the resting place of the ‘Rider’.” It was asked: “And who is the ‘Rider’?” Imam (a.s) said: “Al-Khidr (a.s), peace be upon him, and the house of Idris (a.s) the Prophet, peace be upon him. And no distressed person has ever come to it and prayed in it, between the two evening prayers, and supplicated to Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, except that Allah (swt) relieved his distress.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ziyad ibn Marwan from Yunus ibn Zabian, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The best mosques for your women are their homes.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ زِيَادِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ ظَبْيَانَ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« خَيْرُ مَسَاجِدِ نِسَائِكُمُ اَلْبُيُوتُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ziyad ibn Marwan from Yunus ibn Zabian, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The best mosques for your women are their homes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 277

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about covered mosques, is it disliked to stand in them? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, but prayer in them does not harm you today. And if justice were to be established, you would see for yourselves what would be done in that regard.” He (al-Halabi) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s), ‘May a man hang up his weapon in the mosque?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, but not in the ‘Great Mosque’ (al-Masjid al-Akbar), for my grandfather (Imam Ali ibn Husayn (a.s)), peace be upon him, forbade a man from sharpening an arrowhead (mishqas) in the mosque.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَسَاجِدِ اَلْمُظَلَّلَةِ يُكْرَهُ اَلْقِيَامُ فِيهَا قَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ لَكِنْ لاَ تَضُرُّكُمُ اَلصَّلاَةُ فِيهَا اَلْيَوْمَ وَ لَوْ قَدْ كَانَ اَلْعَدْلُ لَرَأَيْتُمْ أَنْتُمْ كَيْفَ يُصْنَعُ فِي ذَلِكَ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ أَيُعَلِّقُ اَلرَّجُلُ اَلسِّلاَحَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ أَمَّا فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْأَكْبَرِ فَلاَ فَإِنَّ جَدِّي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ نَهَى رَجُلاً يَبْرِي مِشْقَصاً فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about covered mosques, is it disliked to stand in them? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, but prayer in them does not harm you today. And if justice were to be established, you would see for yourselves what would be done in that regard.” He (al-Halabi) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s), ‘May a man hang up his weapon in the mosque?’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, but not in the ‘Great Mosque’ (al-Masjid al-Akbar), for my grandfather (Imam Ali ibn Husayn (a.s)), peace be upon him, forbade a man from sharpening an arrowhead (mishqas) in the mosque.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 277

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam Ali (a.s) used to break the mihrabs when He (a.s) saw them in the mosques and would say: “It is as if they are altars of the Jews.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ طَلْحَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَكْسِرُ اَلْمَحَارِيبَ إِذَا رَآهَا فِي اَلْمَسَاجِدِ وَ يَقُولُ« كَأَنَّهَا مَذَابِحُ اَلْيَهُودِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) used to break the mihrabs when He (a.s) saw them in the mosques and would say: “It is as if they are altars of the Jews.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 278

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s):
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, saw a mosque in Kufah that had been elevated in height, and Imam (a.s) said: “It is as if it is a church,” And Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, Mosques are to be built plainly, not elevated.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ: أَنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ رَأَى مَسْجِداً بِالْكُوفَةِ قَدْ شُرِّفَ فَقَالَ« كَأَنَّهُ بِيعَةٌ» وَ قَالَ« إِنَّ اَلْمَسَاجِدَ تُبْنَى جُمّاً لاَ تُشَرَّفُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, saw a mosque in Kufah that had been elevated in height, and Imam (a.s) said: “It is as if it is a church,” And Imam (a.s) said: “Indeed, Mosques are to be built plainly, not elevated.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 278

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Muhammad al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s):
Imam Ali (a.s), said: “A prayer in ‘Bayt al-Maqdis’ is equal to one thousand prayers, And a prayer in ‘Grand Mosque’ (al-Masjid al-A'zam) is equal to one hundred prayers, And a prayer in ‘Mosque of the Tribe’ (Masjid al-qabila) is equal to twenty-five prayers, And a prayer in the ‘Market Mosque’ (masjid al-suq) is equal to twelve prayers, And the prayer of a man alone in his house is one single prayer.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَسَّانَ عَنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «صَلاَةٌ فِي بَيْتِ اَلْمَقْدِسِ أَلْفُ صَلاَةٍ وَ صَلاَةٌ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْأَعْظَمِ مِائَةُ صَلاَةٍ وَ صَلاَةٌ فِي مَسْجِدِ اَلْقَبِيلَةِ خَمْسٌ وَعِشْرُونَ صَلاَةً وَ صَلاَةٌ فِي مَسْجِدِ اَلسُّوقِ اِثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ صَلاَةً وَ صَلاَةُ اَلرَّجُلِ فِي بَيْتِهِ وَحْدَهُ صَلاَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Muhammad al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s), said: “A prayer in ‘Bayt al-Maqdis’ is equal to one thousand prayers, And a prayer in ‘Grand Mosque’ (al-Masjid al-A'zam) is equal to one hundred prayers, And a prayer in ‘Mosque of the Tribe’ (Masjid al-qabila) is equal to twenty-five prayers, And a prayer in the ‘Market Mosque’ (masjid al-suq) is equal to twelve prayers, And the prayer of a man alone in his house is one single prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 278

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from Habbah al-Urani, who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, went out to al-Hirah and said: “Surely this shall be joined to this” And Imam (a.s) gestured with his hand to Kufah and al-Hirah, (Imam (a.s) continued) “Until land between them shall be sold by dinars, and a mosque shall indeed be built in al-Hirah with five hundred doors, in which the Caliph of the Riser ‘the Qa'im (ajf)’, may Allah (swt) the Exalted hasten his relief, will pray. This is because the ‘Mosque of Kufah’ will be too small for them. And indeed, twelve just Imams (a.s) shall pray in it.” I asked: “O Commander of the Faithful (a.s), will this ‘Mosque of Kufah’ that you describe, be able to accommodate the people on that day?” Imam (a.s) said: “Four mosques shall be built for him (the Qa'im (ajf)); Masjid al-Kufa will be the smallest of them, and this one, and two mosques at the two ends of Kufa, on this side and that side” And Imam (a.s) pointed with his hand toward the Basrans (al-Basriyyin) and the people of al-Ghari (al-Ghariyyin).
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ عُقْبَةَ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ أَبِي اَلْمِقْدَامِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَبَّةَ اَلْعُرَنِيِّ قَالَ: خَرَجَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِلَى اَلْحِيرَةِ فَقَالَ« لَتَصِلَنَّ هَذِهِ بِهَذِهِ» وَأَوْمَى بِيَدِهِ إِلَى اَلْكُوفَةِ وَ اَلْحِيرَةِ« حَتَّى يُبَاعَ اَلذِّرَاعُ فِيمَا بَيْنَهُمَا بِدَنَانِيرَ وَ لَيُبْنَيَنَّ بِالْحِيرَةِ مَسْجِدٌ لَهُ خَمْسُمِائَةِ بَابٍ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ خَلِيفَةُ اَلْقَائِمِ عَجَّلَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى فَرَجَهُ لِأَنَّ مَسْجِدَ اَلْكُوفَةِ لَيَضِيقُ عَنْهُمْ وَ لَيُصَلِّيَنَّ فِيهِ اِثْنَا عَشَرَ إِمَاماً عَدْلاً» قُلْتُ يَا أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَيَسَعُ مَسْجِدُ اَلْكُوفَةِ هَذَا اَلَّذِي تَصِفُ اَلنَّاسَ يَوْمَئِذٍ قَالَ« تُبْنَى لَهُ أَرْبَعُ مَسَاجِدَ مَسْجِدُ اَلْكُوفَةِ أَصْغَرُهَا وَ هَذَا وَ مَسْجِدَ انِ فِي طَرَفَيِ اَلْكُوفَةِ مِنْ هَذَا اَلْجَانِبِ وَ هَذَا اَلْجَانِبِ» وَ أَوْمَى بِيَدِهِ نَحْوَ اَلْبَصْرِيِّينَ وَ اَلْغَرِيَّيْنِ
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam, from his father, from Habbah al-Urani, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, went out to al-Hirah and said: “Surely this shall be joined to this” And Imam (a.s) gestured with his hand to Kufah and al-Hirah, (Imam (a.s) continued) “Until land between them shall be sold by dinars, and a mosque shall indeed be built in al-Hirah with five hundred doors, in which the Caliph of the Riser ‘the Qa'im (ajf)’, may Allah (swt) the Exalted hasten his relief, will pray. This is because the ‘Mosque of Kufah’ will be too small for them. And indeed, twelve just Imams (a.s) shall pray in it.” I asked: “O Commander of the Faithful (a.s), will this ‘Mosque of Kufah’ that you describe, be able to accommodate the people on that day?” Imam (a.s) said: “Four mosques shall be built for him (the Qa'im (ajf)); Masjid al-Kufa will be the smallest of them, and this one, and two mosques at the two ends of Kufa, on this side and that side” And Imam (a.s) pointed with his hand toward the Basrans (al-Basriyyin) and the people of al-Ghari (al-Ghariyyin).
