chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ali ibn Hadid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali:
Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, came intentionally from Medina to the ‘Mosque of Kufah’, and Imam (a.s) prayed in it four units of prayer. Then Imam (a.s) returned until he mounted his riding animal and took the road.
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُصَيْنِ وَ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ اَلثُّمَالِيِّ: أَنَّ عَلِيَّ بْنَ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَتَى مَسْجِدَ اَلْكُوفَةِ عَمْداً مِنَ اَلْمَدِينَةِ فَصَلَّى فِيهِ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ ثُمَّ عَادَ حَتَّى رَكِبَ رَاحِلَتَهُ وَ أَخَذَ اَلطَّرِيقَ
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ali ibn Hadid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Amr ibn Khalid, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s), peace be upon them both, came intentionally from Medina to the ‘Mosque of Kufah’, and Imam (a.s) prayed in it four units of prayer. Then Imam (a.s) returned until he mounted his riding animal and took the road.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 280

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about prayer in Medina, is it like the prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family? Imam (a.s) said: “No. Indeed, the prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, is equal to one thousand prayers, and the prayer in Medina is like the prayer in all other cities.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارِ بْنِ مُوسَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْمَدِينَةِ هَلْ هِيَ مِثْلُ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَالَ «لاَ إِنَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ أَلْفُ صَلاَةٍ وَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي اَلْمَدِينَةِ مِثْلُ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي سَائِرِ اَلْبُلْدَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about prayer in Medina, is it like the prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family? Imam (a.s) said: “No. Indeed, the prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, is equal to one thousand prayers, and the prayer in Medina is like the prayer in all other cities.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 280

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Abdillah al-Dihqan, from Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Keep your children and your insane ones and your buying and selling away from your mosques, and place your wash areas (matahir) at the doors of your mosques.’”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ بَشَّارٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلدِّهْقَانِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« جَنِّبُوا مَسَاجِدَكُمْ صِبْيَانَكُمْ وَ مَجَانِينَكُمْ وَ شِرَاءَكُمْ وَ بَيْعَكُمْ وَ اِجْعَلُوا مَطَاهِرَكُمْ عَلَى أَبْوَابِ مَسَاجِدِكُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Abdillah al-Dihqan, from Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Keep your children and your insane ones and your buying and selling away from your mosques, and place your wash areas (matahir) at the doors of your mosques.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 280

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And with this chain of transmission, he said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Whoever sweeps the mosque on Thursday and the night of Friday and removes from it dust, that can be scattered into the eye, Allah (swt) will forgive him.”
arabicText: وَبِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ:« مَنْ كَنَسَ اَلْمَسْجِدَ يَوْمَ اَلْخَمِيسِ وَلَيْلَةَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ فَأَخْرَجَ مِنْهُ مِنَ اَلتُّرَابِ مَا يُذَرُّ فِي اَلْعَيْنِ غَفَرَ اَللَّهُ لَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And with this chain of transmission, he said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Whoever sweeps the mosque on Thursday and the night of Friday and removes from it dust, that can be scattered into the eye, Allah (swt) will forgive him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 280

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Isa ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar with his chain of transmission, who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: “The boundary of the ‘Mosque of Kufah’ is at the end of the area of the lamp-makers (al-sarrajin); it was marked out by Adam (a.s), peace be upon him, and I dislike entering it while riding.” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘Then who changed it from its original plan?’” Imam (a.s) said: “The first of that was the flood in the time of Nuh (a.s), peace be upon him, then it was changed by the people of Kisra and al-Nu'man, then it was altered by Ziyad ibn Abi Sufyan, may the curse of Allah (swt) be upon him.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ بِإِسْنَادٍ لَهُ قَالَ: قَالَ لَهُ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« حَدُّ مَسْجِدِ اَلْكُوفَةِ آخِرُ اَلسَّرَّاجِينَ خَطَّهُ آدَمُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَأَنَا أَكْرَهُ أَنْ أَدْخُلَهُ رَاكِباً» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَمَنْ غَيَّرَهُ عَنْ خِطَّتِهِ قَالَ« أَمَّا أَوَّلُ ذَلِكَ فَالطُّوفَانُ فِي زَمَانِ نُوحٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ ثُمَّ غَيَّرَهُ أَصْحَابُ كِسْرَى وَ اَلنُّعْمَانِ ثُمَّ غَيَّرَهُ زِيَادُ بْنُ أَبِي سُفْيَانَ لَعْنَةُ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Isa ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar with his chain of transmission, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: “The boundary of the ‘Mosque of Kufah’ is at the end of the area of the lamp-makers (al-sarrajin); it was marked out by Adam (a.s), peace be upon him, and I dislike entering it while riding.” He (narrator) said: “I asked, ‘Then who changed it from its original plan?’” Imam (a.s) said: “The first of that was the flood in the time of Nuh (a.s), peace be upon him, then it was changed by the people of Kisra and al-Nu'man, then it was altered by Ziyad ibn Abi Sufyan, may the curse of Allah (swt) be upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 281

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I asked Abul Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about the grave of (Sayyidah) Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her. Imam (a.s) said: “She (s.a) was buried in her house, and when the Umayyads expanded the mosque, it became part of the mosque.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَبْرِ فَاطِمَةَ عَلَيْهَا اَلسَّلاَمُ فَقَالَ «دُفِنَتْ فِي بَيْتِهَا فَلَمَّا زَادَتْ بَنُو أُمَيَّةَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ صَارَتْ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abul Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about the grave of (Sayyidah) Fatimah (s.a), peace be upon her. Imam (a.s) said: “She (s.a) was buried in her house, and when the Umayyads expanded the mosque, it became part of the mosque.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 281

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ya'la ibn Hamzah, from al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever walks to the mosque, he does not place a foot on anything moist or dry except that the earth glorifies Allah (swt) on his behalf down to the seventh layer of the earth.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْلَى بْنِ حَمْزَةَ عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ مَشَى إِلَى اَلْمَسْجِدِ لَمْ يَضَعْ رِجْلاً عَلَى رَطْبٍ وَ لاَ يَابِسٍ إِلاَّ سَبَّحَتْ لَهُ اَلْأَرْضُ إِلَى اَلْأَرْضِ اَلسَّابِعَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ya'la ibn Hamzah, from al-Hajjal, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever walks to the mosque, he does not place a foot on anything moist or dry except that the earth glorifies Allah (swt) on his behalf down to the seventh layer of the earth.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 281

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
The Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Whoever makes the Quran his speech and the mosque his home, Allah (swt) will build for him a house in Paradise.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ هَاشِمٍ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« مَنْ كَانَ اَلْقُرْآنُ حَدِيثَهُ وَ اَلْمَسْجِدُ بَيْتَهُ بَنَى اَللَّهُ لَهُ بَيْتاً فِي اَلْجَنَّةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Whoever makes the Quran his speech and the mosque his home, Allah (swt) will build for him a house in Paradise.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 281

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his forefathers, from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam Ali (a.s) said: “Whoever eats anything whose odor is offensive, let him not come near the mosque.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ جَدِّهِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ أَكَلَ شَيْئاً مِنَ اَلْمُؤْذِيَاتِ رِيحُهَا فَلاَ يَقْرَبَنَّ اَلْمَسْجِدَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his forefathers, from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) said: “Whoever eats anything whose odor is offensive, let him not come near the mosque.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 281

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
The Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Take care of your sandals at the doors of your mosques, and he forbade a man from putting on his sandals while standing.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْكُوفِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ اَلْقَدَّاحِ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« تَعَاهَدُوا نِعَالَكُمْ عِنْدَ أَبْوَابِ مَسَاجِدِكُمْ وَ نَهَى أَنْ يَتَنَعَّلَ اَلرَّجُلُ وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Prophet, may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: “Take care of your sandals at the doors of your mosques, and he forbade a man from putting on his sandals while standing.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 281

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad from al-Barqi from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, passed by a tall minaret and ordered it to be demolished. Then Imam (a.s) said: “A minaret is not to be raised except to the level of the roof of the mosque.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَرَّ عَلَى مَنَارَةٍ طَوِيلَةٍ فَأَمَرَ بِهَدْمِهَا ثُمَّ قَالَ« لاَ تُرْفَعُ اَلْمَنَارَةُ إِلاَّ مَعَ سَطْحِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad from al-Barqi from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, passed by a tall minaret and ordered it to be demolished. Then Imam (a.s) said: “A minaret is not to be raised except to the level of the roof of the mosque.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 282

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Wahb ibn Wahb from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “If one of you removes a pebble from the mosque, let him return it to its place or to another mosque, for it glorifies Allah (swt) (does tasbih).”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ وَهْبِ بْنِ وَهْبٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا أَخْرَجَ أَحَدُكُمُ اَلْحَصَاةَ مِنَ اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَلْيَرُدَّهَا مَكَانَهَا أَوْ فِي مَسْجِدٍ آخَرَ فَإِنَّهَا تُسَبِّحُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from his father from Wahb ibn Wahb from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “If one of you removes a pebble from the mosque, let him return it to its place or to another mosque, for it glorifies Allah (swt) (does tasbih).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 282

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, peace be upon them:
Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Spitting in the mosque is a sin, and its expiation is to bury it.” (meaning cover it with sand)
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ غِيَاثِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْبُزَاقُ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ خَطِيئَةٌ وَ كَفَّارَتُهُ دَفْنُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Spitting in the mosque is a sin, and its expiation is to bury it.” (meaning cover it with sand)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 282

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Yasar from Ali ibn Ja’far al-Sakuni from Isma’il ibn Muslim al-Shayiri from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, peace be upon them:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever honors the mosque regarding his phlegm (spitting it in a respectful or hidden manner), he shall meet Allah (swt) on the Day of Resurrection smiling, having been given his book (of accountability) in his right hand (kitabahu biyaminihi).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ اَلشَّعِيرِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ وَقَّرَ بِنُخَامَتِهِ اَلْمَسْجِدَ لَقِيَ اَللَّهَ يَوْمَ اَلْقِيَامَةِ ضَاحِكاً قَدْ أُعْطِيَ« كِتٰابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Yasar from Ali ibn Ja’far al-Sakuni from Isma’il ibn Muslim al-Shayiri from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever honors the mosque regarding his phlegm (spitting it in a respectful or hidden manner), he shall meet Allah (swt) on the Day of Resurrection smiling, having been given his book (of accountability) in his right hand (kitabahu biyaminihi).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 282

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abu Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Whoever spits phlegm (tanakhkhaʿa) in the mosque and then swallows it back into his body, there will not remain any illness in his body except that it will be cured.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِي إِسْحَاقَ اَلنَّهَاوَنْدِيِّ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« مَنْ تَنَخَّعَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ ثُمَّ رَدَّهَا فِي جَوْفِهِ لَمْ تَمُرَّ بِدَاءٍ فِي جَوْفِهِ إِلاَّ أَبْرَأَتْهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abu Ishaq al-Nahawandi, from al-Barqi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Whoever spits phlegm (tanakhkhaʿa) in the mosque and then swallows it back into his body, there will not remain any illness in his body except that it will be cured.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 282

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Mihran from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “A man is in the mosque in prayer and wants to spit.” Imam (a.s) said: “To his left. And if he is not in prayer, then he should not spit facing the Qiblah, but he may spit to his right or to his left.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَكُونُ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَيُرِيدُ أَنْ يَبْصُقَ فَقَالَ« عَنْ يَسَارِهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ فِي غَيْرِ صَلاَةٍ فَلاَ يَبْزُقْ حِذَاءَ اَلْقِبْلَةِ وَ يَبْزُقُ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ شِمَالِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Mihran from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “A man is in the mosque in prayer and wants to spit.” Imam (a.s) said: “To his left. And if he is not in prayer, then he should not spit facing the Qiblah, but he may spit to his right or to his left.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 283

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Talhah ibn Zayd from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Let none of you spit during prayer in front of his face, nor to his right, but let him spit to his left and beneath his left foot.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ طَلْحَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يَبْزُقَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قِبَلَ وَجْهِهِ وَ لاَ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ لْيَبْزُقْ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ وَ تَحْتَ قَدَمِهِ اَلْيُسْرَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Talhah ibn Zayd from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Let none of you spit during prayer in front of his face, nor to his right, but let him spit to his left and beneath his left foot.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 283

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar said:
I saw Abu Ja’far al-Thani (a.s) (the Second), peace be upon him, spit in the ‘Sacred Mosque’ (al-Masjid al-Haram) between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone, and Imam (a.s) did not bury it.
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ اَلثَّانِيَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ تَفَلَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرَامِ فِيمَا بَيْنَ اَلرُّكْنِ اَلْيَمَانِيِّ وَ اَلْحَجَرِ اَلْأَسْوَدِ وَ لَمْ يَدْفِنْهُ
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Ja’far al-Thani (a.s) (the Second), peace be upon him, spit in the ‘Sacred Mosque’ (al-Masjid al-Haram) between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone, and Imam (a.s) did not bury it.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 283

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from al-Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Safwan from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman, the client of Tirbal, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, used to pray in the mosque and would spit in front of him, to his right, to his left, and behind him on the pebbles, and he would not cover it.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ مَوْلَى طِرْبَالٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« كَانَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يُصَلِّي فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَيَبْصُقُ أَمَامَهُ وَ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ عَنْ شِمَالِهِ وَ خَلْفَهُ عَلَى اَلْحَصَى وَ لاَ يُغَطِّيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from al-Abbas ibn Ma‘ruf from Safwan from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman, the client of Tirbal, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, used to pray in the mosque and would spit in front of him, to his right, to his left, and behind him on the pebbles, and he would not cover it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 283

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about performing ablution in the mosque. Imam (a.s) disliked it when it was after defecation or urination. (meaning dislike ‘karahah’ for doing wudu in the mosque when the cause for purification was relieving oneself)
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ بْنِ مُوسَى قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْوُضُوءِ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَكَرِهَهُ مِنَ اَلْغَائِطِ وَ اَلْبَوْلِ
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Rifa‘ah ibn Musa who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about performing ablution in the mosque. Imam (a.s) disliked it when it was after defecation or urination. (meaning dislike ‘karahah’ for doing wudu in the mosque when the cause for purification was relieving oneself)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 284

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about sleeping in the ‘Sacred Mosque’ (al-Masjid al-Haram) and the ‘Mosque of the Messenger (saws)’. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. Where else would people sleep?”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلنَّوْمِ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرَامِ وَ مَسْجِدِ اَلرَّسُولِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ أَيْنَ يَنَامُ اَلنَّاسُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahb who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about sleeping in the ‘Sacred Mosque’ (al-Masjid al-Haram) and the ‘Mosque of the Messenger (saws)’. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes. Where else would people sleep?”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 284

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What do you say about sleeping in the mosques?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem except in two mosques; the ‘Mosque of the Prophet (saws)’, peace be upon him and his family, and the ‘Sacred Mosque.’” He (Zurarah) said: “And Imam (a.s) would take me by the hand during part of the night, then withdraw to a side, and sit and talk in the ‘Sacred Mosque’, and Imam (a.s) would sometimes sleep. So I asked Imam (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: ‘It is only disliked to sleep in the part of the mosque that existed during the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. As for that which is in this area, there is no problem with it.’”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَا تَقُولُ فِي اَلنَّوْمِ فِي اَلْمَسَاجِدِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ إِلاَّ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدَيْنِ مَسْجِدِ اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ مَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرَامِ» قَالَ وَ كَانَ يَأْخُذُ بِيَدِي فِي بَعْضِ اَللَّيْلِ فَيَتَنَحَّى نَاحِيَةً ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ فَيَتَحَدَّثُ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلْحَرَامِ فَرُبَّمَا نَامَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ فِي ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ« إِنَّمَا يُكْرَهُ أَنْ يُنَامَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلَّذِي كَانَ عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَأَمَّا اَلَّذِي فِي هَذَا اَلْمَوْضِعِ فَلَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “What do you say about sleeping in the mosques?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem except in two mosques; the ‘Mosque of the Prophet (saws)’, peace be upon him and his family, and the ‘Sacred Mosque.’” He (Zurarah) said: “And Imam (a.s) would take me by the hand during part of the night, then withdraw to a side, and sit and talk in the ‘Sacred Mosque’, and Imam (a.s) would sometimes sleep. So I asked Imam (a.s) about that, and Imam (a.s) said: ‘It is only disliked to sleep in the part of the mosque that existed during the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. As for that which is in this area, there is no problem with it.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 284

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: Do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated’ (Surah An Nisa 4:43). Imam (a.s) said: “(It is referring to) ‘the intoxication of sleep’.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ اَلْمُخْتَارِ عَنْ أَبِي أُسَامَةَ زَيْدٍ اَلشَّحَّامِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَوْلُ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« لاٰ تَقْرَبُوا اَلصَّلاٰةَ وَ أَنْتُمْ سُكٰارىٰ» قَالَ« سُكْرُ اَلنَّوْمِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from Abu Usamah Zayd al-Shahham who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: Do not approach the prayer while you are intoxicated’ (Surah An Nisa 4:43). Imam (a.s) said: “(It is referring to) ‘the intoxication of sleep’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 284

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from one of his companions who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I feel dislike for praying in their mosques (the opponents).” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not dislike it, for there is no mosque that was built except upon the grave of a prophet or the trustee (wasi) of a prophet who was killed, and a sprinkling of his blood reached that spot, so Allah (swt) loved that He (azj) be remembered there. So perform in them (these mosques) the obligatory prayers, and the recommended ones, and make up in them what you have missed (of prayers).”
arabicText: اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي لَأَكْرَهُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي مَسَاجِدِهِمْ فَقَالَ« لاَ تَكْرَهْ فَمَا مِنْ مَسْجِدٍ بُنِيَ إِلاَّ عَلَى قَبْرِ نَبِيٍّ أَوْ وَصِيِّ نَبِيٍّ قُتِلَ فَأَصَابَ تِلْكَ اَلْبُقْعَةَ رَشَّةٌ مِنْ دَمِهِ فَأَحَبَّ اَللَّهُ أَنْ يُذْكَرَ فِيهَا فَأَدِّ فِيهَا اَلْفَرَائِضَ وَ اَلنَّوَافِلَ وَ اِقْضِ مَا فَاتَكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from one of his companions who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I feel dislike for praying in their mosques (the opponents).” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not dislike it, for there is no mosque that was built except upon the grave of a prophet or the trustee (wasi) of a prophet who was killed, and a sprinkling of his blood reached that spot, so Allah (swt) loved that He (azj) be remembered there. So perform in them (these mosques) the obligatory prayers, and the recommended ones, and make up in them what you have missed (of prayers).”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-‘Ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, forbade drawing the sword in the mosque and sharpening arrows in the mosque,” And Imam (a.s) said: “It (Mosque) was only built for other than that.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« نَهَى رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ عَنْ سَلِّ اَلسَّيْفِ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ وَ عَنْ بَرْيِ اَلنَّبْلِ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ» وَ قَالَ« إِنَّمَا بُنِيَ لِغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from al-‘Ala from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, forbade drawing the sword in the mosque and sharpening arrows in the mosque,” And Imam (a.s) said: “It (Mosque) was only built for other than that.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 285

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Ja’far ibn Ibrahim from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, who said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: “Whoever you hear reciting poetry in the mosques, say to him: ‘May Allah (swt) break your mouth! Verily, the mosques were only established for the Qur’an.’”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ اَلْحَجَّاجِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« مَنْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ يُنْشِدُ اَلشِّعْرَ فِي اَلْمَسَاجِدِ فَقُولُوا فَضَّ اَللَّهُ فَاكَ إِنَّمَا نُصِبَتِ اَلْمَسَاجِدُ لِلْقُرْآنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Ja’far ibn Ibrahim from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: “Whoever you hear reciting poetry in the mosques, say to him: ‘May Allah (swt) break your mouth! Verily, the mosques were only established for the Qur’an.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 285

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-‘Alawi from Sahl ibn Jumhur from Abd al-‘Azim ibn Abdillah al-‘Alawi from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-‘Urani from Amr ibn Jumay’ who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about praying in mosques that contain images. Imam (a.s) said: “I dislike that, but it does not harm you today. And if the ‘Just One’ (al Qaim (ajf)) were to rise, you would see what He (ajf) would do regarding that.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ اَلْعَلَوِيِّ عَنْ سَهْلِ بْنِ جُمْهُورٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْعَظِيمِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْعَلَوِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ اَلْعُرَنِيِّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ جُمَيْعٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْمَسَاجِدِ اَلْمُصَوَّرَةِ فَقَالَ« أَكْرَهُ ذَلِكَ وَ لَكِنْ لاَ يَضُرُّكُمْ ذَلِكَ اَلْيَوْمَ وَ لَوْ قَدْ قَامَ اَلْعَدْلُ لَرَأَيْتُمْ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ فِي ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ya‘qub from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-‘Alawi from Sahl ibn Jumhur from Abd al-‘Azim ibn Abdillah al-‘Alawi from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-‘Urani from Amr ibn Jumay’ who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about praying in mosques that contain images. Imam (a.s) said: “I dislike that, but it does not harm you today. And if the ‘Just One’ (al Qaim (ajf)) were to rise, you would see what He (ajf) would do regarding that.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 285

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu al-Jarud who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about a mosque that is within a house, and the people of the house want to expand into part of it, or move it to another place. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that.” He (Abu al-Jarud) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about a place that was previously a refuse area, then it is cleaned and made into a mosque.” Imam (a.s) said: “Let earth be thrown over it until it covers it, for that is purer.”
arabicText: سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْجَارُودِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ يَكُونُ فِي اَلْبَيْتِ فَيُرِيدُ أَهْلُ اَلْبَيْتِ أَنْ يَتَوَسَّعُوا بِطَائِفَةٍ مِنْهُ أَوْ يُحَوِّلُونَهُ إِلَى غَيْرِ مَكَانِهِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ مَكَانٍ يَكُونُ حَشّاًثُمَّ يُنَظَّفُ وَ يُجْعَلُ مَسْجِداً قَالَ« يُطْرَحُ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اَلتُّرَابِ حَتَّى يُوَارِيَهُ فَهُوَ أَطْهَرُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu al-Jarud who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about a mosque that is within a house, and the people of the house want to expand into part of it, or move it to another place. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that.” He (Abu al-Jarud) said: “And I asked Imam (a.s) about a place that was previously a refuse area, then it is cleaned and made into a mosque.” Imam (a.s) said: “Let earth be thrown over it until it covers it, for that is purer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 285

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Safwan from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman, the freed slave of Tirbal, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “The entire earth is a mosque except for a latrine pit, or a graveyard.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ مَوْلَى طِرْبَالٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« اَلْأَرْضُ كُلُّهَا مَسْجِدٌ إِلاَّ بِئْرَ غَائِطٍ أَوْ مَقْبَرَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Safwan from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman, the freed slave of Tirbal, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “The entire earth is a mosque except for a latrine pit, or a graveyard.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 285

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas‘adah ibn Sadaqah al-Ruba‘i from Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked: “Is it permissible for a place that was a refuse area to be made into a mosque?” Imam (a.s) said: “If earth is thrown over it to cover it and to cut off its odor, then there is no problem. And that is because earth is purifying, and with it the Sunnah has proceeded.”
arabicText: سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ هَارُونَ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ مَسْعَدَةَ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ اَلرَّبَعِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَ يَصْلُحُ مَكَانٌ حَشٌّ أَنْ يُتَّخَذَ مَسْجِداً فَقَالَ« إِذَا أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اَلتُّرَابِ مَا يُوَارِي ذَلِكَ وَ يَقْطَعُ رِيحَهُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ وَ ذَلِكَ لِأَنَّ اَلتُّرَابَ طَهُورٌ وَ بِهِ مَضَتِ اَلسُّنَّةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas‘adah ibn Sadaqah al-Ruba‘i from Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked: “Is it permissible for a place that was a refuse area to be made into a mosque?” Imam (a.s) said: “If earth is thrown over it to cover it and to cut off its odor, then there is no problem. And that is because earth is purifying, and with it the Sunnah has proceeded.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 286

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a mosque that is within a house or a room, and its people want to expand into part of it or move it to another place. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that.” I (ibn Sinan) said: “And what about a place that was a refuse area for some time, then it is cleaned and made into a mosque?” Imam (a.s) said: “Throw earth over it until it is covered, for that purifies it, if Allah (swt), the Exalted, wills.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ يَكُونُ فِي اَلدَّارِ وَ فِي اَلْبَيْتِ وَ يَبْدُو لِأَهْلِهِ أَنْ يَتَوَسَّعُوا بِطَائِفَةٍ مِنْهُ أَوْ يُحَوِّلُونَهُ إِلَى غَيْرِ مَكَانِهِ فَقَالَ «لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ» قُلْتُ فَالْمَكَانُ يَكُونُ حَشّاً زَمَاناً فَيُنَظَّفُ وَ يُتَّخَذُ مَسْجِداً فَقَالَ« أَلْقِ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ اَلتُّرَابِ حَتَّى يَتَوَارَى فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ يُطَهِّرُهُ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a mosque that is within a house or a room, and its people want to expand into part of it or move it to another place. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm in that.” I (ibn Sinan) said: “And what about a place that was a refuse area for some time, then it is cleaned and made into a mosque?” Imam (a.s) said: “Throw earth over it until it is covered, for that purifies it, if Allah (swt), the Exalted, wills.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 286

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun from Muhammad ibn Mudharib from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There is no harm in making a mosque over a place of excrement.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُضَارِبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ يُجْعَلَ عَلَى اَلْعَذِرَةِ مَسْجِداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun from Muhammad ibn Mudharib from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There is no harm in making a mosque over a place of excrement.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from al-‘Is ibn al-Qasim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about churches and synagogues, is it permissible to demolish them for the construction of mosques? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعِيصِ بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْبِيَعِ وَ اَلْكَنَائِسِ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ نَقْضُهَا لِبِنَاءِ اَلْمَسَاجِدِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Isma’il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan from al-‘Is ibn al-Qasim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about churches and synagogues, is it permissible to demolish them for the construction of mosques? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Ishaq ibn Yashkur al-Kahili from al-Hakam from Anas who said:
The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: “Whoever lights a lamp in a mosque from among the mosques of Allah (swt), the angels and the bearers of ‘the Throne’ will continue to seek forgiveness for him as long as there is light from that lamp in the mosque.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَسَّانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ يَشْكُرَ اَلْكَاهِلِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَنَسٍ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« مَنْ أَسْرَجَ فِي مَسْجِدٍ مِنْ مَسَاجِدِ اَللَّهِ سِرَاجاً لَمْ تَزَلِ اَلْمَلاَئِكَةُ وَ حَمَلَةُ اَلْعَرْشِ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لَهُ مَادَامَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ ضَوْءٌ مِنْ ذَلِكَ اَلسِّرَاجِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Ishaq ibn Yashkur al-Kahili from al-Hakam from Anas who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said: “Whoever lights a lamp in a mosque from among the mosques of Allah (swt), the angels and the bearers of ‘the Throne’ will continue to seek forgiveness for him as long as there is light from that lamp in the mosque.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali Ibrahim ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “A man leads us in prayer and we follow him, is that more beloved to you, or praying in the mosque?” Imam (a.s) said: “(Praying in) the mosque is more beloved to me.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنَّ رَجُلاً يُصَلِّي بِنَا نَقْتَدِي بِهِ فَهُوَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيْكَ أَوْ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ قَالَ« اَلْمَسْجِدُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali Ibrahim ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “A man leads us in prayer and we follow him, is that more beloved to you, or praying in the mosque?” Imam (a.s) said: “(Praying in) the mosque is more beloved to me.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam Ali (a.s) said: “There is no prayer for the one who does not attend the obligatory prayers with the neighbours of the mosque, when he is free and in good health.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ طَلْحَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ صَلاَةَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَشْهَدِ اَلصَّلَوَاتِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَاتِ مِنْ جِيرَانِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ إِذَا كَانَ فَارِغاً صَحِيحاً»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s) said: “There is no prayer for the one who does not attend the obligatory prayers with the neighbours of the mosque, when he is free and in good health.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the mosque which ‘was founded on piety’. Imam (a.s) said: “The Mosque of Quba.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ اَلَّذِي« أُسِّسَ عَلَى اَلتَّقْوىٰ» فَقَالَ« مَسْجِدُ قُبَاءَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the mosque which ‘was founded on piety’. Imam (a.s) said: “The Mosque of Quba.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 287

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn Isma’il from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa’id who said: Musa ibn Ukayl narrated to me from Abd al-A‘la, the freed slave of the family of Sam, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “How large was the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family?” Imam (a.s) said: “Three thousand and six hundred cubits, irregularly shaped.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي مُوسَى بْنُ أُكَيْلٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلْأَعْلَى مَوْلَى آلِ سَامٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَمْ كَانَ مَسْجِدُ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَقَالَ« ثَلاَثَةُ آلاَفٍ وَ سِتُّمِائَةِ ذِرَاعٍ مُكَسَّراً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ali ibn Isma’il from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Sa’id who said: Musa ibn Ukayl narrated to me from Abd al-A‘la, the freed slave of the family of Sam, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “How large was the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family?” Imam (a.s) said: “Three thousand and six hundred cubits, irregularly shaped.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I heard Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) say: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, built his mosque with samit (a type of simple material), then the Muslims increased in number, so they said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), if only you would command the mosque to be expanded’. Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” So Prophet (saws) commanded it, and it was expanded, and He (saws) built it with sa'idah (palm trunks or branches). Then the Muslims increased again, so they said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), if only you would command the mosque to be expanded’. Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” So Prophet (saws) commanded it, and it was expanded, and its wall was built with ‘al-Untha’ and ‘al-Dhakar’ (with clay bricks called 'female' and 'male'). Then the heat became intense for them, so they said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), if only you would command the mosque to be shaded’. Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” So Prophet (saws) commanded it, and pillars were erected in it from palm trunks, then crossbeams and palm leaves and al-idhkhar (a fragrant desert grass) were placed over them. And they remained in it until rain struck them, and the mosque began to drip on them. So they said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), if only you would command the mosque to be plastered with clay’. The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said to them: “No. A canopy like the canopy of Musa (a.s), peace be upon him.” And it remained like that until the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, passed away. Its wall, before it was shaded, was (equivalent to) a man’s height. And when the shadow (al-fay’) reached one cubit, which is the space of a goat’s resting place, He (saws) would pray the noon prayer (al-Dhuhr). And when it became double that, He (saws) would pray the afternoon prayer (al-Asr).” And Imam (a.s) said: “ ‘As-samit’ is one brick by one brick, ‘As-sa‘idah’ is one and a half bricks, and ‘Al-untha’ and ‘Al-dhakar’ are two differing bricks.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ:« إِنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بَنَى مَسْجِدَهُ بِالسُّمَيْطِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ كَثُرُوا فَقَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ لَوْ أَمَرْتَ بِالْمَسْجِدِ فَزِيدَ فِيهِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» فَأَمَرَ بِهِ فَزِيدَ فِيهِ وَ بَنَاهُ بِالسَّعِيدَةِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ اَلْمُسْلِمِينَ كَثُرُوا فَقَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ لَوْ أَمَرْتَ بِالْمَسْجِدِ فَزِيدَ فِيهِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» فَأَمَرَ بِهِ فَزِيدَ فِيهِ وَ بُنِيَ جِدَارُهُ بِالْأُنْثَى وَ اَلذَّكَرِ ثُمَّ اِشْتَدَّ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلْحَرُّ فَقَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ لَوْ أَمَرْتَ بِالْمَسْجِدِ فَظُلِّلَ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» فَأَمَرَ بِهِ فَأُقِيمَتْ فِيهِ سَوَارِي مِنْ جُذُوعِ اَلنَّخْلِ ثُمَّ طُرِحَتْ عَلَيْهِ اَلْعَوَارِضُ وَ اَلْخَصَفُ وَ اَلْإِذْخِرُ فَعَاشُوا فِيهِ حَتَّى أَصَابَتْهُمُ اَلْأَمْطَارُ فَجَعَلَ اَلْمَسْجِدُ يَكِفُ عَلَيْهِمْ فَقَالُوا يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ لَوْ أَمَرْتَ بِالْمَسْجِدِ فَطُيِّنَ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ« لاَ عَرِيشٌ كَعَرِيشِ مُوسَى عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ» فَلَمْ يَزَلْ كَذَلِكَ حَتَّى قُبِضَ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَكَانَ جِدَارُهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُظَلَّلَ قَامَةً فَكَانَ إِذَا كَانَ اَلْفَيْءُ ذِرَاعاً وَ هُوَ قَدْرُ مَرْبِضِ عَنْزٍ يُصَلِّي اَلظُّهْرَ فَإِذَا كَانَ ضِعْفَ ذَلِكَ صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ» وَ قَالَ «اَلسَّمِيطُ لَبِنَةٌ لَبِنَةٌ وَ اَلسَّعِيدَةُ لَبِنَةٌ وَنِصْفٌ وَ اَلْأُنْثَى وَ اَلذَّكَرُ لَبِنَتَانِ مُخَالِفَتَانِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) say: “Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, built his mosque with samit (a type of simple material), then the Muslims increased in number, so they said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), if only you would command the mosque to be expanded’. Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” So Prophet (saws) commanded it, and it was expanded, and He (saws) built it with sa'idah (palm trunks or branches). Then the Muslims increased again, so they said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), if only you would command the mosque to be expanded’. Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” So Prophet (saws) commanded it, and it was expanded, and its wall was built with ‘al-Untha’ and ‘al-Dhakar’ (with clay bricks called 'female' and 'male'). Then the heat became intense for them, so they said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), if only you would command the mosque to be shaded’. Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” So Prophet (saws) commanded it, and pillars were erected in it from palm trunks, then crossbeams and palm leaves and al-idhkhar (a fragrant desert grass) were placed over them. And they remained in it until rain struck them, and the mosque began to drip on them. So they said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), if only you would command the mosque to be plastered with clay’. The Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said to them: “No. A canopy like the canopy of Musa (a.s), peace be upon him.” And it remained like that until the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, passed away. Its wall, before it was shaded, was (equivalent to) a man’s height. And when the shadow (al-fay’) reached one cubit, which is the space of a goat’s resting place, He (saws) would pray the noon prayer (al-Dhuhr). And when it became double that, He (saws) would pray the afternoon prayer (al-Asr).” And Imam (a.s) said: “ ‘As-samit’ is one brick by one brick, ‘As-sa‘idah’ is one and a half bricks, and ‘Al-untha’ and ‘Al-dhakar’ are two differing bricks.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ibrahim ibn Hashim from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Prophet (saws), peace be upon him and his family, forbade the speaking of foreign languages (ratanat al-a‘ajim) in the mosques.” (meaning to preserve arabic clarity, reverence, and unity in worship)
arabicText: إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ هَاشِمٍ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« نَهَى اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ عَنْ رَطَانَةِ اَلْأَعَاجِمِ فِي اَلْمَسَاجِدِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ibrahim ibn Hashim from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Prophet (saws), peace be upon him and his family, forbade the speaking of foreign languages (ratanat al-a‘ajim) in the mosques.” (meaning to preserve arabic clarity, reverence, and unity in worship)

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
The Prophet (saws) said: “Whoever hears the call to prayer in the mosque, and leaves without an excuse is a hypocrite, unless he intends to return to it.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ:« مَنْ سَمِعَ اَلنِّدَاءَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَخَرَجَ مِنْ غَيْرِ عِلَّةٍ فَهُوَ مُنَافِقٌ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُرِيدَ اَلرُّجُوعَ إِلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: The Prophet (saws) said: “Whoever hears the call to prayer in the mosque, and leaves without an excuse is a hypocrite, unless he intends to return to it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 289

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him (a.s), from his forefathers (a.s), peace be upon them:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Prophet (saws), saw a man flicking a pebble in the mosque. Prophet (saws) said: “It continues to be cursed until it lands.” He (saws) said: “Flicking pebbles in gatherings is from the manners of people of Lut.” Then Prophet (saws), peace be upon him, recited: “And you commit in your gatherings what is detestable” (Surah Al Ankabut 29:29), And Prophet (saws) said: “That is the flicking of pebbles.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَنَّ اَلنَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ أَبْصَرَ رَجُلاً يَخْذِفُ بِحَصَاةٍ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَقَالَ« مَا زَالَتْ تَلْعَنُ حَتَّى وَقَعَتْ»» ثُمَّ قَالَ« اَلْخَذْفُ فِي اَلنَّادِي مِنْ أَخْلاَقِ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ» ثُمَّ تَلاَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ«« وَ تَأْتُونَ فِي نٰادِيكُمُ اَلْمُنْكَرَ»» قَالَ« هُوَ اَلْخَذْفُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him (a.s), from his forefathers (a.s), peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Prophet (saws), saw a man flicking a pebble in the mosque. Prophet (saws) said: “It continues to be cursed until it lands.” He (saws) said: “Flicking pebbles in gatherings is from the manners of people of Lut.” Then Prophet (saws), peace be upon him, recited: “And you commit in your gatherings what is detestable” (Surah Al Ankabut 29:29), And Prophet (saws) said: “That is the flicking of pebbles.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad from al-Barqi from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both:
The Prophet (saws), peace be upon him and his family, said: “Uncovering the navel, the thigh, and the knee in the mosque is from the ‘awrah (private parts to be covered).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ اَلنَّوْفَلِيِّ عَنِ اَلسَّكُونِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ اَلنَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَالَ:« كَشْفُ اَلسُّرَّةِ وَ اَلْفَخِذِ وَ اَلرُّكْبَةِ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ مِنَ اَلْعَوْرَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad from al-Barqi from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both:
thaqalaynMatn: The Prophet (saws), peace be upon him and his family, said: “Uncovering the navel, the thigh, and the knee in the mosque is from the ‘awrah (private parts to be covered).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 289

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-‘Ala ibn Fudayl from one who narrated it from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “When you enter the mosque intending to sit, do not enter it except in a state of purity. And when you enter, face the qiblah, then supplicate to Allah (swt) and ask Him (azj), and mention His (azj) name when you enter it. And praise Allah (swt) and send blessings upon the Prophet (saws), peace be upon him and his family.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلصُّهْبَانِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ فُضَيْلٍ عَمَّنْ رَوَاهُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا دَخَلْتَ اَلْمَسْجِدَ وَ أَنْتَ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَجْلِسَ فَلاَ تَدْخُلْهُ إِلاَّ طَاهِراً وَ إِذَا دَخَلْتَ فَاسْتَقْبِلِ اَلْقِبْلَةَ ثُمَّ اُدْعُ اَللَّهَ وَ اِسْأَلْهُ وَ سَمِّ حِينَ تَدْخُلُهُ وَ اِحْمَدِ اَللَّهَ وَ صَلِّ عَلَى اَلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-‘Ala ibn Fudayl from one who narrated it from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “When you enter the mosque intending to sit, do not enter it except in a state of purity. And when you enter, face the qiblah, then supplicate to Allah (swt) and ask Him (azj), and mention His (azj) name when you enter it. And praise Allah (swt) and send blessings upon the Prophet (saws), peace be upon him and his family.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 289

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah who said:
It was said: “When you enter the mosque, say: ‘In the name of Allah (swt), and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah (swt). Indeed, Allah (swt) and His (azj) angels send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), And peace be upon them and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His (azj) blessings. My Lord (azj), forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your grace.’ And when you leave (the mosque), say the same.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ:« إِذَا دَخَلْتَ اَلْمَسْجِدَ فَقُلْ بِسْمِ اَللَّهِ وَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ إِنَّ اَللَّهَ وَ مَلاَئِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَ رَحْمَةُ اَللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ رَبِّ اِغْفِرْ لِي ذُنُوبِي وَ اِفْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ فَضْلِكَ وَ إِذَا خَرَجْتَ فَقُلْ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Hasan from Zur’ah from Sama’ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: It was said: “When you enter the mosque, say: ‘In the name of Allah (swt), and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah (swt). Indeed, Allah (swt) and His (azj) angels send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), And peace be upon them and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His (azj) blessings. My Lord (azj), forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your grace.’ And when you leave (the mosque), say the same.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Fudayl ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan who said:
It was said: “When you enter the mosque, say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your mercy’. And when you leave, say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), forgive me and open for me the doors of Your grace’.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ فُضَيْلِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ قَالَ:« إِذَا دَخَلْتَ اَلْمَسْجِدَ فَقُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ اِغْفِرْ لِي ذُنُوبِي وَ اِفْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ وَ إِذَا خَرَجْتَ فَقُلِ اَللَّهُمَّ اِغْفِرْ لِي وَ اِفْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ فَضْلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Fudayl ibn Uthman from Abdullah ibn al-Hasan who said:
thaqalaynMatn: It was said: “When you enter the mosque, say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), forgive me my sins and open for me the doors of Your mercy’. And when you leave, say: ‘O’ Allah (swt), forgive me and open for me the doors of Your grace’.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 290

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hajjal from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir from Hassan al-Jammal who said:
I carried Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from Medina to Mecca. He (Hassan al-Jammal) said: “When we reached the ‘Mosque of al-Ghadir’, Imam (a.s) looked towards the left side of the mosque and said: ‘That is the place of the foot of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, where Prophet (saws) said: ‘Whoever I am his master (mawla), then Ali (a.s) is his master (mawla). O’ Allah (swt), befriend whoever befriends him and be the enemy of whoever is his enemy.’” Then Imam (a.s) looked to the other side and said: “This is the place of the tent of ‘so-and-so’ and ‘so-and-so’ and Salim, the mawla (freed slave) of Abu Hudhayfah, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. When they saw Prophet (saws) raising his (Imam Ali (a.s)) hand, some of them said: ‘Look at his eyes, they are turning as if they are the eyes of a madman.’ So Jibra'il (a.s), peace be upon him, descended with the verse: ‘And indeed, those who disbelieve, almost drive you to slip with their eyes when they hear the message, and they say: Indeed, he is mad; but it is nothing except a reminder to the worlds.’” (Surah Al Qalam 68:51-52) Then Imam (a.s) said: “O Hassan, were it not for the fact that you are my camel driver, I would not have narrated this hadith to you.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلصَّمَدِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ حَسَّانَ اَلْجَمَّالِ قَالَ: حَمَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مِنَ اَلْمَدِينَةِ إِلَى مَكَّةَ قَالَ فَلَمَّا اِنْتَهَيْنَا إِلَى مَسْجِدِ اَلْغَدِيرِ نَظَرَ فِي مَيْسَرَةِ اَلْمَسْجِدِ فَقَالَ« ذَاكَ مَوْضِعُ قَدَمِ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ حَيْثُ قَالَ« مَنْ كُنْتُ مَوْلاَهُ فَعَلِيٌّ مَوْلاَهُ اَللَّهُمَّ وَالِ مَنْ وَالاَهُ وَ عَادِ مَنْ عَادَاهُ»» ثُمَّ نَظَرَ فِي اَلْجَانِبِ اَلْآخَرِ فَقَالَ« هَذَا مَوْضِعُ فُسْطَاطِ أَبِي فُلاَنٍ وَ فُلاَنٍ وَ سَالِمٍ مَوْلَى أَبِي حُذَيْفَةَ وَ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ بْنِ اَلْجَرَّاحِ فَلَمَّا أَنْ رَأَوْهُ رَافِعاً يَدَهُ قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ اُنْظُرُوا إِلَى عَيْنَيْهِ تَدُورَانِ كَأَنَّهُمَا عَيْنَا مَجْنُونٍ فَنَزَلَ جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِهَذِهِ اَلْآيَةِ« وَ إِنْ يَكٰادُ اَلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ بِأَبْصٰارِهِمْ لَمّٰا سَمِعُوا اَلذِّكْرَ وَ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُ لَمَجْنُونٌ` وَ مٰا هُوَ إِلاّٰ ذِكْرٌ لِلْعٰالَمِينَ»» ثُمَّ قَالَ« يَا حَسَّانُ لَوْلاَ أَنَّكَ جَمَّالِي لَمَا حَدَّثْتُكَ بِهَذَا اَلْحَدِيثِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hajjal from Abd al-Samad ibn Bashir from Hassan al-Jammal who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I carried Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from Medina to Mecca. He (Hassan al-Jammal) said: “When we reached the ‘Mosque of al-Ghadir’, Imam (a.s) looked towards the left side of the mosque and said: ‘That is the place of the foot of the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, where Prophet (saws) said: ‘Whoever I am his master (mawla), then Ali (a.s) is his master (mawla). O’ Allah (swt), befriend whoever befriends him and be the enemy of whoever is his enemy.’” Then Imam (a.s) looked to the other side and said: “This is the place of the tent of ‘so-and-so’ and ‘so-and-so’ and Salim, the mawla (freed slave) of Abu Hudhayfah, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. When they saw Prophet (saws) raising his (Imam Ali (a.s)) hand, some of them said: ‘Look at his eyes, they are turning as if they are the eyes of a madman.’ So Jibra'il (a.s), peace be upon him, descended with the verse: ‘And indeed, those who disbelieve, almost drive you to slip with their eyes when they hear the message, and they say: Indeed, he is mad; but it is nothing except a reminder to the worlds.’” (Surah Al Qalam 68:51-52) Then Imam (a.s) said: “O Hassan, were it not for the fact that you are my camel driver, I would not have narrated this hadith to you.”
