chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari narrated that he said:
Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, led us in prayer at ‘Baratha’ after returning from fighting the Kharijites, and we totalled around one hundred thousand men. Then a Christian descended from his hermitage and said: “Where is the leader of this army?” We said: “This is he.” (gesturing towards Imam Ali (a.s)) So he (the Christian) approached Imam Ali (a.s) and greeted him with peace, then said: “O my master, are you a prophet?” Imam (a.s) replied: “No, the Prophet (saws), my master, has died.” He (the Christian) said: “Then you are the successor of a prophet?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” Then Imam Ali (a.s) said: “Sit down. How did you ask about this?” He (the Christian) said: “This hermitage was built for the sake of this place, and it is Baratha. And I read in the ‘revealed books’ that none prays in this place with such a gathering except a prophet or the successor of a prophet. And I have come to embrace Islam.” So he accepted Islam and came out with us to Kufah. Then Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: “So who prayed here?” He (the ex-Christian) said: “Isa ibn Maryam (a.s) and his mother prayed here.” Then Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: “Shall I inform you who else prayed here?” He (the ex-Christian) said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him.”
arabicText: وَرَوَى جَابِرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْأَنْصَارِيُّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: صَلَّى بِنَا عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ بِبَرَاثَا بَعْدَ رُجُوعِهِ مِنْ قِتَالِ اَلشُّرَاةِ وَنَحْنُ زُهَاءُ مِائَةِ أَلْفِ رَجُلٍ فَنَزَلَ نَصْرَانِيٌّ مِنْ صَوْمَعَتِهِ فَقَالَ أَيْنَ عَمِيدُ هَذَا اَلْجَيْشِ فَقُلْنَا هَذَا فَأَقْبَلَ إِلَيْهِ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي أَنْتَ نَبِيٌّ فَقَالَ« لاَ اَلنَّبِيُّ سَيِّدِي قَدْ مَاتَ» قَالَ فَأَنْتَ وَصِيُّ نَبِيٍّ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» ثُمَّ قَالَ« اِجْلِسْ كَيْفَ سَأَلْتَ عَنْ هَذَا» قَالَ إِنَّمَا بُنِيَتْ هَذِهِ اَلصَّوْمَعَةُ مِنْ أَجْلِ هَذَا اَلْمَوْضِعِ وَ هُوَ بَرَاثَا وَ قَرَأْتُ فِي اَلْكُتُبِ اَلْمُنَزَّلَةِ أَنَّهُ لاَ يُصَلِّي فِي هَذَا اَلْمَوْضِعِ بِذَا اَلْجَمْعِ إِلاَّ نَبِيٌّ أَوْ وَصِيُّ نَبِيٍّ وَ قَدْ جِئْتُ أَنْ أُسْلِمَ فَأَسْلَمَ فَخَرَجَ مَعَنَا إِلَى اَلْكُوفَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« فَمَنْ صَلَّى هَاهُنَا» قَالَ صَلَّى عِيسَى اِبْنُ مَرْيَمَ وَ أُمُّهُ فَقَالَ لَهُ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« أَ فَأُفِيدُكَ مَنْ صَلَّى هَاهُنَا» قَالَ نَعَمْ قَالَ« اَلْخَلِيلُ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: And Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari narrated that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, led us in prayer at ‘Baratha’ after returning from fighting the Kharijites, and we totalled around one hundred thousand men. Then a Christian descended from his hermitage and said: “Where is the leader of this army?” We said: “This is he.” (gesturing towards Imam Ali (a.s)) So he (the Christian) approached Imam Ali (a.s) and greeted him with peace, then said: “O my master, are you a prophet?” Imam (a.s) replied: “No, the Prophet (saws), my master, has died.” He (the Christian) said: “Then you are the successor of a prophet?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” Then Imam Ali (a.s) said: “Sit down. How did you ask about this?” He (the Christian) said: “This hermitage was built for the sake of this place, and it is Baratha. And I read in the ‘revealed books’ that none prays in this place with such a gathering except a prophet or the successor of a prophet. And I have come to embrace Islam.” So he accepted Islam and came out with us to Kufah. Then Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: “So who prayed here?” He (the ex-Christian) said: “Isa ibn Maryam (a.s) and his mother prayed here.” Then Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: “Shall I inform you who else prayed here?” He (the ex-Christian) said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “Ibrahim (a.s), peace be upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 290

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha' who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Whoever builds a mosque, Allah (swt) will build for him a house in Paradise.” Abu Ubaydah said: “Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, passed by me on the road to Mecca, while I had arranged stones for a mosque, so I asked: ‘May I be your ransom, we hope that this is of that (included in the reward).’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ اَلْحَذَّاءِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« مَنْ بَنَى مَسْجِداً بَنَى اَللَّهُ لَهُ بَيْتاً فِي اَلْجَنَّةِ» قَالَ أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ فَمَرَّ بِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي طَرِيقِ مَكَّةَ وَ قَدْ سَوَّيْتُ أَحْجَاراً لِمَسْجِدٍ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ نَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونَ هَذَا مِنْ ذَاكَ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha' who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Whoever builds a mosque, Allah (swt) will build for him a house in Paradise.” Abu Ubaydah said: “Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, passed by me on the road to Mecca, while I had arranged stones for a mosque, so I asked: ‘May I be your ransom, we hope that this is of that (included in the reward).’” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 291

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Yusuf from his father who said:
I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Indeed, al-Juhani came to the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), I live in the desert and I am with my family, my children, and my servants. I call the adhan and the iqamah and I lead them in prayer. Are we considered a congregation (jama'ah)?’ Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” He (al-Juhani) asked: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), sometimes the servants follow the tracks of the clouds, so I remain with my family and children, and I call the adhan and the iqamah and lead them in prayer, are we considered a congregation?” Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” He (al-Juhani) asked: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), my children go about with the livestock, so I remain with my family, and I call the adhan and the iqamah and lead them in prayer, are we considered a congregation?” Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” He (al-Juhani) asked: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), the woman goes out for her needs, so I remain alone, and I call the adhan and the iqamah, am I considered a congregation?” Prophet (saws) said: “Yes. The believer alone is a congregation.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يُوسُفَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ: «إِنَّ اَلْجُهَنِيَّ أَتَى اَلنَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ إِنِّي أَكُونُ فِي اَلْبَادِيَةِ وَ مَعِي أَهْلِي وَ وُلْدِي وَ غِلْمَتِي فَأُؤَذِّنُ وَ أُقِيمُ وَ أُصَلِّي بِهِمْ أَفَجَمَاعَةٌ نَحْنُ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ إِنَّ اَلْغِلْمَةَ يَتْبَعُونَ قَطْرَ اَلسَّحَابِ فَأَبْقَى أَنَا وَ أَهْلِي وَ وُلْدِي فَأُؤَذِّنُ وَ أُقِيمُ وَ أُصَلِّي بِهِمْ أَفَجَمَاعَةٌ نَحْنُ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ فَإِنَّ وُلْدِي يَتَفَرَّقُونَ فِي اَلْمَاشِيَةِ فَأَبْقَى أَنَا وَ أَهْلِي فَأُؤَذِّنُ وَ أُقِيمُ وَ أُصَلِّي بِهِمْ أَفَجَمَاعَةٌ نَحْنُ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ إِنَّ اَلْمَرْأَةَ تَذْهَبُ فِي مَصْلَحَتِهَا فَأَبْقَى أَنَا وَحْدِي فَأُؤَذِّنُ وَ أُقِيمُ أَفَجَمَاعَةٌ أَنَا فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ اَلْمُؤْمِنُ وَحْدَهُ جَمَاعَةٌ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Yusuf from his father who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “Indeed, al-Juhani came to the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, and said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), I live in the desert and I am with my family, my children, and my servants. I call the adhan and the iqamah and I lead them in prayer. Are we considered a congregation (jama'ah)?’ Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” He (al-Juhani) asked: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), sometimes the servants follow the tracks of the clouds, so I remain with my family and children, and I call the adhan and the iqamah and lead them in prayer, are we considered a congregation?” Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” He (al-Juhani) asked: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), my children go about with the livestock, so I remain with my family, and I call the adhan and the iqamah and lead them in prayer, are we considered a congregation?” Prophet (saws) said: “Yes.” He (al-Juhani) asked: “O Messenger of Allah (swt), the woman goes out for her needs, so I remain alone, and I call the adhan and the iqamah, am I considered a congregation?” Prophet (saws) said: “Yes. The believer alone is a congregation.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Does a man among you not feel ashamed, that he has a female servant, then he sells her, and she says (about him), 'He did not used to attend the prayer'?”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« أَ مَا يَسْتَحِي اَلرَّجُلُ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ تَكُونَ لَهُ اَلْجَارِيَةُ فَيَبِيعَهَا فَتَقُولَ لَمْ يَكُنْ يَحْضُرُ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Does a man among you not feel ashamed, that he has a female servant, then he sells her, and she says (about him), 'He did not used to attend the prayer'?”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 292

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from al-Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Jabir from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Let those who are closest to the imam (of prayer) be those among you who possess understanding and intellect, for if the imam (of prayer) forgets or becomes confused, they can correct him. And the best of the rows is the first one, and the best part of the first row is that which is closest to the imam (of prayer). And the superiority of congregational prayer over the prayer of a man alone is twenty-five degrees in Paradise.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْمُعَلَّى بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْوَشَّاءِ عَنِ اَلْمُفَضَّلِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لِيَكُنِ اَلَّذِينَ يَلُونَ اَلْإِمَامَ أُولِي اَلْأَحْلاَمِ مِنْكُمْ وَ اَلنُّهَى فَإِنْ نَسِيَ اَلْإِمَامُ أَوْ تَعَايَا قَوَّمُوهُ وَ أَفْضَلُ اَلصُّفُوفِ أَوَّلُهَا وَ أَفْضَلُ أَوَّلِهَا مَا دَنَا مِنَ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ فَضْلُ صَلاَةِ اَلْجَمَاعَةِ عَلَى صَلاَةِ اَلرَّجُلِ فَرْداً خَمْسٌ وَ عِشْرُونَ دَرَجَةً فِي اَلْجَنَّةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from al-Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Jabir from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “Let those who are closest to the imam (of prayer) be those among you who possess understanding and intellect, for if the imam (of prayer) forgets or becomes confused, they can correct him. And the best of the rows is the first one, and the best part of the first row is that which is closest to the imam (of prayer). And the superiority of congregational prayer over the prayer of a man alone is twenty-five degrees in Paradise.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 292

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “It will be counted for you (rewards), if you enter with them (in prayer) even if you do not follow them in prayer, the same as it is counted for you (in rewards) when you are with one whom you do follow (in prayer).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يُحْسَبُ لَكَ إِذَا دَخَلْتَ مَعَهُمْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ تَقْتَدِ بِهِمْ مِثْلُ مَا يُحْسَبُ لَكَ إِذَا كُنْتَ مَعَ مَنْ تَقْتَدِي بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “It will be counted for you (rewards), if you enter with them (in prayer) even if you do not follow them in prayer, the same as it is counted for you (in rewards) when you are with one whom you do follow (in prayer).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 292

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Dhubyan ibn Hakim from Musa ibn Ukayl al-Numayri from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, intended to burn the homes of a people who used to pray in their houses and did not attend the congregational prayer. Then a blind man came to Him (saws) and said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), I am blind of sight, and sometimes I hear the call but do not find anyone to lead me to the congregation and prayer with you’. So the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to him: ‘Tie a rope from your house to the mosque and attend the congregation.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ ذُبْيَانَ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ أُكَيْلٍ اَلنُّمَيْرِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي يَعْفُورٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« هَمَّ رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ بِإِحْرَاقِ قَوْمٍ فِي مَنَازِلِهِمْ كَانُوا يُصَلُّونَ فِي مَنَازِلِهِمْ وَ لاَ يُصَلُّونَ اَلْجَمَاعَةَ فَأَتَاهُ رَجُلٌ أَعْمَى فَقَالَ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ إِنِّي ضَرِيرُ اَلْبَصَرِ وَ رُبَّمَا أَسْمَعُ اَلنِّدَاءَ وَ لاَ أَجِدُ مَنْ يَقُودُنِي إِلَى اَلْجَمَاعَةِ وَ اَلصَّلاَةِ مَعَكَ فَقَالَ لَهُ اَلنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ« شُدَّ مِنْ مَنْزِلِكَ إِلَى اَلْمَسْجِدِ حَبْلاً وَ اُحْضُرِ اَلْجَمَاعَةَ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Dhubyan ibn Hakim from Musa ibn Ukayl al-Numayri from Ibn Abi Ya'fur from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, intended to burn the homes of a people who used to pray in their houses and did not attend the congregational prayer. Then a blind man came to Him (saws) and said: ‘O’ Messenger of Allah (swt), I am blind of sight, and sometimes I hear the call but do not find anyone to lead me to the congregation and prayer with you’. So the Prophet (saws), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said to him: ‘Tie a rope from your house to the mosque and attend the congregation.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 292

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer behind the opponents (al-mukhalifin). Imam (a.s) said: “They are, in my view, nothing but like walls.” (meaning it holds no spiritual or religious value or relevance)
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ خَلْفَ اَلْمُخَالِفِينَ فَقَالَ« فَمَا هُمْ عِنْدِي إِلاَّ بِمَنْزِلَةِ اَلْجُدُرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abdillah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer behind the opponents (al-mukhalifin). Imam (a.s) said: “They are, in my view, nothing but like walls.” (meaning it holds no spiritual or religious value or relevance)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 293

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Abu Ali ibn Rashid who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “Your followers have differed, so I pray behind all of them.” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not pray except behind one whose religion and trustworthiness you are confident in.”
arabicText: سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزِيَارَ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيِّ بْنِ رَاشِدٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّ مَوَالِيَكَ قَدِ اِخْتَلَفُوا فَأُصَلِّي خَلْفَهُمْ جَمِيعاً فَقَالَ« لاَ تُصَلِّ إِلاَّ خَلْفَ مَنْ تَثِقُ بِدِينِهِ وَ أَمَانَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Abu Ali ibn Rashid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “Your followers have differed, so I pray behind all of them.” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not pray except behind one whose religion and trustworthiness you are confident in.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 293

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “Some people have narrated from the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, that Imam (a.s) prayed four rak‘ahs after Jumu‘ah without separating them with a taslim.” Imam (a.s) said: “O’ Zurarah, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s) prayed behind a transgressor (fasiq), So when the transgressor said the taslim and departed, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, stood and prayed four rak‘ahs without separating them with a taslim. A man beside Imam Ali (a.s) said: ‘O Abu al-Hasan, you prayed four rak‘ahs without separating them with a taslim?’ Imam Ali (a.s) said: ‘They are four rak‘ahs that resemble one another’ So the man became silent, and by Allah (swt), the man did not understand what Imam Ali (a.s) meant to say to him.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنَّ أُنَاساً رَوَوْا عَنْ أَمِيرِ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ بَعْدَ اَلْجُمُعَةِ لَمْ يَفْصِلْ بَيْنَهُنَّ بِتَسْلِيمٍ فَقَالَ« يَا زُرَارَةُ إِنَّ أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ صَلَّى خَلْفَ فَاسِقٍ فَلَمَّا سَلَّمَ وَ اِنْصَرَفَ قَامَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فَصَلَّى أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ لَمْ يَفْصِلْ بَيْنَهُنَّ بِتَسْلِيمٍ فَقَالَ لَهُ رَجُلٌ إِلَى جَنْبِهِ يَا أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ صَلَّيْتَ أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ لَمْ تَفْصِلْ بَيْنَهُنَّ بِتَسْلِيمٍ فَقَالَ« إِنَّهَا أَرْبَعُ رَكَعَاتٍ مُشَبَّهَاتٍ» فَسَكَتَ فَوَ اَللَّهِ مَا عَقَلَ مَا قَالَ لَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “Some people have narrated from the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, that Imam (a.s) prayed four rak‘ahs after Jumu‘ah without separating them with a taslim.” Imam (a.s) said: “O’ Zurarah, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s) prayed behind a transgressor (fasiq), So when the transgressor said the taslim and departed, the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, stood and prayed four rak‘ahs without separating them with a taslim. A man beside Imam Ali (a.s) said: ‘O Abu al-Hasan, you prayed four rak‘ahs without separating them with a taslim?’ Imam Ali (a.s) said: ‘They are four rak‘ahs that resemble one another’ So the man became silent, and by Allah (swt), the man did not understand what Imam Ali (a.s) meant to say to him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 293

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Abu al-Abbas who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man leading a woman in prayer in his house. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, she stands behind him.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْعَبَّاسِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَؤُمُّ اَلْمَرْأَةَ فِي بَيْتِهِ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ تَقُومُ وَرَاءَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskan from Abu al-Abbas who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man leading a woman in prayer in his house. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, she stands behind him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 293

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Husayn from Aban from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I lead the obligatory prayer with Umm Ali?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, she should be on your right side, and her prostration should be aligned with your feet.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أُصَلِّي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةَ بِأُمِّ عَلِيٍّ قَالَ« نَعَمْ تَكُونُ عَنْ يَمِينِكَ يَكُونُ سُجُودُهَا بِحِذَاءِ قَدَمَيْكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Husayn from Aban from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I lead the obligatory prayer with Umm Ali?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, she should be on your right side, and her prostration should be aligned with your feet.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 293

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdillah ibn Muskan who said:
I sent to Imam (a.s) a question from the questions of Ibrahim, which he was to deliver to Ibn Sadeer. So he asked Imam (a.s) about it while Ibrahim ibn Maymun was sitting regarding a man leading women in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I said: “Ask Imam (a.s) about them when there are young boys with them, who have not yet reached puberty. Do they stand with them in the same row, or do they stand in front of them?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather they stand in front of them, even if they are slaves.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ قَالَ: بَعَثْتُ إِلَيْهِ بِمَسْأَلَةٍ فِي مَسَائِلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ يَدْفَعُهَا إِلَى اِبْنِ سَدِيرٍ فَسَأَلَ عَنْهَا وَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مَيْمُونٍ جَالِسٌ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَؤُمُّ اَلنِّسَاءَ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ» فَقُلْتُ سَلْهُ عَنْهُنَّ إِذَا كَانَ مَعَهُنَّ غِلْمَانٌ لَمْ يُدْرِكُوا أَ يَقُومُونَ مَعَهُنَّ فِي اَلصَّفِّ أَمْ يَتَقَدَّمُونَهُنَّ فَقَالَ «لاَ بَلْ يَتَقَدَّمُونَهُنَّ وَ إِنْ كَانُوا عَبِيداً»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abdillah ibn Muskan who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I sent to Imam (a.s) a question from the questions of Ibrahim, which he was to deliver to Ibn Sadeer. So he asked Imam (a.s) about it while Ibrahim ibn Maymun was sitting regarding a man leading women in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.” I said: “Ask Imam (a.s) about them when there are young boys with them, who have not yet reached puberty. Do they stand with them in the same row, or do they stand in front of them?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather they stand in front of them, even if they are slaves.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 293

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ubaydi from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his father Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about a woman leading other women in prayer, what is the limit for raising her voice in recitation or in takbir? Imam (a.s) said: “As much as it allows them to hear.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى اَلْعُبَيْدِيِّ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْمَاضِي عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ تَؤُمُّ اَلنِّسَاءَ مَا حَدُّ رَفْعِ صَوْتِهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ أَوِ اَلتَّكْبِيرِ فَقَالَ« بِقَدْرِ مَا تُسْمِعُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ubaydi from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his father Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi, peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about a woman leading other women in prayer, what is the limit for raising her voice in recitation or in takbir? Imam (a.s) said: “As much as it allows them to hear.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 294

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother, peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Kadhim about a woman leading women in prayer, what is the limit for raising her voice in recitation or in takbir? Imam (a.s) said: “As much as it allows them to hear.”
arabicText: احمد بن محمد عن موسى بن القاسم عن علي بن جعفر عن اخيه عليه السلام قال سألته عن المرأة تؤم النساء ما حد رفع صوتها بالقراءة أو التكبير؟ قال قدر ما تسمع
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother, peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Kadhim about a woman leading women in prayer, what is the limit for raising her voice in recitation or in takbir? Imam (a.s) said: “As much as it allows them to hear.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 294

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Pray with your family in (Month of) Ramadan the obligatory prayer, and the recommended (nafilah) prayer, for indeed I do so.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «صَلِّ بِأَهْلِكَ فِي رَمَضَانَ اَلْفَرِيضَةَ وَ اَلنَّافِلَةَ فَإِنِّي أَفْعَلُهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Pray with your family in (Month of) Ramadan the obligatory prayer, and the recommended (nafilah) prayer, for indeed I do so.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 294

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from his father, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man praying with another man, while women are with them. Imam (a.s) said: “The man stands beside the man, and the women stand behind them both.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ اَلْوَلِيدِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي مَعَ اَلرَّجُلِ اَلْوَاحِدِ مَعَهُمَا اَلنِّسَاءُ قَالَ« يَقُومُ اَلرَّجُلُ إِلَى جَنْبِ اَلرَّجُلِ وَ يَتَخَلَّفْنَ اَلنِّسَاءُ خَلْفَهُمَا»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from his father, from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man praying with another man, while women are with them. Imam (a.s) said: “The man stands beside the man, and the women stand behind them both.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 294

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Ibn al-Mughirah from Ghiyath from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “One woman is a row, and two women are a row, and three are a row.” (meaning the row of women cannot conjoin with the row of men)
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنِ اِبْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ غِيَاثٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قَالَ:« اَلْمَرْأَةُ صَفٌّ وَ اَلْمَرْأَتَانِ صَفٌّ وَ اَلثَّلاَثُ صَفٌّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Abbas from Ibn al-Mughirah from Ghiyath from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, from his father (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “One woman is a row, and two women are a row, and three are a row.” (meaning the row of women cannot conjoin with the row of men)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 294

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm from Ibn Muskan from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “A woman leads women in prayer and stands in the middle of them, and they stand on her right and her left. She leads them in the recommended (nafilah) prayer and does not lead them in the obligatory (maktoobah) prayer.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْجَهْمِ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« تَؤُمُّ اَلْمَرْأَةُ اَلنِّسَاءَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ تَقُومُ وَسَطاً مِنْهُنَّ وَ يَقُمْنَ عَنْ يَمِينِهَا وَ شِمَالِهَا تَؤُمُّهُنَّ فِي اَلنَّافِلَةِ وَ لاَ تَؤُمُّهُنَّ فِي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm from Ibn Muskan from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “A woman leads women in prayer and stands in the middle of them, and they stand on her right and her left. She leads them in the recommended (nafilah) prayer and does not lead them in the obligatory (maktoobah) prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 295

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Abu al-Abbas ibn al-Mughirah who said: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan narrated to us from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s): “Does a woman lead women in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, except over the deceased (Salat Al Mayyit), if there is no one more entitled than her. She stands in the middle with them in the (same) row, says the takbir, and they say the takbir.”
arabicText: محمد بن مسعود عن ابي العباس بن المغيرة قال حدثنا الفضل بن شاذان عن ابن ابي عمير عن حماد عن حريز عن زرارة عن ابي جعفر عليه السلام قال قلت المرأة تؤم النساء؟ قال لا إلا على الميت إذا لم يكن أحد أولى منها تقوم وسطا معهن في الصف فتكبر ويكبرن
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Abu al-Abbas ibn al-Mughirah who said: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan narrated to us from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s): “Does a woman lead women in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, except over the deceased (Salat Al Mayyit), if there is no one more entitled than her. She stands in the middle with them in the (same) row, says the takbir, and they say the takbir.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 295

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ibrahim ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding a man leading women in prayer, while there is no other man with them, in the obligatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and if there is a boy with him, then let him stand beside him.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلرَّجُلِ يَؤُمُّ اَلنِّسَاءَ وَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُنَّ رَجُلٌ فِي اَلْفَرِيضَةِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ صَبِيٌّ فَلْيَقُمْ إِلَى جَانِبِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ibrahim ibn Maymun from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding a man leading women in prayer, while there is no other man with them, in the obligatory prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and if there is a boy with him, then let him stand beside him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 295

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a woman leading women in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “If they are all women, she may lead them in the recommended (nafilah) prayer. As for the obligatory (maktoobah) prayer, no. And she should not stand in front of them, but rather she should stand in the middle of them (in the same row).”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمَرْأَةِ تَؤُمُّ اَلنِّسَاءَ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كُنَّ جَمِيعاً أَمَّتْهُنَّ فِي اَلنَّافِلَةِ وَ أَمَّا اَلْمَكْتُوبَةُ فَلاَ وَ لاَ تَتَقَدَّمُهُنَّ وَ لَكِنْ تَقُومُ وَسَطاً مِنْهُنَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a woman leading women in prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “If they are all women, she may lead them in the recommended (nafilah) prayer. As for the obligatory (maktoobah) prayer, no. And she should not stand in front of them, but rather she should stand in the middle of them (in the same row).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 295

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurarah who said:
I asked one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, about whether the imam (of prayer) bears responsibility for the prayer of the people. Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَحَدَهُمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْإِمَامِ يَضْمَنُ صَلاَةَ اَلْقَوْمِ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, about whether the imam (of prayer) bears responsibility for the prayer of the people. Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 295

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: ‘Whoever recites (Qur’an) behind an imam (of prayer) whom he follows, and then dies, he will be raised not upon the natural disposition (fitrah, meaning natural belief in oneness of God).’” (meaning reciting Qur’an behind an imam (of prayer) during congregational prayer is incorrect as a muqtadi (follower))
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَمُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالاَ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ كَانَ أَمِيرُ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« مَنْ قَرَأَ خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ يَأْتَمُّ بِهِ فَمَاتَ بُعِثَ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْفِطْرَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “The Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, used to say: ‘Whoever recites (Qur’an) behind an imam (of prayer) whom he follows, and then dies, he will be raised not upon the natural disposition (fitrah, meaning natural belief in oneness of God).’” (meaning reciting Qur’an behind an imam (of prayer) during congregational prayer is incorrect as a muqtadi (follower))

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 296

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding a blind man leading the people in prayer while not facing the qiblah. Imam (a.s) said: “He must repeat the prayer, but they do not, for they made an effort to determine the direction.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلْأَعْمَى يَؤُمُّ اَلْقَوْمَ وَ هُوَ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ وَ لاَ يُعِيدُونَ فَإِنَّهُمْ تَحَرَّوْا»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding a blind man leading the people in prayer while not facing the qiblah. Imam (a.s) said: “He must repeat the prayer, but they do not, for they made an effort to determine the direction.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 296

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurarah who said:
I asked one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, about a man who led people in prayer for two rak‘ahs, then informed them that he was not in a state of wudu. Imam (a.s) said: “The people should complete their prayer, for the imam (of prayer) bears no responsibility.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَحَدَهُمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى بِقَوْمٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَأَخْبَرَهُمْ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى وُضُوءٍ قَالَ« يُتِمُّ اَلْقَوْمُ صَلاَتَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ عَلَى اَلْإِمَامِ ضَمَانٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, about a man who led people in prayer for two rak‘ahs, then informed them that he was not in a state of wudu. Imam (a.s) said: “The people should complete their prayer, for the imam (of prayer) bears no responsibility.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 296

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath from Sa’id ibn Muslim from al-Sha‘bi who said:
Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “A blind man does not lead in prayer in the open land, and a shackled person does not lead those who are free.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ غِيَاثٍ عَنْ صَاعِدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ اَلشَّعْبِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ عَلِيٌّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« لاَ يَؤُمُّ اَلْأَعْمَى فِي اَلْبَرِيَّةِ وَ لاَ يَؤُمُّ اَلْمُقَيَّدُ اَلْمُطْلَقِينَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath from Sa’id ibn Muslim from al-Sha‘bi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam Ali (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “A blind man does not lead in prayer in the open land, and a shackled person does not lead those who are free.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 296

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Ubayd ibn Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “I enter the mosque having already prayed, so I pray with them but I do not count that prayer (as my obligation).” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem. As for me, I pray with them and make it appear to them that I am prostrating, but I do not actually prostrate.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ إِنِّي أَدْخُلُ اَلْمَسْجِدَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّيْتُ فَأُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ فَلاَ أَحْتَسِبُ بِتِلْكَ اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ وَ أَمَّا أَنَا فَأُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ وَ أُرِيهِمْ أَنِّي أَسْجُدُ وَ مَا أَسْجُدُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Ubayd ibn Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “I enter the mosque having already prayed, so I pray with them but I do not count that prayer (as my obligation).” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem. As for me, I pray with them and make it appear to them that I am prostrating, but I do not actually prostrate.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 296

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughirah from Nasih the mu’adhdhin, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I pray at home and then go out to them (the opponents).” Imam (a.s) said: “Consider it a supererogatory (nafilah) prayer, and do not pronounce the takbir with them (the opponents), for that would enter you into the prayer with them, for the key to the prayer is the takbir.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ نَاصِحٍ اَلْمُؤَذِّنِ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي أُصَلِّي فِي اَلْبَيْتِ وَ أَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهِمْ قَالَ« اِجْعَلْهَا نَافِلَةً وَ لاَ تُكَبِّرْ مَعَهُمْ فَتَدْخُلَ مَعَهُمْ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ فَإِنَّ مِفْتَاحَ اَلصَّلاَةِ اَلتَّكْبِيرُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Ibn al-Mughirah from Nasih the mu’adhdhin, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I pray at home and then go out to them (the opponents).” Imam (a.s) said: “Consider it a supererogatory (nafilah) prayer, and do not pronounce the takbir with them (the opponents), for that would enter you into the prayer with them, for the key to the prayer is the takbir.”

author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī

Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yaqub from Abu Basir who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I perform the prayer and then enter the mosque and the congregational prayer is established while I have already prayed.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray with them; Allah (swt) chooses the one He (azj) loves more from the two.”

thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Walid from Yaqub from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I perform the prayer and then enter the mosque and the congregational prayer is established while I have already prayed.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray with them; Allah (swt) chooses the one He (azj) loves more from the two.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Yaqub ibn Yaqtin who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, the time for the noon prayer (Dhuhr) arrives, but we are not able to check the time until they (the public, meaning non-Shia) descend, so we descend with them and pray. Then they (the opponents) rise quickly and we rise and pray the afternoon prayer (Asr), but we make it appear to them as though we are bowing. Then later, they descend for the afternoon prayer (Asr) and they put us forward, so we lead them in prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: “Lead them in prayer, may Allah (swt) not accept their prayer.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ تَحْضُرُ صَلاَةُ اَلظُّهْرِ فَلاَ نَقْدِرُ أَنْ نَنْظُرَ فِي اَلْوَقْتِ حَتَّى يَنْزِلُوا فَنَنْزِلَ مَعَهُمْ نُصَلِّي ثُمَّ يَقُومُونَ فَيُسْرِعُونَ فَنَقُومُ فَنُصَلِّي اَلْعَصْرَ وَ نُرِيهِمْ كَأَنَّا نَرْكَعُ ثُمَّ يَنْزِلُونَ لِلْعَصْرِ فَيُقَدِّمُونَّا فَنُصَلِّي بِهِمْ فَقَالَ« صَلِّ بِهِمْ لاَ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Yaqub ibn Yaqtin who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, the time for the noon prayer (Dhuhr) arrives, but we are not able to check the time until they (the public, meaning non-Shia) descend, so we descend with them and pray. Then they (the opponents) rise quickly and we rise and pray the afternoon prayer (Asr), but we make it appear to them as though we are bowing. Then later, they descend for the afternoon prayer (Asr) and they put us forward, so we lead them in prayer.” Imam (a.s) said: “Lead them in prayer, may Allah (swt) not accept their prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from al-Hasan ibn Abdillah al-Arrajani, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever prays in his house, then comes to one of their (opponent) mosques and prays in it, he departs with their good deeds.” (meaning to promote strategic use of taqiyyah to preserve life and faith)
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْهَيْثَمِ بْنِ وَاقِدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْأَرَّجَانِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« مَنْ صَلَّى فِي مَنْزِلِهِ ثُمَّ أَتَى مَسْجِداً مِنْ مَسَاجِدِهِمْ فَصَلَّى فِيهِ خَرَجَ بِحَسَنَاتِهِمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Haytham ibn Waqid, from al-Hasan ibn Abdillah al-Arrajani, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Whoever prays in his house, then comes to one of their (opponent) mosques and prays in it, he departs with their good deeds.” (meaning to promote strategic use of taqiyyah to preserve life and faith)

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-Mithami from Ishaq ibn Yazid who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, the imam (of prayer) precedes me by one rak‘ah, so I have one and he has two. Should I recite the tashahhud every time I sit?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, indeed the tashahhud is a blessing.”
arabicText: سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ اَلْمِيثَمِيِّ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ يَسْبِقُنِي اَلْإِمَامُ بِالرَّكْعَةِ فَتَكُونُ لِي وَاحِدَةٌ وَ لَهُ ثِنْتَانِ أَفَأَتَشَهَّدُ كُلَّمَا قَعَدْتُ فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ إِنَّمَا اَلتَّشَهُّدُ بَرَكَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-Mithami from Ishaq ibn Yazid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “May I be your ransom, the imam (of prayer) precedes me by one rak‘ah, so I have one and he has two. Should I recite the tashahhud every time I sit?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, indeed the tashahhud is a blessing.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdillah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If the imam (of prayer) precedes you by one rak‘ah and you catch the final recitation, then you recite in the third rak‘ah of his prayer, and it is the second for you. But if you only catch one rak‘ah with him, then you recite in that one and in the one that follows it. And if he precedes you by one rak‘ah, you sit in what is the second for you and the third for him, until the rows become upright standing.” He (narrator) said “And Imam (a.s) said: ‘If you find the imam (of prayer) in prostration, then remain in your place until he raises his head, and if he is sitting, then sit; and if he is standing, then stand.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا سَبَقَكَ اَلْإِمَامُ بِرَكْعَةٍ فَأَدْرَكْتَ اَلْقِرَاءَةَ اَلْأَ خِيرَةَ قَرَأْتَ فِي اَلثَّالِثَةِ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ وَ هِيَ ثِنْتَانِ لَكَ فَإِنْ لَمْ تُدْرِكْ مَعَهُ إِلاَّ رَكْعَةً وَاحِدَةً قَرَأْتَ فِيهَا وَ فِي اَلَّتِي تَلِيهَا وَ إِذَا سَبَقَكَ بِرَكْعَةٍ جَلَسْتَ فِي اَلثَّانِيَةِ لَكَ وَ اَلثَّالِثَةِ لَهُ حَتَّى تَعْتَدِلَ اَلصُّفُوفُ قِيَاماً» قَالَ وَ قَالَ« إِذَا وَجَدْتَ اَلْإِمَامَ سَاجِداً فَاثْبُتْ مَكَانَكَ حَتَّى يَرْفَعَ رَأْسَهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَاعِداً قَعَدْتَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَائِماً قُمْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Abdillah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If the imam (of prayer) precedes you by one rak‘ah and you catch the final recitation, then you recite in the third rak‘ah of his prayer, and it is the second for you. But if you only catch one rak‘ah with him, then you recite in that one and in the one that follows it. And if he precedes you by one rak‘ah, you sit in what is the second for you and the third for him, until the rows become upright standing.” He (narrator) said “And Imam (a.s) said: ‘If you find the imam (of prayer) in prostration, then remain in your place until he raises his head, and if he is sitting, then sit; and if he is standing, then stand.’”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Regarding a man who catches the imam (of prayer) while he is in rukuh, and if he says the takbir (‘Allahu Akbar’) while his back is still upright, then bows before the imam (of prayer) raises his head, (then) he has caught the rak‘ah”.
arabicText: احمد بن محمد عن علي بن النعمان عن ابن مسكان عن سليمان بن خالد قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام في الرجل يدرك الامام وهو راكع فكبر وهو مقيم صلبه ثم ركع قبل ان يرفع الامام رأسه فقد أدرك
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from Ibn Muskan from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Regarding a man who catches the imam (of prayer) while he is in rukuh, and if he says the takbir (‘Allahu Akbar’) while his back is still upright, then bows before the imam (of prayer) raises his head, (then) he has caught the rak‘ah”.

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A‘la from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “I come to the imam (of prayer) and he has preceded me by one rak‘ah in the dawn prayer. When he gave the taslim, it occurred to my heart that I had completed the prayer, so I remained remembering Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, until the sun rose. When it rose, I stood up and remembered that the imam (of prayer) had preceded me by one rak‘ah.” Imam (a.s) said: “If you are still in your place, then complete the prayer with one rak‘ah; but if you have already left (the place of prayer), then you must repeat the prayer.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلنُّعْمَانِ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ أَبِي اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ أَجِيءُ إِلَى اَلْإِمَامِ وَ قَدْ سَبَقَنِي بِرَكْعَةٍ فِي اَلْفَجْرِ فَلَمَّا سَلَّمَ وَقَعَ فِي قَلْبِي أَنِّي أَتْمَمْتُ فَلَمْ أَزَلْ ذَاكِراً لِلَّهِ عَزَّوَجَلَّ حَتَّى طَلَعَتِ اَلشَّمْسُ فَلَمَّا طَلَعَتْ نَهَضْتُ فَذَكَرْتُ أَنَّ اَلْإِمَامَ كَانَ قَدْ سَبَقَنِي بِرَكْعَةٍ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كُنْتَ فِي مَقَامِكَ فَأَتِمَّ بِرَكْعَةٍ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ قَدِ اِنْصَرَفْتَ فَعَلَيْكَ اَلْإِعَادَةُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A‘la from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “I come to the imam (of prayer) and he has preceded me by one rak‘ah in the dawn prayer. When he gave the taslim, it occurred to my heart that I had completed the prayer, so I remained remembering Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, until the sun rose. When it rose, I stood up and remembered that the imam (of prayer) had preceded me by one rak‘ah.” Imam (a.s) said: “If you are still in your place, then complete the prayer with one rak‘ah; but if you have already left (the place of prayer), then you must repeat the prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama’ah from Abu Basir who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prayed with a group while thinking it was the noon (Dhuhr) prayer, but it was actually the afternoon (Asr) prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him count it as the noon (Dhuhr) prayer and let him perform the afternoon (Asr) prayer anew.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ بْنِ أَيُّوبَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى مَعَ قَوْمٍ وَ هُوَ يَرَى أَنَّهَا اَلْأُولَى وَ كَانَتِ اَلْعَصْرَ قَالَ« فَلْيَجْعَلْهَا اَلْأُولَى وَ لْيُصَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from al-Husayn ibn Uthman from Sama’ah from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about a man who prayed with a group while thinking it was the noon (Dhuhr) prayer, but it was actually the afternoon (Asr) prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him count it as the noon (Dhuhr) prayer and let him perform the afternoon (Asr) prayer anew.”
