chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurarah who said:
I asked one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, about an imam (of prayer) who led a group in prayer, then remembered that he was not in a state of wudu. So he withdrew and took the hand of a man, brought him forward, and put him in front. But the one who was brought forward did not know what the group had already prayed. Imam (a.s) said: “He should lead them in prayer, and if he makes a mistake, the group should say ‘SubhanAllah’ to alert him, and he continues based on the prayer of the one who was before him.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَحَدَهُمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ إِمَامٍ أَمَّ قَوْماً فَذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَكُنْ عَلَى وُضُوءٍ فَانْصَرَفَ وَ أَخَذَ بِيَدِ رَجُلٍ فَأَدْخَلَهُ فَقَدَّمَهُ وَ لَمْ يَعْلَمِ اَلَّذِي قُدِّمَ مَا صَلَّى اَلْقَوْمُ قَالَ« يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ فَإِنْ أَخْطَأَ سَبَّحَ اَلْقَوْمُ بِهِ وَ بَنَى عَلَى صَلاَةِ اَلَّذِي كَانَ قَبْلَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, about an imam (of prayer) who led a group in prayer, then remembered that he was not in a state of wudu. So he withdrew and took the hand of a man, brought him forward, and put him in front. But the one who was brought forward did not know what the group had already prayed. Imam (a.s) said: “He should lead them in prayer, and if he makes a mistake, the group should say ‘SubhanAllah’ to alert him, and he continues based on the prayer of the one who was before him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 299

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiyah ibn Wahb who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, one day enter the ‘Sacred Mosque’ at the time of the afternoon (Asr) prayer. When Imam (a.s) was still short of reaching the rows, they bowed, so Imam (a.s) bowed alone and performed the two prostrations, then stood up and continued until Imam (a.s) reached the rows.
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَوْماً دَخَلَ اَلْمَسْجِدَ اَلْحَرَامَ فِي صَلاَةِ اَلْعَصْرِ فَلَمَّا كَانَ دُونَ اَلصُّفُوفِ رَكَعُوا فَرَكَعَ وَحْدَهُ وَ سَجَدَ اَلسَّجْدَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ قَامَ وَ مَضَى حَتَّى لَحِقَ اَلصُّفُوفَ
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiyah ibn Wahb who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, one day enter the ‘Sacred Mosque’ at the time of the afternoon (Asr) prayer. When Imam (a.s) was still short of reaching the rows, they bowed, so Imam (a.s) bowed alone and performed the two prostrations, then stood up and continued until Imam (a.s) reached the rows.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 299

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Uthman ibn Isa from Saeed al-A‘raj who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about a man who comes to the prayer and does not find a place in the row. Should he stand alone until he finishes his prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is no problem, he may stand beside the imam (of prayer).”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ سَعِيدٍ اَلْأَعْرَجِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَأْتِي اَلصَّلاَةَ فَلاَ يَجِدُ فِي اَلصَّفِّ مَقَاماً أَ يَقُومُ وَحْدَهُ حَتَّى يَفْرُغَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ لاَ بَأْسَ يَقُومُ بِحِذَاءِ اَلْإِمَامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa from Saeed al-A‘raj who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about a man who comes to the prayer and does not find a place in the row. Should he stand alone until he finishes his prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is no problem, he may stand beside the imam (of prayer).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 300

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rubi‘i from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “(May) a man moves backward while in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” (meaning it is not allowed) I asked: “Then may he move forward?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, walking toward the qiblah.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنِ اَلْفَضْلِ بْنِ شَاذَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ رِبْعِيٍّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ يَتَأَخَّرُ وَ هُوَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« لاَ» قُلْتُ فَيَتَقَدَّمُ قَالَ« نَعَمْ مَاشِياً إِلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Hammad ibn Isa from Rubi‘i from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “(May) a man moves backward while in prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No.” (meaning it is not allowed) I asked: “Then may he move forward?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, walking toward the qiblah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 300

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who catches imam (of prayer) while he is sitting and reciting tashahhud, and there is no one behind him except a man on his right. Imam (a.s) said: “The imam (of prayer) should not move forward, and the man should not move backward, but the one who enters to pray with him should sit behind the imam (of prayer). When the imam (of prayer) gives the salam, the man should stand and complete his prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُدْرِكُ اَلْإِمَامَ وَ هُوَ قَاعِدٌ يَتَشَهَّدُ وَ لَيْسَ خَلْفَهُ إِلاَّ رَجُلٌ وَاحِدٌ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ قَالَ« لاَ يَتَقَدَّمُ اَلْإِمَامَ وَ لاَ يَتَأَخَّرُ اَلرَّجُلَ وَ لَكِنْ يَقْعُدُ اَلَّذِي يَدْخُلُ مَعَهُ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ اَلْإِمَامُ قَامَ اَلرَّجُلُ فَأَتَمَّ صَلاَتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who catches imam (of prayer) while he is sitting and reciting tashahhud, and there is no one behind him except a man on his right. Imam (a.s) said: “The imam (of prayer) should not move forward, and the man should not move backward, but the one who enters to pray with him should sit behind the imam (of prayer). When the imam (of prayer) gives the salam, the man should stand and complete his prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 300

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Marwak ibn Ubayd from Nashit ibn Salih from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s) (the First), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam al-Kadhim (a.s): “A man among us performs his prayer inside his house with the door closed, then he goes out and prays with his neighbors. Is his prayer alone in his house considered a congregational prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “The one who prays in his house, Allah (swt) multiplies it for him to twice the reward of congregation; he will have fifty degrees (of reward). And the one who prays with his neighbors, Allah (swt) writes for him the reward of one who prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. And if he joins them in their prayer, so he leaves his sins behind with them (the opponents), and departs with their good deeds.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مَرْوَكِ بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ عَنْ نَشِيطِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْأَوَّلِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ اَلرَّجُلُ مِنَّا يُصَلِّي صَلاَتَهُ فِي جَوْفِ بَيْتِهِ مُغْلِقاً عَلَيْهِ بَابَهُ ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُ فَيُصَلِّي مَعَ جِيرَتِهِ تَكُونُ صَلاَتُهُ تِلْكَ وَحْدَهُ فِي بَيْتِهِ جَمَاعَةً فَقَالَ« اَلَّذِي يُصَلِّي فِي بَيْتِهِ يُضَاعِفُهُ اَللَّهُ لَهُ ضِعْفَيْ أَجْرِ اَلْجَمَاعَةِ يَكُونُ لَهُ خَمْسِينَ دَرَجَةً وَ اَلَّذِي يُصَلِّي مَعَ جِيرَتِهِ يَكْتُبُ اَللَّهُ لَهُ أَجْرَ مَنْ صَلَّى خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ يَدْخُلُ مَعَهُمْ فِي صَلاَتِهِمْ فَيُخَلِّفُ عَلَيْهِمْ ذُنُوبَهُ وَ يَخْرُجُ بِحَسَنَاتِهِمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Marwak ibn Ubayd from Nashit ibn Salih from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (a.s) (the First), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam al-Kadhim (a.s): “A man among us performs his prayer inside his house with the door closed, then he goes out and prays with his neighbors. Is his prayer alone in his house considered a congregational prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “The one who prays in his house, Allah (swt) multiplies it for him to twice the reward of congregation; he will have fifty degrees (of reward). And the one who prays with his neighbors, Allah (swt) writes for him the reward of one who prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family. And if he joins them in their prayer, so he leaves his sins behind with them (the opponents), and departs with their good deeds.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 301

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a group in prayer, and another group joins his prayer after he has already performed one rak‘ah or more than that. When he finishes his prayer, and gives the salam, is it permissible for him as the imam (of prayer) to leave his place (of prayer) before those who joined the prayer (later) have finished? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي بِقَوْمٍ فَيَدْخُلُ قَوْمٌ فِي صَلاَتِهِ بَعْدَ مَا قَدْ صَلَّى رَكْعَةً أَوْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَإِذَا فَرَغَ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ وَ سَلَّمَ أَ يَجُوزُ لَهُ وَ هُوَ إِمَامٌ أَنْ يَقُومَ مِنْ مَوْضِعِهِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَفْرُغَ مَنْ دَخَلَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar al-Sabati who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a group in prayer, and another group joins his prayer after he has already performed one rak‘ah or more than that. When he finishes his prayer, and gives the salam, is it permissible for him as the imam (of prayer) to leave his place (of prayer) before those who joined the prayer (later) have finished? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 301

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq who said:
I heard Imam (a.s) say: “It is not proper for the imam (of prayer) to stand up after he has prayed, until everyone behind him has completed what they missed of the prayer.”
arabicText: احمد بن محمد عن علي بن الحكم عن اسماعيل بن عبد الخالق قال سمعته يقول لا ينبغي للامام أن يقوم إذا صلى حتى يقضي كل من خلفه ما قد فاته من الصلاة
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ismail ibn Abd al-Khaliq who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Imam (a.s) say: “It is not proper for the imam (of prayer) to stand up after he has prayed, until everyone behind him has completed what they missed of the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 301

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad from al-Husayn from al-Nadr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who enters the mosque and begins the prayer. While he is standing and praying, the muezzin gives the call to prayer and establishes the congregational prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him complete two rak‘ahs and begin the prayer anew with the imam (of prayer), and let the two rak‘ahs be counted as voluntary (nafl) prayer.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ دَخَلَ اَلْمَسْجِدَ فَافْتَتَحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ فَبَيْنَا هُوَ قَائِمٌ يُصَلِّي إِذْ أَذَّنَ اَلْمُؤَذِّنُ فَأَقَامَ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ« فَلْيُصَلِّ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَسْتَأْنِفُ اَلصَّلاَةَ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ لْتَكُنِ اَلرَّكْعَتَانِ تَطَوُّعاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad from al-Husayn from al-Nadr from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who enters the mosque and begins the prayer. While he is standing and praying, the muezzin gives the call to prayer and establishes the congregational prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Then let him complete two rak‘ahs and begin the prayer anew with the imam (of prayer), and let the two rak‘ahs be counted as voluntary (nafl) prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 301

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who catches the imam (of prayer) while he is sitting after the two rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: “He should begin the prayer anew and should not sit with the imam (of prayer) until the imam (of prayer) stands.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَدْرَكَ اَلْإِمَامَ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ بَعْدَ اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ قَالَ« يَفْتَتِحُ اَلصَّلاَةَ وَ لاَ يَقْعُدُ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ حَتَّى يَقُومَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali from Amr ibn Saeed from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who catches the imam (of prayer) while he is sitting after the two rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: “He should begin the prayer anew and should not sit with the imam (of prayer) until the imam (of prayer) stands.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 301

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil from Sama’ah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding a man whom the imam (of prayer) precedes by one rak‘ah, and the imam (of prayer) makes a mistake and prays five rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: “He should repeat that rak‘ah and should not consider the mistake of the imam (of prayer).”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ سَبَقَهُ اَلْإِمَامُ بِرَكْعَةٍ وَ أَوْهَمَ اَلْإِمَامُ فَصَلَّى خَمْساً قَالَ« يُعِيدُ تِلْكَ اَلرَّكْعَةَ وَ لاَ يَعْتَدُّ بِوَهَمِ اَلْإِمَامِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil from Sama’ah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding a man whom the imam (of prayer) precedes by one rak‘ah, and the imam (of prayer) makes a mistake and prays five rak‘ahs. Imam (a.s) said: “He should repeat that rak‘ah and should not consider the mistake of the imam (of prayer).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 302

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Safwan from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “It is proper for the imam (of prayer) that his prayer be according to the weakest among those behind him.” (meaning that the prayer leader keep the prayer of suitable length according to those following him)
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ تَكُونَ صَلاَتُهُ عَلَى أَضْعَفِ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Safwan from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “It is proper for the imam (of prayer) that his prayer be according to the weakest among those behind him.” (meaning that the prayer leader keep the prayer of suitable length according to those following him)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 302

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Abbas from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), performed the noon (Dhuhr) and afternoon (Asr) prayers and shortened the prayer in the last two rak‘ahs. When Prophet (saws) finished, the people said to Him (saws): ‘O Messenger of Allah (swt), has something occurred in the prayer?’ Prophet (saws) said: “And what is that?” They said: “You shortened the last two rak‘ahs.” So Prophet (saws) said to them: “Did you not hear the cry of the child?’”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« صَلَّى رَسُولُ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ فَخَفَّفَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ فَلَمَّا اِنْصَرَفَ قَالَ لَهُ اَلنَّاسُ يَا رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ أَ حَدَثَ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ شَيْءٌ قَالَ« وَ مَا ذَاكَ» قَالُوا خَفَّفْتَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ« أَ مَا سَمِعْتُمْ صُرَاخَ اَلصَّبِيِّ»»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Abbas from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), performed the noon (Dhuhr) and afternoon (Asr) prayers and shortened the prayer in the last two rak‘ahs. When Prophet (saws) finished, the people said to Him (saws): ‘O Messenger of Allah (swt), has something occurred in the prayer?’ Prophet (saws) said: “And what is that?” They said: “You shortened the last two rak‘ahs.” So Prophet (saws) said to them: “Did you not hear the cry of the child?’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 302

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiyah ibn Wahb who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about a man who catches the end of the prayer of the imam (of prayer), while it is the beginning of the man's own prayer. And the imam (of prayer) does not give him time to recite, Should he make up the recitation at the end of his prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes”.
arabicText: عنه عن علي بن السندي عن حماد بن عيسى عن معاوية ابن وهب قال سألت ابا عبد الله ع عن الرجل يدرك آخر صلاة الامام وهي أول صلاة الرجل فلا يمهله حتى يقرأ فيقضي القراءة في آخر صلاته؟ قال نعم
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiyah ibn Wahb who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about a man who catches the end of the prayer of the imam (of prayer), while it is the beginning of the man's own prayer. And the imam (of prayer) does not give him time to recite, Should he make up the recitation at the end of his prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes”.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 302

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami from Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir who said:
I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “If a man, whose background you do not know, leads the people in prayer and he recites the Quran, then do not recite (for yourselves), and count the prayer as valid.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى اَلْخَثْعَمِيِّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحِيمِ اَلْقَصِيرِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا كَانَ اَلرَّجُلُ لاَ تَعْرِفُهُ يَؤُمُّ اَلنَّاسَ فَقَرَأَ اَلْقُرْآنَ فَلاَ تَقْرَأْ وَ اِعْتَدَّ بِصَلاَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khath'ami from Abd al-Rahim al-Qasir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “If a man, whose background you do not know, leads the people in prayer and he recites the Quran, then do not recite (for yourselves), and count the prayer as valid.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 303

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Amraki from Ali ibn Ja’far who said:
(Ali ibn Ja’far said) “I asked Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, about standing behind the imam (of prayer) in the row, what is its limit?” Imam (a.s) said: “Stand as much as you are able, and if you sit and the space becomes tight, then move forward or backward, there is no problem.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْقِيَامِ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فِي اَلصَّفِّ مَا حَدُّهُ قَالَ« إِقَامَةُ مَا اِسْتَطَعْتَ فَإِذَا قَعَدْتَ فَضَاقَ اَلْمَكَانُ فَتَقَدَّمُ أَوْ تَأَخَّرُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Amraki from Ali ibn Ja’far who said:
thaqalaynMatn: (Ali ibn Ja’far said) “I asked Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, about standing behind the imam (of prayer) in the row, what is its limit?” Imam (a.s) said: “Stand as much as you are able, and if you sit and the space becomes tight, then move forward or backward, there is no problem.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 303

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim from Salim Abu Khadijah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you are the imam (of prayer) of a group, then it is upon you to recite in the first two rak‘ahs, and upon those behind you to say: ‘SubhanAllah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu Akbar’ while they are standing. Then, in the last two rak‘ahs, it is upon those behind you to recite the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah), and upon the imam (of prayer) is the ‘tasbih’ in the same way that the people say in the last two rak‘ahs.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي هَاشِمٍ عَنْ سَالِمٍ أَبِي خَدِيجَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كُنْتَ إِمَامَ قَوْمٍ فَعَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَقْرَأَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ وَ عَلَى اَلَّذِينَ خَلْفَكَ أَنْ يَقُولُوا سُبْحَانَ اَللَّهِ وَ اَلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اَللَّهُ وَ اَللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ وَ هُمْ قِيَامٌ فَإِذَا كَانَ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ فَعَلَى اَلَّذِينَ خَلْفَكَ أَنْ يَقْرَءُوا فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ عَلَى اَلْإِمَامِ اَلتَّسْبِيحُ مِثْلَ مَا يُسَبِّحُ اَلْقَوْمُ فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ اَلْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim from Salim Abu Khadijah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you are the imam (of prayer) of a group, then it is upon you to recite in the first two rak‘ahs, and upon those behind you to say: ‘SubhanAllah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu Akbar’ while they are standing. Then, in the last two rak‘ahs, it is upon those behind you to recite the ‘Fatihat al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatihah), and upon the imam (of prayer) is the ‘tasbih’ in the same way that the people say in the last two rak‘ahs.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 303

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir who said:
I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “(When praying) behind someone I do not follow in prayer, what should I do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Finish (your recitation) before he finishes, for you are in confinement (hisar). If he finishes before you, then cut off your recitation and bow with him.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ مَنْ لاَ أَقْتَدِي بِهِ فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« اُفْرُغْ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَفْرُغَ فَإِنَّكَ فِي حِصَارٍ فَإِنْ فَرَغَ قَبْلَكَ فَاقْطَعِ اَلْقِرَاءَةَ وَ اِرْكَعْ مَعَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Ibn Muskan from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: “(When praying) behind someone I do not follow in prayer, what should I do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Finish (your recitation) before he finishes, for you are in confinement (hisar). If he finishes before you, then cut off your recitation and bow with him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 304

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Abu Bakr who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you lead a group in prayer, then sit for a short while after you give the taslim.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عَمِيرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ بِقَوْمٍ فَاقْعُدْ بَعْدَ مَا تُسَلِّمُ هُنَيْئَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn Umayrah from Abu Bakr who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “When you lead a group in prayer, then sit for a short while after you give the taslim.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 304

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And with this chain of transmission, from Abu Bakr who said:
I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “I lead a group in prayer.” Imam (a.s) said, “You give one taslim and do not turn your head. Say: ‘Peace be upon you, O’ Prophet, and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His blessings. Peace be upon you all.’ And do not recite anything from ‘Alif Lam Mim Ha Mim’ in the dawn (Fajr) prayer.” (meaning Huroof al-Muqatta'at that appear at the beginning of 29 Surahs of the Quran)
arabicText: وَ بِهَذَا اَلْإِسْنَادِ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ إِنِّي أُصَلِّي بِقَوْمٍ فَقَالَ« تُسَلِّمُ وَاحِدَةً وَ لاَ تَلْتَفِتْ قُلِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا اَلنَّبِيُّ وَ رَحْمَةُ اَللَّهِ وَ بَرَكَاتُهُ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَ لاَ تَقْرَأْ فِي اَلْفَجْرِ شَيْئاً مِنْ آلِ حم»
thaqalaynSanad: And with this chain of transmission, from Abu Bakr who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “I lead a group in prayer.” Imam (a.s) said, “You give one taslim and do not turn your head. Say: ‘Peace be upon you, O’ Prophet, and the mercy of Allah (swt) and His blessings. Peace be upon you all.’ And do not recite anything from ‘Alif Lam Mim Ha Mim’ in the dawn (Fajr) prayer.” (meaning Huroof al-Muqatta'at that appear at the beginning of 29 Surahs of the Quran)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 304

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm who said:
I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a group in prayer in a narrow place and there is a curtain between him and them. Does it suffice for him to lead them in prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ اَلْجَهْمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي بِالْقَوْمِ فِي مَكَانٍ ضَيِّقٍ وَ يَكُونُ بَيْنَهُمْ وَ بَيْنَهُ سِتْرٌ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ بِهِمْ قَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who leads a group in prayer in a narrow place and there is a curtain between him and them. Does it suffice for him to lead them in prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sulaym al-Farra’ from Dawud who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who is the muezzin of a mosque in a city and also its imam (of prayer). So when Friday comes, he performs the afternoon (Asr) prayer at its proper time, What should he do about his mosque? Imam (a.s) said: “Pray the afternoon (Asr) prayer at its proper time. Then, when that time comes, in which the people of the city give the call to prayer, you too give the adhan and lead them in prayer at the time in which the people of your city pray.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ سُلَيْمٍ اَلْفَرَّاءِ عَنْ دَاوُدَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَكُونُ مُؤَذِّنَ مَسْجِدٍ فِي اَلْمِصْرِ وَ إِمَامَهُ فَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ اَلْجُمُعَةِ صَلَّى اَلْعَصْرَ فِي وَقْتِهَا كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ بِمَسْجِدِهِ قَالَ« صَلِّ اَلْعَصْرَ فِي وَقْتِهَا فَإِذَا كَانَ ذَلِكَ اَلْوَقْتُ اَلَّذِي يُؤَذِّنُ فِيهِ أَهْلُ اَلْمِصْرِ فَأَذِّنْ وَصَلِّ بِهِمْ فِي اَلْوَقْتِ اَلَّذِي يُصَلِّي بِهِمْ فِيهِ أَهْلُ مِصْرِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sulaym al-Farra’ from Dawud who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who is the muezzin of a mosque in a city and also its imam (of prayer). So when Friday comes, he performs the afternoon (Asr) prayer at its proper time, What should he do about his mosque? Imam (a.s) said: “Pray the afternoon (Asr) prayer at its proper time. Then, when that time comes, in which the people of the city give the call to prayer, you too give the adhan and lead them in prayer at the time in which the people of your city pray.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Barqi from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt and al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf all from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Indeed, I dislike for the believer to pray behind the imam (of prayer) in a prayer in which the recitation is not recited aloud, and he stands (mute) as if he were a donkey.” He (al-Azdi) said: “I asked, ‘May I be your ransom, then what should he do?’” Imam (a.s) said: “He should glorify (say tasbih).” (meaning ‘SubhanAllah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu Akbar’)
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي طَالِبٍ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلصَّلْتِ وَ اَلْعَبَّاسِ بْنِ مَعْرُوفٍ كُلِّهِمْ عَنْ بَكْرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ اَلْأَزْدِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« إِنِّي لَأَكْرَهُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فِي صَلاَةٍ لاَ يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فَيَقُومُ كَأَنَّهُ حِمَارٌ» قَالَ قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فَيَصْنَعُ مَاذَا قَالَ« يُسَبِّحُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Barqi from Abu Talib Abdillah ibn al-Salt and al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf all from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Indeed, I dislike for the believer to pray behind the imam (of prayer) in a prayer in which the recitation is not recited aloud, and he stands (mute) as if he were a donkey.” He (al-Azdi) said: “I asked, ‘May I be your ransom, then what should he do?’” Imam (a.s) said: “He should glorify (say tasbih).” (meaning ‘SubhanAllah, wal-hamdu lillah, wa la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu Akbar’)

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Ibrahim ibn Shaybah who said:
I wrote to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about praying behind someone who shows allegiance to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, yet believes in wiping over the leather socks, or behind someone who forbids wiping, yet he himself wipes. Imam (a.s) wrote: “If you and they are gathered in one place and you have no choice but to pray, then give the adhan for yourself and the iqamah. If he begins the recitation before you, then do tasbih (glorify Allah (swt)).”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ شَيْبَةَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ خَلْفَ مَنْ يَتَوَلَّى أَمِيرَ اَلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ وَ هُوَ يَرَى اَلْمَسْحَ عَلَى اَلْخُفَّيْنِ أَوْ خَلْفَ مَنْ يُحَرِّمُ اَلْمَسْحَ وَ هُوَ يَمْسَحُ فَكَتَبَ« إِنْ جَامَعَكَ وَإِيَّاهُمْ مَوْضِعٌ فَلَمْ تَجِدْ بُدّاً مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ فَأَذِّنْ لِنَفْسِكَ وَأَقِمْ فَإِنْ سَبَقَكَ إِلَى اَلْقِرَاءَةِ فَسَبِّحْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Ibrahim ibn Shaybah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about praying behind someone who shows allegiance to the Commander of the Faithful (a.s), peace be upon him, yet believes in wiping over the leather socks, or behind someone who forbids wiping, yet he himself wipes. Imam (a.s) wrote: “If you and they are gathered in one place and you have no choice but to pray, then give the adhan for yourself and the iqamah. If he begins the recitation before you, then do tasbih (glorify Allah (swt)).”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad from Sa’ad ibn Isma'il from his father from al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Ridha (a.s) was asked regarding a man who commits sin, should we pray behind him or not? Imam (a.s) said: “Do not pray (behind him).”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدٌ عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُقَارِفُ اَلذَّنْبَ نُصَلِّي خَلْفَهُ أَمْ لاَ قَالَ «لاَ تُصَلِّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad from Sa’ad ibn Isma'il from his father from al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Ridha (a.s) was asked regarding a man who commits sin, should we pray behind him or not? Imam (a.s) said: “Do not pray (behind him).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 305

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Barqi from Ja’far ibn al-Muthanna al-Khatib from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: “O Ishaq, do you pray with them (the opponents) in the mosque?” I said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray with them, for the one who prays with them in the first row is like one who draws his sword in the way of Allah (swt).” (meaning to have Shia presence in communal religious spaces is a form of jihad)
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ اَلْمُثَنَّى اَلْخَطِيبِ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قَالَ لِي أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« يَا إِسْحَاقُ أَ تُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ» قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ« صَلِّ مَعَهُمْ فَإِنَّ اَلْمُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ فِي اَلصَّفِّ اَلْأَوَّلِ كَالشَّاهِرِ سَيْفَهُ فِي سَبِيلِ اَللَّهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Barqi from Ja’far ibn al-Muthanna al-Khatib from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said to me: “O Ishaq, do you pray with them (the opponents) in the mosque?” I said: “Yes.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray with them, for the one who prays with them in the first row is like one who draws his sword in the way of Allah (swt).” (meaning to have Shia presence in communal religious spaces is a form of jihad)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 306

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn from Ali ibn Yaqtin who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who bows with the imam (of prayer), following him, then raises his head before the imam (of prayer). Imam (a.s) said: “He must repeat his bowing with him.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَرْكَعُ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ يَقْتَدِي بِهِ ثُمَّ يَرْفَعُ رَأْسَهُ قَبْلَ اَلْإِمَامِ قَالَ« يُعِيدُ رُكُوعَهُ مَعَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn from Ali ibn Yaqtin who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who bows with the imam (of prayer), following him, then raises his head before the imam (of prayer). Imam (a.s) said: “He must repeat his bowing with him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 306

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Barqi from Ibn Faddal who said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding a man who was behind an imam (of prayer), following him, and he bowed before the imam (of prayer) thinking that the imam (of prayer) had bowed. When he bowed, he saw that the imam (of prayer) had not bowed, so he raised his head, then repeated the bowing with the imam (of prayer). Does this invalidate his prayer, or is that rak‘ah valid? Imam (a.s) wrote: “He completes his prayer, and what he did does not invalidate his prayer.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْبَرْقِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ فَضَّالٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي رَجُلٍ كَانَ خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ يَأْتَمُّ بِهِ فَرَكَعَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ اَلْإِمَامُ وَ هُوَ يَظُنُّ أَنَّ اَلْإِمَامَ قَدْ رَكَعَ فَلَمَّا رَكَعَ رَآهُ لَمْ يَرْكَعْ فَرَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ ثُمَّ أَعَادَ اَلرُّكُوعَ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ أَ يُفْسِدُ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ صَلاَتَهُ أَمْ تَجُوزُ تِلْكَ اَلرَّكْعَةُ فَكَتَبَ« يُتِمُّ صَلاَتَهُ وَ لاَ يُفْسِدُ مَا صَنَعَ صَلاَتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Barqi from Ibn Faddal who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding a man who was behind an imam (of prayer), following him, and he bowed before the imam (of prayer) thinking that the imam (of prayer) had bowed. When he bowed, he saw that the imam (of prayer) had not bowed, so he raised his head, then repeated the bowing with the imam (of prayer). Does this invalidate his prayer, or is that rak‘ah valid? Imam (a.s) wrote: “He completes his prayer, and what he did does not invalidate his prayer.”

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Sahl from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Ridha (a.s) said: “The imam (of prayer) bears the mistakes (or forgetfulness) of those behind him, except for the opening takbir (takbirat al-ihram).”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَهْلٍ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلْإِمَامُ يَتَحَمَّلُ أَوْهَامَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ إِلاَّ تَكْبِيرَةَ اَلاِفْتِتَاحِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sahl from Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Ridha (a.s) said: “The imam (of prayer) bears the mistakes (or forgetfulness) of those behind him, except for the opening takbir (takbirat al-ihram).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 306

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiyah ibn Wahb who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Does the imam (of prayer) bear responsibility for the obligatory prayer? For these people claim that he does.” Imam (a.s) said: “He does not bear responsibility, what is it that he would bear responsibility for? Except if he were to lead them in prayer while in a state of janabah or without purity?”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ وَهْبٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَ يَضْمَنُ اَلْإِمَامُ صَلاَةَ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فَإِنَّ هَؤُلاَءِ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّهُ يَضْمَنُ فَقَالَ« لاَ يَضْمَنُ أَيَّ شَيْءٍ يَضْمَنُ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ بِهِمْ جُنُباً أَوْ عَلَى غَيْرِ طُهْرٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Saeed from Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiyah ibn Wahb who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “Does the imam (of prayer) bear responsibility for the obligatory prayer? For these people claim that he does.” Imam (a.s) said: “He does not bear responsibility, what is it that he would bear responsibility for? Except if he were to lead them in prayer while in a state of janabah or without purity?”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 306

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Saeed from al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “There is no harm in praying behind a ‘nasib’ (known enemy of the Ahlulbayt (a.s)), and do not recite behind him in that which is recited aloud, for his recitation suffices you, if you hear it.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ تُصَلِّيَ خَلْفَ اَلنَّاصِبِ وَ لاَ تَقْرَأَ خَلْفَهُ فِيمَا يَجْهَرُ فِيهِ فَإِنَّ قِرَاءَتَهُ تُجْزِيكَ إِذَا سَمِعْتَهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Saeed from al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “There is no harm in praying behind a ‘nasib’ (known enemy of the Ahlulbayt (a.s)), and do not recite behind him in that which is recited aloud, for his recitation suffices you, if you hear it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 307

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Ahmad from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about a woman who leads other women in prayer, what is the limit of how loud her voice should be in recitation and takbir? Imam (a.s) said: “As much as she can hear herself.”
arabicText: سعد عن احمد عن موسى بن القاسم وابي قتادة عن علي ابن جعفر عن اخيه عليه السلام قال سألته عن المرأة تؤم النساء ما حد رفع صوتها بالقراءة والتكبير؟ فقال قدر ما تسمع
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Ahmad from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about a woman who leads other women in prayer, what is the limit of how loud her voice should be in recitation and takbir? Imam (a.s) said: “As much as she can hear herself.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 307

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who forgets while he is behind the imam (of prayer), to say the tasbih in prostration or in bowing, or he forgets to say anything between the two prostrations. Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon him.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَنْسَى وَ هُوَ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُسَبِّحَ فِي اَلسُّجُودِ أَوْ فِي اَلرُّكُوعِ أَوْ يَنْسَى أَنْ يَقُولَ بَيْنَ اَلسَّجْدَتَيْنِ شَيْئاً فَقَالَ« لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who forgets while he is behind the imam (of prayer), to say the tasbih in prostration or in bowing, or he forgets to say anything between the two prostrations. Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 307

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who was inattentive behind an imam (of prayer) after he had initiated the prayer, and he did not say anything, nor did he say the takbir, nor the tasbih, nor the tashahhud, until the imam (of prayer) concluded with the salam. Imam (a.s) said: “His prayer is valid, and if he was inattentive behind the imam (of prayer), there is no obligation upon him to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdata al-sahw), because the imam (of prayer) is responsible for the prayer of those behind him.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَهَا خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ بَعْدَ مَا اِفْتَتَحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فَلَمْ يَقُلْ شَيْئاً وَ لَمْ يُكَبِّرْ وَ لَمْ يُسَبِّحْ وَ لَمْ يَتَشَهَّدْ حَتَّى يُسَلِّمَ فَقَالَ« جَازَتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ إِذَا سَهَا خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ سَجْدَتَا اَلسَّهْوِ لِأَنَّ اَلْإِمَامَ ضَامِنٌ لِصَلاَةِ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who was inattentive behind an imam (of prayer) after he had initiated the prayer, and he did not say anything, nor did he say the takbir, nor the tasbih, nor the tashahhud, until the imam (of prayer) concluded with the salam. Imam (a.s) said: “His prayer is valid, and if he was inattentive behind the imam (of prayer), there is no obligation upon him to perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness (sajdata al-sahw), because the imam (of prayer) is responsible for the prayer of those behind him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 307

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah, from Ali ibn Ja’far, from his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Imam al-Khadim (a.s) about a man who is praying behind the imam (of prayer) and does not know how many units he has prayed, does forgetfulness apply to him? Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ اَلْقَاسِمِ وَ أَبِي قَتَادَةَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ لاَ يَدْرِي كَمْ صَلَّى أَ عَلَيْهِ سَهْوٌ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah, from Ali ibn Ja’far, from his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Khadim (a.s) about a man who is praying behind the imam (of prayer) and does not know how many units he has prayed, does forgetfulness apply to him? Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 308

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “Does the imam (of prayer) guarantee the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, he is not a guarantor.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أَ يَضْمَنُ اَلْإِمَامُ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ« لاَ لَيْسَ بِضَامِنٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “Does the imam (of prayer) guarantee the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “No, he is not a guarantor.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 308

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Bashir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
A man asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about recitation behind the imam (of prayer). Imam (a.s) said: “No. Indeed, the imam (of prayer) is a guarantor for the recitation, and the imam (of prayer) does not guarantee the prayer of those behind him; he only guarantees the recitation.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَهُ رَجُلٌ عَنِ اَلْقِرَاءَةِ خَلْفَ اَلْإِمَامِ فَقَالَ« لاَ إِنَّ اَلْإِمَامَ ضَامِنٌ لِلْقِرَاءَةِ وَ لَيْسَ يَضْمَنُ اَلْإِمَامُ صَلاَةَ اَلَّذِينَ خَلْفَهُ وَ إِنَّمَا يَضْمَنُ اَلْقِرَاءَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Bashir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: A man asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about recitation behind the imam (of prayer). Imam (a.s) said: “No. Indeed, the imam (of prayer) is a guarantor for the recitation, and the imam (of prayer) does not guarantee the prayer of those behind him; he only guarantees the recitation.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 308

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you have prayed a prayer while you are in the mosque and the congregational prayer is established, then if you wish, you may leave, and if you wish, pray with them and make it tasbih (supererogatory prayer).”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ صَلاَةً وَ أَنْتَ فِي اَلْمَسْجِدِ وَ أُقِيمَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَإِنْ شِئْتَ فَاخْرُجْ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَصَلِّ مَعَهُمْ وَ اِجْعَلْهَا تَسْبِيحاً»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “If you have prayed a prayer while you are in the mosque and the congregational prayer is established, then if you wish, you may leave, and if you wish, pray with them and make it tasbih (supererogatory prayer).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 308

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The prayer is established while I have already prayed.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray (the established prayer), and count it for what you have missed.”
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن ابن ابي عمير عن سلمة صاحب السابري عن إسحاق بن عمار قال قلت لابي عبد الله عليه السلام تقام الصلاة وقد صليت فقال صل واجعلها لما فات
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Salamah, the companion of al-Sabiri, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “The prayer is established while I have already prayed.” Imam (a.s) said: “Pray (the established prayer), and count it for what you have missed.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 309

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, who said:
I wrote to Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding a man who was behind the imam (of prayer), following him, and he bowed before the imam (of prayer), thinking that the imam (of prayer) had bowed. Then, when he saw that the imam (of prayer) had not bowed, he raised his head and then repeated the bowing with the imam (of prayer). Does this invalidate his prayer, or is the rak’ah valid for him? Imam (a.s) wrote: “He completes his prayer, and what he did does not invalidate his prayer.”
arabicText: سعد عن ابي جعفر عن الحسن بن علي بن فضال قال كتبت إلى الرضا عليه السلام في الرجل كان خلف الامام يأتم به فركع قبل ان يركع الامام وهو يظن ان الامام قد ركع فلما رآه لم يركع رفع رأسه ثم أعاد الركوع مع الامام أيفسد ذلك صلاته أم تجوز له الركعة؟ فكتب يتم صلاته ولا يفسد ما صنع صلاته
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Abu Ja’far from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Imam al-Ridha (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding a man who was behind the imam (of prayer), following him, and he bowed before the imam (of prayer), thinking that the imam (of prayer) had bowed. Then, when he saw that the imam (of prayer) had not bowed, he raised his head and then repeated the bowing with the imam (of prayer). Does this invalidate his prayer, or is the rak’ah valid for him? Imam (a.s) wrote: “He completes his prayer, and what he did does not invalidate his prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 309

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to Imam (a.s): “I prostrate with the imam (of prayer) and I raise my head before him, should I repeat the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Repeat (the prayer) and prostrate.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ حُكَيْمٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ أَسْجُدُ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ وَ أَرْفَعُ رَأْسِي قَبْلَهُ فَأُعِيدُ اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ« أَعِدْ وَ اُسْجُدْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Mu'awiyah ibn Hakim, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam (a.s): “I prostrate with the imam (of prayer) and I raise my head before him, should I repeat the prayer?” Imam (a.s) said: “Repeat (the prayer) and prostrate.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 309

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “It does not harm you to move back behind you if you find crowding in the row, so you move back to the row that is behind you. And if you are in a row and you wish to move forward to the row in front of you, then there is no harm in walking to it.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:« لاَ يَضُرُّكَ أَنْ تَتَأَخَّرَ وَرَاءَكَ إِذَا وَجَدْتَ ضِيقاً فِي اَلصَّفِّ فَتَتَأَخَّرُ إِلَى اَلصَّفِّ اَلَّذِي خَلْفَكَ وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ فِي صَفٍّ فَأَرَدْتَ أَنْ تَتَقَدَّمَ قُدَّامَكَ فَلاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تَمْشِيَ إِلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “It does not harm you to move back behind you if you find crowding in the row, so you move back to the row that is behind you. And if you are in a row and you wish to move forward to the row in front of you, then there is no harm in walking to it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 309

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Fadalah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Complete the rows when you find a gap, and it does not harm you to fall back if you find tightness in the row, and to walk at an angle until you complete the row.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« أَتِمُّوا اَلصُّفُوفَ إِذَا وَجَدْتُمْ خَلَلاً وَ لاَ يَضُرُّكَ أَنْ تَتَأَخَّرَ إِذَا وَجَدْتَ ضِيقاً فِي اَلصَّفِّ وَ تَمْشِيَ مُنْحَرِفاً حَتَّى تُتِمَّ اَلصَّفَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Fadalah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Complete the rows when you find a gap, and it does not harm you to fall back if you find tightness in the row, and to walk at an angle until you complete the row.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 309

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: Ahmad from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: The same.
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: مِثْلَهُ.
thaqalaynMatn: Ahmad from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: The same.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 309

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about a man who stands alone in the row. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm; they (the rows) only appear one after another.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلصَّبَّاحِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَقُومُ فِي اَلصَّفِّ وَحْدَهُ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ إِنَّمَا يَبْدُو وَاحِداً بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Sabbah, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), about a man who stands alone in the row. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm; they (the rows) only appear one after another.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, one day when He (a.s) entered the ‘Sacred Mosque’ for the Asr prayer. When Imam (a.s) was short of reaching the rows, the people bowed, so He (a.s) bowed, then performed the two prostrations, then stood and continued until He (a.s) joined the rows (of the congregation).
arabicText: الحسين بن سعيد عن حماد بن عيسى عن معاوية ابن وهب قال رأيت ابا عبد الله عليه السلام يوما وقد دخل المسجد الحرام لصلاة العصر فلما كان دون الصفوف ركعوا فركع ثم سجد السجدتين ثم قام فمضى حتى لحق بالصفوف
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I saw Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, one day when He (a.s) entered the ‘Sacred Mosque’ for the Asr prayer. When Imam (a.s) was short of reaching the rows, the people bowed, so He (a.s) bowed, then performed the two prostrations, then stood and continued until He (a.s) joined the rows (of the congregation).

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I enter the mosque and the imam (of prayer) has already bowed, so I bow with his bowing while I am alone (away from the congregation), and I prostrate. When I raise my head, what should I do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Stand and go to them (to join the congregation); if they are standing, then stand with them, and if they are sitting, then sit with them.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلْحَكَمِ بْنِ مِسْكِينٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَدْخُلُ اَلْمَسْجِدَ وَ قَدْ رَكَعَ اَلْإِمَامُ فَأَرْكَعُ بِرُكُوعِهِ وَ أَنَا وَحْدِي وَ أَسْجُدُ فَإِذَا رَفَعْتُ رَأْسِي فَأَيَّ شَيْءٍ أَصْنَعُ فَقَالَ «قُمْ فَاذْهَبْ إِلَيْهِمْ فَإِنْ كَانُوا قِيَاماً فَقُمْ مَعَهُمْ وَ إِنْ كَانُوا جُلُوساً فَاجْلِسْ مَعَهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “I enter the mosque and the imam (of prayer) has already bowed, so I bow with his bowing while I am alone (away from the congregation), and I prostrate. When I raise my head, what should I do?” Imam (a.s) said: “Stand and go to them (to join the congregation); if they are standing, then stand with them, and if they are sitting, then sit with them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Salamah from Sulayman ibn Sama'ah from his uncle from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, peace be upon them:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Whoever leads a group in prayer and singles himself out in supplication has betrayed them.’”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ يَحْيَى عَنْ سَلَمَةَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ عَمِّهِ عَنْ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اَللَّهِ صَلَّى اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَالَ:« مَنْ صَلَّى بِقَوْمٍ فَاخْتَصَّ نَفْسَهُ بِالدُّعَاءِ فَقَدْ خَانَهُمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Salamah from Sulayman ibn Sama'ah from his uncle from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), from his forefathers, peace be upon them:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The Messenger of Allah (swt), may Allah (swt) bless him and his family, said: ‘Whoever leads a group in prayer and singles himself out in supplication has betrayed them.’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar and Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said:
Imam (a.s) was asked about a man who missed one rak‘ah of Maghrib with the imam (of prayer) and caught the remaining two rak’ahs. Are those two (rak’ahs) considered his first, while they are the second and third for the group? And does he recite tashahhud in them? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes”. I asked: “And the second one also?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes”. I asked: “All of them?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, for it is a blessing.”
arabicText: عنه عن ايوب بن نوح عن العباس بن عامر عن الحسين ابن المختار وداود بن الحصين قال سئل عن رجل فاتته ركعة من المغرب مع الامام وأدرك الثنتين فهي الاولى له والثانية للقوم يتشهد فيها؟ قال نعم قلت والثانية أيضا قال نعم قلت كلهن قال نعم فانما هو بركة
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar and Dawud ibn al-Husayn, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam (a.s) was asked about a man who missed one rak‘ah of Maghrib with the imam (of prayer) and caught the remaining two rak’ahs. Are those two (rak’ahs) considered his first, while they are the second and third for the group? And does he recite tashahhud in them? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes”. I asked: “And the second one also?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes”. I asked: “All of them?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, for it is a blessing.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 310

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ishaq, by Abdurrahman ibn Hammad, by Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, by Abu al-Hasan (a.s):
Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) said “One who has marks on his face, should not lead the people in prayer.” (meaning referring to leprosy or vitiligo)
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْحَمِيدِ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ يُصَلِّي بِالنَّاسِ مَنْ فِي وَجْهِهِ آثَارٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ishaq, by Abdurrahman ibn Hammad, by Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, by Abu al-Hasan (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) said “One who has marks on his face, should not lead the people in prayer.” (meaning referring to leprosy or vitiligo)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 311

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about a man who gives the adhan and the iqamah to pray alone, then another man comes and says to him, ‘Let us pray in congregation.’ Is it permissible for them to pray with that same adhan and iqamah? Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather he should give the adhan and the iqamah again.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ اَلسَّابَاطِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُؤَذِّنُ وَ يُقِيمُ لِيُصَلِّيَ وَحْدَهُ فَيَجِيءُ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَيَقُولُ لَهُ نُصَلِّي جَمَاعَةً هَلْ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَا بِذَلِكَ اَلْأَذَانِ وَ اَلْإِقَامَةِ قَالَ« لاَ وَ لَكِنْ يُؤَذِّنُ وَ يُقِيمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about a man who gives the adhan and the iqamah to pray alone, then another man comes and says to him, ‘Let us pray in congregation.’ Is it permissible for them to pray with that same adhan and iqamah? Imam (a.s) said: “No, rather he should give the adhan and the iqamah again.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 311

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from al-Ridha (a.s), said:
I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s) about an imam (of prayer) who is praying in a place, and those behind him are praying in a place lower than his, or he is praying in a place and those behind him are in a place higher than his. Imam (a.s) said: “Their place should be level.” I said: “What if he is prays alone and his prostration is lower than where he stands” Imam (a.s) said: “If he is alone, then there is no harm.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنِ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْإِمَامِ يُصَلِّي فِي مَوْضِعٍ وَ اَلَّذِينَ خَلْفَهُ يُصَلُّونَ فِي مَوْضِعٍ أَسْفَلَ مِنْهُ أَوْ يُصَلِّي فِي مَوْضِعٍ وَ اَلَّذِينَ خَلْفَهُ فِي مَوْضِعٍ أَرْفَعَ مِنْهُ فَقَالَ« يَكُونُ مَكَانُهُمْ مُسْتَوِياً» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَيُصَلِّي وَحْدَهُ فَيَكُونُ مَوْضِعُ سُجُودِهِ أَسْفَلَ مِنْ مَقَامِهِ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ وَحْدَهُ فَلاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from al-Ridha (a.s), said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Ridha (a.s) about an imam (of prayer) who is praying in a place, and those behind him are praying in a place lower than his, or he is praying in a place and those behind him are in a place higher than his. Imam (a.s) said: “Their place should be level.” I said: “What if he is prays alone and his prostration is lower than where he stands” Imam (a.s) said: “If he is alone, then there is no harm.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 311

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about a man who leads a group in prayer, is it permissible for him to wear a sash (yatasashah)? Imam (a.s) said: “No. A man must not lead a group in prayer while he is wearing a sash over his clothes, even if he has many clothes on, because it is not permissible for the imam (of prayer) to pray while wearing a sash.” And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who catches the imam (of prayer) just as he has finished with the salam. Imam (a.s) said: “It is upon him to give the adhan and the iqamah and begin the prayer.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةَ عَنْ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَؤُمُّ بِقَوْمٍ هَلْ يَجُوزُ لَهُ أَنْ يَتَوَشَّحَ قَالَ« لاَ لاَ يُصَلِّي اَلرَّجُلُ بِقَوْمٍ وَ هُوَ مُتَوَشِّحٌ فَوْقَ ثِيَابِهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِ ثِيَابٌ كَثِيرَةٌ لِأَنَّ اَلْإِمَامَ لاَ تَجُوزُ لَهُ اَلصَّلاَةُ وَ هُوَ مُتَوَشِّحٌ» وَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ أَدْرَكَ اَلْإِمَامَ حِينَ سَلَّمَ قَالَ «عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ وَ يُقِيمَ وَ يَفْتَتِحَ اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about a man who leads a group in prayer, is it permissible for him to wear a sash (yatasashah)? Imam (a.s) said: “No. A man must not lead a group in prayer while he is wearing a sash over his clothes, even if he has many clothes on, because it is not permissible for the imam (of prayer) to pray while wearing a sash.” And (Imam (a.s) was asked) regarding a man who catches the imam (of prayer) just as he has finished with the salam. Imam (a.s) said: “It is upon him to give the adhan and the iqamah and begin the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 311

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalf ibn Hammad, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Do not pray behind the extremist (ghali), even if he claims your belief, nor behind the unknown person (majhūl, of unknown beliefs), nor behind the one who openly commits immorality (fasiq), even if he is moderate.”
arabicText: عنه عن محمد بن عيسى عن الحسين بن علي بن يقطين عن عمرو بن ابراهيم عن خلف بن حماد عن رجل عن ابي عبد الله عليه السلام قال لا تصلي خلف الغالي وان كان يقول بقولك والمجهول والمجاهر بالفسق وان كان مقتصدا
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalf ibn Hammad, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Do not pray behind the extremist (ghali), even if he claims your belief, nor behind the unknown person (majhūl, of unknown beliefs), nor behind the one who openly commits immorality (fasiq), even if he is moderate.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 312

chapter: Chapter on the Virtue of Mosques and Prayer Within Them, and the Virtue of Congregational Prayer and Its Rulings
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Imam Ja’far (a.s), from his father (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
