chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the Eclipse
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Kufi from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ubaydullah ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Yaqtin who said:
Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever is struck by an earthquake, let him recite: ‘O’ He who holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to be, and if they were to cease, none could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing, Forgiving” (Surah Fatir 35:41). Send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and withhold from us harm. Indeed, You are capable of all things (Surah Aal Imran 3:26).” Imam (a.s) also said: “Indeed, whoever recites it at bedtime, the house will not collapse upon him, Allah (a.s) willing.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ اَلْكُوفِيِّ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« مَنْ أَصَابَتْهُ زَلْزَلَةٌ فَلْيَقْرَأْ يَا مَنْ« يُمْسِكُ اَلسَّمٰاوٰاتِ وَاَلْأَرْضَ أَنْ تَزُولاٰ وَ لَئِنْ زٰالَتٰا إِنْ أَمْسَكَهُمٰا مِنْ أَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ إِنَّهُ كٰانَ حَلِيماً غَفُوراً» صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ وَ أَمْسِكْ عَنَّا اَلسُّوءَ« إِنَّكَ عَلىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ»» قَالَ« إِنَّ مَنْ قَرَأَهَا عِنْدَ اَلنَّوْمِ لَمْ يَسْقُطْ عَلَيْهِ اَلْبَيْتُ إِنْ شَاءَ اَللَّهُ تَعَالَى»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Kufi from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ubaydullah ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Ibn Yaqtin who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, said: “Whoever is struck by an earthquake, let him recite: ‘O’ He who holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to be, and if they were to cease, none could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing, Forgiving” (Surah Fatir 35:41). Send blessings upon (Prophet) Muhammad (saws) and the family of Muhammad (saws), and withhold from us harm. Indeed, You are capable of all things (Surah Aal Imran 3:26).” Imam (a.s) also said: “Indeed, whoever recites it at bedtime, the house will not collapse upon him, Allah (a.s) willing.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad by al-Husayn by al-Nadr and Fadalah by Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “About the obligatory prayer on a ship while he is able to reach land, except that he fears wild beasts and thieves. And he is with people whose opinion is not united on going out and they do not obey him. And should he place his face (on the ground) when he prays, or gesture with signs, or pray sitting, or standing?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he is able to pray standing, that is better. And if he is not able, then let him pray sitting.” And Imam (a.s) said: “There is no blame upon him for not going out (to land), for my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) was asked about a similar matter by a man, and Imam (a.s) said: ‘Do you turn away from the prayer of Nuh (a.s)?’”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنِ اَلنَّضْرِ وَ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْفَرِيضَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ وَ هُوَ يَجِدُ اَلْأَرْضَ يَخْرُجُ إِلَيْهَا غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ يَخَافُ اَلسَّبُعَ وَ اَللُّصُوصَ وَ يَكُونُ مَعَهُ قَوْمٌ لاَ يَجْتَمِعُ رَأْيُهُمْ عَلَى اَلْخُرُوجِ وَ لاَ يُطِيعُونَهُ وَ هَلْ يَضَعُ وَجْهَهُ إِذَا صَلَّى أَوْ يُومِئُ إِيمَاءً أَوْ قَاعِداً أَوْ قَائِماً فَقَالَ« إِنِ اِسْتَطَاعَ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ قَائِماً فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ صَلَّى جَالِساً» وَ قَالَ« لاَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ لاَ يَخْرُجَ فَإِنَّ أَبِي سَأَلَهُ عَنْ مِثْلِ هَذِهِ اَلْمَسْأَلَةِ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ« أَتَرْغَبُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ نُوحٍ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad by al-Husayn by al-Nadr and Fadalah by Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s): “About the obligatory prayer on a ship while he is able to reach land, except that he fears wild beasts and thieves. And he is with people whose opinion is not united on going out and they do not obey him. And should he place his face (on the ground) when he prays, or gesture with signs, or pray sitting, or standing?” Imam (a.s) said: “If he is able to pray standing, that is better. And if he is not able, then let him pray sitting.” And Imam (a.s) said: “There is no blame upon him for not going out (to land), for my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) was asked about a similar matter by a man, and Imam (a.s) said: ‘Do you turn away from the prayer of Nuh (a.s)?’”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 326

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “A man came to my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) and asked him, saying: 'I am on a ship and the shore (al-jadd) is near to me, so I go out and pray on it.'” Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: “Are you not content to pray with the prayer of Nuh (a.s), peace be upon him?”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلسِّنْدِيِّ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ رَجُلاً أَتَى أَبِي فَسَأَلَهُ فَقَالَ إِنِّي أَكُونُ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ وَ اَلْجَدَدُ مِنِّي قَرِيباً فَأَخْرُجُ فَأُصَلِّي عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ« أَ مَا تَرْضَى أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ بِصَلاَةِ نُوحٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ»»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Sindi from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “A man came to my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) and asked him, saying: 'I am on a ship and the shore (al-jadd) is near to me, so I go out and pray on it.'” Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, said to him: “Are you not content to pray with the prayer of Nuh (a.s), peace be upon him?”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Mu‘awiyah ibn Ammar who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “You face the qiblah with your face, then you pray however it (ship) turns. You pray standing, and if you are not able, then pray sitting. He may combine the prayers in it if he wishes, and he may pray on felt (al-qir) and coarse cloth (al-qufr), and prostrate on it.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ «تَسْتَقْبِلُ اَلْقِبْلَةَ بِوَجْهِكَ ثُمَّ تُصَلِّي كَيْفَ دَارَتْ تُصَلِّي قَائِماً فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ فَصَلِّ جَالِساً يَجْمَعُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِيهَا إِنْ أَرَادَ وَ يُصَلِّي عَلَى اَلْقِيرِ وَ اَلْقُفْرِ وَ يَسْجُدُ عَلَيْهِ»

thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “You face the qiblah with your face, then you pray however it (ship) turns. You pray standing, and if you are not able, then pray sitting. He may combine the prayers in it if he wishes, and he may pray on felt (al-qir) and coarse cloth (al-qufr), and prostrate on it.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn from their father Ali ibn Yaqtin who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (Imam al-Kadhim (a.s)), peace be upon him, about a man who is on a ship. May he place mats upon luggage, or cotton, or straw, or wheat, or barley, and the like, then pray upon it? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْمَاضِيَ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ هَلْ لَهُ أَنْ يَضَعَ اَلْحُصُرَ عَلَى اَلْمَتَاعِ أَوِ اَلْقَتِّ أَوِ اَلتِّبْنِ أَوِ اَلْحِنْطَةِ أَوِ اَلشَّعِيرِ وَ أَشْبَاهِهِ ثُمَّ يُصَلِّيَ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»

thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (Imam al-Kadhim (a.s)), peace be upon him, about a man who is on a ship. May he place mats upon luggage, or cotton, or straw, or wheat, or barley, and the like, then pray upon it? Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Salih ibn al-Hakam who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “A man asked my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) about prayer on a ship, and Imam (a.s) said to him: ‘Do you turn away from the prayer of Nuh (a.s), peace be upon him?’” So I asked the Imam (a.s): “Shall I take with me a clod of earth to prostrate on?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ صَالِحِ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ« إِنَّ رَجُلاً سَأَلَ أَبِي عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ لَهُ« أَتَرْغَبُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ نُوحٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ»» فَقُلْتُ لَهُ آخُذُ مَعِي مَدَرَةً أَسْجُدُ عَلَيْهَا فَقَالَ« نَعَمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Salih ibn al-Hakam who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “A man asked my father (Imam al-Baqir (a.s)) about prayer on a ship, and Imam (a.s) said to him: ‘Do you turn away from the prayer of Nuh (a.s), peace be upon him?’” So I asked the Imam (a.s): “Shall I take with me a clod of earth to prostrate on?” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi from al-Amraki al-Bufaki from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The people of the ships perform the prayer in full in their ships.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ اَلْعَلَوِيِّ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ اَلْبُوفَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ قَالَ:« أَصْحَابُ اَلسُّفُنِ يُتِمُّونَ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي سُفُنِهِمْ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi from al-Amraki al-Bufaki from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “The people of the ships perform the prayer in full in their ships.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There is no harm in praying in congregation on a ship.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْعَبَّاسِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« لاَ بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاَةِ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Abbas from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “There is no harm in praying in congregation on a ship.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi from al-‘Amraki al-Bufaki from Ali ibn Ja’far from Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about a group of people, who prayed in congregation on a ship, where does the imam (of prayer) stand? And if there are women with them, how should they proceed? Should they pray standing or sitting? Imam (a.s) said: “They pray standing, and if they are unable to stand, they pray sitting (all of them). The imam (of prayer) stands in front of them, and the women are behind them. And if the ship is narrow, the women sit and the men pray, and there is no harm if the women are beside them.” And I asked Imam (a.s) about a man whose belongings were taken or drowned, and he remained naked, and the time for prayer arrived. How should he pray? Imam (a.s) said: “If he finds grass (or vegetation) with which he can cover his private parts, he should then complete his prayer with bowing and prostration. And if he does not find anything to cover his private parts, he should gesture while standing.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ اَلْعَلَوِيِّ عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ اَلْبُوفَكِيِّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْمٍ صَلَّوْا جَمَاعَةً فِي سَفِينَةٍ أَيْنَ يَقُومُ اَلْإِمَامُ وَإِنْ كَانَ مَعَهُمْ نِسَاءٌ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُونَ أَقِيَاماً يُصَلُّونَ أَمْ جُلُوساً قَالَ« يُصَلُّونَ قِيَاماً فَإِنْ لَمْ يَقْدِرُوا عَلَى اَلْقِيَامِ صَلَّوْا جُلُوساً هُمْ وَ يَقُومُ اَلْإِمَامُ أَمَامَهُمْ وَاَلنِّسَاءُ خَلْفَهُمْ وَ إِنْ ضَاقَتِ اَلسَّفِينَةُ قَعَدْنَ اَلنِّسَاءُ وَ صَلَّى اَلرِّجَالُ وَ لاَ بَأْسَ أَنْ تَكُونَ اَلنِّسَاءُ بِحِيَالِهِمْ» وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ قُطِعَ عَلَيْهِ أَوْ غَرِقَ مَتَاعُهُ فَبَقِيَ عُرْيَاناً وَ حَضَرَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ كَيْفَ يُصَلِّي قَالَ« إِنْ أَصَابَ حَشِيشاً يَسْتُرُ بِهِ عَوْرَتَهُ أَتَمَّ صَلاَتَهُ بِالرُّكُوعِ وَ اَلسُّجُودِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُصِبْ شَيْئاً يَسْتُرُ بِهِ عَوْرَتَهُ أَوْمَى وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi from al-‘Amraki al-Bufaki from Ali ibn Ja’far from Imam Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon them both, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about a group of people, who prayed in congregation on a ship, where does the imam (of prayer) stand? And if there are women with them, how should they proceed? Should they pray standing or sitting? Imam (a.s) said: “They pray standing, and if they are unable to stand, they pray sitting (all of them). The imam (of prayer) stands in front of them, and the women are behind them. And if the ship is narrow, the women sit and the men pray, and there is no harm if the women are beside them.” And I asked Imam (a.s) about a man whose belongings were taken or drowned, and he remained naked, and the time for prayer arrived. How should he pray? Imam (a.s) said: “If he finds grass (or vegetation) with which he can cover his private parts, he should then complete his prayer with bowing and prostration. And if he does not find anything to cover his private parts, he should gesture while standing.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by Sahl ibn Ziyad from Abu Hashim al-Ja’fari, who said:
I was with Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, on a ship in the ‘Tigris River’, and the time for prayer arrived. So I asked: “May I be your ransom, shall we pray in congregation?” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not pray in congregation in the bottom of a valley.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ عَنْ أَبِي هَاشِمٍ اَلْجَعْفَرِيِّ قَالَ: كُنْتُ مَعَ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فِي دِجْلَةَ فَحَضَرَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ فَقُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ نُصَلِّي فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فَقَالَ« لاَ تُصَلِّ فِي بَطْنِ وَادٍ جَمَاعَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by Sahl ibn Ziyad from Abu Hashim al-Ja’fari, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I was with Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, on a ship in the ‘Tigris River’, and the time for prayer arrived. So I asked: “May I be your ransom, shall we pray in congregation?” Imam (a.s) said: “Do not pray in congregation in the bottom of a valley.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, and Ayyub ibn Nuh from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said: Uyaynah narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Maymun:
(Ibn Maymun) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in congregation, on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ وَ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ حَدَّثَنِي عُيَيْنَةُ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, and Ayyub ibn Nuh from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said: Uyaynah narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Maymun:
thaqalaynMatn: (Ibn Maymun) asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in congregation, on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about prayer on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “He should face the qiblah, and when it (ship) turns, if he is able to reorient himself toward the qiblah, then let him do so; otherwise, let him pray in the direction the ship is facing.” Imam (a.s) said: “If he is able to stand, then let him pray standing; otherwise, let him sit and then pray.”
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: إِنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ« يَسْتَقْبِلُ اَلْقِبْلَةَ فَإِذَا دَارَتْ فَاسْتَطَاعَ أَنْ يَتَوَجَّهَ إِلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَلْيَفْعَلْ وَإِلاَّ فَلْيُصَلِّ حَيْثُ تَوَجَّهَتْ بِهِ» قَالَ« فَإِنْ أَمْكَنَهُ اَلْقِيَامُ فَلْيُصَلِّ قَائِماً وَ إِلاَّ فَلْيَقْعُدْ ثُمَّ لْيُصَلِّ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Abdillah (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about prayer on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “He should face the qiblah, and when it (ship) turns, if he is able to reorient himself toward the qiblah, then let him do so; otherwise, let him pray in the direction the ship is facing.” Imam (a.s) said: “If he is able to stand, then let him pray standing; otherwise, let him sit and then pray.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the obligatory prayer on a ship while it is moving east and west. Imam (a.s) said: “Face the qiblah, then say the takbir, then follow the ship and turn with it wherever it turns with you.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ وَ هِيَ تَأْخُذُ شَرْقاً وَ غَرْباً فَقَالَ« اِسْتَقْبِلِ اَلْقِبْلَةَ ثُمَّ كَبِّرْ ثُمَّ اِتْبَعِ اَلسَّفِينَةَ وَ دُرْ مَعَهَا حَيْثُ دَارَتْ بِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about the obligatory prayer on a ship while it is moving east and west. Imam (a.s) said: “Face the qiblah, then say the takbir, then follow the ship and turn with it wherever it turns with you.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in the Euphrates and in rivers weaker than it, while on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “If you pray (on the ship), it is good, and if you go out (to pray on land), it is good also.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ فَضَّالٍ عَنِ اَلْمُفَضَّلِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِي اَلْفُرَاتِ وَ مَا هُوَ أَضْعَفُ مِنْهُ مِنْ اَلْأَنْهَارِ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ فَقَالَ« إِنْ صَلَّيْتَ فَحَسَنٌ وَ إِنْ خَرَجْتَ فَحَسَنٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal from al-Mufaddal ibn Salih who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about prayer in the Euphrates and in rivers weaker than it, while on a ship. Imam (a.s) said: “If you pray (on the ship), it is good, and if you go out (to pray on land), it is good also.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn from their father Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about the ship, if its rider is not able to stand, should he pray while sitting, gesturing, or prostrating? Imam (a.s) said: “He should stand, even if he bends his back.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ يَقْطِينٍ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلسَّفِينَةِ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ صَاحِبُهَا عَلَى اَلْقِيَامِ أَ يُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ يُومِئُ أَوْ يَسْجُدُ قَالَ« يَقُومُ وَ إِنْ حَنَى ظَهْرَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn from their father Ali ibn Yaqtin from Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about the ship, if its rider is not able to stand, should he pray while sitting, gesturing, or prostrating? Imam (a.s) said: “He should stand, even if he bends his back.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from more than one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Prayer on a ship is by gesturing (ima’).”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« اَلصَّلاَةُ فِي اَلسَّفِينَةِ إِيمَاءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from more than one of our companions from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Uyaynah the seller of reeds, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “We travel to Ahwaz on ships, and we combine the prayers in them.” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is no harm in it.” I asked: “And we prostrate on what is in them, and on pitch (al-qir)?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عُيَيْنَةَ بَيَّاعِ اَلْقَصَبِ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ نَخْرُجُ إِلَى اَلْأَهْوَازِ فِي اَلسُّفُنِ فَنَجْمَعُ فِيهَا اَلصَّلاَةَ قَالَ« نَعَمْ لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ» قُلْتُ وَ نَسْجُدُ عَلَى مَا فِيهَا وَ عَلَى اَلْقِيرِ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Uyaynah the seller of reeds, from Ibrahim ibn Maymun who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “We travel to Ahwaz on ships, and we combine the prayers in them.” Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, there is no harm in it.” I asked: “And we prostrate on what is in them, and on pitch (al-qir)?” Imam (a.s) said: “There is no harm.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer in the Ship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Walad who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I had gone out from Kufah on a ship to Qasr Ibn Hubayrah, and it is about twenty farsakhs from Kufah by water. So I travelled that day, shortening the prayer. Then in the night, I decided to return to Kufah, and I did not know whether I should pray on my return with shortening or with full (prayer)? What should I do? Imam (a.s) said: “If you had travelled on the day you departed, a distance of one ‘barid’, then it was upon you, when you returned, to pray with shortening (the prayer), because you remained a traveller until you reached your home.” Imam (a.s) said: “And if you did not travel a distance of one ‘barid’ on the day you departed, then it is incumbent upon you to make up every prayer you performed that day with shortening (the prayer), with full prayers, before you move from that place. This is because you did not reach the location in which shortening is permissible before you returned. So it is obligatory upon you to make up what you shortened. And when you return, you must perform the prayer in full until you reach your home.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي وَلاَّدٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ إِنِّي كُنْتُ خَرَجْتُ مِنَ اَلْكُوفَةِ فِي سَفِينَةٍ إِلَى قَصْرِ اِبْنِ هُبَيْرَةَ وَهُوَ مِنَ اَلْكُوفَةِ عَلَى نَحْوِ عِشْرِينَ فَرْسَخاً فِي اَلْمَاءِ فَسِرْتُ يَوْمِي ذَلِكَ أُقَصِّرُ اَلصَّلاَةَ ثُمَّ بَدَا لِي فِي اَللَّيْلِ اَلرُّجُوعُ إِلَى اَلْكُوفَةِ فَلَمْ أَدْرِ أُصَلِّي فِي رُجُوعِي بِتَقْصِيرٍ أَمْ بِتَمَامٍ وَكَيْفَ كَانَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ أَصْنَعَ فَقَالَ« إِنْ كُنْتَ سِرْتَ فِي يَوْمِكَ اَلَّذِي خَرَجْتَ فِيهِ بَرِيداً فَكَانَ عَلَيْكَ حِينَ رَجَعْتَ أَنْ تُصَلِّيَ بِالتَّقْصِيرِ لِأَ نَّكَ كُنْتَ مُسَافِراً إِلَى أَنْ تَصِيرَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِكَ» قَالَ« وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ لَمْ تَسِرْ فِي يَوْمِكَ اَلَّذِي خَرَجْتَ فِيهِ بَرِيداً فَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تَقْضِيَ كُلَّ صَلاَةٍ صَلَّيْتَهَا فِي يَوْمِكَ ذَلِكَ بِالتَّقْصِيرِ بِتَمَامٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَرِيمَ مِنْ مَكَانِكَ ذَلِكَ لِأَنَّكَ لَمْ تَبْلُغِ اَلْمَوْضِعَ اَلَّذِي يَجُوزُ فِيهِ اَلتَّقْصِيرُ حَتَّى رَجَعْتَ فَوَجَبَ عَلَيْكَ قَضَاءُ مَا قَصَّرْتَ وَ عَلَيْكَ إِذَا رَجَعْتَ أَنْ تُتِمَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ حَتَّى تَصِيرَ إِلَى مَنْزِلِكَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Walad who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s): “I had gone out from Kufah on a ship to Qasr Ibn Hubayrah, and it is about twenty farsakhs from Kufah by water. So I travelled that day, shortening the prayer. Then in the night, I decided to return to Kufah, and I did not know whether I should pray on my return with shortening or with full (prayer)? What should I do? Imam (a.s) said: “If you had travelled on the day you departed, a distance of one ‘barid’, then it was upon you, when you returned, to pray with shortening (the prayer), because you remained a traveller until you reached your home.” Imam (a.s) said: “And if you did not travel a distance of one ‘barid’ on the day you departed, then it is incumbent upon you to make up every prayer you performed that day with shortening (the prayer), with full prayers, before you move from that place. This is because you did not reach the location in which shortening is permissible before you returned. So it is obligatory upon you to make up what you shortened. And when you return, you must perform the prayer in full until you reach your home.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Zur’ah from Sama’ah who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the prisoner who is taken captive by the polytheists, and the time of prayer comes, while the one who captured him prevents him from performing it. Imam (a.s) said: “He should gesture (perform the prayer) by gesturing (ima’a)”.
arabicText: احمد بن محمد بن خالد عن ابيه عن زرعة عن سماعة قال سألته عن الاسير يأسره المشركون فتحضره الصلاة فيمنعه الذي أسره منها قال يؤمي إيماءا
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Zur’ah from Sama’ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about the prisoner who is taken captive by the polytheists, and the time of prayer comes, while the one who captured him prevents him from performing it. Imam (a.s) said: “He should gesture (perform the prayer) by gesturing (ima’a)”.

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma’il who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) and said: “I am on the road to Mecca, and we leave the prayer in places where there are Bedouins. Should we pray the obligatory prayer on the ground and recite only ‘Umm al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatiha), or should we pray on the mount and recite ‘al-Fatiha’ and a surah?” Imam (a.s) said: “If you are afraid, then perform the obligatory prayer and others on the mount. If you recite ‘al-Hamd’ and a surah, that is more beloved to me. But I do not see any harm in what you did.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِسْمَاعِيلَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ فَقُلْتُ أَكُونُ فِي طَرِيقِ مَكَّةَ فَنَتْرُكُ اَلصَّلاَةَ فِي مَوَاضِعَ فِيهَا اَلْأَعْرَابُ أَ نُصَلِّي اَلْمَكْتُوبَةَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ فَنَقْرَأُ أُمَّ اَلْكِتَابِ وَحْدَهَا أَمْ نُصَلِّي عَلَى اَلرَّاحِلَةِ فَنَقْرَأُ فَاتِحَةَ اَلْكِتَابِ وَ اَلسُّورَةَ فَقَالَ« إِذَا خِفْتَ فَصَلِّ عَلَى اَلرَّاحِلَةِ اَلْمَكْتُوبَةَ وَغَيْرَهَا فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ اَلْحَمْدَ وَ سُورَةً أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ وَلاَ أَرَى بِالَّذِي فَعَلْتَ بَأْساً»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma’il who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) and said: “I am on the road to Mecca, and we leave the prayer in places where there are Bedouins. Should we pray the obligatory prayer on the ground and recite only ‘Umm al-Kitab’ (Surah al-Fatiha), or should we pray on the mount and recite ‘al-Fatiha’ and a surah?” Imam (a.s) said: “If you are afraid, then perform the obligatory prayer and others on the mount. If you recite ‘al-Hamd’ and a surah, that is more beloved to me. But I do not see any harm in what you did.”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “About the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “But if you fear, then (pray) on foot or riding” (Surah Al Baqarah 2:239). How do we pray? And what do you say if one fears a wild beast or a thief, how should he pray?” Imam (a.s) said: “He says the takbir and gestures with his head.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجٰالاً أَوْ رُكْبٰاناً» كَيْفَ نُصَلِّي وَ مَا تَقُولُ إِنْ خَافَ مِنْ سَبُعٍ أَوْ لِصٍّ كَيْفَ يُصَلِّي قَالَ« يُكَبِّرُ وَ يُومِئُ بِرَأْسِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s): “About the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: “But if you fear, then (pray) on foot or riding” (Surah Al Baqarah 2:239). How do we pray? And what do you say if one fears a wild beast or a thief, how should he pray?” Imam (a.s) said: “He says the takbir and gestures with his head.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 331

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali from his father from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When the horses move about in turmoil with swords clashing, two takbirs suffice him (for prayer). This is another form of shortening (taqsir).”
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عُذَافِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« إِذَا جَالَتِ اَلْخَيْلُ تَضْطَرِبُ بِالسُّيُوفِ أَجْزَأَهُ تَكْبِيرَتَانِ فَهَذَا تَقْصِيرٌ آخَرُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali from his father from Amr ibn Uthman from Muhammad ibn Udhafir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “When the horses move about in turmoil with swords clashing, two takbirs suffice him (for prayer). This is another form of shortening (taqsir).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 332

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: ‘Then there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may harm you’ (Surah An Nisa 4:101) Imam (a.s) said: “In (from) the two rak‘ahs, one is reduced from them.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ: فِي قَوْلِ اَللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ« فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنٰاحٌ أَنْ تَقْصُرُ وا مِنَ اَلصَّلاٰةِ إِنْ خِفْتُمْ أَنْ يَفْتِنَكُمُ اَلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا» قَالَ« فِي اَلرَّكْعَتَيْنِ يَنْقُصُ مِنْهُمَا وَاحِدَةٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding the saying of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic: ‘Then there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may harm you’ (Surah An Nisa 4:101) Imam (a.s) said: “In (from) the two rak‘ahs, one is reduced from them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 332

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-‘Amraki ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about a man who encounters a wild beast (al-sab‘) and the time for prayer has arrived, but he is unable to walk out of fear of the beast. If he stands to pray, he fears during his bowing and prostration, and the beast is in front of him, not in the direction of the qiblah. So if he turns to face the qiblah, he fears that the lion will leap upon him. What should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should face the lion and pray, and gesture with his head as indication (of bowing and prostration), while standing, even if the lion is not in the direction of the qiblah."
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنِ اَلْعَمْرَكِيِّ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَنْ أَخِيهِ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَلْقَى اَلسَّبُعَ وَ قَدْ حَضَرَتِ اَلصَّلاَةُ وَ لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُ اَلْمَشْيَ مَخَافَةَ اَلسَّبُعِ فَإِنْ قَامَ يُصَلِّي خَافَ فِي رُكُوعِهِ وَ فِي سُجُودِهِ وَاَلسَّبُعُ أَمَامَهُ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ فَإِنْ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى اَلْقِبْلَةِ خَافَ أَنْ يَثِبَ عَلَيْهِ اَلْأَسَدُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ فَقَالَ «يَسْتَقْبِلُ اَلْأَسَدَ وَ يُصَلِّي وَ يُومِئُ بِرَأْسِهِ إِيمَاءً وَ هُوَ قَائِمٌ وَ إِنْ كَانَ اَلْأَسَدُ عَلَى غَيْرِ اَلْقِبْلَةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Yahya from al-‘Amraki ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja’far from his brother Abu al-Hasan (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Kadhim (a.s) about a man who encounters a wild beast (al-sab‘) and the time for prayer has arrived, but he is unable to walk out of fear of the beast. If he stands to pray, he fears during his bowing and prostration, and the beast is in front of him, not in the direction of the qiblah. So if he turns to face the qiblah, he fears that the lion will leap upon him. What should he do? Imam (a.s) said: "He should face the lion and pray, and gesture with his head as indication (of bowing and prostration), while standing, even if the lion is not in the direction of the qiblah."

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 332

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Basir who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “When they meet and engage in battle, then the prayer at that time is with the takbir. And if they are standing, then the prayer is by gesturing [ima'].”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ:« إِذَا اِلْتَقَوْا فَاقْتَتَلُوا فَإِنَّمَا اَلصَّلاَةُ حِينَئِذٍ بِالتَّكْبِيرِ فَإِذَا كَانُوا وُقُوفاً فَالصَّلاَةُ إِيمَاءً»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, say: “When they meet and engage in battle, then the prayer at that time is with the takbir. And if they are standing, then the prayer is by gesturing [ima'].”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 332

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya‘qub from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “When the Maghrib prayer is in a situation of fear, he (imam of prayer) divides them into two groups. He prays with one group two rak‘ahs, then sits with them. Then he signals to them with his hand, so each person among them stands and prays one rak‘ah, then they say the taslim. Then they take the place of their companions. And the other group comes, says the takbir, and enters into the prayer, and the imam (of prayer) stands and prays with them one rak‘ah, then says the taslim. Then each man among them stands and prays one rak‘ah, pairing it with the one he prayed with the imam (of prayer). Then he stands and prays a rak‘ah in which there is no recitation. Thus, the imam (of prayer) completed three rak‘ahs, and the first group had two rak‘ahs in congregation, and the latter group prayed individually. So the first group had the takbir and the opening of the prayer, and the latter had the taslim.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:« إِذَا كَانَ صَلاَةُ اَلْمَغْرِبِ فِي اَلْخَوْفِ فَرَّقَهُمْ فِرْقَتَيْنِ فَيُصَلِّي بِفِرْقَةٍ رَكْعَتَيْنِ ثُمَّ جَلَسَ بِهِمْ ثُمَّ أَشَارَ إِلَيْهِمْ بِيَدِهِ فَقَامَ كُلُّ إِنْسَانٍ مِنْهُمْ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ سَلَّمُوا فَقَامُوا مَقَامَ أَصْحَابِهِمْ وَ جَاءَتِ اَلطَّائِفَةُ اَلْأُخْرَى فَكَبَّرُوا وَ دَخَلُوا فِي اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ قَامَ اَلْإِمَامُ فَصَلَّى بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ سَلَّمَ ثُمَّ قَامَ كُلُّ رَجُلٍ مِنْهُمْ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَةً فَشَفَعَهَا بِالَّتِي صَلَّى مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ ثُمَّ قَامَ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَةً لَيْسَ فِيهَا قِرَاءَةٌ فَتَمَّتْ لِلْإِمَامِ ثَلاَثُ رَكَعَاتٍ وَ لِلْأَوَّلِينَ رَكْعَتَانِ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ وَ لِلْآخَرِينَ وُحْدَاناً فَصَارَ لِلْأَوَّلِينَ اَلتَّكْبِيرُ وَ اِفْتِتَاحُ اَلصَّلاَةِ وَ لِلْآخَرِينَ اَلتَّسْلِيمُ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya‘qub from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “When the Maghrib prayer is in a situation of fear, he (imam of prayer) divides them into two groups. He prays with one group two rak‘ahs, then sits with them. Then he signals to them with his hand, so each person among them stands and prays one rak‘ah, then they say the taslim. Then they take the place of their companions. And the other group comes, says the takbir, and enters into the prayer, and the imam (of prayer) stands and prays with them one rak‘ah, then says the taslim. Then each man among them stands and prays one rak‘ah, pairing it with the one he prayed with the imam (of prayer). Then he stands and prays a rak‘ah in which there is no recitation. Thus, the imam (of prayer) completed three rak‘ahs, and the first group had two rak‘ahs in congregation, and the latter group prayed individually. So the first group had the takbir and the opening of the prayer, and the latter had the taslim.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 333

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText: And this report was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Fudayl and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: in the same manner.
arabicText: وَ رَوَى هَذَا اَلْخَبَرَ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ أُذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ وَ فُضَيْلٍ وَ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ.
thaqalaynMatn: And this report was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Muhammad ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah and Fudayl and Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him: in the same manner.

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 333

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “For the Maghrib prayer in a situation of fear (Salat al-Khawf), he (imam of prayer) prays one rak‘ah with the first group, and they make up two rak‘ahs, and he (imam of prayer) prays two rak‘ahs with the second group, and they make up one rak‘ah.”
arabicText: رَوَى سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ اَلْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَ قَالَ:« صَلاَةُ اَلْخَوْفِ اَلْمَغْرِبَ يُصَلِّي بِالْأَوَّلِينَ رَكْعَةً وَ يَقْضُونَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يُصَلِّي بِالْآخَرِينَ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يَقْضُونَ رَكْعَةً»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn Uthman from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “For the Maghrib prayer in a situation of fear (Salat al-Khawf), he (imam of prayer) prays one rak‘ah with the first group, and they make up two rak‘ahs, and he (imam of prayer) prays two rak‘ahs with the second group, and they make up one rak‘ah.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 333

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Abu al-Mi‘za from Abu Basir who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “What if you saw me at the bank of the Euphrates, praying while I am afraid of a wild beast?” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Should you not have prayed while you were mounted?”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْمِعْزَى عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ لَوْ رَأَيْتَنِي وَ أَنَا بِشَطِّ اَلْفُرَاتِ أُصَلِّي وَ أَنَا أَخَافُ اَلسَّبُعَ فَقَالَ لِي« أَ فَلاَ صَلَّيْتَ وَ أَنْتَ رَاكِبٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from Fadalah from Abu al-Mi‘za from Abu Basir who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him: “What if you saw me at the bank of the Euphrates, praying while I am afraid of a wild beast?” Imam (a.s) said to me: “Should you not have prayed while you were mounted?”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 334

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Ahmad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) and the prayer of travel, Are both to be shortened? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) has more right to be shortened than the prayer of travel, in which there is no fear.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ وَ عَبْدِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي نَجْرَانَ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنْ صَلاَةِ اَلْخَوْفِ وَ صَلاَةِ اَلسَّفَرِ تُقْصَرَانِ جَمِيعاً قَالَ« نَعَمْ وَ صَلاَةُ اَلْخَوْفِ أَحَقُّ أَنْ تُقْصَرَ مِنْ صَلاَةِ اَلسَّفَرِ لَيْسَ فِيهِ خَوْفٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Ahmad from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) and the prayer of travel, Are both to be shortened? Imam (a.s) said: “Yes, and the prayer of ‘al Khawf’ (prayer of fear) has more right to be shortened than the prayer of travel, in which there is no fear.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 334

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of Fear
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Sa’adan from al-Husayn ibn Hammad from Ishaq ibn Ammar from someone who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “One who fears a wild beast, or fears an enemy that may attack him, or fears thieves; he performs the obligatory prayer on his mount by gesturing (ima’a).”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ مُوسَى بْنِ سَعْدَانَ عَنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ إِسْحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ عَمَّنْ حَدَّثَهُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ:« فِي اَلَّذِي يَخَافُ اَلسَّبُعَ أَوْ يَخَافُ عَدُوّاً يَثِبُ عَلَيْهِ أَوْ يَخَافُ اَللُّصُوصَ يُصَلِّي عَلَى دَابَّتِهِ إِيمَاءً اَلْفَرِيضَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Sa’adan from al-Husayn ibn Hammad from Ishaq ibn Ammar from someone who narrated to him from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “One who fears a wild beast, or fears an enemy that may attack him, or fears thieves; he performs the obligatory prayer on his mount by gesturing (ima’a).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 334

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I heard Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) say, regarding one who is unconscious; Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever Allah (swt) has caused to overcome him (for him to faint), then Allah (swt) is more entitled to excuse.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصِ بْنِ اَلْبَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: فِي اَلْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ قَالَ« مَا غَلَبَ اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِالْعُذْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bukhtari from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I heard Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) say, regarding one who is unconscious; Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever Allah (swt) has caused to overcome him (for him to faint), then Allah (swt) is more entitled to excuse.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 334

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Ibrahim al-Khazzaz Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who was unconscious for days, and did not pray, then regained consciousness. Should he make up what he missed? Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing (of qadha) upon him.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ يُونُسَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ اَلْخَزَّازِ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَيَّاماً لَمْ يُصَلِّ ثُمَّ أَفَاقَ أَ يُصَلِّي مَا فَاتَهُ قَالَ« لاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Ibrahim al-Khazzaz Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who was unconscious for days, and did not pray, then regained consciousness. Should he make up what he missed? Imam (a.s) said: “There is nothing (of qadha) upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 335

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Murazim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a sick person who is not able to perform the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever Allah (swt) has caused to overcome him (to faint), then Allah (swt) is more entitled to excuse.”
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ حَدِيدٍ عَنْ مُرَازِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمَرِيضِ لاَ يَقْدِرُ عَلَى اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ فَقَالَ« كُلَّمَا غَلَبَ اَللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِالْعُذْرِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Murazim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a sick person who is not able to perform the prayer. Imam (a.s) said: “Whatever Allah (swt) has caused to overcome him (to faint), then Allah (swt) is more entitled to excuse.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 335

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hajjal from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun from Ma‘mar ibn Umar who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the sick person, does he make up the prayer if he was unconscious? Imam (a.s) said: “No.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَجَّالِ عَنْ ثَعْلَبَةَ بْنِ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ مَعْمَرِ بْنِ عُمَرَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمَرِيضِ يَقْضِي اَلصَّلاَةَ إِذَا أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ« لاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Hajjal from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun from Ma‘mar ibn Umar who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the sick person, does he make up the prayer if he was unconscious? Imam (a.s) said: “No.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 335

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman who said:
I wrote to the jurist (faqih) Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about the one who falls unconscious for a day or more. Does he have to make up the prayers that he missed or not? So Imam (a.s) wrote: “He does not make up the fast, nor does he make up the prayer.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى اَلْفَقِيهِ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلْعَسْكَرِيِّ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ يَوْماً أَوْ أَكْثَرَ هَلْ يَقْضِي مَا فَاتَهُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ أَمْ لاَ فَكَتَبَ« لاَ يَقْضِي اَلصَّوْمَ وَ لاَ يَقْضِي اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to the jurist (faqih) Abu al-Hasan al-Askari (a.s), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about the one who falls unconscious for a day or more. Does he have to make up the prayers that he missed or not? So Imam (a.s) wrote: “He does not make up the fast, nor does he make up the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 335

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Ayyub ibn Nuh who said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s) (the Third), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about the one who falls unconscious for a day or more. Does he have to make up the prayers that he missed or not? So Imam (a.s) wrote: “He does not make up the fast, nor does he make up the prayer.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَيُّوبَ بْنِ نُوحٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ اَلثَّالِثِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ أَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ اَلْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ يَوْماً أَوْ أَكْثَرَ هَلْ يَقْضِي مَا فَاتَهُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ أَمْ لاَ فَكَتَبَ« لاَ يَقْضِي اَلصَّوْمَ وَ لاَ يَقْضِي اَلصَّلاَةَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Ayyub ibn Nuh who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith (a.s) (the Third), peace be upon him, asking Imam (a.s) about the one who falls unconscious for a day or more. Does he have to make up the prayers that he missed or not? So Imam (a.s) wrote: “He does not make up the fast, nor does he make up the prayer.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 335

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about the sick person who falls unconscious. He said: “If three days pass over him, then there is no obligation upon him to make it up; and if he is unconscious for three days, then he must make up the prayers during them.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرِيضِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ قَالَ« إِذَا جَازَ عَلَيْهِ ثَلاَثَةُ أَيَّامٍ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ قَضَاءٌ وَ إِذَا أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ ثَلاَثَةَ أَيَّامٍ فَعَلَيْهِ قَضَاءُ اَلصَّلاَةِ فِيهِنَّ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about the sick person who falls unconscious. He said: “If three days pass over him, then there is no obligation upon him to make it up; and if he is unconscious for three days, then he must make up the prayers during them.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 336

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the one who falls unconscious. Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up the prayer of one day.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ قَالَ فَقَالَ« يَقْضِي صَلاَةَ يَوْمٍ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Yaqub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the one who falls unconscious. Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up the prayer of one day.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 336

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Alaa ibn al-Fudayl, said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who falls unconscious from the day until the night, then regains consciousness. Imam (a.s) said: “If he regains consciousness before sunset, then he must make up the prayer of that day. But if he remains unconscious for a number of days, then he is only required to make up the prayer of the last of those days, if he regains consciousness before sunset. Otherwise, there is nothing upon him to make up.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اَلْجَبَّارِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ بْنِ اَلْفُضَيْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ يَوْماً إِلَى اَللَّيْلِ ثُمَّ يُفِيقُ قَالَ« إِنْ أَفَاقَ قَبْلَ غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَعَلَيْهِ قَضَاءُ يَوْمِهِ هَذَا فَإِنْ أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ أَيَّاماً ذَوَاتِ عَدَدٍ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَقْضِيَ إِلاَّ آخِرَ أَيَّامِهِ إِنْ أَفَاقَ قَبْلَ غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ وَ إِلاَّ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ قَضَاءٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Alaa ibn al-Fudayl, said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man who falls unconscious from the day until the night, then regains consciousness. Imam (a.s) said: “If he regains consciousness before sunset, then he must make up the prayer of that day. But if he remains unconscious for a number of days, then he is only required to make up the prayer of the last of those days, if he regains consciousness before sunset. Otherwise, there is nothing upon him to make up.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 336

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
And Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Abu Basir from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the sick person, who falls unconscious and then regains consciousness, how does he make up his prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up the prayer whose time he caught.”
arabicText: وَ رَوَى أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرِيضِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُفِيقُ كَيْفَ يَقْضِي صَلاَتَهُ قَالَ« يَقْضِي اَلصَّلاَةَ اَلَّتِي أَدْرَكَ وَقْتَهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri’ab from Abu Basir from one of the two Imams (a.s), peace be upon them, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about the sick person, who falls unconscious and then regains consciousness, how does he make up his prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up the prayer whose time he caught.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 336

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Sa’ad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubaydullah al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam (a.s) about the sick person, does he make up the prayer if he falls unconscious? Imam (a.s) said: “No, except for the prayer during which he regained consciousness.”
arabicText: سَعْدٌ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ اَللَّهِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرِيضِ هَلْ يَقْضِي اَلصَّلاَةَ إِذَا أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ« لاَ إِلاَّ اَلصَّلاَةَ اَلَّتِي أَفَاقَ فِيهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Sa’ad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ubaydullah al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam (a.s) about the sick person, does he make up the prayer if he falls unconscious? Imam (a.s) said: “No, except for the prayer during which he regained consciousness.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 336

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “He makes up the prayer during which he regained consciousness.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَفْصٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« يَقْضِي اَلصَّلاَةَ اَلَّتِي أَفَاقَ فِيهَا»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hafs from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “He makes up the prayer during which he regained consciousness.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 336

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Everything you left of your prayer due to an illness, in which you were rendered unconscious, make it up when you regain consciousness.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« كُلُّ شَيْءٍ تَرَكْتَهُ مِنْ صَلاَتِكَ لِمَرَضٍ أُغْمِيَ عَلَيْكَ فِيهِ فَاقْضِهِ إِذَا أَفَقْتَ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (a.s):
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) said: “Everything you left of your prayer due to an illness, in which you were rendered unconscious, make it up when you regain consciousness.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 337

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Safwan from al-Alaa from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s) about the man who falls unconscious, and then regains consciousness. Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up what he missed, he gives the adhan for the first prayer and gives the iqamah for the rest (when making up missed prayers).”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنِ اَلْعَلاَءِ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ ثُمَّ يُفِيقُ قَالَ« يَقْضِي مَا فَاتَهُ يُؤَذِّنَ فِي اَلْأُولَى وَ يُقِيمُ فِي اَلْبَقِيَّةِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Safwan from al-Alaa from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Baqir (a.s) about the man who falls unconscious, and then regains consciousness. Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up what he missed, he gives the adhan for the first prayer and gives the iqamah for the rest (when making up missed prayers).”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 337

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding the one who falls unconscious. Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up everything that he missed.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: فِي اَلْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ قَالَ« يَقْضِي كُلَّ مَا فَاتَهُ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Safwan from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked regarding the one who falls unconscious. Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up everything that he missed.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 337

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rifaa'ah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the one who falls unconscious for a month, what does he make up of the prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up all of it. Indeed, the matter of prayer is severe.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ رِفَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ شَهْراً مَا يَقْضِي مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ قَالَ« يَقْضِيهَا كُلَّهَا إِنَّ أَمْرَ اَلصَّلاَةِ شَدِيدٌ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr from Rifaa'ah from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the one who falls unconscious for a month, what does he make up of the prayer? Imam (a.s) said: “He makes up all of it. Indeed, the matter of prayer is severe.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 337

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad who said:
I wrote to him; “May I be ransomed for you, it has been narrated from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding a sick person who becomes unconscious for several days. Some have said he makes up the prayer of the day in which he regains consciousness, and some have said he makes up the prayers of three days and leaves what is beyond that, and some have said that there is no make-up upon him.” So Imam (a.s) wrote: “He makes up the prayer of the day in which he regains consciousness.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَيْهِ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ رُوِيَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ فِي اَلْمَرِيضِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ أَيَّاماً فَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ يَقْضِي صَلاَةَ يَوْمِهِ اَلَّذِي أَفَاقَ فِيهِ وَقَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ يَقْضِي صَلاَةَ ثَلاَثَةِ أَيَّامٍ وَ يَدَعُ مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ وَ قَالَ بَعْضُهُمْ إِنَّهُ لاَ قَضَاءَ عَلَيْهِ فَكَتَبَ« يَقْضِي صَلاَةَ اَلْيَوْمِ اَلَّذِي يُفِيقُ فِيهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I wrote to him; “May I be ransomed for you, it has been narrated from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, regarding a sick person who becomes unconscious for several days. Some have said he makes up the prayer of the day in which he regains consciousness, and some have said he makes up the prayers of three days and leaves what is beyond that, and some have said that there is no make-up upon him.” So Imam (a.s) wrote: “He makes up the prayer of the day in which he regains consciousness.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 337

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who falls unconscious during the day and then regains consciousness before sunset. Imam (a.s) said: “He performs the Dhuhr and Asr prayers, and if he regains consciousness during the night before dawn, he makes up the night (Isha) prayers.”
arabicText: فَأَمَّا مَا رَوَاهُ اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنْ شُعَيْبٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ نَهَاراً ثُمَّ يُفِيقُ قَبْلَ غُرُوبِ اَلشَّمْسِ فَقَالَ« يُصَلِّي اَلظُّهْرَ وَ اَلْعَصْرَ وَ مِنَ اَللَّيْلِ إِذَا أَفَاقَ قَبْلَ اَلصُّبْحِ قَضَى صَلاَةَ اَللَّيْلِ»
thaqalaynSanad: As for what was narrated by al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about a man who falls unconscious during the day and then regains consciousness before sunset. Imam (a.s) said: “He performs the Dhuhr and Asr prayers, and if he regains consciousness during the night before dawn, he makes up the night (Isha) prayers.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 337

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the one suffering from abdominal illness (al-mabtun). Imam (a.s) said: “He builds upon his prayer.” (meaning performs ablution again, and continues from where he left it)
arabicText: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْرٍ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلْمَبْطُونِ فَقَالَ« يَبْنِي عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, about the one suffering from abdominal illness (al-mabtun). Imam (a.s) said: “He builds upon his prayer.” (meaning performs ablution again, and continues from where he left it)

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 338

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Muhammad ibn Nusayr from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The one afflicted with overpowering abdominal illness (sahib al-batn al-ghalib) performs ablution for his prayer and completes what remains.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ نُصَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:« صَاحِبُ اَلْبَطْنِ اَلْغَالِبِ يَتَوَضَّأُ فِي صَلاَتِهِ فَيُتِمُّ مَا بَقِيَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud from Muhammad ibn Nusayr from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja’far ibn Bashir from Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja’far (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Baqir (a.s) said: “The one afflicted with overpowering abdominal illness (sahib al-batn al-ghalib) performs ablution for his prayer and completes what remains.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 338

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from Muhammad ibn Nusayr from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about the dripping of urine (incontinence). Imam (a.s) said: “He should place a pouch (khariitah, to absorb), when he prays.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ نُصَيْرٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى عَنِ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنِ اَلْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ: سُئِلَ عَنْ تَقْطِيرِ اَلْبَوْلِ قَالَ« يَجْعَلُ خَرِيطَةً إِذَا صَلَّى»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from Muhammad ibn Nusayr from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about the dripping of urine (incontinence). Imam (a.s) said: “He should place a pouch (khariitah, to absorb), when he prays.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 338

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about the sick person who is not able to sit. He said: “Then let him pray while lying down, and let him place something on his forehead when he prostrates, for it suffices for him. And Allah (swt) will not burden a soul beyond its capacity.”
arabicText: اَلْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدٍ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرِيضِ لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُ اَلْجُلُوسَ قَالَ« فَلْيُصَلِّ وَ هُوَ مُضْطَجِعٌ وَ لْيَضَعْ عَلَى جَبْهَتِهِ شَيْئاً إِذَا سَجَدَ فَإِنَّهُ يُجْزِي عَنْهُ وَ لَنْ يُكَلِّفَ اَللَّهُ مَا لاَ طَاقَةَ لَهُ بِهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about the sick person who is not able to sit. He said: “Then let him pray while lying down, and let him place something on his forehead when he prostrates, for it suffices for him. And Allah (swt) will not burden a soul beyond its capacity.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 338

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
From him, from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:
I asked him about a man who has water in his eyes and has it removed, and then lies on his back for many days; forty days, less or more and refrains from prayer during those days while he is in that condition. He said: “There is no harm in that, and there is nothing among what Allah (swt) has forbidden except that He (azj) has made it lawful for the one who is compelled to it.”
arabicText: عَنْهُ عَنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ زُرْعَةَ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَكُونَ فِي عَيْنَيْهِ اَلْمَاءُ فَيَنْزِعُ اَلْمَاءَ مِنْهَا فَيَسْتَلْقِي عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ اَلْأَيَّامَ اَلْكَثِيرَةَ أَرْبَعِينَ يَوْماً أَقَلَّ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ فَيَمْتَنِعُ مِنَ اَلصَّلاَةِ اَلْأَيَّامَ وَ هُوَ عَلَى حَالٍ فَقَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ وَ لَيْسَ شَيْءٌ مِمَّا حَرَّمَ اَللَّهُ إِلاَّ وَ قَدْ أَحَلَّهُ لِمَنِ اُضْطُرَّ إِلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: From him, from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked him about a man who has water in his eyes and has it removed, and then lies on his back for many days; forty days, less or more and refrains from prayer during those days while he is in that condition. He said: “There is no harm in that, and there is nothing among what Allah (swt) has forbidden except that He (azj) has made it lawful for the one who is compelled to it.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 338

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Iys who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man upon whom a year's worth of prayer has accumulated, due to illness. Imam (a.s) said: “He does not make them up.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ اَلْحُسَيْنِ عَنْ صَفْوَانَ عَنْ عِيصٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ اِجْتَمَعَ عَلَيْهِ صَلاَةُ سَنَةٍ مِنْ مَرَضٍ قَالَ« لاَ يَقْضِي»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Iys who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, about a man upon whom a year's worth of prayer has accumulated, due to illness. Imam (a.s) said: “He does not make them up.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 339

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I said to Imam al-Baqir (a.s): “A man fell ill and left the supererogatory prayer (al-nafilah).” Imam said: “O Muhammad, it is not an obligation. If he makes it up, then it is a good deed that he does, and if he does not do it, then there is nothing upon him.”
arabicText: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَّادٍ عَنْ حَرِيزٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ رَجُلٌ مَرِضَ فَتَرَكَ اَلنَّافِلَةَ قَالَ« يَا مُحَمَّدُ لَيْسَتْ بِفَرِيضَةٍ إِنْ قَضَاهَا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ يَفْعَلُهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلْ فَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I said to Imam al-Baqir (a.s): “A man fell ill and left the supererogatory prayer (al-nafilah).” Imam said: “O Muhammad, it is not an obligation. If he makes it up, then it is a good deed that he does, and if he does not do it, then there is nothing upon him.”

gradingsFull.reference_en: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām fī Sharḥ al-Muqniʿah, vol. 3, p. 339

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Ali from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Mu'awiyah ibn Maysarah: that Sinan asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about a man who stretches out one of his legs in front of him while sitting. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem, and I do not see it except, in the case of someone afflicted (al-mu'tall) or sick (al-marid).”
arabicText: عَلِيٌّ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ بْنِ اَلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ مَيْسَرَةَ: أَنَّ سِنَاناً سَأَلَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يَمُدُّ إِحْدَى رِجْلَيْهِ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ قَالَ« لاَ بَأْسَ وَ لاَ أَرَاهُ إِلاَّ فِي اَلْمُعْتَلِّ أَوِ اَلْمَرِيضِ»
thaqalaynSanad: Ali from his father from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah from Mu'awiyah ibn Maysarah: that Sinan asked Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him:
thaqalaynMatn: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) was asked about a man who stretches out one of his legs in front of him while sitting. Imam (a.s) said: “There is no problem, and I do not see it except, in the case of someone afflicted (al-mu'tall) or sick (al-marid).”

chapter: Chapter on the Prayer of the One in Necessity
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī
englishText:
Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the sick person, whether it is permissible for him to stand on his bed and prostrate on the ground? Imam (a.s) said: “If the bed is thick to the extent of a brick (ajurrah) or less, then it is correct for him to stand on it and prostrate on the ground. But if it is more than that, then no.”
arabicText: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَحْمَدَ عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ اَلْحَسَنِ عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ سَعِيدٍ عَنْ مُصَدِّقِ بْنِ صَدَقَةً عَنْ عَمَّارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اَللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ اَلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ اَلْمَرِيضِ أَيَحِلُّ لَهُ أَنْ يَقُومَ عَلَى فِرَاشِهِ وَ يَسْجُدَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ قَالَ فَقَالَ« إِذَا كَانَ اَلْفِرَاشُ غَلِيظاً قَدْرَ آجُرَّةٍ أَوْ أَقَلَّ اِسْتَقَامَ لَهُ أَنْ يَقُومَ عَلَيْهِ وَ يَسْجُدَ عَلَى اَلْأَرْضِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَلاَ»
thaqalaynSanad: Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from Ammar from Abu Abdillah (a.s), peace be upon him, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: I asked Imam al-Sadiq (a.s) about the sick person, whether it is permissible for him to stand on his bed and prostrate on the ground? Imam (a.s) said: “If the bed is thick to the extent of a brick (ajurrah) or less, then it is correct for him to stand on it and prostrate on the ground. But if it is more than that, then no.”
